  • 2+ years in hospitality, hotel, retail, or travel
  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • Comfort with software, apps, and property management tools
  • Detail orientation and a proactive approach to anticipating needs
  • A polished, professional appearance
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds (package volume is real, especially Q4)

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 10 AM to 7 PM, at a rate of $23.08 per hour with bonus eligibility. Bozzuto's benefits package covers medical, dental, and vision, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Bilingual Senior Service Manager - North Atlanta
job.description:
Bilingual maintenance leadership at the senior level draws on a specific combination of skills: deep technical knowledge across multiple trades, the ability to develop people who may be early in their careers, and enough Spanish fluency to communicate clearly when it counts. This role at Cortland's Peachtree Corners community puts all three to work every day.

The Technical Side of the Work

You'll oversee all maintenance operations for a multifamily community, which means scheduling preventative maintenance, inspecting technician work, and stepping in personally on complex repairs involving HVAC, electrical, plumbing, appliances, gas fixtures, and flooring. The paperwork side is real too: service request logs, vacant unit documentation, refrigerant logs, pool logs, MSDS records, and HAZCOM materials all need to stay current. Universal EPA certification, CPO, and HVAC certifications are required coming in, not something you'll earn on the job here.

Vendor coordination falls under your scope as well. When a repair goes beyond what the in-house team handles, you're the one managing the relationship, holding vendors accountable for quality, and keeping costs in line with the approved budget.

Leading the Team

You'll hire, onboard, coach, and evaluate maintenance technicians. That includes writing performance plans, running on-call rotations, and making sure the team works in compliance with ADA, Fair Housing, OSHA, EPA, and lead-based paint regulations. Strong candidates for this role tend to be teachers by instinct. The technical skills matter, but the real differentiator at the senior level is whether you can bring up the people around you, not just fix things yourself.

The bilingual requirement reflects the community's resident population. Spanish fluency helps during resident interactions, service request follow-ups, and team communication. It's listed as preferred, but given the location and the team dynamics in North Atlanta's multifamily market, it's a genuine advantage.

What to Expect Day-to-Day

A typical day might start with a morning walkthrough to check exterior conditions and review overnight service requests, then move into coordinating make-ready turns on vacant units, meeting with a vendor about a pending repair, and closing out the day's punch list with your team. On-call rotations mean some evenings and weekends will come with calls that pull you away from whatever else you had planned. That's not a complaint buried in the job description, it's just the nature of senior maintenance work in multifamily.

Cortland operates as a vertically integrated owner-operator, which means decisions about the asset tend to move faster than they do at third-party managed properties. You're working inside the ownership structure, not between a management company and a separate owner. For a Senior Service Manager, that usually translates to clearer budget authority and fewer layers of approval for day-to-day operational decisions.

What This Role Requires

  • 5 to 6 or more years of maintenance experience spanning carpentry, plumbing, electrical, and HVAC; multifamily experience is preferred
  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred
  • Universal EPA, CPO, and HVAC certifications required
  • Valid Class E driver's license
  • High school diploma or equivalent; technical training or college coursework is a plus
  • Working knowledge of ADA, Fair Housing, OSHA, and EPA regulations
  • Ability to read technical manuals and equipment documentation
  • Physical ability to perform hands-on maintenance tasks, including lifting and climbing
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call rotation

job.title: Business Manager (Property Manager) - Phoenix, AZ
job.description:
Most multifamily operators separate the financial stewardship of an asset from the day-to-day people management. The reality is those two things are inseparable, and the Business Manager role at Olympus Property is built around that truth. You're running the full operation: NOI, occupancy, team performance, and resident experience all sit on the same desk.

What the Role Actually Covers

Olympus uses the title "Business Manager" deliberately. This is a conventional Property Manager position in scope, but the framing reflects what they expect: someone who reads a T-12 with the same fluency they use to walk a punch list. You'll own the annual budget, monthly variance reporting, and business plan forecasts while keeping the Regional Manager and Regional VP informed on performance trends and strategy. On any given week, that might mean reviewing delinquency with your leasing team in the morning and negotiating a vendor contract in the afternoon.

The day-to-day also includes supervising both office and maintenance staff, which means you're accountable for the full cycle of the resident experience from traffic through renewal. Olympus places real emphasis on retention programs and renewal strategy, so if your instinct is to chase new leases rather than protect existing ones, that's worth reflecting on before applying. Market-ready unit condition and regular property inspections are part of the cadence here, not occasional checkboxes.

Luxury Class A experience is preferred, which signals the expectation around service standards, finish quality, and the kind of resident who has options and knows it.

What Olympus Brings to the Table

Olympus has earned recognition as a top employer through the National Apartment Association three consecutive years, which in our industry means their internal culture metrics hold up to outside scrutiny. They offer a compensation structure that includes base pay, monthly commissions, and quarterly and annual bonuses. The base range for this Phoenix role sits at $75,000 to $80,000, with the variable comp giving strong operators real upside.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, an apartment rental allowance, and tuition reimbursement. They also offer a sabbatical program and structured career pathing, including Budget Camp and leadership conferences, which is worth noting if you're a PM who wants to move toward a Regional role. That's typically where this position leads for high performers, and Olympus appears to build that ladder intentionally.

Who Fits This Role

  • Minimum two years of experience as a Property Manager in multifamily
  • Comfort with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite is strongly preferred
  • Available Monday through Friday with flexibility for resident events and emergencies outside standard hours
  • Able to lead a mixed team of leasing and maintenance staff without leaning too hard on either side

The candidates who tend to thrive in roles like this are the ones who don't need to be reminded that financial performance and resident satisfaction aren't competing priorities. They move between a budget spreadsheet and a community tour without losing a step. If you've managed a Class A asset and have the financial reporting experience to back it up, Phoenix is a market where Olympus has real presence and this role has real teeth.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Assistant Community Manager at Millis and Main in Jamestown, NC sits at the intersection of leasing production and financial operations. On any given day, that means walking a prospect through an available home in the morning, then spending part of the afternoon reviewing ledgers for billing accuracy or making weekly delinquency follow-up calls. It's a full-cycle role where occupancy and NOI both land on your desk.

On the leasing side, you'll handle incoming traffic, conduct tours, manage the application and renewal pipeline, and work toward occupancy targets alongside the Community Manager. You'll also own the community's social media presence, which at a garden-style property like this one means keeping resident events visible and the community's identity consistent online.

The financial piece is more substantial than it is in a pure leasing role. You'll oversee rent collection, payment posting, and check scanning, monitor delinquency, and coordinate eviction procedures when necessary. Regular ledger reviews to verify payment applications and account accuracy are part of the routine, not an occasional task. You'll also contribute to reporting for regional leadership, so comfort with financial documentation matters here.

When the Community Manager is off-site or unavailable, you step into the lead position. That means keeping the team focused, handling escalated resident concerns, and making sure daily operations don't lose momentum.

What You Bring

  • Two years of property management experience, with at least six months in an assistant community manager capacity preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to read and act on financial reports, including delinquency tracking and basic ledger review
  • Leasing experience with a track record of converting traffic to signed leases
  • Strong conflict resolution skills and the composure to de-escalate difficult resident situations professionally
  • Valid driver's license required; a CALP designation is a plus
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to maintain a 40-hour week. Some evening or weekend availability may come up for resident events.

The Role in Context

Hawthorne Residential Partners is a Southeast-based multifamily operator that ranks among the 50 largest in the country. The Piedmont Triad market, where Jamestown sits, has seen steady apartment demand anchored by the Greensboro-High Point metro's distribution, healthcare, and manufacturing employment base. For an ACM building their career, Hawthorne's internal Career Path Program offers a direct route toward a Community Manager title, and the financial exposure built in this role, specifically the delinquency management, ledger review, and reporting experience, is exactly what separates candidates who move up quickly from those who stay in leasing-heavy roles longer than they need to.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k with match, paid time off including your birthday, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Snoqualmie, WA
job.description:
It's 7 AM and a resident just flagged a leaking water heater before heading to work. By 8, you've assessed it, ordered the part, and updated the work order. That's the rhythm here.

The Work

Echo Ridge is a Berkshire-owned and managed community in Snoqualmie, WA, which means you're working for the owner, not a third-party fee manager. That distinction matters: decisions move faster, standards are consistent, and the property you maintain today is the same one the company plans to hold long-term.

As a Maintenance Technician, you carry a broad scope. Curb appeal, unit turns, make-ready punch lists, work orders across plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry. You'll also help manage shop inventory, equipment upkeep, and key security. Safety compliance isn't a checkbox here; you're expected to actively enforce it. The role supports management directly, which means you'll occasionally be the first person a resident talks to when something goes wrong, and how you handle that interaction matters as much as the repair itself.

Berkshire uses the phrase "jack of all trades," and they mean it. A technician who gets tripped up by a tricky appliance diagnosis or a minor carpentry fix is going to struggle with the pace. The candidates who do well here have a working knowledge across all the core trades and enough confidence to triage a problem before escalating it.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Practical knowledge of appliances, plumbing, electrical systems, carpentry, and general building maintenance
  • Comfort with computers and property management software for work order tracking
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • A resident-first mindset, because this role is customer-facing whether you're fixing a garbage disposal or walking the grounds

One honest note about this market: Snoqualmie sits in the foothills east of Seattle, and Pacific Northwest winters are real. Exterior maintenance, drainage issues, and weather-related work orders pick up seasonally. If you've worked in wet climates before, that experience translates directly here.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and solid insurance coverage. They're a nationally recognized residential investment firm with a track record of promoting from within. A strong technician who builds diagnostic depth and some supervisory presence often moves toward a Lead Tech or Maintenance Supervisor role over time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II (Colorado Blvd Central)
job.description:
RedPeak has operated exclusively in Denver for over two decades. They own, operate, and develop their own communities, which means decisions move faster and accountability sits closer to the people doing the work. This Maintenance Technician II role sits at a 269-unit, single-building community on Colorado Boulevard, a corridor that sees real resident turnover and expects consistent upkeep at a level that matches the neighborhood.

The day-to-day here covers the full range: plumbing, electrical, drywall, appliance repair, HVAC, and painting. You'll run service requests from open to close, support the Service Supervisor on scheduling and vendor oversight, and hold your portion of the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. The building also expects you to manage security systems, including cameras, lock hardware, and key access for residents and vendors. That's a broader scope than a lot of tech II positions carry.

Preventative maintenance is part of the rhythm too. Daily grounds and interior inspections keep deficiencies from compounding, and accurate Yardi work order records keep the whole team aligned. At 269 units, volume matters. Busy periods can stack quickly, and the ability to triage efficiently without letting quality slip is what separates a strong tech from an average one.

RedPeak provides company-paid EPA and HVAC certifications, and they run an in-house advanced maintenance training center. For a tech who already holds some certifications and wants to build a more complete skill set, that's a concrete development path. Technicians who round out their HVAC, CPO, and electrical credentials often move into lead or Service Supervisor roles, where they're managing vendor relationships and influencing the maintenance budget alongside the property manager.

What the role requires

  • Intermediate working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems
  • 1 to 2 years in multifamily maintenance, construction, or a comparable trade environment
  • Comfortable with Yardi or a similar work order platform
  • Ability to support Fire Life Safety systems and property security infrastructure
  • Reliable transportation, valid driver's license
  • HVAC/EPA, CPO, or trade certifications are preferred but not required at hire

Pay runs $22 to $26 per hour with bonus potential tied to maintenance performance. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with on-call rotation included. Benefits include full medical, dental, and vision, a 30% rent discount, 401(k) with immediate vesting, 16 PTO days, 13 paid holidays, and a student debt repayment program.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician - Bay
job.description:
Maintenance work in multifamily housing builds a skill set that compounds faster than most trades roles. You're not working on a single system in a controlled environment. You're moving between plumbing calls, HVAC diagnostics, appliance repairs, and unit turns inside the same shift, reading each situation quickly and executing without a lot of hand-holding. At AIR Communities' Bay Apartments in San Diego, that's exactly the kind of work this Maintenance Technician role delivers every day.

The Skills This Role Puts to Work

Proficiency in at least two technical trades is the baseline here. Plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, and carpentry are all in play depending on the day. Beyond the hands-on technical work, this role asks you to use property management technology to triage and prioritize service requests, which means your efficiency becomes measurable. Technicians who can move through a punch list without sacrificing quality are genuinely valuable in this environment. AIR also uses well-stocked, organized on-site shops, so you're spending time fixing things rather than hunting for parts.

Turn work is a core part of the job. Completing make-ready units to a consistent standard, so incoming residents have a clean move-in experience, is a skill that carries weight throughout a property management career. It's detail work that connects directly to resident retention and leasing outcomes, and doing it well signals readiness for supervisory responsibilities down the line.

Responsibilities and Day-to-Day Shape

  • Complete resident-requested repairs across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and appliances with general direction from leadership
  • Execute apartment turns and make-ready work to meet move-in standards
  • Assist with vendor quality oversight and move-in/move-out inspections as needed
  • Provide technical guidance to less experienced technicians on the team
  • Respond to on-call emergency requests after hours (at least one week per month)

Schedule flexibility matters here. Evenings, weekends, and rotating on-call shifts are part of the job, particularly during high-turnover seasons. Reliable transportation for after-hours emergency response is a requirement, not an afterthought.

Where This Role Leads

AIR runs a maintenance development program called Ascend, which is built around individual career paths rather than a one-size track. For technicians with strong diagnostic skills and consistent customer service scores, the natural progression runs toward Lead Technician and Maintenance Supervisor roles. The monthly customer service bonus (up to $250) is a small but telling signal: this company treats resident satisfaction as a measurable output, not a soft value, and technicians who internalize that tend to get noticed. The 50% rent discount at any AIR community is a practical benefit worth calculating into total compensation, especially in the San Diego market.

Two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment is the floor. Candidates who bring HVAC certification, EPA 608, or documented appliance repair experience alongside a second trade will stand out. Tuition assistance and full reimbursement for job-related certifications mean the role can help you add credentials you don't yet have.

job.title: Assistant General Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This AGM role at Bozzuto's Edina, MN community puts you squarely in the operational middle: close enough to daily leasing and resident interactions to drive occupancy numbers directly, senior enough to run the property when the GM steps out. That's a meaningful combination. You're not just supporting the GM, you're the operational continuity plan.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, convert traffic into signed leases, and work the retention side of the equation with equal focus. Resident retention is where NOI gets quietly protected, and Bozzuto tracks that. You'll post rental receipts, collect rent, and manage delinquency with enough hands-on involvement that you'll know your T-3 and your MTM exposure without having to ask someone else to pull it. Community appearance, both interior and exterior, falls under your watch too. A punch list that actually gets resolved is a reflection of your standards.

Weekend availability is part of the job structure here, one to two weekends per month, which is when prospect traffic peaks. You'll get two weekdays off in exchange. That trade-off is standard in multifamily and worth knowing upfront.

When the GM is out, you lead. That means coaching team members, handling escalated resident issues, and keeping operations moving without waiting for direction. The role rewards people who already know what good looks like and act on it.

What You Bring

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years working in one of those industries, with real exposure to rent collection, budgets, and accounts receivable
  • Comfort with Yardi or comparable property management software
  • Social media fluency, specifically Facebook and Instagram, with the ability to create content that actually connects with a local audience
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, and a professional presentation that reflects the brand
  • A sales instinct that shows up in how you run tours and handle objections

Where This Role Fits

The Edina submarket sits in one of the Twin Cities' more competitive rental corridors. Residents here have options, which means retention work carries real weight. Strong AGMs in markets like this tend to develop a sharp read on concessions strategy and lease renewal timing, skills that translate directly into GM-level financial accountability.

For candidates who are serious about moving into a General Manager role, the AGM position at a company like Bozzuto is one of the cleaner paths in the industry. You're running delinquency, influencing NOI outcomes, leading a team part-time, and building the operational judgment that GM-level ownership requires. The compensation range for this role runs from $53,560 to $67,000, with bonus eligibility on top of that, plus full benefits including medical, dental, vision, 20 days of PTO, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Lease Administrator
job.description:
Lease administration sits at the intersection of legal documents and live data, and in a portfolio of any real scale, the gap between what a lease says and what the system reflects can cost real money. Lincoln Property Company's commercial platform manages well over 700 million square feet across institutional clients, which means their lease admin function isn't a back-office afterthought. It's a core data integrity role.

This position supports the lease administration department in their Washington, DC office, working under the Leasing Manager to keep lease records accurate, current, and audit-ready. The role is fully in-office, standard business hours, no exceptions noted.

The Day-to-Day

Most of your time goes toward abstracting and verifying lease documents: pulling critical dates, clauses, and financial terms from executed leases and amendments, then confirming that information is correctly entered into the database. You'll maintain a daily lease document tracker, run monthly production and tracking reports, and process client-specific reporting requirements. When property managers, accounting staff, area managers, or outside counsel need lease data, you're the one who retrieves it and makes sure what they get is accurate.

You'll also maintain the portfolio-wide property database, ensure lease files meet institutional quality standards, and participate in team meetings. Vendor and client communication is part of the job, written and verbal, so the ability to communicate clearly across organizational levels matters here.

What This Role Requires

  • At least two years in database administration or commercial real estate, with property management or real estate accounting experience preferred
  • Genuine comfort reading lease agreements, amendments, subordination agreements, and title commitments (not just skimming them)
  • Proficiency in Word and Excel, plus working knowledge of Yardi, MRI, or Visual Lease
  • Strong attention to detail and solid math comprehension
  • High school diploma required; associate's degree or higher preferred
  • Ability to pass a criminal background check

The salary range for this position is $85,000 to $95,000. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with traditional and Roth options, flexible time off, paid sick leave, company-paid life insurance and long-term disability, and an employee assistance program.

One honest note on what separates strong candidates here: it's not just data entry speed. The better lease administrators we've seen are the ones who catch a discrepancy between a lease abstract and the underlying document before it becomes a reporting error or, worse, a billing dispute with a tenant. If you're the kind of person who notices when something doesn't quite add up and follows it through, that instinct will serve you well in this role. Lease admin done well is unglamorous and genuinely important.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operated for over 70 years, and that tenure shows in how they approach staffing. They invest in people who show up, work hard, and take pride in what they do. This Groundskeeper opening at Bexley Grapevine in Grapevine, TX is a straightforward role with a clear value proposition: do good work, stay consistent, and there's genuine room to grow.

The work itself is physical and repetitive by design. Daily rounds include picking up litter and pet waste, maintaining outdoor spaces, operating equipment like backpack blowers and power washers, and supporting the maintenance team with light painting, housekeeping tasks, and trash-outs as needed. You'll be on your feet for most of the shift, lifting up to 50 pounds regularly, and working outdoors through Texas heat, humidity, and the occasional cold snap. Anyone who's spent time on a property knows the groundskeeper sets the first impression. Curb appeal directly affects traffic, and a well-kept community signals to prospective residents that the property is managed with care.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, which is a genuine advantage in this type of role. Starting pay is $16.50 per hour with quarterly bonuses, and there's a $1,000 stay-on bonus available after 90 days in good standing.

What separates strong candidates here isn't a specific credential. It's a combination of reliability, self-direction, and the willingness to handle tasks that aren't glamorous without cutting corners. The team notices who picks up trash without being asked, who spots a problem before it becomes a complaint, and who communicates proactively with the maintenance and leasing staff.

For someone with a growth mindset, this role builds real skills. You'll develop familiarity with property equipment, learn how a well-run apartment community operates at the ground level, and position yourself for a move into a maintenance technician role over time. Weinstein explicitly trains from within, and groundskeeper is a common entry point for people who eventually earn EPA certifications and take on full maintenance responsibilities.

What You'll Bring

  • Reliability and punctuality. This is non-negotiable in a role where daily tasks repeat regardless of who shows up.
  • Comfort working independently and completing a route without close supervision
  • Attention to detail across the property, including noticing issues before they escalate
  • Physical stamina for prolonged outdoor work, bending, stooping, and lifting
  • A collaborative attitude when the maintenance or leasing team needs an extra hand
  • Willingness to take on varied tasks, including ones that require getting dirty

Weinstein Properties operates over 60 communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. Their hands-on management approach means the people doing the work are seen and recognized. If you're dependable and coachable, this is a place where that gets noticed.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing runs on a different rhythm than conventional multifamily. Leases align with academic calendars, traffic spikes arrive in waves tied to housing fairs and move-in weekends, and the resident base turns over almost entirely each year. If you want to build leasing skills in that environment, this role at Redpoint West Lafayette gives you a concentrated education in all of it.

Skills This Role Requires From Day One

The Experience Team Member position draws heavily on interpersonal communication and adaptability. You'll conduct community and amenity tours, field objections from prospective residents (and their parents), and represent the property in conversations that happen both inside the office and around campus. That takes genuine customer-service instincts, not just a script. You'll also need to be organized enough to manage package logging, maintenance request follow-ups, and office operations without letting any of it slip. Scion calls this role a combination of marketing, relationship building, administration, and customer service, and that description is accurate. The workload shifts depending on the week, and availability during Turn periods and summer is a real requirement, not a footnote.

Skills This Role Builds Over Time

What you'll develop here goes beyond leasing basics. Working in student housing teaches you how to read traffic patterns against a leasing calendar, how to adjust messaging when occupancy targets aren't being met, and how to contribute to social media and local marketing in ways that actually connect with a collegiate audience. You'll learn to give useful feedback on sales barriers to your management team, which is a habit that sharpens your own understanding of why prospects don't convert. The after-hours on-call rotation, including lockout assistance, builds the kind of composure that carries into every future property management role you'll hold.

Student housing leasing also trains you to work through an annual lease-up cycle with a defined end date. That pressure is real, and learning to perform inside it makes conventional multifamily leasing feel more manageable by comparison.

What Makes This Specific Opportunity Worth Considering

Scion manages student communities across the country and has built operational systems around the particular demands of the collegiate market. Working at Redpoint West Lafayette means you're operating near a large Big Ten university with consistent demand, competitive traffic, and a resident base that expects amenities and experience to match their expectations. The role sits at the property full-time, so you'll develop real fluency with the community rather than splitting attention across a portfolio.

  • Strong candidates bring genuine curiosity about what drives leasing decisions, not just enthusiasm for talking to people
  • Reliability during high-demand periods (Turn, move-in, peak leasing season) is where this role is actually won or lost
  • Comfort with social media as a leasing tool is increasingly useful in this market segment

Applicants must be eligible to work in the United States. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

job.title: Desk Clerk (Shores Landing)
job.description:
A resident approaches the front desk frustrated about a noise complaint from the night before. You document it, radio the appropriate staff, and log it before the next visitor has even signed in. That rhythm, steady, detail-oriented, and people-facing, defines this role at Shores Landing.

What This Role Covers

MidPen Housing has been developing and managing affordable housing across Northern California since 1970. Their portfolio spans more than 142 properties and serves over 22,000 residents, including working families, seniors, and people with special needs. Shores Landing is one of those communities, and the Desk Clerk position is the operational heartbeat of its front office.

Under the Community Manager, you'll monitor all traffic in and out of the building, maintain the visitor and daily logs, answer phones, and direct residents, guests, and applicants appropriately. You'll complete work orders, write incident reports, post and distribute resident notices, and monitor the video camera system. Keeping the lobby and entrance area orderly is part of the job, and so is enforcing community policies and house rules with consistency and professionalism. Fair Housing compliance applies to every interaction.

The pay range is $17.69 to $19.90 per hour, based on experience, and the benefits package includes health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, FSA options, an employee education reimbursement program, an EAP, pet insurance, paid time off, company holidays, and wellness days.

Who Fits This Role

  • High school diploma or GED with at least one year of receptionist or administrative experience
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with Microsoft Word and Excel is a plus
  • Flexibility to handle varied tasks and shifting priorities throughout a shift
  • Genuine alignment with MidPen's mission around affordable housing and community stability

From a career standpoint, this role builds a specific kind of fluency that transfers well in property management: you learn how to document accurately under pressure, communicate across a wide range of residents and situations, and maintain professionalism in a setting where the stakes for residents are real. Desk Clerk experience at an affordable housing property is a credible stepping stone toward leasing coordinator, assistant manager, or compliance roles, particularly within mission-driven organizations where understanding resident services and community operations matters as much as technical skills. Candidates who thrive here tend to be people who stay calm when the front desk gets busy, take logging seriously rather than treating it as busywork, and understand that consistency in enforcement protects residents as much as it protects the property.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
It's 8:45 on a Tuesday and you're already on your second property walk, flagging a burnt-out light in the breezeway and texting the make-ready team about a unit that needs to be turned by Friday. That's the rhythm of this role.

Hillpointe is a fully integrated developer and builder working across the Sun Belt, focused on market-rate workforce housing. They control the full stack: land acquisition, construction, procurement, asset management. That means a Community Manager here isn't inheriting someone else's product. These are new builds, delivered in-house, and the expectation is that they stay that way. Units should look like move-in day every time a new resident walks in. Amenities should hold up. The asset should look and perform like Hillpointe built it yesterday, because they did.

What This Role Covers

You'll report to a Regional Manager and carry the full weight of day-to-day operations at the property level. Occupancy and rent levels are the headline metrics, but the job runs deeper than that. You're coordinating with the Facilities Maintenance Group, managing vendor relationships, keeping accounts payable moving, and doing regular property walks that are less about checking a box and more about protecting asset value. Revenue optimization is part of the job description, and Hillpointe expects you to be actively looking for opportunities, not waiting to be asked.

Lease administration, budget oversight, and technology-driven reporting all fall under your scope. Hillpointe uses Entrata, and proficiency there matters. You'll also need solid spreadsheet skills for financial records and fiscal reporting. This is a hands-on role: you're in the office, you're outside in all weather, and you need to be reachable outside standard hours except during approved time off. That's not a small ask, and it's worth knowing going in.

What Hillpointe Is Looking For

  • Prior property management experience, with a preference for candidates who've managed a full-cycle operation
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort with legal documents and resident-facing conversations
  • Proficiency in property management software, ideally Entrata
  • Mathematical competency for budgets, financial records, and percentage-based reporting
  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Valid driver's license (including for golf cart use on property)
  • Ability to access all parts of the community physically and to lift up to 20 pounds independently
  • Compliance with any state or local licensing requirements

One thing worth noting for candidates coming from third-party management backgrounds: Hillpointe's in-house model means you're working closer to ownership than most fee management setups allow. Decisions move faster. Accountability sits closer to the surface. For the right Community Manager, that's the appeal.

The Savannah market has seen consistent multifamily demand, and workforce housing in particular has held up well as Class A rents have stretched affordability limits. A Community Manager who understands how to maintain occupancy without over-relying on concessions will fit this environment well.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor (Nantucket Cove)
job.description:
Mechanical fluency is the foundation of this role. At Nantucket Cove in Champaign, IL, BAM Companies is looking for a Maintenance Supervisor who can read a problem before it becomes a work order, keep HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems running without drama, and hold a team accountable to standards that residents actually notice. That combination of hands-on technical skill and supervisory follow-through is what separates a functional maintenance department from a reactive one.

What This Role Demands Technically

You'll need EPA Type 2 or Universal Certification and at least two to three years of property maintenance experience to hit the ground running here. The day-to-day is split between systems-level work (HVAC diagnostics, plumbing repairs, electrical troubleshooting) and property-level upkeep: grounds, common areas, curb appeal. Preventative maintenance scheduling sits squarely in your lap, which means building inspection routines that catch issues before they generate resident complaints or emergency spend. You'll also manage supply purchases and keep maintenance costs in line with operational budgets, so comfort with cost tracking matters.

The Leadership Side of the Job

This position carries real supervisory weight. You're not just the most experienced tech on the crew. You're training your team, setting quality standards, running feedback conversations, and modeling the work ethic you expect from others. BAM describes its culture as family-oriented and team-driven, which in practice means the people around you are invested in each other's development. That's a reasonable environment for a supervisor who wants to build something rather than just manage it. You'll also need a valid driver's license and reliable vehicle.

Where Strong Candidates Stand Out

The supervisors who thrive in roles like this tend to think in systems, not just tasks. They look at a make-ready and immediately see the punch list sequence that gets a unit turned fastest. They run preventative maintenance programs that actually reduce emergency calls over a 90-day period, which shows up in both resident satisfaction and operational costs. If you can point to specific improvements in turn time, PM compliance, or team efficiency from a previous role, that's the kind of track record BAM is hiring toward.

Pay for this position runs $26 to $29 per hour depending on experience. BAM offers medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off that includes 14.5 holidays plus PTO after 90 days, rent discounts at BAM properties, and a stated commitment to internal growth and professional development.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work in residential property management is one of the most skill-diverse roles in the industry. Plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, and curb appeal all fall under the same umbrella, and a technician who can move fluidly between them builds a foundation that almost every senior maintenance and facilities role in this field requires. This opening at Berkshire Residential Investments, based at Berkshire Main Street, is worth taking seriously if you're thinking about where you want to be in five years.

What This Role Actually Demands

The core of the position is property preservation. You'll own the physical condition of the community, which means responding to work orders, supporting make-ready turns, and keeping common areas and curb appeal at a standard that reflects the property's reputation. You'll work alongside management to uphold community policies, enforce safety measures, and maintain shop organization, including equipment, inventory, and key security.

The job requires at least one year of hands-on residential maintenance experience and working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems. Computer proficiency matters here too. Work order platforms and digital communication are part of daily operations at most professionally managed communities, and Berkshire is no different.

Customer interaction is a real part of this role. Residents notice how maintenance staff treat them, and that interaction shapes renewal decisions as much as the physical product does. If you're someone who takes that seriously, it shows.

Skills That Compound Over Time

What makes this kind of role particularly valuable for career growth is the breadth of technical exposure. Technicians who develop fluency across multiple trade areas, rather than specializing narrowly early on, tend to move into lead technician and maintenance supervisor positions faster. From there, the path to facilities manager or regional maintenance director becomes much cleaner. Berkshire manages its own portfolio rather than operating as a third-party firm, which means internal advancement tends to follow consistent standards and relationships that actually carry weight.

The property itself gives you repetition. Every turn is a chance to sharpen your punch list efficiency. Every work order is a data point in understanding how a building ages and where to get ahead of capex before it becomes urgent. That pattern recognition is what separates a strong lead tech from someone who's just responsive.

What Berkshire Brings to the Table

Berkshire Residential operates as an owner-operator, meaning the decisions about maintenance standards, capital investment, and staffing reflect long-term ownership thinking rather than short-term fee management pressure. For a technician, that distinction matters. You're more likely to have the resources and organizational backing to do the job properly. The company offers three weeks of vacation, personal development planning, competitive insurance, and a 25% rent discount for employees.

If you're a technician with a year or more of residential experience who wants to work within a nationally recognized portfolio and build the kind of cross-trade skill set that opens real doors, this is a position worth a close look.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Student housing maintenance runs on a compressed cycle that most multifamily operators never experience. Turns happen in a matter of weeks, not months, and the volume of work orders during move-in season can overwhelm a team that isn't organized and technically sharp. Redstone Residential, one of the largest third-party student housing managers in the country with more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor for their Rexburg, Idaho community to keep that cycle running smoothly year-round.

What This Role Actually Requires

The core of this position is twofold: keeping the physical asset in good condition and making sure residents feel that maintenance is responsive and competent. Curb appeal and grounds upkeep are daily responsibilities, not seasonal ones. You'll handle hands-on repairs alongside your team, oversee apartment turnovers, and make sure each unit is in top condition before a new resident takes the keys. When emergencies come up, you're expected to respond according to established procedures and keep the Community Manager informed of anything that needs escalation.

On the technical side, Redstone requires at least two years of HVAC experience along with a solid background in plumbing and electrical. That's a meaningful bar. They're not looking for someone who can change filters and reset breakers. They want someone who can diagnose problems, execute repairs correctly the first time, and catch issues before they become costly. Property management experience is a plus, but the trade skills carry more weight here.

The physical demands are real: shifts run 8 to 10 hours, and the role requires lifting up to 75 pounds. Plan accordingly.

Skills This Role Builds

If you're a strong tradesperson who hasn't yet worked in a supervisory capacity, this role develops something that's harder to teach than HVAC: the ability to manage resident expectations while managing a punch list. Student housing residents have high expectations and aren't shy about voicing them. Learning to deliver genuine customer service under that pressure, while coordinating turns and keeping a property presentable, is the kind of operational experience that carries directly into Maintenance Director or Regional Maintenance roles.

What separates strong candidates here is the combination of technical depth and communication skills. Redstone is a third-party operator with systems and standards that require clear reporting up the chain. A supervisor who can complete quality work and communicate clearly about what still needs attention is far more valuable than one who can only do one or the other.

  • 2+ years of HVAC experience (required)
  • 2+ years of general maintenance experience including plumbing and electrical
  • Ability to lift 75 lbs. and sustain 8 to 10 hour active shifts
  • Strong customer service orientation and attention to detail
  • Property management experience is a plus

Compensation ranges from $18.00 to $20.00 per hour depending on experience. Benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, short-term disability, and access to continued education and professional development programs.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Maintenance management at an affordable housing portfolio demands a different skill set than luxury or market-rate work. The residents depend on fast, reliable service, and the operator depends on you to keep aging or mixed-vintage systems running efficiently without the budget latitude that Class A properties sometimes enjoy. At Fairstead, that challenge is real and so is the scale: over 30,000 apartments across 28 states, managed under a single integrated platform that combines development, construction, and property operations.

What This Role Actually Covers

The Service Manager position in Jacksonville puts you at the center of day-to-day building operations. You'll supervise a maintenance team, which means your organizational skills and ability to set priorities matter as much as your hands-on trade knowledge. You'll handle inspection and repair of electrical equipment and mechanical systems, lead special projects, and hold the line on safety compliance and sanitation standards across the property. Routine work you'll carry independently. More complex projects come with support.

Overtime is part of the picture when emergencies arise or special projects demand it. That's honest. Maintenance leadership at the property level means being reachable when systems fail outside business hours.

Skills You Bring vs. Skills You'll Sharpen

Fairstead requires at least three years of property maintenance experience and genuine proficiency in a specific trade, whether that's HVAC, electrical, plumbing, or another mechanical discipline. You also need working knowledge of building systems terminology, a real understanding of safety protocols, and comfort with Microsoft Office. Yardi and RealPage experience is a plus, not a requirement.

What this role builds is supervisory depth. Leading a team through a demanding make-ready cycle, managing a punch list across multiple units while keeping occupied buildings clean and safe, and implementing or improving maintenance procedures all develop the kind of operational judgment that carries well into regional maintenance director or facilities management positions over time.

  • Three or more years of hands-on property maintenance experience
  • Proficiency in at least one skilled trade with broad general maintenance ability
  • Strong safety knowledge and adherence to precautionary standards
  • Organizational and project management skills sufficient to lead a team
  • Ability to evaluate and improve existing maintenance policies and procedures
  • Microsoft Office proficiency; Yardi or RealPage familiarity is a bonus

The Broader Context

Fairstead positions itself as a tech-forward affordable housing operator, which matters for maintenance managers more than it used to. The company's emphasis on data-driven decision-making and digital tools means you'll likely encounter work order systems and reporting structures that go beyond a clipboard. Candidates who already think in terms of documentation, system performance trends, and process improvement tend to fit this environment better than those who rely purely on reactive repair habits.

The benefits package is substantive: employer-contributed medical coverage through Meritain Health, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with a 100% match on the first 3% and 50% on the next 2%, 15 PTO days, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays, along with a flexible spending account, disability coverage, and employee discount programs.

job.title: Community Assistant Manager - Peoria Grand
job.description:
Peoria Grand is a CloudTen Residential community in Peoria, AZ, and this Assistant Community Manager role sits right at the center of how the property runs day to day. CloudTen operates a genuinely varied multifamily portfolio across the West, including hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning projects. That breadth matters here because the company approaches operations with the same standards across all of it, and this role reflects that.

The work itself spans a lot of ground. You'll handle the financial side of community operations: collecting and posting rent, preparing bank deposits, reconciling accounts, processing invoices, and pulling together weekly and monthly reports. You'll also be the person who follows up on delinquent accounts, serves notices when needed, and coordinates with the Community Manager on eviction proceedings when it comes to that. On the leasing side, you'll respond to prospective resident inquiries, tour the property, maintain accurate lease documentation, and keep an eye on what competing communities are doing with pricing and marketing.

When the Community Manager is out, you're running the show. That's worth sitting with. This isn't a purely administrative support position. CloudTen is transparent that it's designed as a training ground for future Community Managers, so the expectation is that you're absorbing operations, financials, and team leadership in parallel with doing them.

The human dynamics piece is real here. You'll be the point of contact for resident concerns and service requests, coordinating with maintenance to make sure work orders get closed within 24 to 48 hours and communicating with residents when they don't. You'll also assist with move-in and move-out administration, including unit inspections and security deposit dispositions. That means being organized and consistent under pressure, especially around turns when the pace picks up and details matter most.

What separates strong candidates in this kind of role is the combination of financial literacy and genuine people skills. A lot of candidates bring one or the other. The ones who grow into Community Manager positions quickly tend to understand that a delinquency conversation and a renewal conversation require the same underlying skill: knowing how to be direct without being cold.

What you'll bring

  • At least two years of property management, leasing, or closely related experience
  • Solid working knowledge of Fair Housing laws and state landlord-tenant regulations
  • Comfort with property management software and Microsoft Office
  • Basic accounting knowledge and an eye for financial reporting accuracy
  • Strong communication skills and the organizational discipline to manage competing priorities
  • The kind of curiosity and self-sufficiency that doesn't wait to be told what to do next

Pay runs $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience. CloudTen offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, FSA options, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off. The company is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a drug-free workplace.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Property management companies that own and operate attainable housing carry a particular kind of operational weight. Residents aren't just customers; in many cases, stable housing is genuinely consequential to their lives. That context shapes what this role actually looks like day to day at Dream Live Prosper Communities, a subsidiary of DLP Capital operating out of Wind Gap, PA.

What the Job Actually Involves

This is an assistant community manager position at Dream Lehigh Valley, a residential property in Wind Gap. The work covers a broad slice of on-site operations: rent collection, lease administration, renewals, vendor coordination, and resident relations. You'll handle invoice processing, pull bids from vendors, and keep lease and contract files organized and current. When evictions become necessary, you'll attend the hearings. That part of the job isn't glamorous, but it's real, and the people who do it well understand that the process protects the financial health of the property for everyone who lives there.

You'll also work alongside project and construction teams as the company develops new assets, which means this role has some exposure to lease-up operations, not just stabilized management. AppFolio experience will make your first weeks considerably smoother, though it's listed as preferred rather than required. Insurance experience is a plus as well, particularly for certificate tracking and vendor compliance.

The schedule includes weekend availability. That's standard for residential community management, and worth knowing before you apply.

Who Fits This Role

  • Three or more years of property management or real estate experience, with apartment management specifically preferred
  • Comfort managing resident concerns directly, including difficult conversations about late rent or lease violations
  • Strong organizational habits, particularly around lease files, vendor records, and inspection documentation
  • Familiarity with AppFolio or willingness to get up to speed quickly
  • Ability to work across teams, from leasing staff to construction crews, depending on what the property needs that week

The candidates who tend to thrive in assistant manager roles at this level aren't just good with people. They're good with paperwork. Delinquency follow-up, renewal tracking, inspection punch lists, vendor invoices: these tasks don't resolve themselves, and the property manager depends on the assistant to keep them moving without constant oversight. If you're the kind of person who closes loops without being reminded, that skill matters here more than almost anything else on your resume.

Compensation includes a base plus monthly commission and bonus potential. Benefits include health, dental, vision, and life insurance, 401(k) matching, PTO, volunteer time, and educational incentives.

job.title: Housekeeper
job.description:
Housekeeping at a luxury apartment community covers more ground than most people expect. You're not just cleaning units. You're maintaining the standard that residents paid a premium to live within, and your work directly shapes how the property presents to prospects walking through on a tour.

What the Work Actually Involves

At Griffis Residential's Seattle community, the housekeeper role spans both common areas and apartment interiors. Common areas include the clubhouse, fitness center, business center, and leasing office. These spaces get daily attention, and the standard you hold them to reflects the property's overall brand. On the apartment side, you'll follow make-ready cleaning procedures using provided checklists to get units ready for incoming residents. If a ready unit has been sitting for more than a week, you'll return to refresh it so it stays move-in ready. You'll also communicate any maintenance issues you notice to the Service Manager, which makes you an extra set of eyes for the broader facilities team.

Daily tasks come from the Community and Service Managers, so you'll need to work comfortably within a structured schedule while also responding to what you find as you move through the property. Following product safety labels and cleaning protocols correctly matters here, both for resident safety and for protecting surfaces in a higher-finish environment.

Skills This Role Requires and Skills It Builds

You need to bring attention to detail, physical stamina, and at least a year of cleaning experience in multifamily housing, hospitality, or a comparable setting. Strong communication skills matter too, since you'll be interacting with residents and associates regularly. Bilingual ability in Spanish is a plus given Seattle's diverse resident base.

What this role builds is a working knowledge of the make-ready process and how turns function within a multifamily operation. That's a transferable skill. Housekeepers who understand make-ready standards, punch list thinking, and unit condition expectations are much better positioned to move into maintenance coordinator or make-ready technician roles over time. You're learning how a luxury property operates from the inside out.

Compensation and Benefits

The hourly range is $23 to $24.50. Full-time associates receive a 50% rental discount, a quarterly bonus program tied to occupancy and online reputation, 401(k) with up to 4% company match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, at least three weeks of PTO accruing from day one, 11 paid holidays, and tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 annually. The benefit package is notably more comprehensive than what most hospitality or hotel housekeeping roles offer at comparable pay.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • One year of experience in multifamily, hospitality, or similar preferred
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to follow cleaning checklists and safety protocols
  • Clear communication skills; bilingual in Spanish is a plus
  • Ability to work within a team structure directed by Community and Service Managers

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Maintenance Supervisor roles at student housing and multifamily companies tend to blend trade work with crew oversight more than most candidates expect. At PeakMade, the split is explicit: roughly 60 to 70 percent of your time is hands-on repairs, and the rest goes toward directing your team, managing vendors, and keeping the operation running on budget.

What the Job Actually Looks Like

This is a working supervisor position at an apartment community in Los Angeles. You're not managing from an office. You're on the property daily, inspecting grounds, completing or assigning service requests, and making sure vacant units are turned and ready for marketing. You'll run the turn process end to end: scheduling workers, supervising contractors, and pushing units through make-ready within budget. You'll also maintain the preventative maintenance program, manage supply inventory, and keep the maintenance shop organized and OSHA-compliant. When capital improvements come up, you'll work directly with the National Facilities Director to gather bids.

Resident interaction is part of the role. Move-ins, move-outs, unresolved concerns. You're expected to handle those professionally and without delay.

What PeakMade Needs From You

  • At least 2 years of maintenance supervisory experience, preferably in multifamily
  • EPA Type II certification required; CPO preferred
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license, current auto insurance, and a reliable personal vehicle
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property
  • Basic hand tools (your own)
  • Ability to diagnose and repair: HVAC, intermediate plumbing, intermediate electrical, major appliances, sheetrock, general carpentry, pool systems, roofing, painting, irrigation, and landscaping
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at height on ladders, and perform tasks in extreme temperatures

Additional licenses or certifications may be required depending on local and state code. The posting notes other certifications as applicable by law, so candidates should be prepared for that review.

Compensation and Growth

The pay range is $80,000 to $90,000 annually, with final offers based on experience and internal equity. PeakMade includes monthly renewal bonuses, a 401(k) match, paid parental leave, 15 days PTO plus two wellbeing days, and access to a facilities leadership program with technical certifications available in HVAC and CPO.

That leadership program matters. Strong maintenance supervisors at companies like PeakMade often move into regional facilities roles or facilities director positions as they build out their portfolio experience and vendor management track record. The exposure to capex bidding here gives you a skill set that carries real weight at that next level.

PeakMade specializes in off-campus student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities. The Los Angeles market means a dense regulatory environment, so comfort with local permitting, pool regulations, and sign ordinances is genuinely useful from day one.

job.title: Part Time Clubhouse Monitor Manufactured Housing Community
job.description:
Skandia Mobile Country Club sits in Huntington Beach, a 167-home manufactured housing community managed by Investment Property Group, a firm that owns and operates over 150 properties across 13 states. This part-time Clubhouse Monitor role is a straightforward position with a specific scope: opening and closing the community's shared amenities on a consistent weekly schedule, and keeping those spaces safe and presentable for residents.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday evenings for closing duties, plus Saturday and Sunday mornings and evenings for both opening and closing. That adds up to roughly 10 hours per week, including holidays. At $17.50 per hour, it suits someone who wants a reliable part-time commitment without variable or unpredictable hours.

The work itself centers on securing the clubhouse, laundry room, and pool area each night, then reopening those same spaces on weekend mornings. Beyond locking and unlocking, you'll test and log pool water chemistry using established procedures, restock bathroom and kitchen supplies, clear debris or spills, and remove standing water from the pool deck to reduce slip hazards. After a resident rents the clubhouse for a private event, you'll inspect the space to confirm it's been left in proper condition. Anything that rises to the level of a genuine concern gets reported to the park manager promptly.

This role requires reliability above almost everything else. The residents of a manufactured housing community depend on consistent access to shared amenities, and a monitor who shows up late or skips a shift creates real problems for people planning their evenings or weekends around those spaces. Independent judgment matters too: you'll often be working alone, so you need to recognize what falls within your scope to handle and what requires escalation.

From a skill-building standpoint, this position introduces the operational rhythms of community management at a small scale. You'll develop familiarity with amenity maintenance standards, basic pool compliance documentation, and the kind of property walk discipline that carries into groundskeeper, maintenance, and eventually leasing or assistant manager roles. For someone newer to property management who wants to get a foot in the door with an established operator like IPG, consistent performance here is a visible track record.

What You'll Need

  • Availability for approximately 10 hours per week, including weekday evenings and both weekend days
  • Reliable transportation to and from the property
  • Ability to pass a background check
  • Comfort following safety protocols and documenting results accurately
  • Dependability and punctuality, consistently, not occasionally

job.title: Assistant General Manager
job.description:
Bozzuto operates some of the most recognized multifamily communities in the country, and the Assistant General Manager role at their Chicago location sits at the center of daily operations. This is a property management position with real financial accountability. You're not an observer here. You're collecting rent, managing delinquency, tracking occupancy, and running tours that close leases, all while covering leadership responsibilities whenever the GM steps away.

The financial side of the role is genuine. You'll contribute directly to meeting occupancy targets and revenue objectives by handling rent posting, monitoring accounts receivable, and keeping delinquency in check. On a given morning, you might be reviewing outstanding balances before walking a prospective resident through the community on a personalized tour. That afternoon could involve coaching a leasing consultant on follow-up technique. The range is real, and candidates who thrive here tend to be energized by it rather than stretched thin by it.

Resident retention is as important as new traffic in this role. Bozzuto places serious emphasis on the resident experience, and the AGM is expected to own that culture when the GM isn't present. That means handling resident issues with care, staying visible, and building the kind of community loyalty that shows up in renewal rates. Strong candidates for this role tend to have a natural instinct for connecting with people, whether that's a prospective resident on a Saturday tour or a team member who needs a quick coaching conversation before a busy open house.

Weekend availability is part of the job. One to two weekends per month, with weekday trade-off days. That's a standard expectation at high-performing lease-up and stabilized communities alike, and Bozzuto is upfront about it.

What Bozzuto is Looking For

  • Four-year degree or equivalent experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years working in one of those industries
  • Hands-on exposure to rent collection, budgets, and accounts receivable
  • Comfort with Yardi or comparable property management software
  • Active presence on social platforms with the ability to create content that reflects the community's brand
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • A real estate license, or the ability to obtain one within 90 days of hire where required

The salary range for this position is $66,500 to $75,000, with additional bonus opportunities on top of base. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

For candidates thinking about trajectory: the AGM role at a company like Bozzuto is one of the cleaner paths to a General Manager or Property Manager seat. You're already running operations in the GM's absence, managing financials, and developing team members. The skills built here, specifically delinquency management, NOI awareness, and leasing conversion, translate directly into senior site leadership and eventually regional or portfolio-level roles.

job.title: Account Settlement Specialist - Atlanta, GA
job.description:
Post move-out collections is one of the more technically demanding back-office functions in multifamily operations. It sits at the intersection of lease interpretation, fair debt compliance, payment reconciliation, and resident communication, and when it's done well, it directly improves NOI by converting delinquent balances into recovered cash rather than write-offs. Cortland, one of the largest vertically integrated multifamily owners and operators in the country, is hiring an Account Settlement Specialist in Atlanta to own this function across an assigned portfolio of closed accounts.

What This Role Actually Involves

Your daily work centers on former resident accounts after move-out. You'll contact ex-residents to resolve outstanding balances, work through disputes by reviewing lease terms and documentation, and negotiate settlements or payment plans within established guidelines. Payment processing is a real part of the job: you'll post payments in OneSite, process credit card and ACH transactions, and reconcile daily collections activity against cash reports. On the compliance side, you'll maintain Final Account Statements, complete surety bond claims through programs like Jetty when applicable, and document every resident and third-party communication thoroughly. When accounts hit the threshold for external placement, you'll coordinate the transition to third-party collection agencies and support placement readiness. Complex disputes or legal concerns get escalated through a defined workflow, so knowing when to escalate is as important as knowing how to resolve.

Collaboration matters here. You'll work regularly with onsite teams, Revenue Recovery, and Accounting to untangle account discrepancies. The role is centralized, but the accounts you manage touch properties across a large portfolio, so clear communication with site staff is part of making resolutions stick.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

Coming in, Cortland expects you to bring at least two years of experience in collections, property management, or a closely related customer service field. You need strong negotiation instincts, comfort with payment processing, solid written and verbal communication, and the organizational discipline to manage a high volume of accounts without letting documentation slip. OneSite experience is a plus. PCI compliance and Fair Debt Collection practices are not things you'll learn from scratch here; familiarity with both is expected.

What the role builds is more nuanced. Working inside a vertically integrated operation at Cortland's scale gives you exposure to how post move-out recovery connects to property-level financial reporting and portfolio-wide write-off trends. You'll develop sharper lease interpretation skills, a deeper understanding of guarantor and surety bond programs, and the kind of compliance fluency that transfers directly to roles in property accounting, revenue management, or collections leadership. Specialists who perform well here often move into senior recovery roles or transition into broader accounting and compliance functions within large multifamily organizations.

  • High school diploma required; some college preferred
  • 2+ years in collections, property management, or related customer service
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; OneSite or collections software experience preferred
  • Strong negotiation, documentation, and analytical skills
  • Familiarity with Fair Debt Collection practices and PCI compliance protocols
  • Ability to manage independent workload while coordinating across internal teams

job.title: Assistant Manager - Gainesville, GA
job.description:
The Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

An Assistant Manager role at a well-run apartment community is one of the best skill-building positions in residential property management. You're doing financial reconciliation, delinquency tracking, rent collection, and deposit accounting on one side of the desk. On the other, you're handling resident relations, inspecting make-ready units before move-in, and stepping into leasing when traffic demands it. That combination is exactly what trains people to run a property independently.

At Olympus Property's Gainesville community, the role asks for both precision and flexibility in the same week. You'll safeguard and accurately post incoming rent receipts, manage move-out account statements, and keep resident files airtight. You'll also monitor local submarket conditions, track nearby construction, and flag anything that could affect occupancy or income. That's a skill set that compounds: operators who understand both ledger accuracy and market positioning tend to move into Property Manager roles faster than those who specialize in only one.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

Most of your core hours run Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with some flexibility expected for the first weekend of each month and occasional resident events after hours. Practically speaking, mornings often involve posting deposits and clearing the prior day's transactions before the bank close deadline. Mid-day shifts toward resident touchpoints, whether that's addressing a complaint, walking a make-ready unit with a punch list in hand, or covering the leasing floor when a consultant is tied up. Late afternoon can pull you back to the books or into a conversation with the Property Manager about delinquency trends.

When the Property Manager is out, you run the operation. That exposure to full-site accountability, even temporarily, is something you can't replicate in a pure leasing role.

What Olympus Brings to This Position

Olympus Property has earned recognition as a top employer through the National Apartment Association three consecutive years running (2023, 2024, 2025). That's not accidental in a sector where turnover is notoriously high. The benefits package here is substantive, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and an apartment rental allowance. There's also a formal career pathing program, which matters if your goal is to move from Assistant Manager to Property Manager and eventually into a regional or portfolio role.

Candidates who tend to succeed here bring onsite experience, either as an Assistant Manager or as a cross-trained leasing consultant, and familiarity with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite. Comfort with both detail-level financial work and face-to-face resident interaction is the combination Olympus looks for. If you've been strong on leasing but want to build the operational and financial side of your resume, this is a natural next step. If you're already handling books but want a company with defined growth tracks, Olympus is worth a close look.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
job.description:
Apartment maintenance is where NOI gets protected or eroded, one work order at a time. A slow turn, a recurring HVAC call, a pool that's out of compliance , each one chips away at occupancy, resident satisfaction scores, and ultimately the property's bottom line. Weinstein Properties understands this, which is why they staff their communities with technicians who can actually solve problems, not just log tickets.

The open position is at 3Sixty Flats in Grand Prairie, TX. Weinstein owns and manages their portfolio in-house, so there's no third-party management layer adding noise to communication or slowing down approvals. The people making decisions about the property are the same people supporting the maintenance team day to day.

The Role in Practice

This is a full-cycle maintenance position. Your week will move between occupied unit work orders, make-ready turns on vacants, HVAC diagnosis and repair, plumbing, electrical, appliance troubleshooting, and general upkeep of grounds, amenities, and pool areas. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with participation in a rotating emergency on-call schedule. On-call pays a flat $150 per week regardless of call volume, plus an additional $150 for holiday coverage. That kind of predictable structure matters when you're planning your life around an on-call rotation.

Base pay starts at $24 per hour and goes up depending on experience. There's also a quarterly bonus of up to $980 tied to property and team performance, a sign-on bonus (details discussed at interview), and a rent discount for those who want to live on-site. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, PTO, paid holidays, and birthday time off.

What Weinstein Is Looking For

  • Minimum 3 years of apartment or residential maintenance experience
  • EPA Certification, Type II or Universal (this is a firm requirement, not a preference)
  • Hands-on HVAC troubleshooting, repair, and installation experience
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose and repair appliances, plumbing, and electrical systems independently
  • Comfort with work order platforms and basic computer/mobile use
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and work outdoors year-round in Texas heat
  • Reliable transportation; background check required

The technicians who stand out in a role like this are the ones who can close work orders cleanly the first time. Callbacks on incomplete repairs slow down turns, frustrate residents, and create delinquency risk when renewals stall. If your instinct is to diagnose thoroughly before you fix, you'll fit the culture here better than someone who patches and moves on.

Weinstein has a track record of promoting from within. For a technician with strong HVAC chops and leadership interest, a lead tech or maintenance supervisor path is a realistic next step inside a company that manages its own assets long-term.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - 3300 Tamarac
job.description:
Leasing consultant roles at stabilized properties tend to get undersold. The job looks simple from the outside: show units, sign leases, answer phones. In practice, you're the first impression, the closer, the complaint handler, and the occupancy driver, often all before noon. MG Properties is filling that role at 3300 Tamarac Apartments in Denver, and they've been at this long enough (30-plus years across the Western U.S.) to know what good leasing actually looks like.

What the Day Actually Looks Like
