Your mornings often start with traffic from the previous day: follow-up calls, applications to qualify, files to update. When prospects walk in, you're greeting them, qualifying them, and moving them through the process with enough professionalism that they want to sign. When a new resident moves in, you're coordinating with maintenance to make sure the unit is ready and the experience lands well. Lease files need to stay current and accurate. Rent conversations happen, including the ones where someone's running late on payment. That's the job, and it's a full one.

MG Properties promotes from within, which means a leasing role here has a real path. Strong performers in leasing tend to move into assistant manager positions, where the same skills apply to delinquency management, reporting, and broader operations. The foundation you build here transfers directly.

What They're Looking For

  • At least one year of property management experience, preferred but not a hard wall
  • Genuine sales ability paired with customer service instincts, these need to coexist
  • Attention to detail on files, data entry, and lease execution
  • Professional communication with residents, including when the conversation is difficult
  • Comfort working in a team environment and interest in growing with the company

The candidates who stand out in leasing roles aren't just personable. They follow through. A prospect who toured three days ago and hasn't heard back is a lost lease. Organized, consistent follow-up separates the consultants who move occupancy from the ones who just answer questions.

Compensation runs $22 to $23 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonuses and company profit sharing. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, paid holidays, and a rental discount. This position is anticipated to be filled in September 2026.

job.title: Asset Manager
job.description:
Asset management at the single-family rental scale Roofstock operates is a different discipline than what most multifamily AM roles train you for. You're not managing one asset or a small portfolio in a single submarket. You're monitoring performance trends across regional markets, advising third-party property managers on leasing strategy, and producing financial deliverables for institutional partners, all simultaneously.

What This Role Actually Covers

The Asset Management team at Roofstock functions as the decision-making layer between raw operating data and investor outcomes. You'll conduct high-volume rent underwriting on both new acquisitions and existing portfolio properties, lead regional market meetings focused on occupancy, renewal performance, and turn velocity, and complete hold/sell analysis on underperforming assets. Budget development and variance tracking are steady parts of the workload, as are lender tape deliverables and quarterly performance reports for institutional partners.

You'll also work directly with internal data teams to build reporting visibility into operational performance, contribute to the asset management playbook and cross-functional SOPs, and advise the buying team on market conditions and buy box strategy. Occasional market visits are required, roughly 10% travel.

Skills This Role Requires

  • 3 to 5 years of asset management experience in multifamily or SFR
  • Strong Excel modeling skills, specifically working with large datasets
  • Experience building ad hoc KPI reports that produce actionable insights
  • Comfort interfacing with institutional investors and managing those relationships professionally
  • Ability to run multiple workstreams independently across cross-functional teams
  • Broad market knowledge across major SFR geographies, including rent trends, values, and demand drivers
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience

Skills This Role Builds

What makes this position genuinely developmental is the scale and variety of investor types you'll manage. Institutional partners have different reporting expectations, risk tolerances, and NOI targets than retail investors, and learning to produce outcomes for both sharpens your ability to frame asset performance in ways that actually move decisions. Working inside a platform that spans acquisition, property management, tenant screening, and financial software also gives you a rare view of how each operational layer connects to portfolio-level returns. Asset managers who develop that systems-level fluency tend to move into VP-level AM roles or transition into acquisitions leadership with a credibility that pure financial analysts don't carry.

This is a remote position within the greater Dallas-Fort Worth area. If your background sits at the intersection of SFR operations and institutional reporting, and you're comfortable with the ambiguity that comes with a high-growth platform still building its processes, this role offers real scope.

job.title: Maintenance Technician I (Biltmore)
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. and you've already got three service requests from overnight, a unit turning Friday, and a resident flagging a leaky faucet on your way through the courtyard. That's a normal Tuesday at the Biltmore in Cupertino.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Prometheus calls residents "Neighbors," which sets the tone for how they approach maintenance. This isn't a fix-it-and-move-on shop. The Maintenance Technician I role at the Biltmore covers the full scope of day-to-day upkeep: service requests, make-readies, and the troubleshooting that keeps a community running at a level residents notice. You'll handle appliance repairs and installs, basic electrical, plumbing, carpentry, and paint. Turns are a real part of this job, and Prometheus expects them done completely and on time. On-call rotation is part of the deal, and standby pay is included in the compensation package for those hours.

Two years of hands-on apartment maintenance experience is the baseline requirement. A high school diploma or GED, solid communication skills in English, and basic computer proficiency round out what they're looking for. The physical side is real: you're on your feet, outdoors much of the time, climbing, lifting up to 50 lbs., and moving through units at pace. If you've done this work before, none of that is a surprise.

Compensation and Benefits

The hourly range sits at $27.75 to $28.75, with a discretionary semi-annual bonus and on-call premium pay on top of that. Prometheus also offers referral bonuses, renovation bonuses, and lease-up bonuses where applicable. The benefits package is genuinely strong for this industry:

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage at 100% company-paid (including eligible dependents), with buy-up options
  • Life insurance, AD&D, and long-term disability
  • 401(k) with employer matching
  • Behavioral health support available around the clock
  • Tax-free FSA options
  • 10 vacation days to start, increasing with tenure, plus a 40-hour anniversary vacation grant at milestones
  • 9 sick days and 12 paid holidays, including your birthday
  • Paid volunteer time
  • Tenure-based housing discounts
  • Educational assistance and tuition reimbursement

One thing worth noting for anyone thinking about longevity: Technician I roles at well-run companies like Prometheus tend to have a real ladder. Strong performers move into Technician II and eventually lead tech or maintenance supervisor positions, sometimes with portfolio-level responsibility. The educational assistance benefit signals they're willing to invest in that progression. In a market like Cupertino, where qualified maintenance staff are genuinely hard to find, that kind of internal mobility matters.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning at Enclave at 38 Twenty Two, and before the leasing office opens at nine, you're already pulling a delinquency report, flagging accounts that need follow-up calls before the week slips away. By noon, you've walked two prospects through available floor plans, posted a rent payment, and helped a resident work through a renewal question. The pace is real, and so is the variety.

What the Role Actually Covers

Hawthorne Residential Partners operates this Greensboro community as part of a portfolio rooted in the Southeast, and the Assistant Community Manager sits at the center of daily operations. You'll support leasing from lead response through signed lease, conduct tours, and make sure applications and renewals are processed accurately and on time. Occupancy goals matter here, and so does retention. Keeping residents happy enough to renew is just as important as bringing in new traffic.

On the financial side, you'll handle rent collection, payment posting, and ledger reviews. Delinquency management is a real part of the job: weekly follow-up calls, coordination with the Community Manager on escalated accounts, and staying on top of eviction procedures when it comes to that. You'll also assist with financial reporting for regional leadership, so comfort reading a basic financial summary is genuinely useful.

When the Community Manager is out, you step into the lead role. That means keeping the team focused, handling resident concerns, and maintaining the operational rhythm without someone above you in the building. It's a meaningful responsibility that separates this position from a pure leasing role.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of prior assistant community manager experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a plus

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to keep the week at 40 hours. Some evening and weekend availability may come up for resident events.

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance. Hawthorne also runs a formal Career Path Program aimed at moving Assistant Community Managers into Community Manager roles.

The candidates who tend to do well here combine genuine comfort with numbers and a real ability to de-escalate. Greensboro's rental market has grown steadily with university-driven demand and an influx of mid-size employers, which means resident expectations are rising alongside competition. Knowing how to hold occupancy while managing delinquency in a market with real options for renters is a skill this role will sharpen quickly.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Hillpointe builds and manages workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and this Community Manager role sits at the center of that operation in Savannah. You'd be running a market-rate property from the ground up on the operational side: occupancy, financials, resident experience, and the daily coordination between maintenance and management. Because Hillpointe handles development, construction, and asset management in-house, community managers here tend to work closely with the broader organization rather than operating in isolation from ownership.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

A significant part of this role is keeping the asset performing the way ownership expects. That means regular property walks to catch issues before they become deferred maintenance problems, making sure units are genuinely make-ready standard before a new resident takes possession, and ensuring amenities stay in condition that reflects the property's positioning. You'll also manage accounts payable, submit invoices correctly, and support your Regional Manager in hitting and holding budgeted occupancy and rent levels.

On the leasing and revenue side, you're expected to stay active, not reactive. Identifying additional revenue opportunities, keeping concessions in check, and maintaining traffic conversion are all part of the job. Entrata experience is a real plus here since that's the platform Hillpointe works with, and comfort with spreadsheets and financial reporting is genuinely necessary rather than optional.

  • Oversee daily property operations and financial performance against budget
  • Coordinate with the Facilities Maintenance Group to address property-level needs
  • Manage vendor relationships and ensure proper invoice processing
  • Administer leases and maintain compliance with applicable regulations
  • Drive occupancy through leasing support, marketing strategy, and resident retention
  • Conduct routine property inspections and maintain asset standards

Who Fits This Role Well

Savannah's rental market has grown meaningfully over the past several years, with workforce housing demand driven by a mix of logistics, healthcare, and hospitality employment. Residents at properties like this often have specific expectations around value and responsiveness, and the managers who do well here are the ones who take both seriously. Strong candidates communicate clearly with residents and vendors alike, stay organized across multiple operational tracks at once, and bring genuine comfort with property management software and financial reporting. Prior community management experience gives you a real edge, but the combination of financial literacy, people skills, and operational follow-through matters more than any single credential.

Flexibility and Availability

This role requires a flexible schedule and consistent availability by phone and email outside of approved time off. Some local travel is expected for bank deposits, training, and business needs. Physical access to all areas of the community, including exterior spaces in varying weather, is part of the job. A valid driver's license is required.

For someone who wants to grow in multifamily operations, a vertically integrated developer like Hillpointe offers real exposure to how properties perform from the ownership side, which tends to accelerate the learning curve for managers who pay attention.

job.title: Centralized Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Centralized leasing roles differ from on-site positions in one key way: you're handling traffic and applications across multiple properties at once, not just one community. At Ackermann Group, a Midwest developer and manager with roots going back to 1938, this position sits at corporate headquarters in Cincinnati and covers leasing activity across their residential portfolio.

What the Work Looks Like

Your day runs from first contact to lease signed. Prospects reach you by phone or through digital channels, and your job is to convert those inquiries into tours and move-ins. You'll manage guest cards, prepare leases, track follow-ups, and document interactions in Yardi Voyager and Rent Cafe. The CRM is your paper trail, and keeping it accurate matters as much as your sales close rate.

Because you're covering multiple properties, product knowledge is a real requirement. You need to know unit counts, building specs, utility setups, and local market conditions well enough to speak to each community confidently and adjust your pitch accordingly. Fair housing compliance runs through every part of this job, from how you answer inquiries to how you document decisions.

You'll also field basic resident service needs, route work order requests, and support renewal conversations. It's a full-cycle leasing role with administrative depth. Occasional light physical tasks come with the territory.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of leasing experience with measurable results
  • Comfort working across Yardi Voyager, Rent Cafe, and CRM platforms
  • Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to build rapport quickly
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Must live in the Greater Cincinnati area
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, plus Saturdays as needed

The Bigger Picture

Centralized leasing is increasingly common as operators look to reduce per-property overhead while keeping leasing velocity up. The skill set you build here, managing volume across a portfolio, tracking leads in a CRM, and staying current on multiple micro-markets, transfers well to leasing manager and portfolio management roles. Ackermann offers commission on new leases and renewals, a quarterly bonus structure, health benefits, 401k with company match, and an employee rent discount at any community in their portfolio.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Enclave on Golden Triangle in Fort Worth needs a maintenance technician, and Cottonwood Residential is open to someone still building their skill set. This is a genuine entry point into apartment maintenance, which means you won't be expected to walk in knowing everything. You will be expected to show up, work hard, and learn fast.

The day-to-day work covers the full range of what keeps a residential community running: plumbing repairs, basic electrical, carpentry, and grounds upkeep. Turns and make-readies are part of the rhythm. You'll move through units on punch lists, respond to resident work orders, and handle the kind of repairs that pile up on a busy property. Some of it is satisfying problem-solving. Some of it is crawling into tight spaces or hauling materials in Texas summer heat. Both are real.

On-call is part of this role. After-hours emergencies happen, and you'll rotate into that coverage with support from the Service Manager. That support matters, especially early on, but you should go in knowing that the phone can ring at inconvenient times. That's the nature of residential maintenance, and it's worth being honest with yourself about before you apply.

Physically, the job asks a lot. You'll be on your feet most of the day, climbing ladders, stooping, kneeling, and lifting items up to 50 pounds. A valid driver's license is required. If you hold EPA Type II or Universal certification, or have HVAC troubleshooting experience, that carries real weight here. CPO certification is a plus as well, though none of these are hard requirements for an entry-level candidate.

What Cottonwood is looking for

  • Ability to communicate clearly in English, written and spoken, for work orders and safety procedures
  • Comfort working evenings, weekends, and on-call rotations
  • Physical ability to handle the demands described above
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA Type II or Universal, HVAC experience, or CPO certification (preferred, not required)

Benefits kick in quickly, within the first month, and include full medical, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage. The 401k and HSA both come with company matching. In your first year you'd be eligible for three weeks of paid time off plus 10.5 paid holidays, which is a solid package for a technician role at this level.

For someone early in their maintenance career, this kind of role builds a foundation that transfers anywhere in the industry. Technicians who develop strong HVAC and plumbing skills at a community like this often move into lead tech or Service Manager roles within a few years. The learning curve is real, but so is the ceiling.

job.title: Temporary Maintenance Technicians Needed (Pittsburgh or Greensburg)
job.description:
Birgo manages residential properties across the Pittsburgh area, and right now they need a few extra sets of skilled hands to keep things running. These are temporary maintenance technician roles covering Greensburg, North Versailles, and the South Hills, with a realistic duration of one to three months. If things go well, there's room for the work to extend or convert to a full-time position.

The day-to-day work spans the full range of residential maintenance: make-readies, grounds upkeep, common area care, and general repairs covering drywall, painting, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and HVAC. You'll also contribute to preventative maintenance routines. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, with shifts either 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. or 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., plus participation in an on-call rotation. Pay runs $19 to $24 per hour, paid weekly, and the role is overtime eligible. Mileage reimbursement, paid time off, and PPE are included.

Because you'll be moving between properties, a valid driver's license and your own reliable transportation are required. You'll also need to comfortably lift and carry 50 pounds, work in confined spaces, and handle ladders and staircases safely.

Temp roles like this one reward technicians who come in ready to contribute without a long ramp-up period. The people who tend to stand out are the ones who carry a genuinely broad skill set, communicate clearly when something unexpected comes up on a unit, and treat residents with the same care they'd give a full-time property. Birgo's culture puts a lot of weight on how people show up with each other and with residents, so attitude matters as much as technical range here.

What they're looking for

  • Authorization to work in the United States
  • Valid driver's license and personal, reliable transportation
  • Ability to lift 50 pounds unassisted and work safely with power tools
  • Comfort in confined spaces and on ladders
  • Well-rounded building maintenance skills across trades
  • Strong communication and resident-facing professionalism

If you've done residential maintenance work before and you're between positions or looking to pick up temporary work while you weigh your next move, this is a practical opportunity to stay active, earn competitive hourly pay, and get a real look at how Birgo operates before deciding if a longer-term fit makes sense.

job.title: Experienced Field Maintenance Technician- West Valley (3+ Years Required)
job.description:
Third-party property services at scale creates a different kind of maintenance career than traditional on-site work. Instead of owning one building, you own a portfolio of work orders across multiple properties, which means your diagnostic speed, organizational habits, and trade depth get tested daily in ways a single-site role rarely demands.

Lessen operates a tech-enabled platform that processes millions of work orders each year across residential and commercial real estate. Their field technicians in the West Valley are the ground-level execution layer for that model, and they're looking for someone in the Glendale area with at least three years of verifiable, hands-on maintenance experience who can carry that weight independently.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This role puts you in a company fleet vehicle with a fuel card, moving through a defined territory and closing out work orders with an emphasis on quality over volume. You'll manage budgets tied to individual jobs, coordinate comprehensive maintenance across a portfolio of properties, and be expected to arrive on site already knowing your trade. Lessen provides OSHA training and a monthly tool and equipment allowance, but the expectation is that you bring the experience and problem-solving instincts. The schedule is weekday-only with no on-call rotation, which is a real structural difference from most maintenance positions in property management.

On the compensation side, the base rate starts between $24 and $27 per hour depending on your qualifications and skill depth. There's a $1,500 sign-on bonus, a quarterly discretionary bonus of up to 5% of quarterly earnings, plus the vehicle, fuel card, and monthly allowances for tools and a cell phone.

Where This Role Can Take You

The career path here is clearly defined: strong technicians move into Lead Technician roles, and from there into Field Maintenance Manager positions as Lessen expands nationally. That trajectory matters because the skills you build in a multi-property, work-order-driven environment translate well across the broader industry. Managing your own schedule, triaging jobs by priority, tracking spend against a budget, and maintaining documentation through a technology platform are exactly the competencies that separate senior technicians from those who plateau. Companies running scattered-site portfolios, single-family rental operators, and third-party managers all prize technicians who've worked in this model because the self-direction required is harder to teach than any specific trade skill.

  • Minimum 3 years of hands-on maintenance or related trade experience (verifiable)
  • Ability to manage work orders independently across multiple properties
  • Solution-oriented approach to scope and budget decisions in the field
  • Comfortable working within a tech platform for job tracking and communication
  • Based in or able to cover the West Valley / Glendale, AZ area

If you've spent years on a single property and want to see how your skills hold up across a real portfolio, this is the kind of role that answers that question fast.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Maintenance work at a student housing community is a different animal than conventional multifamily. Turnover is high-volume and seasonal, residents are hard on units, and the on-call rotation is real. The skills that carry a technician here are broad-spectrum troubleshooting across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances, combined with the discipline to keep a preventative maintenance schedule from slipping when service request volume spikes. Pool maintenance and chemical logging are part of the job, not an afterthought. If you've held EPA Type I and II certification, that's the baseline PeakMade is looking for.

Curb appeal and common area upkeep matter more in student housing than most operators admit publicly. Prospective residents and their parents tour constantly during leasing season, and first impressions drive traffic conversion. Keeping breezeways, grounds, and common areas in shape is part of the daily rhythm here, not something that happens when there's spare time.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Complete service requests and repairs thoroughly and within expected timeframes
  • Support the Maintenance Supervisor on inventory levels for parts, tools, and supplies
  • Participate in the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies
  • Perform scheduled preventative maintenance per manufacturer specs and operating manuals
  • Assist with turn events, including make-ready work during the summer peak period
  • Maintain pool chemical logs and handle pool cleaning and upkeep
  • Inspect grounds and buildings regularly to identify liability concerns before they escalate
  • Adhere to the company's safety and hazard communications programs
  • Contribute to the cleanliness of common areas, the office, and model units

You'll need reliable transportation and must live within 30 miles of the property. Weekend and holiday availability is part of the schedule, not the exception.

What Makes This Role Worth Considering at PeakMade

PeakMade operates off-campus student housing, conventional multifamily, and build-to-rent communities across the country out of their Atlanta headquarters. The Wilmington property fits into a portfolio that takes technical development seriously. They offer HVAC certification and CPO certification support, plus a facilities leadership track for technicians who want to move toward a supervisory role. Monthly renewal bonuses and a recognition program add to base compensation in ways that flat hourly roles typically don't.

One honest note on the candidate profile: the technicians who thrive here tend to be genuinely comfortable with residents, not just mechanically skilled. Student housing means frequent interaction with people who have never rented before, which takes a particular kind of patience. Strong communication skills matter as much as knowing how to pull a capacitor.

You'll need to bring your own hand tools. That's standard in this trade and worth knowing upfront.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
It's a Saturday morning at The Ellington at Kirby, and a prospective resident walks in during your punch list review of the model. You shift gears, pull up availability in OneSite, and turn a casual walk-through into a signed lease by noon. That kind of flexibility defines this role.

Makowsky Ringel Greenberg is a well-established name in Memphis property management, and The Ellington at Kirby is the kind of community where the assistant manager genuinely runs the day-to-day. MRG operates with a hands-on, third-party management approach, which means the team at each property carries real operational weight rather than waiting on distant corporate approvals.

What the Role Covers

This is a full-cycle leasing and operations position. You'll handle incoming traffic, work prospects through the leasing process, and collect and post rental payments. Daily inspections of the model, common areas, and amenities are part of your routine, and you'll assist with vacant unit inspections to keep make-ready status current. Resident service requests and maintenance coordination fall under your scope as well. When the property manager is out, you step into that seat. Saturday availability is a firm requirement, not a flex arrangement.

What MRG Is Looking For

  • One to two years of residential leasing or property management experience
  • Working knowledge of OneSite or Yardi (OneSite preferred)
  • Ability to walk the property and manage stairs as part of daily inspections
  • Weekend availability
  • Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and proof of insurance
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Must clear credit, background, and drug screening

Compensation includes a competitive base salary, a performance bonus program, and a full benefits package: medical, dental, vision, short- and long-term disability, company-paid life insurance, additional group-rate insurance options, apartment discounts, paid holidays, PTO, and a 401(k) with profit-sharing.

One thing worth noting about this role specifically: the Memphis market has seen steady rent growth in the mid-South corridor, and Kirby is one of the stronger submarkets in the city. Candidates who understand how to maintain occupancy and manage delinquency in a competitive environment, rather than relying on a lease-up pipeline to carry numbers, will do well here. Strong candidates bring more than leasing ability. They track their traffic accurately, follow up consistently, and stay current on their comp set. That discipline is what separates an assistant who grows into a property manager from one who stays in the support seat.

job.title: Maintenance Technician 50% RENT DISCOUNT - Hidden Cove
job.description:
Apartment maintenance is one of the few roles where your morning could start with a plumbing call and end with a completed make-ready, and no two days look exactly the same. AIR Communities runs a 334-unit garden-style community in Escondido called Hidden Cove, and they're building out the maintenance team there. The work is hands-on, resident-facing, and supported by tech-driven task management that helps technicians stay organized across a full day of service requests and turns.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

Most of your time splits between completing resident service requests and supporting apartment turns between leases. On the service side, you'll troubleshoot and repair plumbing, basic electrical systems, HVAC equipment, and appliances, usually with general direction rather than someone looking over your shoulder. On the turn side, you'll follow AIR's make-ready process to get units prepped and punched out before a new resident moves in. Depending on your experience level, you may also help guide junior technicians, work with vendors, and conduct move-in and move-out inspections. Responsibilities shift with the seasons and with community needs, so the scope of your work isn't static.

On-call is part of the job. You'll carry at least one week of on-call per month, which means being reachable for after-hours emergencies and having reliable transportation to respond. That's worth naming plainly because it shapes your schedule in ways that matter.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities, building, or residential setting
  • Solid skills in at least two trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, or carpentry
  • Comfortable using technology to manage and prioritize work orders throughout the day
  • Able to handle physical demands, including lifting and moving heavy equipment
  • Available for flexible scheduling, including evenings and weekends as community needs dictate

The technicians who stand out here tend to be the ones who take the resident experience seriously, not just the technical fix. AIR ties a monthly bonus of up to $250 to customer satisfaction scores, so your communication style and follow-through with residents actually show up in your paycheck. That's a real signal about how the company weights service alongside technical skill.

Compensation runs $24 to $26 per hour based on experience, and the 50% rent discount at any AIR community is a meaningful part of the package, including the option to live at Hidden Cove itself. AIR also runs a maintenance development program called Ascend, which is tailored to individual career paths. For technicians who want to move toward lead or supervisor roles, that kind of structured development is worth paying attention to.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Cielo
job.description:
A resident submits a work order at 8 AM: no hot water. By 9, you've diagnosed a faulty heating element, swapped it out, and updated the ticket in the system before the office team even opens their email. That rhythm, moving from diagnosis to resolution without a lot of hand-holding, is what this role runs on.

The Work at Cielo

Cielo is an Olympus Property community in Charlotte, and this full-time Maintenance Technician position runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with emergency availability when needed. You'll work alongside the Lead Maintenance Technician and the broader service team, handling the full scope of day-to-day repairs: HVAC maintenance and filter changes, plumbing repairs and fixture replacements, appliance work across refrigerators, washers, dryers, ovens, and stoves, electrical switches and fixtures, and lock changes or door repairs. Preventative maintenance on HVAC units, including coil cleaning, is a regular part of the calendar. You'll also help maintain grounds, common areas, and pool areas, and keep the maintenance shop organized and properly stocked. Work orders get tracked through property management software, so staying current on documentation matters as much as the wrench work.

The pay range starts at $24 to $25 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonuses on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, short and long-term disability, life insurance, paid time off, an apartment rental allowance, educational assistance, and pet insurance.

What Olympus Looks For

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in residential, apartment, or commercial settings
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems; an EPA 608 certification or HVAC license is a plus
  • Hands-on comfort with plumbing, electrical, carpentry, painting, and appliance repair
  • Ability to operate hand tools and power tools safely and independently
  • Willingness to be available for emergency calls outside regular hours

Olympus has earned a spot on the National Apartment Association's Top Employer list for 2023, 2024, and 2025. That kind of recognition tends to reflect how a company treats people day to day, and the benefit package and bonus structure here back it up.

From a career standpoint, a role like this builds the kind of documented, multi-trade experience that moves technicians toward Lead Technician and eventually Service Manager positions. Technicians who develop strong HVAC diagnostic skills in particular tend to have real leverage in the market, since that competency is consistently hard for operators to find. Two or three years of solid work order history, good resident interaction habits, and a growing EPA certification puts you in a strong position for the next step up in portfolio management.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Part Time
job.description:
It's Saturday morning, a prospect walks in five minutes before their tour, and two current residents are waiting at the desk with questions. That's a pretty average Saturday in leasing. If that scenario sounds manageable rather than overwhelming, keep reading.

The Role at Bexley Village at Concord Mills

Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operated for over 70 years, with a portfolio of more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That longevity isn't accidental. The company runs a hands-on operation and has built a reputation for developing people from within. This part-time Leasing Consultant position at their Concord Mills location reflects that philosophy directly.

The schedule runs approximately 20 hours per week. Saturdays are part of the rotation, and weekday hours fall in the 9am to 6pm window with some flexibility on which days you work. Pay starts at $18 per hour and increases based on experience, with quarterly bonuses added on top.

Day to day, you'll handle prospect traffic, conduct tours, follow up on leads, and convert interest into signed leases. That's the sales side. You'll also handle administrative tasks, address resident concerns, assist with property appearance, and occasionally support resident events. In leasing, everyone does a little of everything, and Weinstein is straightforward about that expectation.

What They're Looking For

Weinstein is genuinely open to candidates without prior leasing experience. The training program is real, not a disclaimer. That said, a few qualities tend to separate people who thrive in this role from those who struggle:

  • Clear, warm communication, both in person and in writing
  • A customer-first instinct, especially when a situation gets uncomfortable
  • Comfort with shifting priorities mid-day without losing composure
  • Willingness to pitch in on tasks outside your immediate lane
  • Goal orientation and basic organizational discipline

The people who do well here tend to be the ones who treat a prospect walking through the door with the same energy at 5pm as they did at 9am. Consistency matters more than flash in leasing.

One honest note worth mentioning: this is a physically active role. You'll be on your feet, walking units, inspecting make-readies, and engaging with people throughout your shift. It's not a desk job, and Weinstein is clear about that upfront.

For someone looking to build a career in property management, leasing is the standard entry point, and for good reason. You learn traffic patterns, closing techniques, resident relations, and the operational rhythms of a property all at once. Many regional managers and corporate roles in this industry trace back to a leasing desk. Weinstein's internal promotion history reflects that path.

Weinstein Properties is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

Student housing puts a specific set of demands on an Assistant Community Manager that conventional multifamily doesn't. You'll use your financial acumen daily: posting damage charges from quarterly inspections, reconciling accounts receivable at month end, keeping delinquency under 2%, and managing utility billing with the kind of consistency that makes audits uneventful. Alongside that, you'll work the sales side, conducting weekly market surveys, tracking KPIs, managing concessions within budget, and directing leasing activity to hit occupancy and revenue targets. The operational and financial threads run in parallel here, and the ability to hold both at once is what separates a strong ACM from one who's perpetually behind.

Entrata proficiency matters at this property. Scion lists it as preferred, and in student housing that preference is usually a soft requirement once you're in the seat. Move-in assignments, room transfers, move-outs, and resident account management all flow through the system. If you've worked in Entrata, you'll recognize the workflow. If you haven't, plan to get comfortable with it fast.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-scope ACM position at Central House Columbia, a student community on South Rock Quarry Road. The General Manager owns the asset's overall performance, and you support that directly while running your own lane across operations, leasing, resident relations, and staff development.

  • Coach and hold accountable onsite staff, including coverage for after-hours on-call rotation
  • Own resident account management: AR reconciliation, NSF and late fee enforcement, move-out billing and deposit disposition
  • Lead and execute annual turn alongside the GM, which in student housing is a compressed, high-volume process requiring precise coordination
  • Inspect vacant units monthly and walk grounds and common areas regularly to maintain curb appeal and code compliance
  • Coordinate work orders with maintenance staff and vendors
  • Handle escalated resident concerns and manage eviction filings in accordance with local ordinances and company policy
  • Manage promotional materials, marketing messaging, and local outreach to drive traffic during lease-up cycles
  • Step into the GM role during absences, which means you need to understand the full picture, not just your own tasks

A word on the turn: at a student property, the annual turn is its own season. Hundreds of move-outs and move-ins compressed into a short window, punch lists running simultaneously across the building, damage assessments, billing, key exchanges. If you've done it before, you know. If you haven't, expect the first one to be a steep and instructive week.

What's Distinctive About This Role at Scion

Scion operates at scale in the student housing sector, which means the systems, training infrastructure, and operational playbooks are more developed than you'd find at a smaller regional operator. There's genuine room to grow here. ACMs at student properties who handle the financial side well tend to move into GM roles faster than their conventional multifamily counterparts, partly because the operational complexity of student housing translates cleanly to larger assets.

Scion also offers learning reimbursement, which is worth noting if you're considering credentials or continuing education in property management. The benefit structure includes health, dental, vision, 401k matching, and paid parental leave, along with a discretionary annual bonus.

You need at least one year of experience in property management or a residential community setting. Strong written and verbal communication is non-negotiable in a role that involves resident notices, staff coaching, and direct leasing conversations. The detail orientation required here is real: this isn't the kind of position where close enough works on account reconciliation or Fair Housing compliance.

job.title: Maintenance Technician I (Crystal Springs Terrace)
job.description:
It's 7:45 a.m. and you've already got three service requests queued, a unit turning Friday, and a resident at the office door with a leaky faucet. That's a normal Tuesday at a Prometheus property.

Prometheus Real Estate Group is hiring a Maintenance Technician I at Crystal Springs Terrace in San Bruno, California. This is a general maintenance role covering the full scope of day-to-day upkeep: service requests, apartment turns, and the ongoing repairs that keep a residential community running. The pay range sits at $27.75 to $28.75 per hour, with standby and on-call premium pay on top of that.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Turns are a significant part of this role. You'll move through punch lists, handle make-ready prep, and coordinate repairs across appliances, plumbing, carpentry, electrical, and paint. Beyond turns, you're fielding resident service requests and troubleshooting mechanical systems, both major and minor. Prometheus calls their residents "Neighbors," and that framing reflects something real about how they expect their maintenance team to operate: with care and responsiveness, not just technical competency. Residents notice the difference between a tech who fixes the problem and one who also treats the interaction like it matters.

On-call availability is required. If that's new to you, budget some mental energy for it. It's a real part of the job, not a footnote.

What Prometheus Is Looking For

  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of appliances, plumbing, basic electrical, carpentry, and paint
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Basic computer proficiency
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. occasionally; comfortable working outdoors in moderate temperatures
  • Clear written and verbal communication in English

The benefits package here is genuinely strong by industry standards. Prometheus covers 100% of medical, vision, and dental premiums, including eligible dependents, with buy-up options available. There's a 401(k) with employer matching, a behavioral health program accessible around the clock, paid volunteer time, and tenure-based housing discounts that become more meaningful the longer you stay. They also offer a semi-annual discretionary bonus and several bonus categories tied to specific performance milestones, including renovation and lease-up bonuses that can apply depending on property needs at a given time.

For technicians who want a clear path upward, this kind of role builds the foundation. Strong performers in Technician I positions typically move toward lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles as they accumulate experience across more complex systems and demonstrate reliability on call rotation. The San Bruno Bay Area market means properties generally run at high occupancy with demanding resident expectations. That pressure sharpens your skills faster than a slower-moving market would.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Hillpointe builds and operates market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and they do it vertically integrated: land acquisition, construction, procurement, and asset management all run in-house. That means the maintenance team isn't just servicing a stabilized asset. They're also expected to support lease-up communities as they come online and get to occupancy.

What the Role Actually Covers

As Maintenance Supervisor, you own the full physical operation of the community. Service requests, preventative maintenance, make-ready turns, grounds and amenity appearance, vendor oversight, and inventory management all fall under your scope. On the make-ready side, you're managing inspections and repairs on vacant units to keep them rent-ready and minimize days off-market. Every day a unit sits unready is a day of lost rent, so turn speed and punch list quality matter directly to NOI.

You'll also conduct safety meetings, maintain OSHA compliance, and inspect work completed by contractors and your own team. Hillpointe's development pipeline means you may periodically assist with the setup and stabilization of new communities as they open, which gives this role exposure beyond typical property maintenance work.

On-call rotation is real here. Evenings, weekends, and early mornings are part of the schedule, and after-hours emergency response is expected. That's standard for this level in multifamily, but worth knowing going in.

Certifications and Qualifications

  • EPA Type I and II or Universal refrigerant certification (required)
  • CPO certification preferred, or willingness to obtain it
  • All state and local certifications as required by jurisdiction
  • Valid driver's license
  • Proficiency with hand tools, mechanical equipment, and basic office software
  • High school diploma, GED, or equivalent hands-on experience
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly, climb ladders, and work in variable outdoor conditions

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The supervisory piece matters as much as the technical skills here. Hillpointe is a top-ranked NMHC builder and developer with multiple communities in various stages across the Sun Belt. A candidate who can train and onboard new maintenance staff, hold vendors accountable on quality and timeline, and keep a punch list moving without hand-holding will outperform someone who's only strong on the wrench side. Jacksonville's heat and humidity also mean HVAC and pool systems take real abuse in summer, so hands-on mechanical troubleshooting in those areas is a genuine day-to-day advantage. The candidates who grow fastest in roles like this tend to move into Regional Maintenance Director positions as a company scales its portfolio.

job.title: Business Manager 1500-2500 - Remote, Washington
job.description:
Remote accounting roles in multifamily tend to get underestimated. The title says "Business Manager," but the actual work sits at the intersection of collections strategy, resident relations, and operational compliance across a significant portfolio. At Berkshire Residential Investments, this role covers communities in the 1,500 to 2,500 unit range, which means the decisions you make on delinquency and account management carry real NOI weight.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day centers on resident accounts and the financial health of multiple communities. You'll pursue recovery of delinquent balances, coordinate with attorneys when accounts reach eviction action, and ensure that process stays compliant with state and local law. You'll process security deposit dispositions, manage former resident accounts through collections, and handle FAS processing. Beyond the collections cycle, you're also reviewing rental applications and approving or flagging prospects, which means you're touching the front end of occupancy as well as the back end of delinquency.

The role is remote, but it's not independent. You'll work closely with on-site property management teams to keep resident ledgers accurate and to coordinate eviction and abandoned unit timelines. The flexible 40-hour schedule adjusts to the time zone needs of the properties you support, so your day may shift depending on where your communities are located.

  • Three or more years in property management, with multifamily experience preferred
  • At least two years in accounts receivable or payable
  • Two or more years in customer service or sales
  • Yardi experience strongly preferred
  • Strong communication skills across both property teams and residents
  • Comfort working independently in a remote environment with multiple properties

Skills That Compound From Here

This role builds a specific and transferable skill set. Managing delinquency across 1,500 to 2,500 units at once trains you to think at portfolio scale, not just property level. That's the kind of exposure that typically positions people for regional accounting roles, compliance-focused positions, or transitions into asset management support. The application review component adds leasing and risk assessment judgment to your profile, which makes you more rounded than a pure collections specialist. If you're three to five years into multifamily and want to build depth on the financial operations side, this is a logical next step.

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means you're working within a vertically integrated structure. That matters because your counterparts on-site have real authority and real accountability, and so do you. The collaboration here isn't just coordination; it directly affects occupancy outcomes and community financial performance.

job.title: Maintenance Porter - Part-Time
job.description:
Curb appeal is one of the first things a prospective resident notices, and one of the last things a departing resident remembers. At a student housing community, where high turnover is built into the calendar and first impressions drive leasing traffic, the porter role carries real weight in how a property presents itself day to day.

Redstone Residential operates more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, with a portfolio that spans student housing and conventional multifamily. This part-time porter position sits within their Statesboro, Georgia community and pays $16.00 per hour, with a 401(k) plan that includes up to 6% employer matching.

What This Role Requires

The core of this position is maintaining cleanliness and safety across the property. That means common areas, hallways, the clubhouse, office, and model unit all need consistent attention. Outdoor grounds require regular upkeep: trash and debris removal, landscaping maintenance, watering, and keeping walkways and parking areas clear. You'll also assist with basic repairs and general maintenance tasks as needed.

The qualifications Redstone is looking for reflect the practical nature of the work:

  • Prior janitorial or cleaning experience in a relevant setting
  • Ability to work independently and complete daily tasks without close supervision
  • Comfortable standing for 4 to 6 hour shifts and able to lift 50 or more pounds
  • A genuinely friendly, team-oriented approach to the work

What This Role Builds

Porters who pay attention tend to become valuable eyes on the property. Because you're moving through common areas and grounds regularly, you're often the first to spot a maintenance issue before it becomes a work order, a safety hazard before it becomes a liability, or a resident concern before it escalates. That awareness, once developed, is directly transferable to make-ready and maintenance technician roles.

In student housing specifically, the porter role sharpens your ability to maintain quality under real time pressure. Turn season at a student property compresses a significant volume of work into a short window, and team members who've built strong independent work habits and understand property presentation standards are the ones who tend to move into broader maintenance responsibilities when those opportunities open up.

If you're early in a property management career and want to learn the physical side of operations from the ground up, this is a practical entry point with a company that manages at genuine scale.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Fairstead operates at a scale that most affordable housing owners don't reach: 30,000-plus units across 28 states, with development, construction, and property management all running under one roof. At the site level in Columbia, Maryland, that integration means the maintenance team is held to a professional standard that matches what you'd expect at a market-rate operation. This Service Manager role sits at the center of that.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

The title says Service Manager, and that's accurate. This is a working supervisor position. You'll carry tools and you'll also direct people. On a given day that might mean pulling an HVAC diagnosis in the morning, reviewing a punch list from a turn unit midday, and coaching a tech through a repair they haven't done solo before in the afternoon. Fairstead uses Yardi and RealPage on the operational side, so comfort with work order software matters, even if you're not running reports all day.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Supervising maintenance staff and taking point on special projects
  • Performing skilled repairs across mechanical, electrical, and general building systems
  • Maintaining the property's physical condition in line with Fairstead's safety standards
  • Working independently on routine work, escalating or pulling in help on more complex jobs
  • Occasional overtime for emergencies or project-driven needs

The company is explicit that they want someone with depth in at least one trade, not a generalist who knows a little about everything. Three years of property maintenance experience is the floor. If you've got a background in HVAC, electrical, or plumbing with solid general skills layered on top, that's the profile that tends to fit well here.

The Affordable Housing Context

Working for an affordable housing operator means the resident population often has fewer alternatives when something breaks. That's not a minor detail. The maintenance function carries real weight here, and a Service Manager who understands that tends to run a tighter, more responsive operation than one who treats it like any other multifamily gig. Fairstead's tech-forward approach also means you'll likely encounter digital work order systems and data tracking tools that some smaller operators haven't adopted yet. That's a skill that transfers well if you eventually move toward a portfolio-level or regional maintenance role.

Compensation and Benefits

The pay range for this position runs $23 to $25 per hour, depending on experience and location factors. Benefits include employer-contributed medical coverage through Meritain Health, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with a dollar-for-dollar match on the first 3% and 50% match on the next 2%, 15 PTO days, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays. Flexible spending accounts, disability coverage, and pet insurance round out the package.

Fairstead is an equal opportunity employer and considers diversity in background and experience a genuine operational asset, not just a policy statement.

job.title: Community Manager - Roving - Nevada Region
job.description:
What This Role Actually Is

A roving community manager position at a multifamily company covers more ground than a standard site manager role, literally and figuratively. You're not anchored to one address. CloudTen Residential, a Nevada-based operator with a portfolio that spans hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning plays across the West, needs someone who can drop into different properties, read the room quickly, and run operations without a long ramp-up period. Valid driver's license is a hard requirement. The pay range is $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience.

This kind of role tends to attract people who get bored doing the same thing at the same address every week. It also demands that you already know what you're doing. When you're covering for a site, the team looks to you for direction from day one, not week three.

What You're Responsible For

The scope here is full-cycle community management across each property you cover. On the financial side, that means rent collections, delinquency follow-up, non-payment notices, daily deposits, and adherence to accounting directives including weekly and monthly reporting. You'll also flag capex needs, gather bids, and make budget recommendations to the regional manager. Reviewing renewals and preparing rate increase recommendations based on market conditions and the operating budget is part of the job.

Leasing and marketing responsibilities are equally hands-on. You'll work traffic, demonstrate units, secure commitments and deposits, monitor closing ratios on leasing staff, and keep an eye on competitive properties to anticipate shifts that could affect NOI. Lease administration accuracy matters here: names, addresses, rates, addenda, all of it.

On the administrative and leadership side, you'll conduct inspections of common areas, models, and vacant units, manage move-in and move-out administration, oversee on-site staff including hiring and coaching, and hold regular team meetings. Resident relations, service request follow-up, and retention programs round out the day-to-day.

Who Tends to Thrive Here

We've seen roving managers succeed or struggle based on one thing more than any other: the ability to build credibility with an unfamiliar team fast. You can't rely on history with the staff or deep familiarity with a single property's quirks. What you can rely on is strong process discipline, clean communication, and the kind of operational instinct that lets you walk a property and spot what needs attention before anyone tells you.

Candidates who come from lease-up or repositioning backgrounds tend to adapt well to the variety this role brings. If your experience is limited to stable, single-site operations, the context-switching here can be an adjustment. That's worth knowing going in.

Organizationally, CloudTen describes itself as people-focused and service-driven, with a portfolio that includes some genuinely varied asset types. For a roving manager, that variety is a feature. You'll see more in a year here than most site managers see in three.

job.title: Resident Manager - Franklin Apartments
job.description:
Resident management at a smaller community like Franklin Apartments in El Cajon draws on a specific blend of skills that bigger portfolio roles don't always develop: direct resident contact, hands-on leasing, and enough financial oversight to keep a property running cleanly without a full back-office team behind you. This role sits at that intersection.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Leasing competence is central here. You'll conduct tours, qualify applicants, and complete documentation in full compliance with California Civil Code and Fair Housing requirements. California's landlord-tenant laws are among the most detailed in the country, and El Cajon's rental market includes a significant Spanish-speaking population, which is why bilingual ability in English and Spanish carries real weight in this posting. It's not a checkbox preference; it's a practical need for genuine resident communication.

Financial accountability matters at this scale too. You'll collect rent, maintain accounting records, make bank deposits, and flag delinquency to supervisors before any legal process begins. It's a contained scope, but it requires accuracy and consistency. Disorganized records create compliance exposure under California's security deposit statutes, and that risk lands on the on-site manager first.

On the operations side, you'll coordinate maintenance work orders targeting 24 to 48-hour turnaround, oversee move-in and move-out inspections, manage vendor compliance (insurance, licensing, labor law), and handle regular inspections of units and common areas. Strong organizational habits matter more than technical maintenance knowledge here. You're coordinating and documenting, not turning wrenches.

What the Role Actually Looks Like Week to Week

This is a part-time, on-site position with a minimum of roughly 12 hours per week and some schedule flexibility. Living on-site is a requirement. Because you're the on-site representative for Sunrise Management, residents will approach you informally as well as through official channels. The ability to stay professional and consistent in that environment, where the property is also your home, is a real skill that the job description gestures toward but doesn't fully articulate.

  • Minimum 2 years of property management or directly related experience
  • Working knowledge of California landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing requirements
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and property management software
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Bilingual English and Spanish preferred
  • Ability to live on-site at the property

What Makes This Role at Sunrise Distinctive

Sunrise Management operates with a resident hospitality orientation, which in practice means they expect their on-site staff to treat resident satisfaction as an operational priority, not an afterthought. For a candidate who has worked in higher-volume, more transactional environments, this culture tends to suit people who genuinely prefer a smaller, relationship-based community over a high-traffic lease-up setting. The pay range is $16.90 to $19.00 per hour depending on experience. This position does not qualify for company benefits plans.

Candidates who stand out typically bring a combination of leasing confidence and the kind of calm judgment that keeps minor resident issues from escalating. In a part-time on-site role, that judgment matters more than any single technical credential.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Solis at Flamingo
job.description:
Solis at Flamingo is a 524-unit luxury community in Las Vegas, and this Maintenance Technician role sits at the center of keeping it running well. The work is real and physical: apartment turns, resident service requests, HVAC troubleshooting, plumbing repairs, appliance fixes, basic electrical work. Some days you'll move through a punch list of make-readies; other days you're responding to something unexpected that a resident needs fixed now. Both matter equally here.

What You'll Actually Do

Turns are a core part of the rhythm. When a resident moves out, you're the one making the unit ready for the next person. That means working through a punch list carefully, fixing things right rather than fast, and treating the make-ready as your signature on the work. Beyond turns, you'll handle resident-submitted service requests across the trade areas you're strongest in, with general direction from the team. AIR uses tech tools to help prioritize and track work orders, which cuts down on the back-and-forth and keeps you moving efficiently through the day.

Depending on your skill level, you may also provide guidance to junior technicians, assist with vendor oversight, and participate in move-in and move-out inspections. The scope shifts with the season and what the community needs, so flexibility is real, not just a line in the posting.

On-call is part of the job. At least one week per month, you'll need to be reachable and able to respond to after-hours emergencies. That means having reliable transportation and being ready to handle something urgent at an inconvenient hour. That's the honest reality of apartment maintenance, and it's worth knowing before you apply.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment
  • Proficiency in at least two trade areas: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, or carpentry
  • Willingness to work evenings, weekends, and rotating on-call shifts
  • Physical ability to move heavy equipment and machinery as needed
  • A track record of fixing things correctly the first time, not just closing out work orders

Compensation and What Comes With It

The hourly rate runs $20 to $22, placed based on your actual skills and experience. On top of that, AIR offers a monthly customer service bonus of up to $250 for technicians who consistently earn strong resident satisfaction scores. The 50% rent discount at any AIR community is one of the more substantial perks in the industry, and there's an option to live on-site if that appeals to you. The company also covers short and long-term disability, offers up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, and reimburses up to 100% of costs for job-related certifications and licenses.

For technicians who want to grow, AIR runs a maintenance development program called Ascend, which builds a path based on your individual goals rather than a generic training checklist. HVAC certification reimbursement, for example, is the kind of support that can meaningfully change your earning ceiling in this industry. If you're interested in moving toward a lead or service manager role over time, the structure here is set up to support that.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Multifamily properties in Boston's urban core run complex mechanical systems, tight turn schedules, and demanding residents. Bozzuto's Cambridge community needs an Assistant Maintenance Manager who can handle all three without losing composure.

This is a working leadership role. You'll carry a wrench and a clipboard. You'll pull service tickets, troubleshoot HVAC and plumbing issues, and also coach the technicians around you. The make-ready process is a real priority here: apartment turns need to be tight and on schedule so units can lease and new residents can move in without delays. Preventative maintenance gets the same attention as reactive work.

Day-to-Day Scope

Most of your week splits between resident service requests and building systems. You're diagnosing and resolving issues across HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance repair. You're walking the property for general upkeep, grounds maintenance, and safety compliance. In winter, that includes snow removal. You'll also manage punch list completion on turns, support preventative maintenance scheduling, and keep the operation running inside applicable building and safety codes.

Weekend availability is required, and you'll participate in the emergency on-call rotation. That's a real commitment. Properties like this don't go quiet after business hours.

What the Role Requires

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • Hands-on proficiency with HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and appliance repair
  • HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems: central plant, boilers, chillers, split systems
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Knowledge of OSHA standards, risk management practices, and MSDS
  • Supervisory experience or demonstrated leadership in a team setting
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying weather conditions

Strong candidates for this role tend to think like building owners. They notice the things residents haven't reported yet, track patterns in recurring failures, and don't let punch lists linger. If you've managed turns at a Class A mid-rise or high-rise and kept delinquency in your maintenance queue close to zero, that experience translates directly here.

The salary range is $62,000 to $72,000, with additional bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Bilingual Screening & Applications Specialist - Sandy Springs, GA
job.description:
A prospective resident calls in frustrated. Their application has been pending for two days, they're trying to move in before their lease ends across town, and they're not sure their documents uploaded correctly. Your job, in that moment, is to be the calm, competent voice that turns that anxiety into a clear next step.

Cortland, one of the largest multifamily owners and operators in the country, runs a centralized Contact Center that handles application processing and resident screening across its portfolio. This bilingual Screening and Applications Specialist role sits inside that operation, serving as the main point of contact for applicants from the moment they submit an application through move-in. The work is phone-heavy, documentation-intensive, and requires genuine patience alongside real organizational discipline.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You'll be reviewing and processing rental applications, verifying documentation, and keeping applicants informed at each stage of the process. Calls, emails, and chat inquiries come in simultaneously, and you'll be managing multiple applicants at different points in the pipeline at any given time. When something stalls, whether a missing document or a compliance question, you're the one who figures out the path forward and communicates it clearly. De-escalating tense conversations is part of the job, and Fair Housing compliance is non-negotiable throughout.

Cortland uses platforms like RealPage, OneSite, and Funnel, so comfort with property management software matters. You'll also be working inside CRM tools and adapting to system updates as they roll out. The environment moves quickly and the volume is real.

Bilingual fluency is central to this role. Applicants who speak Spanish (or another language, depending on the market) deserve the same quality of communication as anyone else, and your ability to bridge that gap directly affects their experience and Cortland's conversion rates.

Who Fits Well Here

  • 2 or more years of customer service experience, preferably in a high-volume contact center or multifamily leasing environment
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Bilingual proficiency (English plus at least one additional language)
  • Demonstrated ability to handle confidential applicant information with care and discretion
  • Strong attention to detail when reviewing applications and verifying documents under volume pressure
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and comfort with property management platforms
  • Flexibility to work weekends and extended hours when the business needs it

The candidates who tend to thrive in centralized leasing operations like this one aren't just organized. They're also good at reading the emotional temperature of a conversation and adjusting accordingly. Applicants are often stressed. They're making a significant financial and personal decision. The specialists who stand out treat that seriously without letting it slow down their throughput.

This role can serve as a strong foundation for moving into leasing management, compliance coordination, or operations roles within a large vertically integrated portfolio. Cortland handles design, construction, and property operations in-house, which means there's genuine internal mobility for people who perform well and want to grow.

job.title: Housekeeper - Texcoco
job.description:
MG Properties runs apartment communities across the Western U.S. and has been doing it for over 30 years. Their portfolio spans acquisition, development, rehab, and day-to-day management. The Housekeeper role at Texcoco in San Diego is a ground-level position that directly affects how residents experience the property every single day.

What You'll Actually Do

This job covers the full footprint of a residential community. Common areas, hallways, laundry rooms, waste disposal areas, the leasing office, clubhouse, restrooms, and model units all fall under your scope. You'll also prep vacant apartments for incoming residents, which means cleaning and staging them to move-in-ready condition and keeping them that way until occupied.

Daily sanitizing of the leasing office and clubhouse is part of the routine. You'll also track cleaning supplies and flag shortages to management before they become a problem. Safety concerns you spot during your rounds get reported, not ignored.

What You Bring

  • Solid knowledge of cleaning chemicals and equipment, including safe handling and application
  • Strong attention to detail and consistent follow-through on cleanliness standards
  • Ability to work independently and manage your time without close supervision
  • Reliable transportation (required, no exceptions)
  • Punctuality and dependability as baseline work habits
  • A cooperative attitude when working alongside maintenance and leasing teams

Compensation and Context

Pay runs $21 to $23 per hour depending on experience. The role includes monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and full medical, dental, and vision coverage. PTO, paid holidays, personal days, and paid sick time are included. MG Properties also offers rental discounts, which matters if you're looking to live closer to where you work.

One thing worth knowing: make-ready cleaning on vacant units is where attention to detail gets tested most. A unit that looks clean on the surface but has grime in corners, residue in appliances, or smudged windows will get flagged during inspection. The strongest housekeepers in multifamily work treat every vacant unit like it's the one a prospective resident will walk through that afternoon, because sometimes it is.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work in single-family rental requires a specific kind of independence. You're not working alongside a team at one property. You're moving between houses across a market, diagnosing problems without a second opinion nearby, and closing out work orders through your phone. That's the core skill set this role runs on: self-directed troubleshooting, mobile-first field operations, and the hands-on range to handle HVAC, plumbing, and electrical without calling a specialist for every ticket.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Roofstock manages single-family rental homes, which shapes the day significantly. There's no leasing office to check into, no on-site team. You'll drive a company vehicle (gas card included) between properties across the Charlotte area, handling a mix of routine repairs, make-readies, and move-in and move-out inspections. When a unit turns, you're the one walking it, building the punch list, and getting it rent-ready. You'll also audit vendor work, which means you need to know what a completed job actually looks like, not just what was invoiced.

Work orders and communication run through mobile apps, so comfort with that workflow matters. Posting legal notices is part of the job too. Physical demands are real: expect lifting up to 50 pounds, climbing, bending, and working in both indoor and outdoor conditions depending on the day.

One thing worth noting directly: this role has no on-call requirement and no weekend schedule. In single-family rental, that's genuinely uncommon. Most technician roles in this space carry after-hours exposure. This one doesn't.

What Roofstock Needs From You

  • HVAC Type II Certification (required); Universal Certification preferred
  • Valid driver's license with a clean enough record to operate a company vehicle
  • Comfort working independently and managing your own daily schedule in the field
  • Strong diagnostic instincts across trades, especially when you're the only one on site
  • Ease with mobile apps for work order management and field communication
  • High school diploma or GED; U.S. work authorization required

What Makes This Role at Roofstock Distinctive

Single-family rental at scale is a relatively young model, and companies like Roofstock are still building out how field operations work efficiently across dispersed assets. That means technicians here tend to develop a broader operational view than those working traditional multifamily. You're not just fixing things. You're functioning as the eyes on properties that don't have on-site staff. Technicians who perform well in this environment often move into lead or regional field roles as portfolios grow, because the institutional SFR sector is still expanding and field-level experience is genuinely hard to find.

Pay runs $25 to $30 per hour based on experience, licensure, and location. The company provides a vehicle and gas card, a generous PTO policy with 12 paid holidays, 401k, parental leave, volunteer time off, and monthly subsidies for wellness and home office or cell phone costs. Health, dental, and vision coverage round out the package.

job.title: Community Manager (Summer Oaks)
job.description:
A resident stops by the office with questions about their re-certification paperwork. Your maintenance tech radios in about a plumbing issue in building two. You've got a unit turn to track and a compliance deadline on Friday. That's a normal Tuesday at Summer Oaks.
