When the holiday package volume hits, there's physical work involved too. Bozzuto specifies the ability to lift up to 25 pounds, and if you've worked a luxury building during peak delivery season, you know that's a real part of the role.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • At least two years in hospitality, hotel, retail, or travel environments
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with software, apps, and property management tools
  • A professional appearance and detail-oriented mindset
  • Genuine instinct for anticipating what a customer needs before they ask

The salary range is $45,760 to $49,920, with additional bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

One thing worth knowing: the strongest concierges in luxury multifamily are the ones who treat resident relationships as a long-term investment. Knowing a resident's dog by name, remembering a preference, flagging a concern before it becomes a complaint. Those small things compound into retention, and retention is one of the metrics Bozzuto tracks closely. If you've built that kind of rapport in a hotel or hospitality setting, those skills transfer directly here.

job.title: Community Relations Manager - Cortland Sugar Land
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in after touring three other communities that morning. They're tired, they're skeptical, and they have questions the other leasing teams didn't bother to answer. How you handle the next 45 minutes determines whether Cortland Sugar Land earns that lease.

That moment captures a lot of what this role is about. The Community Relations Manager at Cortland Sugar Land sits at the intersection of sales performance and resident experience, working closely with the Community Manager to keep daily operations running and to bring in qualified residents who stay, renew, and refer their friends. It's a position that rewards people who are equally comfortable closing a lease and walking a make-ready unit to confirm it meets brand standards before move-in day.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

On the operations side, you'll support the onsite leadership team in keeping the property compliant with Fair Housing guidelines, OSHA requirements, and company standards. That includes conducting regular community inspections, covering vacant units, model homes, and move-in and move-out walkthroughs. You'll monitor curb appeal and flag maintenance needs, and you'll manage vendor relationships to make sure projects get completed on time and at the quality level the property demands.

On the leasing and revenue side, you'll actively manage your pipeline, follow up with prospects, and close leases using consultative techniques that match each person's situation rather than running through a script. CRM discipline matters here. Cortland tracks lead activity, conversion metrics, and pipeline health closely, and your records need to reflect reality accurately. You'll also help shape the community's marketing presence, including social media, and you'll plan and execute resident events that build genuine connection rather than just filling a calendar.

Resident concerns are part of the job too. When something goes wrong, whether it's a maintenance issue that's taken too long or a billing question that's created frustration, you'll be expected to handle it with real empathy and real urgency, not just a polished brush-off.

Who Fits Well Here

  • At least two years of measurable sales success in a high-velocity, short-cycle environment. Multifamily experience is a natural fit, but Cortland also looks at candidates from luxury retail, hospitality, premium automotive, or similar fields where closing and service coexist.
  • A demonstrated track record of hitting or exceeding leasing targets and KPIs, with organized follow-up habits to back it up.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to build rapport quickly with people who may be cautious or indecisive.
  • Comfort with property management software, CRM platforms, Microsoft Office, and social media for marketing purposes.
  • High school diploma required; a bachelor's degree or equivalent is preferred.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this type of role: they don't treat the operational duties as a distraction from leasing. The community manager notices when someone treats inspections and vendor follow-ups as secondary, and so do residents. The people who thrive here carry the same attention and ownership across both sides of the job.

Cortland is a vertically integrated owner-operator with in-house design, construction, and management capabilities, which means the resources and support structure here are different from what you'd find at a smaller fee management shop. For someone who wants to grow into a senior community manager or property management leadership role, the platform offers real runway, provided you build the operational credibility alongside the sales record.

job.title: Lead Maintenance Technician - Lirio
job.description:
It's 7:45 AM and a work order for a tripped breaker in Building C is already in the queue. By 8:15, you've triaged two more service requests, confirmed a contractor is on-site for the pool resurfacing, and checked in with your tech about the make-ready schedule for four upcoming turns. That's the cadence of this role at Lirio, a residential community in San Antonio managed by Olympus Property.

What This Role Requires

Olympus is looking for a Lead Maintenance Technician with at least three years of hands-on experience in residential or apartment maintenance, including time in a supervisory capacity. EPA/HVAC certification is required before you start. Beyond the technical baseline, this role demands genuine organizational skill: you'll manage a team's daily, weekly, and monthly workloads, coordinate third-party contractors, and keep the maintenance shop stocked, clean, and compliant. Full-time availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM, with on-call rotation included.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Overseeing all maintenance operations across the apartment community, common areas, and grounds
  • Managing turn-key operations and coordinating make-ready units with the leasing office and Business Manager
  • Performing and scheduling preventative maintenance on HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, irrigation, pools, and structural systems
  • Conducting monthly, quarterly, and annual property inspections
  • Ordering and maintaining tool, parts, and supply inventories
  • Hiring and developing service team members
  • Tracking service requests and work orders through property management software
  • Ensuring safety, security, and regulatory compliance across the property

What This Role Builds

Candidates who grow the most in a Lead Maintenance role are the ones who treat team development as seriously as their technical work. You'll supervise other technicians and coordinate outside vendors, which sharpens your ability to delegate clearly, hold people accountable, and keep a punch list moving without babysitting every task. Those skills transfer directly into a Maintenance Director or Regional Facilities role down the line.

Strong candidates also learn to think in terms of NOI impact. Every deferred repair, every slow turn, every unplanned capex expense affects the property's bottom line. The best Lead Techs understand that keeping a unit rent-ready and a work order queue short isn't just housekeeping, it's asset protection. Olympus uses software systems to track inventory and completed action items, so comfort with digital reporting tools is a practical skill this role reinforces over time.

Pay runs $30 to $35 per hour depending on experience, with monthly and quarterly bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, and an apartment rental allowance. Olympus has earned recognition as a top employer by the National Apartment Association three consecutive years, and the culture emphasis here is genuine rather than decorative: the company's stated values center on care, teamwork, and trust at every level of the organization.

job.title: Maintenance Assistant Supervisor
job.description:
Apartment maintenance leadership is a balancing act. You're expected to keep your hands in the work while also keeping the team organized, the vendors accountable, and the residents satisfied. Weinstein Properties is hiring a Maintenance Assistant Supervisor at Abbington West End in Henrico, VA to do exactly that.

The Work

Weinstein is a family-owned operator with over 70 years in the business and a portfolio of 60-plus communities across five states. They own and manage everything in-house, which means decisions move faster and the team you're part of actually has authority over how things get done. This role sits between the service team and the Maintenance Supervisor, coordinating daily workflow while staying hands-on with repairs.

Day to day, you'll assign and manage work orders, schedule turns, coordinate vendor access, and make sure make-ready units move through the punch list efficiently. You'll also be in the field working alongside your team on HVAC, electrical, plumbing, appliances, drywall, carpentry, and pool maintenance. When things break, you diagnose them. When vendors come on site, you supervise them directly.

On-call rotation is shared with other team members. That's worth knowing upfront. The compensation reflects it: a $150 weekly on-call bonus whether calls come in or not, plus an extra $150 for holiday on-call coverage.

What Qualifies You

  • At least 4 years of hands-on trade experience across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general building maintenance
  • At least 1 year in a lead, assistant supervisor, or supervisory role in apartment maintenance specifically
  • EPA/CFC certification (Type I and II or Universal) required before starting
  • Comfortable using software to manage work orders, track supplies, and communicate via email
  • Valid driver's license, personal transportation, and your own tools
  • Willing to share on-call responsibilities with the team

Starting pay is $26/hour depending on experience, with a $1,500 sign-on bonus (details discussed during the interview), quarterly performance bonuses up to $1,110, and a standard benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, 401k with company match, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, and a rent discount.

Strong candidates in this kind of role tend to be people who don't need a supervisor watching over them to stay organized. If you can hold your team accountable, communicate clearly with residents when something goes wrong, and still turn a wrench when the job calls for it, that's the profile Weinstein is looking for. The in-house ownership model also means this role has a clear path upward for someone who performs well and wants to grow into a full Maintenance Supervisor position over time.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Leases turn in bulk, move-in weekends bring hundreds of residents through the door at once, and the customer is often a first-time renter whose parents are also watching. The Assistant Community Manager role at Alight State College exists inside that reality, supporting the General Manager across every function that keeps the community running and the resident experience intact.

Scion Group operates student living communities across the country, and this position in State College, Pennsylvania puts you inside a collegiate environment where occupancy cycles, traffic patterns, and customer expectations all move to the academic calendar. The role carries real operational weight. You're expected to step in as acting General Manager when needed, which means this isn't a role where you shadow from a distance.

What the Work Actually Involves

The scope here is wide. On the administrative side, you'll manage resident accounts, utility billing, accounts receivable reconciliation, and delinquency tracking with a target of keeping delinquency below 2% at month end. You'll handle notices, coordinate eviction filings in compliance with local ordinance, and respond to escalated resident concerns including public reviews on Google and Yelp. Financial performance reporting, market surveys, and managing promotional materials and concessions round out the business operations piece.

Facilities oversight is a consistent thread through the week. Monthly property walks, scorecard assessments, work order coordination, and curb appeal checks are part of the regular rhythm. During annual turn, the role goes hands-on. That means walking units for move-out damage assessments, processing charges and disputes, coordinating vendors, tracking progress through Turnable, and at times physically helping move furniture or assist the facilities team with punch list items. Turn in student housing is compressed and high-volume. If that kind of organized chaos energizes you, it fits. If it doesn't, that's worth knowing upfront.

On the people side, you'll assist with hiring, scheduling on-call coverage, coaching team members, and supporting retention efforts. The GM leads, but you're an active partner in keeping the team functioning and the culture intact.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

  • Comfort with Entrata or a comparable property management system. Scion also uses ClickUp, Greenhouse, Lattice, Qualtrics, and Turnable, so tech fluency matters.
  • At least one year of experience in property management or residential living operations, with enough exposure to understand leasing cycles, resident communication, and basic financial reconciliation.
  • Genuine attention to detail in written communication. Resident notices, damage charge documentation, and review responses all carry legal or reputational weight.
  • Ability to shift between a spreadsheet and a mop bucket without losing composure. Turn season at a student property demands both.

This role develops the full operating picture of a residential community. Candidates who do well here typically move into General Manager positions or transition into regional support roles. The exposure to financial reporting, staff development, and customer experience management across a high-volume property builds a foundation that carries across conventional and student housing alike.

The position is exempt and includes health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid parental leave, floating holidays, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. Work authorization in the United States is required. Visa sponsorship is not available.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager (Fetters, Celestina Gardens)
job.description:
A resident stops by the office to sort out a documentation issue before her annual recertification appointment. You pull her file, walk her through what's needed, and schedule a follow-up. That kind of interaction is the center of gravity for this role at Fetters and Celestina Gardens, two affordable communities in Sonoma managed by MidPen Housing.

What This Role Covers Day to Day

MidPen has operated affordable housing across Northern California since 1970, and their property management teams carry real weight in that mission. As Assistant Community Manager, you report to the Community Manager and share responsibility for keeping two properties running with care and precision.

The compliance side of this work is substantial. Affordable housing operates under layered regulatory requirements, and this role touches all of them: income verifications, lease preparation, waitlist management, and assistance with recertifications, welfare exemptions, MOR reviews, and TCAC compliance. If you've worked in affordable housing before, you already know how carefully these processes need to be tracked. If you're coming from general residential property management, expect a meaningful learning curve on the compliance side, and plan to invest time in it.

Beyond compliance, the role covers rent collection, security deposit processing, petty cash logs, and bank deposit preparation. You'll also schedule vacancies, prepare and monitor turn forms, coordinate maintenance inspections with facilities staff, and make sure work orders move through the system without stalling. Regular property inspections keep you connected to physical conditions on the ground, and you'll maintain resident and property files with appropriate confidentiality throughout.

Resident relations here go beyond collecting rent and issuing notices. MidPen's Resident Services team works alongside property management, which means the people living at these communities have real support structures around them. Your job includes communicating emergency preparedness procedures, coordinating resident meetings, and maintaining working relationships with local law enforcement and emergency agencies.

What MidPen Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED, plus at least one year of residential property management, customer service, or administrative experience (or an equivalent combination)
  • Proficiency in MS Office; experience with RealPage is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple tasks with minimal supervision
  • Genuine alignment with MidPen's mission of providing stable, dignified housing to people who need it

Candidates who stand out in affordable housing roles at this level tend to be people who take compliance seriously without losing warmth in their resident interactions. The recertification process can feel bureaucratic from the outside, but handled well, it's one of the most direct ways a property team keeps residents housed and stable. That dual focus, accuracy and relationship, is what separates strong candidates from those who struggle.

Pay ranges from $21.15 to $23.80 per hour based on experience. MidPen offers a benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, employee education reimbursement, FSA options, an EAP, pet insurance, paid time off, company holidays, and wellness days.

job.title: Leasing and Experience Manager (Hadley)
job.description:
It's a Saturday afternoon at Hadley in Mountain View, and the leasing office is at full tilt. Prospects are touring, a neighbor stopped in with a maintenance concern, and your team needs a quick coaching moment before the next walk. This is the rhythm this role runs on.

The Position

Prometheus Real Estate Group, the largest privately held apartment owner in the Bay Area with over 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle, is hiring a Leasing and Experience Manager for Hadley. The title is specific to Prometheus and carries more weight than a standard assistant manager role. You'll blend leasing production, team supervision, neighbor relations, and daily operations into a single position, and all of it matters equally.

On the leasing side, you'll work alongside the leasing team to close prospects, build out sales and marketing strategies, and track market conditions closely enough to make real pricing recommendations. Mountain View sits in one of the most competitive multifamily markets in the country, where concession strategy and traffic conversion can swing occupancy meaningfully from one quarter to the next. You'll need to know your submarket well.

Operationally, you'll stay close to neighbor profiles, collections, occupancy reporting, and concessions. You'll also carry supervisory responsibility for the leasing staff, which means setting goals, running training, and recognizing performance. Prometheus takes the culture side of this seriously, and milestone celebration is built into the expectation, not just encouraged.

Weekends are a firm part of this schedule. The busiest leasing traffic comes on Saturdays and Sundays, and your regular days off will fall during the week. That's the tradeoff for a role at a property where weekend foot traffic actually matters.

What Prometheus Is Looking For

  • At least two years of leasing experience, with enough reps to guide others through the closing process
  • Genuine comfort in a customer-facing environment, including handling neighbor concerns with professionalism and following through on resolution
  • Supervisory experience or clear readiness to step into a team lead capacity
  • A high school diploma or GED is required; a bachelor's degree is preferred
  • Familiarity with sales and marketing fundamentals as they apply to leasing, not just transactional leasing activity

Compensation runs between $33.75 and $37.00 per hour, with a $200 per-lease incentive, weekend shift premium pay, and a discretionary semi-annual bonus. Additional bonuses apply for referrals, lease-up activity, and training responsibilities. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage (including eligible dependents), 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and tenure-based housing discounts. Prometheus also offers paid volunteer time and recognizes birthdays as a paid holiday.

Prometheus is a Certified B Corporation and a vertically integrated owner-operator, which means this role connects directly to a company that handles acquisitions, development, renovations, and operations under one roof. For someone building a property management career, that kind of platform offers real exposure across the full ownership cycle.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Assistant Community Manager role at Hawthorne Residential Partners sits squarely at the intersection of leasing, finance, and team operations. At the Enclave at Deep River, a Hawthorne-managed community in Greensboro, NC, you'll spend your days moving between tasks that require different mental gears: walking a prospect through a tour in the morning, posting rent payments and reviewing ledgers midday, then de-escalating a resident concern before close of business. The work is varied by design.

On the leasing side, you'll handle inbound leads, conduct tours, guide applicants through the leasing process, and work toward occupancy goals through both new leases and renewals. You'll also take ownership of social media content for the community, which means showcasing resident events and keeping the property's online presence active and genuine.

The financial piece is where many ACMs grow the most. You'll oversee rent collection, payment posting, and check scanning. Weekly delinquency follow-ups and ledger audits are part of the routine. When eviction procedures are necessary, you'll coordinate them alongside the Community Manager. You'll also assist with financial reporting that flows up to regional leadership.

When the Community Manager is out, the property runs through you. That means holding the team accountable, keeping daily operations on track, and making judgment calls without a safety net.

What You Bring

  • Two years of property management experience (preferred), with at least six months in an assistant manager capacity
  • Comfort reading and interpreting financial reports, identifying discrepancies, and making decisions within budget constraints
  • Leasing fundamentals: lead conversion, application processing, renewal conversations, and basic occupancy strategy
  • A valid driver's license
  • A CALP designation is a plus, though not required to apply

Where This Role Takes You

Hawthorne runs a formal Career Path Program, and the ACM position is a well-worn step toward Community Manager. The skills you build here, specifically delinquency management, ledger accuracy, and stepping into leadership under pressure, are exactly what regional directors look for when promoting from within. Candidates who advance quickly tend to be the ones who treat the financial reporting side of the role with the same attention they give leasing. Strong leasing numbers get you noticed; clean books and low delinquency keep you in the conversation for the next step.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off each week to hold the total at 40 hours. Some evenings or weekend availability may come up around resident events. Monthly leasing and renewal commissions, plus quarterly performance bonuses, supplement the hourly base pay.

job.title: Leasing Specialist
job.description:
Workforce housing in the Sun Belt is one of the more active development segments in multifamily right now, and Hillpointe sits near the top of that market. The company builds, owns, and manages its communities entirely in-house, which means a Leasing Specialist here works inside a vertically integrated operation rather than a third-party fee management structure. That distinction matters: the leasing team's performance feeds directly into asset outcomes that the same organization controls from land acquisition through stabilization.

This opening is based in Davenport, a fast-growing corridor in Polk County that sits between Orlando and Lakeland. The area has absorbed significant new multifamily supply over the past few years, driven by affordability pressure pushing renters southwest out of Orange County. Workforce housing in this submarket competes on value and lifestyle, which means a leasing specialist's ability to translate community features into genuine prospect fit carries real weight on occupancy numbers.

What the Role Involves Day to Day

The core of this position is the tour experience. You'll greet prospects, walk them through the community, and tailor what you highlight to what each person actually needs. That requires listening as much as presenting. Between tours, you're coordinating appointment schedules with the leasing experience coordinators, following up with prospects by phone, text, and email, and keeping the tour path, model units, and amenity areas in showing condition. The leasing office is your home base, but a meaningful part of the day happens outdoors across the property in Florida heat, so physical stamina matters.

Weekends are part of the schedule. Leasing activity in this market doesn't follow a Monday-through-Friday pattern, and traffic tends to peak on Saturdays. Candidates who've worked hospitality, retail sales, or apartment leasing before will recognize the rhythm.

What Hillpointe Is Looking For

  • Prior experience in leasing, customer service, hospitality, or sales (preferred, not required)
  • Strong communication skills across a range of personalities and backgrounds
  • Comfort with follow-up outreach across multiple channels
  • Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and occasional holidays
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license
  • Fair housing awareness and commitment to compliance

Candidates who separate themselves in this role tend to be genuinely curious about what prospects are looking for before they start selling. Workforce housing renters often have specific budget constraints and practical priorities. A leasing specialist who asks the right questions early and connects those answers to specific unit or amenity features will close more leases than one who delivers the same scripted tour every time.

For someone building a career in multifamily, this role is a natural foundation. Strong performers in leasing typically move into senior leasing roles, leasing manager positions, or community manager tracks, especially within a company that promotes from within and manages its own assets through the full cycle.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - West Loop
job.description:
It's 10 a.m. on a Tuesday and the punch list already has six items: a resident reported low water pressure in 4B, the lobby trash needs a run, and a vendor is arriving at noon to rod a sewer line you scheduled last week. That's a normal start to this role.

The Work Itself

Reside Living manages roughly 3,000 apartments across Chicago, and this position supports one of their West Loop properties. You'll report directly to the Building Engineer and carry out the hands-on maintenance work that keeps the building operating and residents satisfied. That means completing service requests within agreed SLAs, performing janitorial and grounds work when needed, and assisting with apartment turns between residents. Seasonal responsibilities are real here: Chicago winters require snow removal equipment operation, and you'll be expected to handle that without being told twice.

Preventative maintenance is a core part of the schedule. You'll coordinate HVAC filter replacements, sewer line rodding, and other recurring tasks before they become emergencies. When water infiltration or mold appears, you treat it with urgency and escalate appropriately. You'll also coordinate vendor and contractor access, working alongside project management staff on larger capital work.

The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., with on-call availability for after-hours emergencies. This is a full-time hourly position at $25.00 per hour. A $50 monthly phone stipend is included, since you'll use a mobile app to document completed work orders and inspections.

What This Role Requires and What It Builds

Coming in, you need between two and five years of maintenance experience in a residential, hospitality, or institutional setting. Mechanical aptitude across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and hot water systems is preferred, and EPA certification is required (or must be obtained within 90 days). You'll need to be comfortable with hand and power tools, measuring devices, and mechanical equipment like pumps, compressors, and augers. A valid driver's license is preferred.

Strong candidates distinguish themselves through two things that don't appear on any tool list: communication and follow-through. You're interfacing with residents daily, coordinating with vendors, and keeping the Building Engineer informed. The technicians who advance in this kind of role are the ones who close the loop without being asked.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • EPA certification required or obtained within 90 days of hire
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and mobile work order systems
  • Ability to be on your feet 66 to 100 percent of the time; full physical demands apply
  • OSHA safety compliance required, including appropriate PPE for each task
  • Personal smartphone (iOS or Android) required; $50/month stipend provided

For a technician looking to grow, this role offers a clear path. Working directly under a Building Engineer gives you exposure to building systems at a scale that builds the diagnostic thinking you need to eventually move into an engineer or facilities manager role. Reside Living's expanding Chicago portfolio means internal mobility is a realistic outcome for performers who demonstrate reliability and technical range.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist (Leasing/Customer Service)
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday afternoon, a little overwhelmed after touring four other communities that week. Within ten minutes, they're laughing with you, they understand the pricing, and they've seen the exact unit that fits their situation. That moment is the core of what this role is about.

What the Role Actually Involves

The Customer Experience Specialist at The Richmond Apartments in Salt Lake City is a full-cycle leasing and service position. You'll handle traffic from first contact through move-in, which means answering calls and texts promptly, keeping available units show-ready daily, and walking the tour path and amenities to make sure nothing falls below Cottonwood's standards before a prospect sets foot on the property. You'll know the pricing and availability cold, so you can give honest, useful answers to anyone asking about floor plans or lease terms.

Beyond leasing, the role carries genuine service responsibilities. Residents have questions, packages arrive constantly and need organizing, vendors need coordinating, and community events need planning. You'll also support social media marketing efforts, which means this position touches more of the business than a pure leasing role typically does.

The schedule is full-time and includes evenings and weekends. That's standard for leasing, and it's worth knowing upfront: peak traffic hits on weekends, and the team needs coverage when prospects are actually available to tour.

Who Builds a Career From Here

Cottonwood is explicit about growth potential, and that's worth taking seriously. Leasing consultant roles like this one are where most successful property managers started. The skills that compound here are the ones that matter most at the next level: reading prospective residents accurately, managing delinquency conversations with empathy, coordinating turns and make-readies so units are genuinely move-in ready, and building vendor relationships that hold up under pressure.

Candidates who move up quickly from this type of role tend to share a few traits. They treat every inquiry, phone call, or office visit as a data point on the customer experience, not just a transaction to close. They learn the financial side of the property early, even when it's not required of them. And they treat the tour path and common areas as a direct reflection of their own standards, not just a checklist.

Cottonwood also notes its early adoption of self-guided tours, which signals a company that invests in technology-forward leasing. Experience with that model is increasingly transferable across operators who are expanding it, making this a useful credential beyond this specific role.

  • Full-time schedule with weekend and evening availability required
  • Quarterly bonus structure on top of base pay
  • Health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits starting within 30 days
  • 401k and HSA with company match
  • Three weeks of paid time off in the first year, plus 10.5 paid holidays

If you're early in a property management career and want a role that builds real leasing fluency while leaving room to grow into a management track, The Richmond is a reasonable place to start that progression.

job.title: Limpiador de Plaza Exterior - Alexandria
job.description:
Comstock's ParkX Porter team keeps Alexandria's shared spaces running at a standard that residents and visitors actually notice. This exterior porter role covers the common areas, sidewalks, lobbies, restrooms, and public-facing spaces across an assigned site, and the work shows up directly in how a property feels to everyone who walks through it.

What You'll Actually Do

Daily responsibilities center on keeping common areas clean and presentable from the start of every shift. That means walking assigned zones, collecting debris, pressure washing hardscape surfaces, cleaning windows, and working through scheduled checklists with attention to what's actually done versus what's just initialed. You'll stock and organize the cleaning supply room, track inventory, and handle chemicals according to safety protocols. When events come up, you'll support setup and breakdown on the ground level. You document anything that needs management attention: safety hazards, maintenance issues, equipment damage. At shift end, you complete required paperwork and hand off cleanly to the next shift.

This role also puts you in direct contact with residents, staff, and guests throughout the day. Greeting people professionally, responding to cleaning concerns as they come in, and staying composed in a high-traffic environment are all part of the job. Weekend availability is expected, especially around events or high-activity periods.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Flexibility to work weekends and outside standard hours when needed
  • Ability to lift, push, or pull up to 50 pounds and stay on your feet for extended periods
  • Comfort working in variable conditions: heat, cold, outdoor exposure, cleaning chemicals
  • Strong time management and the ability to prioritize without close supervision
  • Reliable, punctual, and professional in all interactions with residents and staff
  • Genuine attention to detail, not just speed

The Bigger Picture

Porter work sits closer to the operational core of a property than most people assume. Cleanliness scores feed directly into resident satisfaction, and resident satisfaction connects to renewal rates and overall occupancy. A site that consistently looks sharp costs less to lease and holds residents longer. Porters who build strong habits around documentation and communication often move into lead or facilities coordinator roles as they develop familiarity with the property and its systems. Comstock offers annual professional development funds and internal growth paths across a growing portfolio, which makes this a reasonable place to build from if you want more responsibility over time.

Comstock provides medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) matching, life insurance, free parking, EV charging, and parental leave. Benefits may vary by position.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Santa Ana is a competitive submarket, and a 288-unit community doesn't run on autopilot. Property Management Associates is looking for a leasing consultant who can do more than hand out floor plan brochures: someone who closes, follows up, and understands that traffic converts when the experience is right from the first phone call through the lease signing.

PMA has been operating in the greater Los Angeles area for over 30 years, managing both residential and commercial assets across Southern California. They run a full-service shop, which means the infrastructure is there. This is an in-office, on-site role. One weekend day is part of the schedule.

The day-to-day looks like this: you're touring prospects, walking the community, handling applications, and pushing leases through to execution. You're also supporting marketing efforts, which in this market means social media and online platforms matter as much as signage. Yardi Voyager experience is a plus, and if you've already got time logged in Voyager, say so clearly on your resume.

Compensation runs $20 to $23 per hour, with lease commissions on top: $100 per new lease, $50 per renewal. For a 288-unit property with normal turnover, that commission structure adds up. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance with an employer contribution, 401(k) after one year, short- and long-term disability, and a PTO package covering vacation, holidays, and sick time.

What they're looking for

  • At least one year of leasing experience
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Comfort with the full application and lease signing process
  • Familiarity with online and social media marketing for rentals
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; Yardi Voyager a plus
  • Availability to work one weekend day per week

What separates a good leasing consultant from a forgettable one at a property this size is follow-through. Plenty of people can give a decent tour. Fewer actually track their leads, re-engage cold prospects, and close the ones who "need to think about it." If your leasing history shows consistent occupancy contribution rather than just activity, that's the story worth telling here.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Student housing leasing has its own rhythm. Lease-up cycles compress into short windows, renewals require early and consistent outreach, and traffic management demands both speed and warmth. The Leasing Manager role at Redstone Residential in Kent, Ohio sits squarely inside that rhythm, supporting the Community Manager across daily operations while owning the leasing function as its primary focus.

Redstone is one of the larger third-party student housing operators in the country, managing over 38,000 beds across 20 states. Their Kent property is part of a growing conventional portfolio alongside their student housing base, which means this role carries real operational weight at the community level.

What This Role Requires

The Leasing Manager handles the full leasing cycle: prospect calls, property tours, email follow-up, and renewal campaigns. You'll work inside Entrata's leasing workflow, manage online and social marketing touchpoints, and apply basic SEO thinking to the property's digital presence. Resident ledger accuracy falls under this role as well, so comfort with numbers and attention to detail on account balances matter. Customer service and sales skill aren't incidental here. They're the core of the job.

  • Strong customer service and sales instincts, especially under volume
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Gmail, Google Drive, and Dropbox
  • High school diploma or GED required; some college experience is preferred
  • Ability to stay organized and composed during high-traffic leasing periods

What This Role Builds

Leasing Manager is one of the clearest development paths in property management. The skills you'll sharpen here, running leasing strategy, motivating a team around occupancy goals, keeping delinquency in check, and reading what's working in your marketing mix, translate directly into Community Manager readiness. You'll also get exposure to budget performance and staff administration, which are disciplines most pure leasing consultant roles don't touch.

Working inside a large third-party management platform like Redstone's gives you something smaller operators can't: standardized systems, professional development programming, and a continued education benefit that rewards people who want to grow. The 401K match (up to 6%), paid parental leave, and 15 days of PTO round out a compensation structure that reflects a company building for retention, not just filling seats.

The position pays $18.00 per hour and is classified full-time, non-exempt. If you have a feel for leasing, enjoy working with people, and want to develop the operational skills that move careers forward in property management, this is a role worth taking seriously.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Multi site
job.description:
Multi-site maintenance supervision is one of the harder gigs in residential property management. You're not anchored to one address, one manager, or one team. Sunrise Management is staffing this role across three San Diego-area communities: Kelvin in Lemon Grove, Textur in La Mesa, and Dezi in San Diego proper. That geographic spread is the defining feature of this position.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this role is keeping three communities physically sound, presentable, and compliant. Turns are a significant piece of that. Sunrise holds a 3-to-5 day make-ready standard, which means you'll need to coordinate painting, carpet cleaning, appliance checks, and general punch list items without the luxury of being on-site full time. When you're at Kelvin, Textur still needs coverage. That tension is real, and managing it well is what separates a strong multi-site supervisor from someone who just drives between properties putting out fires.

Beyond turns, the day-to-day includes preventive maintenance across all three sites, 24-hour service request completion targets, pool and spa upkeep, life-safety compliance (fire systems, lighting, signage), HVAC and water heater monitoring, and grounds inspection. You'll also carry on-call emergency responsibility. The role requires a valid driver's license because you'll genuinely need it, not as a formality.

On the people side, you'll supervise maintenance staff at the individual sites, participate in hiring and performance reviews alongside property managers, and run monthly safety meetings. MSDS recordkeeping, PPE compliance, and adherence to Sunrise's Injury and Illness Prevention and Hazardous Materials policies are part of the job, not afterthoughts. Fair Housing knowledge is expected.

What Sunrise Is Looking For

  • At least one year of property maintenance experience (more is better here)
  • Prior supervisory experience, required
  • Hands-on competency across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, pool systems, and carpentry
  • Valid driver's license with reliable transportation between sites
  • Comfort with expense control and purchase approval processes
  • Detail-oriented and proactive, especially around life-safety and preventive maintenance documentation

A Note on What Makes Someone Good at This

Candidates who thrive in multi-site maintenance roles tend to be strong self-schedulers. When no single manager is watching your full day, your ability to prioritize across three work orders lists, three sets of resident concerns, and three preventive maintenance logs is what keeps everything from slipping. The pay range here is $27 to $30 per hour depending on experience. That ceiling reflects the complexity of the role. If you've held a single-site lead position and you're ready to take on broader scope, this is a reasonable next step with tangible skills that transfer directly to maintenance director or regional maintenance coordinator roles over time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II (Downing Central)
job.description:
Multifamily maintenance at scale requires technicians who can shift gears fast. This role covers 449 apartments across 11 buildings, which means the work order queue moves constantly and no two days look the same. RedPeak has operated in the Denver market for over two decades, and this position sits at a mid-senior level on the maintenance team, directly supporting the Service Supervisor with scheduling, vendor oversight, and quality control alongside hands-on repair work.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The bulk of your day runs through service requests: electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliance repair, drywall, and painting. You'll also handle preventative maintenance and grounds inspections, flagging and addressing deficiencies before they become resident complaints. When outside contractors are on site, you're the one coordinating their work and checking quality. On-call rotation is part of the job, so emergency response comes with the territory.

Security systems fall under this role too. That includes installing and monitoring cameras, managing lock and key access, and tracking vendor key checkouts. You'll keep maintenance records current in Yardi, which is the platform RedPeak uses for work orders and inventory.

The multi-site scope matters here. Managing high request volumes across 11 buildings requires strong time management and the ability to triage effectively. Technicians who thrive in this environment tend to be the ones who can diagnose accurately on the first visit and solve for the long-term fix rather than the quick patch.

Qualifications and Certifications

  • 1 to 2 years of multifamily maintenance, construction, or equivalent hands-on experience
  • Intermediate working knowledge of electrical, HVAC, plumbing, and mechanical systems
  • Familiarity with Yardi or comparable work order platforms
  • EPA 608 and CPO certifications preferred (RedPeak covers the cost if you need to earn them)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation required
  • Technical degree or equivalent training is a plus, not a hard requirement

Pay runs $24 to $27 per hour with bonus potential. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., with on-call availability as needed. Benefits include full medical, dental, and vision, a 30% rent discount, 401(k) with immediate vesting, 16 PTO days, 13 paid holidays, and a student debt repayment program. The office is at 1044 N. Downing St. in Denver's Capitol Hill neighborhood.

One thing worth noting for candidates considering the step from Tech I to Tech II: this level carries real supervisory exposure. Assisting with scheduling and vendor management gives you line-of-sight into how a property runs operationally, which is the groundwork for a Service Supervisor or Maintenance Director path. If that trajectory interests you, this role builds the right foundation.

job.title: Maintenance Tech
job.description:
Maintenance work at a student housing or build-to-rent community is a different animal than a conventional apartment. Turnover is aggressive, resident expectations run high, and the technician on the ground sets the standard for how well the physical asset performs. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a Maintenance Technician for their Indianapolis community, and the role sits at the center of daily operations.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your days will involve completing service requests across mechanical, plumbing, electrical, and appliance systems. You'll follow a preventative maintenance schedule, keep chemical logs for the pool, and help coordinate turns when units flip between residents. Curb appeal, breezeway cleanliness, and the condition of common areas all fall within your scope. You'll also carry a share of the on-call rotation, which means after-hours calls are part of the job. That's worth stating plainly: this role requires flexibility with scheduling, including weekends and holidays.

Inventory management is part of the technician's responsibility here too. Working alongside the Maintenance Supervisor, you'll help track tools, parts, and supplies, and you'll be expected to flag shortages before they create delays. Budget awareness matters, not just wrench-turning.

What You Bring vs. What You'll Build

This role requires at least one year of maintenance experience, ideally in the apartment industry. You'll need the ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances without supervision on routine calls. EPA Type I and II certification is preferred, and you'll need to supply your own hand tools. Reliable transportation and the ability to live within 30 miles of the property are non-negotiable given the on-call structure.

What the role builds is different. PeakMade offers HVAC and CPO certification support, a facilities leadership program, and ongoing technical training. For a technician who's solid on the fundamentals but wants a clear path toward a Maintenance Supervisor or Facilities Manager role, this structure gives you a visible track. The monthly renewal bonuses also reward quality work in a measurable way, which keeps skill-building tied directly to compensation.

Who Performs Well Here

  • Technicians who communicate proactively with residents and supervisors, not just complete the ticket and move on
  • People who treat make-ready turns with the same care as a standard service call
  • Anyone who's comfortable working outdoors in both summer heat and winter cold without cutting corners on safety
  • Candidates who understand that in student housing, occupancy and resident satisfaction are directly tied to how fast and how well maintenance responds

PeakMade is an Atlanta-based company with a portfolio spanning student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities. Their culture leans collaborative and team-driven, and the Indianapolis position reflects that. If you've been doing solid maintenance work and want a company that invests in certifications and career structure, this is a role worth a close look.

job.title: Leasing Consultant Affordable Apartment Community
job.description:
Pierce Park Apartments in Pacoima is a 430-unit affordable community operating under both tax credit and project-based Section 8 programs. That combination shapes everything about this Leasing Consultant role. Applicants, income certifications, agency relationships, and resident interactions all carry a layer of compliance and care that you won't find at a conventional market-rate lease-up.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Investment Property Group, a Park City-based firm with 150 properties across 13 states, is looking for a Leasing Consultant to handle the full leasing cycle at this community. Day to day, that means conducting property tours, processing applications, managing phone and email inquiries, and working through move-in and move-out procedures in line with company policy. You'll also track competitor activity and local market conditions to help the team stay sharp on occupancy strategy.

The resident base here includes households navigating income qualifications and housing assistance programs, so how you communicate matters as much as how well you close. You'll coordinate closely with the property manager and maintenance team to keep things running, and you'll help spot inefficiencies and suggest better ways to operate the community.

What This Role Requires

  • At least one year of leasing experience at a multifamily community of 100 or more units (preferred)
  • Prior exposure to LIHTC, tax credit, or project-based Section 8 properties (a real advantage here)
  • Bilingual Spanish and English skills (preferred given the Pacoima resident demographic)
  • Strong conflict resolution and customer service skills suited to an affordable housing environment
  • Solid written and verbal communication for interactions with residents, vendors, and housing agencies
  • Marketing and sales ability to support occupancy goals

Where This Role Can Take You

Leasing Consultants who develop real fluency in affordable housing compliance, particularly around LIHTC and Section 8 administration, tend to move into Assistant Manager or Compliance Coordinator roles faster than their conventional-property peers. Those skills are in short supply and carry weight across the industry. IPG's footprint across 13 states also means internal mobility is a realistic outcome for strong performers.

Compensation runs $21.00 to $25.00 per hour depending on experience and qualifications, with a Monday through Friday schedule. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, an HSA, an employee assistance program, a 401(k) with company match, and four weeks of accrued PTO.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - 50% Rent Discount
job.description:
Vaughan Place sits just off Wisconsin Avenue in the Cathedral Heights neighborhood, a 380-plus-unit luxury community within easy reach of Georgetown, Embassy Row, and Glover Archbold Park. AIR Communities operates it as part of a portfolio of Class A assets in major markets, and they run a tight ship on the maintenance side. This is a full-time technician role, not a light-duty position. You'll be doing turns, handling resident service requests, troubleshooting HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances, and occasionally guiding less experienced techs on the team.

The pay range runs $24 to $27 an hour depending on your actual skill set, with the possibility of up to $250 per month in customer satisfaction bonuses tied to resident feedback. The 50% rent discount applies at any AIR community, so you can live on-site and eliminate your commute entirely, or pick a different AIR property nearby. That's a real benefit in a market like DC, where rent levels are what they are.

AIR has invested in technology to help technicians prioritize work orders and move through the day more efficiently. Shops are stocked and organized. They've also built out a maintenance development program called Ascend, which is designed around individual career paths rather than a generic training checklist. For a technician who wants a clear line toward a lead or maintenance supervisor role, that structure matters.

What They're Looking For

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment
  • Proficiency in at least two trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, or carpentry
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts (roughly one week per month)
  • A reliable way to get to the property for after-hours emergency calls
  • Physical capability to handle heavy equipment and machinery

On-call is the part of this job that tends to separate people who last from people who don't. One week a month of after-hours availability is the stated expectation, and at a luxury community with residents who expect quick responses, that's a real commitment. If you've worked in multifamily before, you already know this. If you're coming from commercial facilities, the pace of resident-facing service requests is a different rhythm than scheduled PMs.

The technicians who perform well in roles like this one tend to be the people who genuinely close out a work order correctly the first time, document it properly, and communicate with the resident before and after. At a Class A property, the service standard is high and residents notice when it slips. The customer satisfaction bonus structure reflects exactly that expectation.

Benefits include a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, company-paid short and long-term disability, 14 paid holidays, paid parental leave up to 16 weeks, and tuition reimbursement up to 100% for job-related certifications and licenses. That last piece is worth noting if you're working toward an HVAC certification or EPA 608 and haven't finished it yet.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A Role Built on Relationship Skills and Market Instincts

Student housing runs on a different rhythm than conventional multifamily. Lease-up cycles compress into a few intense months, traffic spikes around campus visit weekends, and your prospects are often making their first major housing decision without much experience. The Leasing Consultant role at The Reserve at Clemson puts you at the center of that dynamic, and the skills it develops compound quickly across a property management career.

The core of this position is sales, but the kind of sales that requires genuine relationship-building rather than a pitch script. You'll tour prospects through the community, field objections, and report back to management on what's actually stopping people from signing. That feedback loop matters. Consultants who can articulate why a prospect walked, and what messaging might have changed the outcome, develop market instincts that carry into leasing manager and assistant manager roles faster than those who just track traffic numbers.

Beyond the leasing floor, you'll handle property administration work: package management, office organization, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout coverage. These aren't filler tasks. Understanding how a property runs operationally, from the front office through to maintenance follow-up, gives you a much clearer picture of NOI and resident satisfaction than leasing alone ever would.

What This Role Demands Week to Week

Student housing has defined pressure points, and availability during those periods is a real requirement here. Turn periods, when an entire community flips occupancy in a matter of days between academic terms, are intense and all-hands. Summer is peak leasing season. Holidays require coverage. If your schedule can flex to meet those demands, you'll get exposure to operational complexity that most entry-level roles never offer.

Marketing is also a meaningful part of this position. You'll contribute to social media, help plan and execute resident engagement events, and identify local outreach opportunities near the Clemson campus. Student housing communities compete hard for the same pool of prospects each year, and the consultants who understand both the digital and in-person sides of that effort tend to move up.

What Strong Candidates Bring to This Role

  • A customer-first mindset that stays consistent even on high-volume days
  • Strong verbal communication across a genuinely diverse resident and prospect population
  • Self-discipline and reliability, especially for on-call and after-hours responsibilities
  • Comfort with a schedule that shifts based on leasing season and campus calendar
  • Some familiarity with social media platforms used for community engagement

Scion operates specifically in the student housing segment, which means the institutional knowledge you'd build here is specialized and transferable to any university-adjacent market. For someone early in a property management career, that specialization is an asset worth developing.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Hawthorne Residential Partners operates a portfolio of apartment communities where the maintenance supervisor carries real operational weight. At a property like Hawthorne at the Glen in Concord, NC, the physical condition of the asset ties directly to occupancy, resident satisfaction scores, and renewal rates. This role owns that connection.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day runs on a blend of scheduled work and reactive triage. The preventative maintenance calendar keeps HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems running before they fail. Work orders come in, get triaged, and get assigned. Unit turns are tracked against move-in dates, and you personally inspect each vacant unit before it's handed off to leasing. A punch list that gets missed at move-in becomes a service request on day three and a detractor on a renewal survey six months later. You'll keep that from happening.

You'll also manage vendor partners, pull bids on capital improvement projects, and keep the grounds and common areas in condition that supports curb appeal and resident confidence. On-call rotation is part of the schedule. After-hours emergencies happen, and this team handles them.

What Qualifies You

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least three years in apartment maintenance or a skilled trade such as HVAC, plumbing, or electrical
  • Prior experience in a supervisory or lead technician capacity, strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license and current EPA certification
  • CPO certification highly preferred (required in some states)

The technical floor matters, but so does the supervisory piece. You're scheduling a team, mentoring techs, and holding vendors accountable to deadlines. Someone who can swing a wrench but struggles to delegate will hit a ceiling here fast. The candidates who perform well in this role tend to be organized enough to run a tight make-ready schedule while staying available for the urgent stuff that interrupts it.

Compensation and Growth

Hawthorne structures maintenance supervisor pay with multiple bonus layers on top of the hourly rate: monthly renewal bonuses, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses. That last one is worth noting. When resident satisfaction scores move, this role shares in the upside. It's a direct tie between maintenance quality and take-home pay.

Hawthorne also runs a formal Career Path Program with dedicated learning and development support, plus an education reimbursement program aimed at expanding technical skills. For a maintenance professional who wants to move toward a regional or facilities director track, that infrastructure matters. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and company-paid life insurance.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Skills at the Center of This Role

Maintenance work at a residential property draws on a surprisingly wide skill set, and this position at Fairstead puts most of them to use. Electrical diagnosis, HVAC systems, preventative maintenance planning, make-ready prep for turns, and safety compliance all show up regularly. If you've spent time as a service technician and found yourself handling whatever came through the door, this role will feel familiar in the best way. The breadth is the point.

Fairstead manages more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states as an integrated owner and operator, which means the people maintaining their properties work within a system that connects development, construction, and property management under one roof. That structure matters for a technician because decisions move faster and resources tend to be more accessible than in third-party management environments.

What You'll Be Building Day to Day

The core of the role covers routine inspections of buildings and equipment, identifying what needs repair before it becomes an emergency. You'll carry out preventative maintenance on schedule, respond to work orders, and handle turns: cleaning and prepping vacated units so they're ready for incoming residents. Electrical checks, safety system testing, and maintaining inventory of tools and supplies round out the regular work. You'll also participate in an on-call rotation, which means some after-hours emergency response is part of the job. That's worth knowing upfront.

Preferred credentials include HVAC certification or a CMRP designation, and the physical demands are real: standing for extended periods and lifting up to 70 pounds unassisted. Attention to detail and solid communication skills matter too, especially when coordinating with property management staff or documenting completed work.

Where This Role Tends to Lead

For technicians thinking about trajectory, a role like this one builds a skill profile that translates directly into lead maintenance or maintenance supervisor positions. The combination of hands-on systems knowledge, preventative maintenance discipline, and experience working within a professionally managed affordable housing portfolio carries weight. Operators at Fairstead's scale run structured systems, so technicians who learn to work within those systems, and contribute to improving them, tend to move up faster than those in smaller, less formalized environments.

What separates strong candidates here is the blend of technical range and reliability. Electrical competence combined with HVAC knowledge is a meaningful differentiator in affordable housing maintenance. Operators at this scale can't afford single-skill technicians. The more systems you can confidently touch, the more valuable you become to the team and the more options you create for yourself down the road.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Multi-site
job.city: Elan - Poway Hills ; Elan - Scripps Terrace
job.description:
Multi-site maintenance supervision is one of the most skill-intensive roles in residential property management, and it's genuinely undervalued as a career-building position. You're not just fixing things. You're running a small operations department across multiple communities, managing people, controlling costs, and keeping physical assets performing at a level that directly affects NOI and resident retention. Sunrise Management is hiring for exactly that kind of role, covering two San Diego-area communities: Elan Scripps Terrace in San Diego and Elan Poway Hills in Poway.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a working supervisor position, meaning you'll be hands-on with appliance repair, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, pool/spa maintenance, and carpentry while also directing the maintenance team's daily priorities. Make-readies are a core responsibility. The expectation is that vacated units are turned and market-ready within three to five days, which means coordinating paint, carpet cleaning, punch list items, and general repairs without letting the schedule slip. That turnaround window is tight by industry standards and requires both personal productivity and effective delegation.

On the preventive side, you'll own the monthly PM program across lighting, fire safety, pool/spa systems, and life-safety equipment, and you'll keep the maintenance logs current. Knowing the location of every shutoff, cleanout, and mechanical system across both properties isn't optional. It's the baseline for responding fast when something goes wrong after hours, which it will.

Expense control is part of the job description, not an afterthought. You'll need manager approval for expenditures, which means you're expected to plan ahead, communicate clearly, and make a case for what you need. Capex recommendations, contract input, and bid awareness are also in scope at this level.

The supervisory load includes hiring involvement, training, performance feedback, and monthly safety meetings with your team. Timekeeping for direct reports is also your responsibility.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least two years of hands-on property maintenance experience, with prior supervisory time in a residential setting
  • Practical working knowledge across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and pool systems (CPO certification is a meaningful differentiator here)
  • A valid driver's license in good standing. Regular travel between the two sites is built into the schedule
  • Comfort with Fair Housing standards and hazardous materials documentation, including MSDS recordkeeping
  • Organized communication habits. Site management needs to hear about deficiencies proactively, not reactively

The pay range is $27 to $33 per hour depending on experience. On-call emergency response is part of the role, which is standard at this level but worth factoring into your decision.

From a career standpoint, multi-site maintenance supervisors who develop strong cost-control instincts and team management skills tend to move into Maintenance Director or Regional Maintenance roles, or transition into property operations with a credible technical foundation that most managers lack. The combination of field competency and supervisory experience you build here is genuinely portable across Class A, B, and C assets, and increasingly valuable as properties invest more in preventive programs to manage deferred capex.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Griffis Residential runs a luxury apartment portfolio with communities across Colorado and beyond, and their Colorado Springs presence reflects that same positioning. The Springs has seen steady multifamily growth over the past several years, with Class A communities competing on amenity quality and resident experience as much as on rent. That context matters for this role: a maintenance technician here isn't just fixing things, they're actively protecting the product that justifies premium rents.

Working under the Service Manager, you'll handle the full range of unit and common-area maintenance: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, carpentry, and make-ready work that gets units turned and leased. Resident service requests come with a 30-minute response expectation, which is a real standard to meet consistently. You'll also carry responsibilities around pool and spa chemical logs, preventative maintenance schedules, community inspections, litter pickup, and seasonal snow and ice removal. Colorado Springs winters are real, and that last item is more than a formality from October through March.

A CPO license and EPA certification are preferred at hire and required within your first six months. If you don't have them yet, build that into your timeline. HVAC knowledge is genuinely central to this work, not a secondary skill.

What separates a strong technician in a luxury community from an average one usually comes down to resident communication. The technical repair is table stakes. Showing up on time, explaining what you did, and leaving the unit in better shape than you found it is what drives the online reputation scores that feed directly into the community's bonus structure.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year of experience in multifamily, hospitality, or a related trade environment
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and appliances
  • CPO and EPA certification preferred; required within six months of hire
  • Ability to lift up to 75 pounds and work in outdoor conditions year-round
  • Basic computer skills for work order and inventory management
  • Strong communication skills; bilingual Spanish is a plus

Compensation runs between $25.00 and $27.50 per hour. Benefits include a 50% rental discount, quarterly and occupancy-based bonuses, 11 paid holidays, a minimum of three weeks PTO accruing from day one, 401(k) with up to 4% company match, full medical, dental, and vision, tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 annually, and paid parental leave. The bonus structure tied to online reputation and occupancy gives this role a direct financial connection to how well the community performs.

job.title: Experienced Field Maintenance Technician (3+ Years Required)
job.description:
What This Role Actually Involves

Field maintenance at a tech-enabled property services company operates differently than a traditional apartment maintenance role. Instead of being tied to a single asset or a handful of buildings, you're working across a portfolio, managing your own work orders through a platform that tracks scope, completion, and quality at scale. Lessen runs more than 3.5 million work orders annually across over one million properties, so the infrastructure around you is substantial. Your job is to show up as a skilled technician who can own the work from diagnosis to close-out without needing a supervisor to walk you through it.

Skills Required and Skills Built

Three years of verifiable, hands-on experience in property maintenance or a related trade is the floor here, not a soft suggestion. You need to arrive with working knowledge of general repairs, the ability to manage budgets tied to individual work orders, and the judgment to prioritize quality over volume. Lessen's model means your output directly reflects on a client relationship, so the ability to troubleshoot independently and communicate clearly with property owners and managers is part of the job, not a bonus trait.

What the role builds is equally worth naming. Working inside a technology platform that surfaces data on work order history, property condition, and vendor performance gives you exposure to how maintenance operations look at scale. Technicians who pay attention to that layer tend to develop a stronger instinct for cost management and scoping, skills that transfer directly into lead technician and field maintenance manager roles, which Lessen explicitly identifies as a growth path from this position.

Key qualifications and terms:

  • Minimum 3 years of hands-on property maintenance or trade experience, verifiable
  • Comfortable owning work orders independently, including budget accountability
  • Solution-oriented approach to repairs and property condition issues
  • Weekday schedule, no on-call rotation
  • Company fleet vehicle and fuel card provided
  • Tool and equipment allowance of $50 per month, plus $50 cell phone allowance
  • OSHA training provided
  • $1,500 sign-on bonus and quarterly discretionary bonus eligibility up to 5% of quarterly earnings
  • Pay range starting at $24 to $27 per hour, based on qualifications and experience

Where Strong Candidates Stand Out

The technicians who thrive in a portfolio model like this one tend to have strong time management habits and a clean track record on work order completion. Because you're not anchored to one property, you need to carry context about multiple sites and switch gears efficiently. The no on-call structure is a real quality-of-life benefit, but it also means the weekday hours need to count. If you've worked in third-party or fee management settings before, or handled maintenance across scattered single-family or small multifamily assets, that background translates well here. Atlanta's rental market continues to expand, and Lessen's national growth trajectory means this market will likely see increasing workload and opportunity for technicians who perform consistently.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Makowsky Ringel Greenberg has been a fixture in Memphis property management for decades, and this technician role sits inside that established operation. You'd be working across an apartment community with a full ticket load covering HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, lock work, and make-ready prep. The Monday through Friday schedule is the baseline, but rotating on-call is part of the deal, and you should go in with that expectation set clearly.

The HVAC certification requirement signals where this role puts its weight. Universal EPA 608 is preferred, and if you hold that, you already know how to handle the full range of refrigerant work that comes with managing residential units. The rest of the scope, plumbing, electrical, lock rekeying, preventive maintenance, rounds out what a well-rounded technician handles at a mid-size apartment community. You'll also document your work daily, which keeps the property's maintenance history clean and matters more than most techs initially expect when deferred items start compounding.

From a career standpoint, this kind of role builds the foundation for a lead technician or service manager position. Two or more years in apartment maintenance teaches you how to triage competing priorities, manage your time across a property without someone standing over your shoulder, and handle resident-facing situations with professionalism. Those skills translate directly into supervisory roles where you're coordinating a team and owning the maintenance budget rather than just executing on it. MRG's structure, with quarterly and annual performance bonuses on top of a sign-on, suggests they're invested in retaining people who perform, which is worth factoring into how you think about the role's longer-term value.

What separates strong candidates here is the combination of genuine HVAC competency and the discipline to keep documentation current under a full work order load. Technicians who treat the paperwork as an afterthought create headaches for the whole operation. If you come in with your own tools, a reliable vehicle, a valid license, and the habit of closing tickets cleanly, you'll stand out.

What you'll need to qualify

  • HVAC certification required; Universal EPA 608 preferred
  • Two or more years of apartment maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, and general building systems
  • Physical ability to perform the assigned tasks
  • Familiarity with applicable building codes and safety standards, including OSHA
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Your own tools and a reliable vehicle for maintenance work
  • Valid driver's license and current auto insurance
  • Ability to pass a background check, credit check, and drug screening

The compensation package includes a $1,000 sign-on bonus, quarterly and annual performance bonuses, a fuel allowance, and a full benefits suite covering medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance, along with a 401(k) and profit-sharing plan.

job.title: Apartment Leasing Sales Consultant - Lakeview at Gateway
job.description:
Leasing velocity is the lifeblood of any stabilized apartment community. A single strong leasing consultant can move occupancy meaningfully in a single month, and that's exactly the kind of production AIR Communities is building toward at Lakeview at Gateway in Denver.

AIR Communities owns and operates apartment communities across major U.S. markets. This onsite role at their Denver property puts you at the front of the sales funnel: generating traffic, converting prospects into signed leases, and keeping current residents engaged enough to renew. The comp structure reflects how seriously AIR takes leasing performance. Base pay runs $19.50 to $20.00 per hour, and commission tiers stack in multiple directions.
