You earn more per lease when you close on a higher-rent unit, when you exceed your monthly goal, and when you lock in longer lease terms (18 months or more). That last point matters operationally: longer lease terms reduce turn frequency and stabilize the rent roll, so AIR has a real incentive to reward consultants who push them.

What the Role Actually Involves

You'll follow AIR's structured sales process, which means prompt follow-up with active prospects, scheduled tours, and consistent pipeline discipline. This isn't a passive information-desk role. You're expected to meet or exceed monthly leasing goals, contribute to community marketing, and support leasing across the broader AIR portfolio when coverage is needed. Weekend availability is required, and hours shift with the season. Fair Housing compliance is non-negotiable.

The 25% rent discount at any AIR community is a genuine benefit worth noting. Living onsite eliminates commute time entirely, which has real value for someone working a schedule that includes weekends and peak-season surges.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least one year of sales or customer service experience with measurable goal attainment (property management, hospitality, and retail backgrounds all translate well)
  • Comfort following a repeatable sales process rather than freelancing every interaction
  • Flexibility across hours and properties as business needs shift
  • Reliable transportation and strong English communication skills

The consultants who outperform in this type of role tend to obsess over their own conversion metrics. They know their traffic-to-tour ratio, their tour-to-application close rate, and exactly how far they are from the next commission tier at any point in the month. If you've worked roles where you tracked those numbers closely and took them personally, you'll fit the culture AIR is describing here.

AIR also offers a seasonal extended break after peak leasing season ends, with benefits and the rent discount continuing through the unpaid period. It's an unusual structure in residential property management, and for the right person it's a meaningful lifestyle benefit.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance options, HSA and FSA plans, short and long-term disability covered by the company, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, tuition assistance, and 15 paid hours annually for community service.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits between hands-on trades work and team leadership, and you'll feel that tension every day. You're not managing from a distance. You're diagnosing HVAC problems, pulling service tickets, walking the make-ready units, and checking punch lists alongside your team. When something breaks at 11pm, you're in the on-call rotation. That's the job, and it's worth saying plainly before you apply.

Day to day, you'll handle maintenance requests across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair while keeping the turn process moving so vacant units hit leasing-ready status on time. Preventative maintenance programs are yours to execute consistently, not just when things slow down. You'll also stay on top of grounds, common areas, and building systems, making sure everything from lighting to mechanical rooms reflects the standard the property is held to. Code compliance and safety practices aren't paperwork exercises here. They're part of how the operation runs.

The leadership piece matters. You'll set the tone for how your team approaches the work. If you cut corners on a punch list, they will too. Bozzuto's properties attract residents with high expectations, and the maintenance team is a direct factor in retention.

What You Bring

  • At least 5 years working in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Solid working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair, plus basic carpentry, drywall, and painting
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems including central plant, split systems, boilers, or chillers is a plus
  • Supervisory experience or a demonstrated ability to lead and motivate a small team
  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards, risk management practices, and MSDS requirements
  • Comfort with technology platforms, work order systems, and basic Microsoft Office tools
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb ladders, and work in outdoor conditions year-round
  • Availability for weekend coverage and emergency on-call rotation

Context Worth Knowing

The Edgewater/Wynwood corridor in Miami has seen significant Class A development over the past several years, and resident expectations in that market reflect it. Residents in these communities expect fast response times and a well-kept property. Deferred maintenance gets noticed quickly, and so does a maintenance team that actually follows through. If your background is in hospitality facilities or high-end residential, that attention to presentation will translate well here.

The salary range for this position is $63,000 to $67,000, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. For someone who wants to grow into a Maintenance Manager role, this position builds exactly the combination of technical depth and supervisory experience that makes that move possible.

job.title: Cortland at the Village Maintenance Hiring Event - 8/14/2026
job.description:
It's 8:47 a.m. on a Monday and there's already a work order for a down HVAC unit, a leak under a kitchen sink, and a resident locked out of her unit. That's maintenance in multifamily. Cortland knows it, and they're looking for people who can handle that before lunch without losing their composure.

Cortland is hosting a facilities open house at Cortland at the Village in Smyrna, GA on Friday, August 14th from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. The address is 2085 Lake Park Dr SE, Smyrna, GA 30080. They're hiring across three levels of maintenance, and they'll be meeting candidates in person that day.

Who They're Hiring

Three roles are on the table, each with distinct experience expectations:

  • Maintenance Technician: Two to five years of hands-on experience required. An active EPA certification is required for this level.
  • Service Technician: At least one year of experience. EPA certification is not required at this level, which makes this a reasonable entry point for candidates still building credentials.
  • Service Manager: Three to five years of experience, plus both an active EPA and an active CPO. This is the senior track, so bring the paperwork.

When you show up, bring an updated resume, your driver's license, and copies of any relevant certifications. If your EPA or CPO is sitting in a filing cabinet somewhere, dig it out the night before.

About Cortland

Founded in 2005 and headquartered in Atlanta, Cortland is a vertically integrated owner-operator ranked among the top 10 multifamily firms in the country. They handle design, construction, and operations in-house, which means their maintenance teams work within a more coordinated structure than you'd find at a typical third-party management shop. Work orders, capital projects, and make-ready standards tend to be more systematized at that scale, which is a plus if you like clarity and a challenge if you prefer doing things your own way.

For maintenance professionals in the Atlanta metro, Cortland's portfolio depth matters. Getting in at a property like Cortland at the Village can open doors to other assets in the portfolio, and the company's size means there's a real path upward for Service Technicians who earn their EPA and develop their diagnostic skills. We've seen plenty of techs move from wrench-turning to supervising a team within a few years at operators this size. The infrastructure to grow is there if you use it.

Cortland is an equal opportunity employer and participates in E-Verify. The company maintains a drug-free workplace policy.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
It's 9 a.m. on the first of the month, and the CAM reconciliation package is due to a client by noon. Three vendor invoices hit the AP queue overnight, a tenant submitted a maintenance escalation, and the Property Manager needs the monthly report drafted before a 10 o'clock ownership call. That's a normal Tuesday in this role.

The Work

Lincoln Property Company is hiring an Assistant Property Manager to support day-to-day operations across a commercial portfolio in Burlington, MA. The portfolio spans office, industrial, and retail assets, so exposure here is broad. You'll work directly alongside the Property Manager on financial reporting, lease administration, and tenant relations, with enough ownership over specific workstreams to build real operational depth.

On the financial side, you'll help prepare monthly reports and budget packages for institutional clients, manage operating expense reconciliation data (CAM/OpX), and review vendor invoices for accuracy and compliance with the management agreement and authorization limits. These aren't rubber-stamp tasks. Clients expect clean numbers delivered on time, and you'll be accountable for the inputs that make that happen.

Lease administration runs through this role as well: setting up new leases in applicable systems, processing changes, and coordinating tenant move-ins and move-outs, including walk-throughs with tenants and tenant improvement teams. You'll also support procurement and vendor bidding activities, help maintain emergency response plans, and provide direction to any direct reports on your team.

What Lincoln Is Looking For

  • A bachelor's degree (BA/BS) preferred, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience
  • 1 to 2 years of experience in commercial property management or a closely related field
  • Intermediate to advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel
  • Familiarity with AP and CMMS platforms is a plus
  • Ability to calculate percentages, discounts, and basic financial figures with accuracy
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work through tenant and vendor issues while keeping relationships intact
  • Solid organizational habits and a track record of hitting deadlines under real workload pressure

This position is fully in-office in Burlington. No remote or hybrid option is available. Monthly property inspections and travel to assigned sites are part of the schedule.

Candidates who tend to separate themselves in this type of role are the ones who can hold the financial detail and the people side simultaneously. CAM reconciliation accuracy matters, but so does how you handle a frustrated tenant at 8:45 a.m. before the inbox is even clear. Lincoln operates a 720-million-square-foot portfolio nationally, which means the systems, reporting standards, and client expectations here are institutional-grade. If you're early in your commercial PM career and want exposure to that level of operation, this role delivers it.

job.title: Business Manager, Property Operations
job.description:
What This Role Does

Asset Living is a third-party management firm with a national portfolio spanning multifamily, affordable housing, build-to-rent, student housing, and single-family rentals. This Business Manager position sits between regional leadership and site teams, keeping operations tight across a portfolio rather than running a single property. The work is operational and financial in equal measure.

Day to day, you're tracking delinquency, overseeing collections, and making sure move-out charges and timelines hold up under jurisdictional rules. You're monitoring work order completion rates and maintenance follow-through. You're reviewing capex spend against approved budgets and keeping vendor invoices moving through AP without bottlenecks. When legal matters come up, including evictions and lease enforcement, you coordinate with attorneys and keep the process on track.

Occupancy management is also in scope. That means supporting renewal workflows, handling resident escalations, and administering tenant-based voucher programs where applicable. You'll work alongside Regional Portfolio Managers, Community Managers, and leasing staff to hit portfolio KPIs, and you'll analyze operational and financial data to flag trends before they become problems.

What the Role Requires

  • At least three years in multifamily property management, operations, or asset management
  • Hands-on experience with Yardi, RealPage, MRI, or a comparable platform
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office and Google Workspace
  • Solid grasp of leasing operations, financial controls, and regulatory compliance
  • Strong written and verbal communication; bilingual Spanish/English preferred
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree in Business, Real Estate, or a related field preferred

The posting lists Portland and Seattle as locations, but candidates must reside in Reno, Nevada. Confirm that detail before applying. The Washington pay range is listed at $80,000 to $85,000.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Candidates who do well in roles like this tend to have experience managing compliance across multiple jurisdictions, not just one market. Affordable housing background helps here too, particularly if you've touched tenant-based voucher administration. The volume of financial detail in this role, delinquency tracking, capex reporting, PO-to-invoice matching, rewards people who stay organized under load rather than those who do well in calm conditions. Third-party management adds another layer: you're accountable to both Asset Living's internal standards and individual client expectations, and those don't always align without active effort.

job.title: Groundskeeper - Rocket Pointe
job.description:
Curb appeal is a leasing tool. Prospects form their first impression before they ever reach the leasing office, and a well-kept exterior can move someone from "maybe" to "yes" faster than any concession. The Groundskeeper at Rocket Pointe in Durango, CO is the person who makes that first impression count, every single day.

What the Role Actually Looks Like

This is a full-time, Monday through Friday position running 9 AM to 6 PM. The work is physical and outdoor-focused, which means you're out there in Durango's weather year-round, whether that's a clear Colorado morning or a February cold snap. Prior experience in landscaping, grounds maintenance, facilities work, or janitorial is required.

Day-to-day, you're keeping the community's common areas, parking lots, breezeways, hallways, and laundry rooms clean and presentable. Trash and debris pickup, manicured landscaping, and maintaining the kind of curb appeal that holds occupancy. You'll also handle light cleaning and prep work ahead of resident move-ins, track cleaning supply inventory, and occasionally assist the office team with door notices. The ability to lift 25 pounds and operate light equipment comes with the territory.

Olympus has been recognized as a National Apartment Association Top Employer three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), and the benefits package reflects that. Compensation starts at $20 to $22 per hour depending on experience and location, with monthly bonuses available. The full package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, pet insurance, short and long-term disability, and a sabbatical program.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Grounds roles at apartment communities often get treated as interchangeable, but the people who thrive in them tend to share a few specific traits. Attention to detail matters more than most applicants expect. A property that looks sharp on a Tuesday morning but has overflowing trash receptacles by Thursday afternoon is not actually well-maintained. Consistency is the job. The candidates who stand out show up with a systems mindset, keeping a mental map of what needs attention when, and they communicate proactively with maintenance and leasing teams when something looks off.

  • Demonstrated experience in landscaping, grounds care, facilities, or janitorial work
  • Comfortable working outdoors across varying weather and temperature conditions
  • Able to lift 25 pounds and operate standard light equipment
  • Reliable and consistent with a Monday through Friday schedule
  • Team-oriented and willing to support office staff when needed

Rocket Pointe sits in Durango, a market where residents have real choices and community presentation carries real weight. Olympus Property builds career paths from roles like this one, and groundskeeping experience translates directly into maintenance technician tracks for those who want to grow into broader property operations over time.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
A prospect walks in unannounced on a Saturday morning, two other people are waiting on a callback, and your inbox has three new internet leads from overnight. That's a normal start to a shift at Bexley Wolf Ranch, and it's exactly the kind of morning this role is built for.

Weinstein Properties, a family-owned company with over 70 years in the business, manages more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. The Georgetown, TX location is hiring an Assistant Property Manager to support daily operations at Bexley Wolf Ranch. Starting pay is $23 per hour, with increases based on experience and quarterly bonuses. A sign-on bonus is also available (details come up during the interview). Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with company match, rent discount, paid holidays, birthday time off, and an Employee Assistance Program.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This role covers a wide range of on-site responsibilities. On the leasing side, you'll respond to internet leads and phone inquiries, schedule and conduct tours, process applications, assemble lease paperwork, and collect deposits and signatures. You'll work with current residents on renewals, notices to vacate, early terminations, pet addendums, and transfer requests. Posting rent, following up on outstanding balances, and handling delinquency conversations are part of the routine too.

You'll coordinate closely with the maintenance team, walking units to confirm make-ready quality before move-in and following up with residents on open work orders. Move-out processing and security deposit dispositions also fall in your court. Beyond the transactional work, you'll help plan and host resident events, which sometimes means evening or weekend hours. Rotating Saturdays are a set part of the schedule.

Assisting and occasionally leading the team, supporting training, and helping the Property Manager hit operational goals rounds out the position. This is a hands-on role. Expect to be on your feet, not at a desk.

What Weinstein Is Looking For

Prior property management experience is a genuine plus, but the company will train someone who comes from a customer-facing background in sales, hospitality, or service management. What matters more is how you handle pressure, communicate under stress, and follow through on detail-heavy tasks.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially in difficult conversations
  • Comfort managing shifting priorities without losing track of open items
  • A customer-first orientation that holds up when residents are frustrated
  • Willingness to pitch in on tasks outside your direct job description
  • Goal orientation and the ability to stay organized in a high-traffic environment

One honest note worth mentioning: the assistant manager role is where a lot of the resident friction lands. Lease questions, billing disputes, maintenance frustrations. You'll handle these conversations directly and often. The candidates who thrive here tend to be people who find problem-solving satisfying even when the person across the desk isn't happy. That skill, developed at the site level, is exactly what prepares people for property manager roles down the line. Weinstein has a stated track record of promoting from within, and many of their current leaders came up through leasing and assistant manager positions.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - 3300 Tamarac
job.description:
Maintenance work at a 200-unit apartment community covers a lot of ground in a single shift. One morning you might be troubleshooting a tripped breaker in a resident's unit, running a make-ready punch list on a recently vacated apartment, and responding to a plumbing call before lunch. MG Properties is hiring a Maintenance Technician for 3300 Tamarac Apartments in Denver, and the role reflects exactly that kind of variety.

What You'll Actually Do

The day-to-day work spans the full range of apartment maintenance: service requests, appliance repairs, painting, grounds and common area upkeep, and unit turns. Turns deserve a specific mention because they're a real part of the workload at a property this size. Getting units make-ready on schedule directly affects occupancy, so the ability to move through a punch list efficiently matters. You'll also carry on-call rotation, which means after-hours calls are part of the deal. That's true of almost every apartment maintenance role, but it's worth stating plainly rather than burying it in the fine print.

What You Bring

  • At least 2 years of apartment maintenance experience, ideally at a property of 200 units or more
  • Working knowledge across trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and general appliance repair
  • A straightforward, professional approach with residents when handling service requests
  • Reliable transportation (this one's non-negotiable given the on-call component)
  • Comfort working as part of a team and adapting when priorities shift mid-day

The Bigger Picture

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. That kind of track record usually means established systems, defined processes, and a maintenance operation that's had time to mature. For a technician, that often translates to clearer expectations and better support than you'd find at a smaller or newer operator.

Pay runs $24 to $25 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of base. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k with employer match, PTO, paid holidays, and rental discounts. One detail worth noting: this position is anticipated to close in September 2026, so it carries a defined end date. Factor that into your decision.

Strong candidates at this level tend to be the ones who can work independently without needing direction on every task, communicate honestly with residents even when a repair takes longer than expected, and treat turns with the same attention they give to occupied-unit service calls. Those habits are what separate a technician who's technically competent from one who's actually an asset to a maintenance team.

job.title: Associate, Asset Management
job.description:
Asset management at the property level requires two distinct skill sets working in parallel: financial modeling sharp enough to justify major capital decisions, and operational fluency to hold execution accountable. This role at The Scion Group uses both, consistently.

What This Role Actually Does

The Scion Group focuses on student housing, a sector with its own rhythms around lease-up cycles, annual turn seasons, and enrollment-driven demand. As an Asset Management Associate, you'll carry direct oversight of a portfolio of owned assets. That means building and owning the financial models that underpin capex decisions, tracking whether projected rent premiums are actually materializing post-renovation, and flagging performance gaps before they compound.

You'll also handle the retail side of mixed-use assets: negotiating letters of intent, working through TI scopes, CAM structures, insurance compliance, and concession terms. Quarterly investor reporting packages fall in your lane too, as does contributing to the annual budget process.

On-site inspections are part of the job. You're expected to develop a ground-level understanding of each asset and bring that context back into your analysis, not just model from a spreadsheet.

The Skills This Role Runs On

  • Advanced financial modeling in Excel. This is the core tool. You'll use it to justify repositioning strategies, project ROI on capital improvements, and build investor-facing packages.
  • Commercial real estate asset management experience, specifically. Prior exposure to operations, capital projects, and retail leasing is the baseline.
  • Communication that translates complex data into clear recommendations for both internal teams and external partners.
  • A proactive approach to identifying issues and repositioning opportunities, not waiting for problems to surface in reports.

A bachelor's degree in real estate, finance, economics, or a related STEM field is required. An MBA or advanced degree is a plus. Expect to travel up to 20% of the time, with some flexibility needed during peak periods.

What Makes This Role Specific to Scion

Student housing operates on a compressed annual cycle. Lease-up happens in a narrow window, turn costs are significant, and occupancy swings can be sharp. Asset managers here need to understand those dynamics and factor them into both underwriting assumptions and operational conversations. If your background is purely in conventional multifamily or office, there's a real learning curve on the demand-side drivers.

The role is based at Scion's Chicago corporate office. Compensation is targeted between $105,000 and $125,000 base, plus discretionary bonus and a full benefits package including 401k matching, health, dental, vision, parental leave, and learning reimbursement.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II (Park Place)
job.description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Maintenance work in a residential apartment community draws on a wider range of technical skills than most people realize until they're doing it. At Prometheus's Park Place community in Mountain View, a Maintenance Technician II handles the full spectrum: appliance repairs and installs, plumbing, basic electrical, carpentry, and painting. Turns and make-readies are a real part of the rhythm here, so knowing how to move efficiently through a punch list without cutting corners matters as much as raw technical ability. If you've got at least two years of hands-on apartment maintenance experience and you're comfortable troubleshooting most mechanical systems independently, the technical side of this role will feel familiar.

What separates a solid Technician II from a great one at a community like this is the interpersonal piece. Residents at Park Place aren't just submitting tickets into a void. They're interacting with you, sometimes while they're stressed about a leak or a broken appliance affecting their day. The ability to communicate clearly, follow through on what you said you'd do, and leave a resident feeling genuinely taken care of is a real skill. Prometheus calls their residents "Neighbors," and that's not just branding. The expectation is that you treat the people who live here like they matter, because they do.

Day-to-Day Realities

Most days involve a mix of service requests and ongoing upkeep tasks across the property. Turnover work picks up as units vacate, and you'll be part of getting those apartments ready for the next resident. On-call availability is required, so there will be after-hours situations. That's the honest reality of residential maintenance. Prometheus does offer standby pay and on-call premium pay to compensate for that availability, and the bonus structure includes renovation and lease-up incentives for techs who get involved in those phases of a property's life cycle.

The physical demands are real too: you'll be on your feet most of the day, often outdoors, lifting up to 50 lbs., climbing, and working through a range of tasks that require both fine-motor precision and some physical effort. Basic computer proficiency matters for logging work orders and communicating with the broader team.

What Prometheus Brings to the Table

Prometheus has operated in the Bay Area since 1965 and owns more than 13,000 apartments across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle as a privately held company. That scale means internal career paths exist for technicians who want to grow into lead or supervisory roles, and the company's vertically integrated structure, including in-house renovations and value-add work, creates real opportunities to expand your skill set over time.

The compensation range for this position is $31.00 to $32.25 per hour, with a semi-annual discretionary bonus and additional incentives for things like referrals, training coaching, and renovation projects. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for eligible employees and dependents, a 401(k) with employer matching, tenure-based housing discounts, and tuition reimbursement. These are meaningful benefits, especially in a high cost-of-living market like Mountain View.

  • Minimum two years of apartment maintenance experience required
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Must be available for on-call rotations
  • Comfortable with plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, and painting
  • Basic computer proficiency for work order systems
  • Able to lift up to 50 lbs. and perform physically demanding tasks regularly

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Part-Time)
job.description:
Part-time leasing roles at residential communities tend to attract two kinds of people: those who treat it as a weekend side job, and those who treat it as a real entry point into property management. At John M. Corcoran & Company, the expectation is clearly the latter. JMC has operated in New England since 1951, and they've built a track record of promoting from within and developing careers over the long haul.

This position is based at Dexter Street Commons in Pawtucket, RI, and runs Saturday and Sunday, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm. Sixteen hours a week sounds modest, but weekends are when most prospective residents actually have time to tour. That means your two days carry real weight for the property's traffic and occupancy numbers.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your core job is converting interest into signed leases. You'll show apartments, walk prospects through pricing and lease terms, process rental applications, and build lease packages that set new residents up for a smooth move-in. You'll also handle property inspections to keep curb appeal sharp, which matters more than people realize when a prospect is deciding between two similar units.

Beyond the transactional side, you'll stay in communication with residents throughout their tenancy and contribute to the property's marketing presence through social media, website activity, and local networking. Setting your own leasing goals and finding creative ways to hit them is part of the role, not an afterthought.

Who Tends to Do Well Here

  • High School Diploma or equivalent (education or relevant experience)
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with computers and basic tech tools
  • Genuine organization and time management, not just the buzzword version
  • A steady, positive presence with prospective and current residents alike

The candidates who stand out in leasing roles like this one tend to be naturally curious about people. They ask good questions during a tour, they remember details, and they follow up without being prompted. Sales experience helps, but the ability to make someone feel genuinely heard in a 20-minute apartment showing matters just as much.

The Bigger Picture

JMC offers competitive hourly pay ($23 to $27.50, depending on experience) plus a $1,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off and holidays, and a 401(k) with a company match. For a part-time position, that's a meaningful package.

For someone early in their property management career, a weekend leasing role at a well-established company is a genuinely useful starting point. You pick up leasing fundamentals, you learn how a residential community runs day-to-day, and you build relationships with a team that, based on JMC's history, tends to stick around. From leasing consultant, the natural next steps are full-time leasing, assistant manager, or property manager. Those paths open faster when you've already shown you can close, communicate, and take care of residents. This role gives you the chance to do exactly that.

job.title: Housekeeper
job.description:
What the Job Actually Looks Like

Housekeeper roles in residential property management don't get a lot of attention, but they're doing real work that directly affects how a community looks and feels to residents and prospects. At Paragon Properties, this position focuses on the interior common areas and amenities across their communities. Lobbies, hallways, laundry rooms, clubhouses, fitness areas, anything shared gets cleaned and sanitized on a consistent schedule. When the maintenance team needs a hand turning apartments, you may step in there too.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm. No nights, no weekends. That's a genuine quality-of-life factor in a field where plenty of positions blur those lines.

What the Work Requires

This is a physical job. You'll be on your feet most of the day, covering ground across the property. Lifting up to 25 pounds is part of the routine. You'll need reliable transportation to get to the site consistently, and attention to curb appeal matters here too, not just interior cleanliness.

Previous professional cleaning experience is preferred, but the posting doesn't require it. What it does require is someone detail-oriented enough to catch what others miss, because common area condition shows up immediately in how residents feel about where they live. A dingy hallway or a neglected amenity space affects perception the same way a slow maintenance response does.

  • Clean and sanitize interior common areas and amenities
  • Assist the maintenance team with apartment cleaning as needed during turns
  • Maintain attention to curb appeal and overall property presentation
  • Reliable, consistent attendance on a 40-hour weekly schedule

Pre-employment requirements include a background check, drug screening, and physical. Paragon operates a drug-free workplace.

Compensation and Benefits

Pay runs up to $19 per hour depending on experience. The benefits package is more complete than most hourly property roles offer. Paragon provides affordable medical, dental, and optical coverage with a short waiting period, plus company-paid life and disability insurance. You'll also get paid time off, paid holidays, a 401(k) with employer contribution, and a quarterly team profit-sharing bonus. A rent discount, employee referral program, and employee assistance program round things out.

The guaranteed 40-hour schedule is worth noting. Hourly roles in property management sometimes float on available hours. This one doesn't.

For someone who takes pride in maintaining a space and wants a stable weekday schedule with real benefits, this is a solid fit.

job.title: Maintenance Technician 2 - The Metropolitan-Fishers
job.description:
A resident submits an emergency work order at 7 a.m.: water pooling under the kitchen sink, unit 214 needs attention before they leave for work. You grab your tools, assess the supply line, make the fix, and log it before the morning standup. That's the rhythm of this role.

The Work at The Metropolitan

The Metropolitan is a 304-unit community in Fishers, Indiana, managed by Ackermann Group, a Midwest real estate and property management company with roots going back to 1938. As a Maintenance Technician 2, you'll work across the full scope of community upkeep: unit make-readies, intermediate repairs, grounds maintenance, and preventive maintenance tasks on equipment and common areas. The make-ready process will be a regular part of your week, which means working through punch lists between turns and coordinating with the maintenance supervisor to keep vacant units rent-ready.

Repair work spans plumbing, electrical, carpentry, appliance repair, HVAC, and painting. You'll also participate in move-in and move-out inspections, support pool water management when applicable, handle janitorial duties tied to common areas and facilities, and take part in snow removal preparation and response. After-hours emergency calls rotate among the maintenance team, so availability outside standard hours is a real part of the job, not an occasional footnote.

The posted schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with that on-call rotation layered in as designated by the Community Manager.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

This is explicitly a training role. Ackermann has structured the Technician 2 level to develop proficiency across the maintenance trade, which means you don't need to arrive with mastery in every discipline. What you do need is at least one year of general maintenance experience, solid attention to detail, a team-first attitude, a valid driver's license with proof of insurance, and a high school diploma or equivalent.

Certifications like EPA Type I and II, CAMT, or CPO aren't required but carry real weight in the hiring process. If you don't hold them yet, this role is a practical environment to work toward them. The skills you develop here, particularly across HVAC, plumbing, and the make-ready process, transfer directly to a Maintenance Supervisor track or a lead tech position at a larger community.

  • 1 or more years of general maintenance experience
  • Broad working knowledge across common repair categories
  • EPA Type I and II, CAMT, or CPO certifications (preferred, not required)
  • Valid driver's license with proof of insurance
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Availability for after-hours emergency on-call rotation

Technicians who advance fastest in roles like this are the ones who treat every make-ready as a learning rep and ask questions during preventive maintenance rounds rather than waiting for formal training moments. The variety of work at a 304-unit community means you'll see a wide range of repair scenarios in a relatively short period, which accelerates hands-on skill development in ways smaller properties simply can't match.

Ackermann offers competitive hourly pay with quarterly bonus potential and lease renewal commissions, health benefits including medical, dental, and vision, a 401(k) with company match, paid time off including your birthday, an employee rent discount at any Ackermann community, and career coaching resources.

job.title: Multi-Site Leasing Consultant (Myerton & Park Georgetown)
job.description:
This role splits your week across two Van Metre communities in Arlington: three days at Park Georgetown Apartments and two days at The Myerton. You're not bouncing between properties randomly. You're building resident relationships and driving occupancy at both, which means staying organized, keeping your product knowledge current at each site, and managing your time across two distinct communities.

What You'll Actually Do

The core of the job is leasing and retention. You'll handle inbound traffic, conduct tours, follow up with prospects by phone and email, process applications, and work lease renewals. Alongside that, you'll do grassroots marketing to bring in new traffic, coordinate with the service team on maintenance requests, and help plan resident events.

There's a physical component too. You'll walk the exterior of each community three times a week, noting anything that needs attention: landscaping, paint, damage, curb appeal issues. You'll also inspect vacant units and flag repairs before turns are complete. These aren't optional tasks. They're part of maintaining the product quality that supports leasing performance.

Weekend availability is required.

What You Bring

  • 0 to 2 years in customer service, sales, hospitality, or a comparable role
  • Comfortable conducting exterior and interior inspections in all weather
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Organized enough to manage tasks and follow-ups across two sites
  • Sales-minded with a focus on hitting occupancy goals
  • Bilingual is a plus
  • Social media skills are relevant here given grassroots marketing responsibilities

Compensation and Context

Base pay runs $20 to $21 per hour depending on experience. On top of that, the role carries up to $5,000 in annual bonus paid quarterly, plus leasing and renewal commissions. Benefits include 11 paid holidays, 10 vacation days, 10 sick days, personal days, a birthday day off, winter break, and comprehensive parental leave. Van Metre also offers a 401(k) with company match, up to $900 in annual wellness reimbursement, tuition reimbursement, and a rental discount.

One thing worth knowing about multi-site leasing roles: the split schedule sharpens skills that transfer well into property management. You learn to adapt your pitch and service style to different resident profiles, manage competing priorities across sites, and build credibility with multiple teams. Candidates who thrive in this kind of setup tend to move into assistant manager or management roles faster than those working a single property.

Van Metre has operated in the Washington, D.C. area since 1955. Arlington is a competitive submarket, and both Park Georgetown and The Myerton are positioned at the upper end of the rental market, so you'll be expected to represent the brand at a consistent level across both communities.

job.title: Customer Experience Manager
job.description:
Park Avenue Apartments sits in one of Salt Lake City's more competitive rental corridors, where Class A communities have been stacking up and renters have real choices. That context matters for this role. Cottonwood Residential is looking for a Customer Experience Manager who can turn traffic into signed leases and signed leases into residents who actually want to stay.

The title signals what Cottonwood emphasizes: this is a leasing and resident relations position built around service, not just transaction processing. Day to day, you'll work prospects from first inquiry through move-in, handle applications and lease documentation, and support move-outs with the same attention you'd give a new lease. You'll also carry some supervisory weight, overseeing Customer Experience Specialists and stepping into a lead role when the Community Manager is away. That's meaningful exposure for someone who wants to grow toward a community manager seat.

Cottonwood adopted self-guided tours early, which shapes how this team operates. A solid chunk of your traffic arrives having already toured on their own schedule. That means your follow-up and conversion work carries more weight than it does at communities where every prospect gets a staffed tour. You need to be sharp on follow-through and comfortable working leads who came in without a personal handshake.

The marketing piece is real, not just a line item. Outreach marketing, social media, and online reputation management are part of the job, and the team coordinates resident events alongside leasing activity. If you've only ever worked inbound traffic, this role will stretch you.

Entrata Core experience is a plus here, which makes sense given how widely it's used across Utah's multifamily market. Fair Housing knowledge is expected, not optional.

What Cottonwood is looking for

  • At least one year of multifamily property management experience
  • Background in leasing, sales, or customer service
  • General marketing and social media experience, including online channels
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with basic accounting concepts (a plus, not a hard requirement)
  • Entrata Core familiarity (preferred)
  • Weekend availability (required)

The schedule is full-time with flexibility expected across evenings and weekends. Benefits kick in within the first thirty days and include full medical, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage, a 401k with company match, HSA matching, three weeks of PTO in year one, and ten and a half paid holidays.

Candidates who stand out in this type of role tend to be the ones who treat every interaction as a potential referral source. Salt Lake City's rental market is tight-knit enough that word travels, and Cottonwood's #HomeAtLast positioning is only as good as the experience residents actually have at move-in and beyond.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Masonry
job.description:
Birgo has been contracting out masonry work for years. They've decided it's time to own that capability directly, and this role is how they're building it. If you're a skilled mason who also carries a broad maintenance toolkit, this is a chance to be the person who establishes something from the ground up inside a company that clearly invests in its people.

The day-to-day splits into two modes. Some days you're doing exterior and structural work: brick repair, tuckpointing, repointing, waterproofing. The kind of work that protects a building's envelope and keeps small problems from becoming expensive ones. Other days you're inside units doing turns and work orders, drywall, paint, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, the full range of general maintenance. You'll float across roughly 14 communities spread across Buffalo, North Tonawanda, Hamburg, and Lockport, so you'll need your own reliable transportation and Birgo covers mileage.

The schedule is straightforward: Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 4:30 PM. No rotating on-call, no weekend surprises built into the base schedule. For a skilled trades role, that kind of predictability matters.

Pay runs $26 to $28 an hour, paid weekly, with flexibility for the right candidate. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with employer contribution, PTO, paid holidays, sick time, a 401(k) match, professional development reimbursement, boots reimbursement, and discounted rent at Birgo properties.

What tends to separate strong candidates in a role like this is the combination: genuine masonry skill paired with comfort doing general apartment maintenance. A pure mason who can't pivot to a punch list item, or a generalist who's never done serious brick work, won't fit as well here. Birgo is specifically trying to stop outsourcing this work, which means they need someone who can carry both sides without leaning too hard on one.

The company describes itself as mission-driven, and their internal language reflects it. They talk about servant-heartedness and humility alongside excellence and integrity. That's worth taking seriously when you're evaluating fit. Workplaces that use that kind of language genuinely tend to run differently than ones that don't, and the people who thrive there usually share some of those instincts.

What you'll need

  • Demonstrated masonry skills, specifically brick repointing and tuckpointing
  • Well-rounded general maintenance background (drywall, paint, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, HVAC basics)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable personal transportation
  • Ability to lift and carry 50 pounds unassisted, work in confined spaces, and use ladders safely
  • Eligibility to work in the United States

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
The Role and Where It Sits

Maintenance at a well-run multifamily property runs on two people: the Maintenance Supervisor who sets the direction, and the Assistant Maintenance Supervisor who makes sure the work actually gets done. That's the position Berkshire Residential is filling at Ellington Metro West. If you've spent time in the field doing real maintenance work and you're ready to step into a coordination role without fully leaving the hands-on side behind, this is a natural next move.

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions get made closer to the ground than at a typical third-party shop. There's no management company layer to route everything through. That structure tends to give on-site teams more ownership over outcomes, and more accountability for them too.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You're supporting the Maintenance Supervisor on scheduling and quality control, helping coordinate make-ready repairs, and stepping in alongside technicians when the work volume demands it. You're also the person who keeps the shop organized: supplies, equipment, inventory, and key security. Tour routes and models fall under your eye too. A scuffed baseboard or a burned-out bulb in a model unit reflects on everyone, and at a property like this, those details matter.

You'll report major repairs and spending needs to both the Maintenance Supervisor and the Property Manager before anything gets approved. Safety enforcement is part of the job, not a side item. And on the resident-facing side, you're expected to bring a service mindset to every interaction, whether it's a work order follow-up or a conversation in the parking lot.

Qualifications Berkshire is looking for:

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience across general maintenance disciplines
  • Comfort with technology and property management software
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • Ability to meet the physical demands of a maintenance role
  • A genuine ability to work with and coach a team

The posted base salary range is $68,800 to $79,500, with placement depending on experience and skills. Benefits include three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, health insurance, and personal development plans.

One thing worth knowing about this career path: the Assistant Maintenance Supervisor role is one of the more reliable pipelines to a Maintenance Supervisor seat in this industry. You're building the scheduling habits, vendor relationships, and quality control instincts that the top job requires. A year or two of strong performance here, especially at a company that promotes from within, tends to open that door.

job.title: Cleaner - Part-Time
job.description:
Part-time cleaning roles at student housing properties get overlooked on job boards, but they're genuinely useful positions to hold early in a property management career. You're on the ground every day, moving through every corner of the community, which means you develop an eye for what a well-run property actually looks like from the inside out.

Redstone Residential operates over 38,000 beds across 20 states, making it one of the larger third-party student housing management companies in the country. Their Rexburg location is a student community, which comes with its own rhythm: high turnover seasons, move-in pushes, and the kind of cleaning checks that keep resident relations from becoming maintenance headaches. This role sits at the center of that.

Day to day, you'll handle scheduled cleaning checks of resident apartments, keep common areas like hallways, the clubhouse, and the leasing office in good shape, and manage exterior upkeep including trash, debris, landscaping, and snow and ice removal when the Idaho winters arrive. There's some light maintenance assistance involved as well. The shifts run four to six hours and the pay is $12.00 per hour, part-time and non-exempt.

What makes someone good at this role isn't just attention to detail, it's the ability to self-direct. You'll often be working without someone checking on you every hour, so the candidates who do well here are people who take ownership of their checklist and finish it without being prompted. A friendly demeanor matters too, since cleaning checks put you inside residents' living spaces, and how you carry yourself there affects how residents feel about the property overall.

From a career standpoint, this kind of role builds real fluency with property operations. Porters and cleaners who stay curious tend to move into maintenance tech roles or leasing support positions. You start to understand turn prep, punch list work, and curb appeal in a way that's hard to teach in a classroom. At a company managing a portfolio this size, there are also internal paths worth asking about during the interview.

What Redstone Is Looking For

  • Some background in janitorial or cleaning work
  • Ability to complete daily tasks independently, without close supervision
  • Comfortable with physical work: lifting 50-plus pounds and standing for a full shift
  • Friendly and professional when interacting with residents

Redstone offers a 401(k) with up to 6% matching, which is worth noting for a part-time hourly position. If you're based in Rexburg and want a foothold in property management, this is a practical place to start building one.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
PeakMade Real Estate manages off-campus student housing across the country, and their College Station property sits in one of the more demanding student housing markets in Texas. With Texas A&M enrollment consistently above 70,000, the Bryan/College Station market runs high occupancy most of the year and compresses turn windows considerably. A Maintenance Supervisor here needs to be comfortable executing fast, clean turns while keeping daily service levels high during the academic year.

What You'll Actually Do

This role splits roughly 60 to 70 percent hands-on work and the remainder on supervision, vendor oversight, and coordination with the property manager. On any given day that means completing service requests alongside your team, walking the grounds to catch issues before residents do, and making sure the maintenance shop stays organized and OSHA-compliant. You'll own the preventative maintenance program, manage supply inventory within budget, and keep the hazard communications program current.

Turn season is where this role gets tested. You'll schedule and direct all make-ready activity, supervise contractors throughout the process, and push vacant units through restoration and cleaning so they're ready to market on time. The pace during turn can be relentless, and your ability to keep the team coordinated and the punch list moving is what determines whether the property hits its lease-up deadlines. Outside of turn, you'll conduct monthly unit inspections, assist with move-ins and move-outs, manage key control, and work with the National Facilities Director when capital improvement bids are needed.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least 2 years of maintenance supervisory experience; multifamily background strongly preferred
  • EPA Type II certification required; CPO preferred (PeakMade offers technical certifications if you're not yet certified)
  • Valid driver's license, current auto insurance, and a reliable personal vehicle (required for the role)
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property
  • Your own basic hand tools
  • Hands-on repair ability across HVAC, intermediate plumbing, intermediate electrical, appliances, sheetrock, carpentry, painting, pool care, roofing, irrigation, and landscaping
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at heights on ladders, and work outdoors in Texas heat or cold

Context Worth Knowing

Student housing maintenance supervision differs from conventional multifamily in a few specific ways. Resident turnover is annual and largely synchronized, which means the turn window is compressed and high-volume. Wear and tear patterns in student communities also tend to run heavier than in conventional properties, so your diagnostic speed and carpentry and appliance skills will get consistent use. Supervisors who thrive here are the ones who can execute at the technician level without losing track of their team's workload or the broader property condition. The path from this role often leads to regional facilities roles or community director positions for candidates who develop both the technical depth and the management fundamentals PeakMade's leadership program is designed to build.

PeakMade's benefits package includes paid parental leave, 15 days of PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, 401(k) match, monthly renewal bonuses, and a ten-year milestone trip. The company is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

job.title: Part Time Groundskeeper Manufactured Housing Community
job.description:
Garden Terrace Estates is a 104-home manufactured housing community in Garden Grove, and Investment Property Group is looking for a part-time groundskeeper to keep it looking sharp. The schedule is straightforward: Monday through Friday, 8am to noon, 20 hours a week. Pay runs $18 to $22 an hour depending on what you bring to the table.

The work itself is what you'd expect from a well-run MHC that takes curb appeal seriously. Morning inspections of common areas, grounds maintenance, irrigation system checks, litter removal, trash-outs, and operating equipment like mowers, trimmers, blowers, and chainsaws when tree limbs need to come down. You'll also cover interior common spaces: clubhouse floors, restrooms, breezeways. The role supports the broader service team rather than operating as a solo act, so communication with the maintenance supervisor and community manager matters.

Manufactured housing communities have their own rhythm. Residents own their homes but lease the land, which means the physical condition of common areas and the overall streetscape carries real weight in how residents feel about where they live. A tidy community with functioning irrigation and clean common spaces isn't a luxury in this asset class. It's directly tied to resident retention and occupancy. The groundskeeper role is more visible here than it might be at a large multifamily complex where maintenance staff can blend into the background.

IPG owns and operates 150 properties across 13 states, so there's organizational depth behind this community-level role. For the right candidate, a part-time groundskeeper position at a company this size can open doors to full-time maintenance technician work as experience accumulates and positions turn over.

What the role requires

  • At least one year of maintenance or grounds experience at a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100 or more units
  • Comfort operating and maintaining power tools and mechanical equipment safely
  • Physical stamina for a full shift of walking, lifting, bending, and standing
  • Basic landscaping and light general maintenance knowledge
  • Professional interaction with residents, staff, and visitors
  • Ability to spot problems and flag them before they become bigger issues

Benefits include a 401k with company match, PTO accrual at one hour per 30 hours worked, critical illness and accident coverage, an employee assistance program, and an employee referral program. For a part-time role, that's a reasonable package.

job.title: Service Technician - Zerzura
job.description:
Maintenance technicians at apartment communities spend their days moving between two very different kinds of work: the planned and the unexpected. At Zerzura in Las Vegas, you'll handle both, supporting current residents through service requests and preparing units for incoming ones through the turn process.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical day might start with a punch list from yesterday's move-out inspection, pull you into a plumbing call mid-morning, and end with a resident appliance repair that takes a little more troubleshooting than expected. AIR Communities uses tech-driven tools to organize and prioritize that workflow, which means less time figuring out where to go next and more time actually fixing things. The shop is stocked and organized, so you're not hunting for parts when a resident is waiting.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Completing apartment turns and make-readies to meet move-in standards
  • Handling resident-requested repairs across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and general carpentry
  • Supporting move-in and move-out inspections as needed
  • Potentially providing guidance to less experienced technicians on the team
  • Assisting with vendor quality checks depending on your experience level

The role requires at least two areas of trade proficiency, two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment, and the flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts at least one week per month. Las Vegas summers are demanding on HVAC systems, so expect that to be a real part of the seasonal workload. Reliable transportation for after-hours emergency calls is a hard requirement.

The People Side of This Role

Residents notice how you communicate almost as much as how fast you fix things. AIR ties quarterly bonuses (up to $250/month) to customer satisfaction scores, which tells you something about what the company values day to day. You're interacting with people in their homes, often when something's gone wrong, and the technicians who do well here tend to be the ones who treat that interaction with some care.

The team dynamic matters too. Depending on the community's needs, you may be mentoring newer technicians or learning from more senior ones. That kind of cross-training builds the kind of multi-trade fluency that opens doors to lead technician and maintenance supervisor roles over time.

Compensation and Support

Base pay starts at $22.00 per hour. Beyond that, AIR offers a 50% rent discount at any of their communities (including the option to live on-site at Zerzura), a 401(k) with employer contribution, up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, and full reimbursement for job-related certifications and licenses. AIR's Ascend program is worth noting if professional growth matters to you: it's a development path customized to where you are technically and where you want to go, not a generic training checklist.

The application deadline is August 15, 2026, with rolling review after that date. Pre-employment screening includes reference checks, employment verification, background check, and a four-panel drug screen that excludes marijuana.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
It's 6:45 a.m. on a Monday and your phone already has two work orders from overnight: a unit reported no heat, and a common area light fixture is out near the entrance. Before the leasing office opens, you want both resolved.

That's the pace of this role. Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager for a residential property in Jersey City, NJ. The position sits between hands-on trade work and team leadership. You're still in the tools regularly, but you're also responsible for making sure others are doing the work correctly and on time.

What the Work Actually Involves

The make-ready process is central to this job. Turns need to move quickly and cleanly so apartments are ready to lease without delays. You'll own the punch list mentality: thorough walkthroughs, no shortcuts, units handed off in move-in condition. Beyond turns, you'll handle HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repairs across the property, respond to resident service tickets with genuine follow-through, and keep preventative maintenance programs running on schedule rather than reacting to failures after the fact.

The building itself demands attention. Grounds upkeep, snow removal, common area cleanliness, and safety compliance all fall within your scope. Bozzuto places real weight on asset preservation, which means this role isn't just about fixing things when they break. It's about protecting the long-term condition of the property. You'll also be expected to work weekends and participate in the emergency on-call rotation. That part of the job is real, and it's worth knowing upfront.

What You Need to Bring

  • At least 5 years of experience in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Familiarity with OSHA, MSDS, and risk management standards
  • Exposure to complex mechanical systems such as boilers, chillers, central plant, or split systems is a plus
  • Prior supervisory experience, even informal, is preferred
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds regularly, climb ladders, and work in variable weather

The candidates who tend to stand out here combine technical depth with real communication skills. You can diagnose a failing boiler and also explain the timeline to a frustrated resident without getting defensive. That combination is rarer than most people assume, and it's exactly what separates a strong assistant maintenance manager from a good technician.

Compensation for this role falls between $70,000 and $72,000 annually, with additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Groundskeeper / Maintenance Technician - Montair at Somerset Hill
job.description:
Grounds and maintenance roles at apartment communities tend to get underestimated. They're actually the first impression a property makes, every single day, before a single leasing conversation happens. At Montair at Somerset Hill in Tumwater, WA, Olympus Property is hiring a Groundskeeper/Maintenance Technician to own that first impression.

What the Role Involves

Your primary focus is curb appeal and cleanliness across the community. That means daily trash and debris pickup through common areas, parking lots, breezeways, hallways, laundry rooms, and other shared spaces. You'll also handle light cleaning and minor repairs as part of the make-ready process before new residents move in, keep an accurate inventory of cleaning supplies and equipment, and assist the office team periodically with door notices. The schedule is full-time, Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM.

Prior experience in landscaping, grounds maintenance, facilities work, or janitorial services is required. You'll be working outdoors regularly, in all kinds of Pacific Northwest weather, so comfort with variable conditions is part of the job, not an occasional inconvenience. Physical requirements include the ability to lift 25 pounds and operate light equipment.

Skills This Role Builds

If you're early in a property management career, a grounds role teaches you things that are hard to learn any other way. You develop an eye for what makes a property look and feel well-maintained, a skill that translates directly if you move into maintenance technician, lead tech, or facilities supervisor positions down the road. You also learn how a community operates from the outside in: traffic patterns, resident habits, the relationship between curb appeal and occupancy. Those observations matter more than most people realize.

The technicians and groundskeepers who grow quickly in this industry are the ones who treat the property like it's theirs. They notice the thing that needs attention before anyone asks. They communicate with the office team clearly. They show up with consistency. That's the baseline Olympus is looking for here.

The Company Behind the Role

Olympus Property has been recognized by the National Apartment Association as a top employer three years running (2023, 2024, and 2025). The benefits package here is genuinely comprehensive:

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 401(k) with employer matching
  • Educational assistance and tuition reimbursement
  • Apartment rental allowance
  • Pet insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability
  • Life and AD&D insurance
  • Paid time off and sabbatical
  • Monthly performance bonuses for eligible team members

The starting pay range is $23.00 to $25.00 per hour, depending on experience and location. For a grounds role with a defined schedule, a real benefits package, and a company that has a documented track record of promoting from within, this is a strong entry point into property management.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is where occupancy gets won or lost. A community can have great amenities and a solid location, but if the person greeting prospects at the door can't convert traffic into signed leases, none of that matters. Weinstein Properties understands this, which is why they invest heavily in training the people who hold this role, even when those people have never worked a day in property management.

Weinstein is a family-owned operator headquartered in Richmond, Virginia, with more than 70 years in the business and over 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. The Bexley Westshore community in Cumming, GA is hiring a Leasing Consultant. Starting pay is $20/hour and scales with experience. Quarterly bonuses are part of the package, and this specific opening includes an alternate schedule bonus of $80 per pay period for working Saturdays and taking a weekday off instead.

The Schedule and Compensation Structure

This is an alternate-schedule position. You'll work five days per week including Saturdays (9am to 5pm), with Sundays and one weekday off each week. Weekday hours run 9am to 6pm. The schedule stays consistent week to week, which makes it easier to plan your life around. In addition to base pay and the alternate schedule bonus, you'll earn quarterly bonuses tied to performance. Benefits include a rent discount, health, dental and vision insurance, 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, vacation, and sick time.

What the Role Actually Involves

Leasing Consultants at Weinstein are the first point of contact for prospective residents and a daily resource for current ones. You'll handle tours, follow up on leads, process applications, and support the administrative side of the leasing office. Property walks, unit inspections, and helping maintain the overall appearance of the community are part of the job too. Resident events and occasional weather-related situations may pull you outside standard hours from time to time.

Weinstein is explicit that prior leasing experience is not required. Their training program is built to bring motivated people up to speed from the ground. What they screen for is attitude, communication, and the ability to stay organized when priorities shift mid-day, which happens constantly in a leasing office.

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Comfort engaging with people in person, by phone, and via email
  • Organized, goal-oriented, and able to manage competing tasks
  • Team-oriented with a willingness to pitch in beyond a defined job description
  • Flexible availability, including Saturdays

One thing worth knowing about this career path: leasing consultant roles at well-run operators like Weinstein are genuine entry points into property management. Strong performers typically move into Assistant Manager roles where they own the financial reporting side, including rent collections, delinquency tracking, and NOI contribution at the property level. Weinstein notes that many of their current leaders started exactly where this role begins.

Cumming sits in Forsyth County, one of the fastest-growing counties in Georgia, which means lease-up pressure and steady traffic are real factors at communities in this market. For a leasing consultant, that translates to a high-volume environment with genuine opportunity to build conversion skills quickly.

job.title: Community Manager - Bear Valley
job.description:
MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over three decades. Bear Valley Apartments in Denver is one of those communities, and they're looking for a Community Manager who can run the full operation: team development, leasing performance, budget oversight, and day-to-day property management.

Denver's multifamily market rewards operators who can balance occupancy with NOI discipline. The city has absorbed significant new supply in recent years, which means community managers at stabilized properties have to work harder on retention and traffic conversion than they did five years ago. Concessions are part of the conversation in certain submarkets, and budget management matters more when rent growth is measured rather than assumed. Bear Valley sits in the southwest part of the city, a more established residential area compared to the high-rise corridors downtown, which typically means a different resident profile and a different leasing rhythm.

This role carries real authority. You'll hire and develop your on-site team, set the operational tone, manage the property's budget, and own the marketing strategy. MG Properties wants someone who has already done this, not someone building toward it. Yardi experience is a plus, and a valid driver's license is required.

What strong candidates bring

  • Recent, hands-on experience managing a residential apartment community (not just assistant-level work)
  • Proven ability to build and lead an on-site team through hiring, training, and performance management
  • Demonstrated budget management skills, including variance analysis and expense control
  • Marketing and leasing acumen, with an understanding of how to drive traffic and improve conversion
  • Yardi proficiency (preferred)
  • Valid driver's license and proof of insurance

The compensation range is $79,000 to $81,000 annually, with monthly and performance-based incentive bonuses on top of that. MG Properties also offers company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid holidays, paid sick time, and rental discounts. This position is expected to be filled by September 2026.

Community managers who perform well at properties like this one tend to move into multi-site or regional roles over time. MG Properties is a growing owner-operator, which means internal advancement is a realistic path rather than a talking point.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Most assistant manager roles in multifamily sit at the crossroads of leasing and collections, and that's exactly where this one lives. At Evolve Palm Coast, a Hawthorne Residential Partners community in Palm Coast, FL, the Assistant Community Manager keeps daily operations moving while the Community Manager handles the bigger picture. It's a real dual-track role: you're closing leases in the morning and reviewing delinquency reports in the afternoon.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On the leasing side, you'll handle tours, respond to incoming leads, process applications, and push renewals through on time. Occupancy is a shared responsibility here, and you'll feel the weight of that number. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which means creating content that actually reflects what's happening on the property, not just stock graphics.

The financial piece is where this role separates itself from a pure leasing position. You'll oversee rent collection and payment posting, run weekly delinquency follow-up calls, and coordinate eviction procedures when it gets to that point. Ledger reviews are part of the routine, checking that billing and payment applications are accurate before they become problems. You'll also pull together financial documentation for the Community Manager and regional leadership. If numbers make you uncomfortable, this role will push you past that quickly.

When the Community Manager is out, you step up. That means keeping the team focused, handling resident concerns, and making sure nothing falls through. Hawthorne calls it their "Live It" culture, but practically speaking, it means you're expected to de-escalate difficult conversations with professionalism and actually follow through, not just smooth things over.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. You'll get one weekday off to keep things at 40 hours. Resident events and community needs can pull you into evenings occasionally, so flexibility matters.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • At least six months in an assistant community manager role preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP certification is a plus

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with company match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance. Hawthorne also runs a Career Path Program specifically designed to move Assistant Community Managers into Community Manager roles, and their Learning and Development team actively supports that progression.

The candidates who do well here tend to be comfortable with financial reports, direct with residents when situations require it, and organized enough to juggle leasing traffic and back-office tasks in the same shift. The ones who struggle are usually strong in one area but not the other. This role demands both.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Workforce housing is one of the most active development segments across the Sun Belt right now, and Hillpointe sits near the center of it. As a fully integrated developer and builder, they control the full cycle from land acquisition through construction and into operations. That integration means the Community Manager here works inside a company that has genuine visibility into how each decision at the property level connects to asset performance and long-term value.

This role at their Four Corners, FL community carries the full weight of on-site leadership. You'll own daily operations, occupancy, financial performance, resident experience, and vendor coordination. Hillpointe expects its Community Managers to think like operators, not administrators.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

Your mornings might start with a property walk, checking that amenities are in like-new condition and flagging anything that needs attention before residents head out for the day. From there, you're likely shifting between reviewing accounts payable, checking leasing traffic, and talking through a maintenance request with the facilities team. You're the connective tissue between what residents experience and what the regional manager sees on a report.

You'll work closely with your Regional Manager to hit and hold budgeted occupancy and rent levels, which means staying on top of lease activity, monitoring concessions, and identifying additional revenue opportunities when they appear. Entrata proficiency will help you move quickly here. Budget oversight, vendor management, and lease administration all run through this role. The expectation is availability outside standard hours except during approved time off, which is worth knowing before you apply.

Who Fits Well Here
