This is a remote customer support role sitting inside one of the larger third-party management operations in the country. Asset Living runs a wide portfolio spanning multifamily, single-family rentals, student housing, affordable, and build-to-rent, so the calls you field will cover a real range of situations. You're the first voice a resident, applicant, or partner hears. You'll handle a high volume of inbound inquiries, work through issues on the spot or route them to the right department, and keep things moving without letting the pace affect your professionalism.

Beyond phones, the role carries some administrative weight: word processing, spreadsheet work, formatting reports and presentations, and booking travel arrangements through platforms like Concur. That last piece is a genuine requirement here, not an afterthought. If you've never touched a travel and expense platform before, that's worth noting before you apply.

Day to day, you're also expected to spot patterns. If the same issue keeps surfacing across calls, the expectation is that you flag it up the chain. That kind of awareness separates someone who handles tickets from someone who actually improves the operation over time.

What You Bring

  • Prior customer service or support experience, ideally in a high call volume setting
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with a calm, professional manner under pressure
  • Experience booking travel and processing expense reports; Concur or similar platform familiarity is a plus
  • Comfort working inside structured performance metrics
  • High school diploma or equivalent required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • Bilingual or multilingual skills are a genuine advantage given the scope of Asset Living's portfolio
  • Reliable home internet setup capable of supporting consistent call and system availability

A Note on What Makes This Work

Third-party management at scale means the support function touches a lot of different property types and client expectations at once. The candidate who does well here tends to be someone who stays organized when the queue is deep, doesn't need much hand-holding on tone and professionalism, and treats the administrative side of the job with the same care as the calls. Bilingual ability is listed as preferred, and in a portfolio this broad, it's genuinely useful rather than a checkbox.

Asset Living holds an AMO designation through IREM and ranks in the NMHC top 50, which reflects the size and seriousness of the operation you'd be supporting. This is a fully remote position with no travel requirement.

job.title: Assistant Manager - The Hawthorne
job.description:
Assistant Manager roles at apartment communities tend to sit at the intersection of finance, leasing, and resident relations. At a well-run property, that overlap is manageable. At a busy one, it means your day shifts direction without warning. This role at The Hawthorne with Olympus Property reflects that reality, and it's worth understanding what the job actually asks of you before you apply.

The Work Itself

Your primary anchor is the financial side of the property. Rent collection, daily deposits, delinquency follow-up, and move-out account statements are yours to own. When a resident disputes a charge or a payment doesn't clear, you're the one resolving it. You'll also inspect make-ready apartments before move-in, which means you're accountable for what residents walk into on day one.

Beyond the ledger, you'll support the leasing team directly, showing apartments and contributing to retention efforts and community events. When the Property Manager is out, you step into that seat. That's not occasional coverage. It means understanding how the whole operation runs, not just your slice of it.

Resident complaints land on your desk too. Some are straightforward. Some aren't. The expectation is that you handle them promptly and escalate liability issues or legal complaints to the appropriate people without delay.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with some flexibility expected for resident events and the first weekend of each month. If your availability has hard edges, that's worth thinking through before moving forward.

What Olympus Is Looking For

  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant
  • Comfort with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite (strongly preferred, not optional in practice)
  • Strong time management, especially when multiple priorities arrive at the same time
  • The ability to lead a team when the Property Manager is absent
  • Clear, steady communication with residents during complaints or conflicts

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The candidates who thrive in this type of role already understand that financial accuracy and resident experience are connected. A deposit entered late or a move-out statement that's wrong creates downstream problems, including delinquency disputes and bad debt. Strong applicants also know their local submarket. Keeping tabs on nearby construction, hiring trends, and competing communities isn't extra credit here. It directly informs how the property responds to occupancy pressure.

Olympus has been recognized by the National Apartment Association as a top employer three consecutive years. Pay for this role runs $21 to $24 per hour depending on experience and location, with monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses on top of base. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
job.description:
It's 8:15 on a Tuesday morning at Kings Crossing. You've already cleared two overnight work orders, and the make-ready on unit 214 is halfway through punch list. That rhythm, steady, skilled, purposeful, is exactly what this role looks like most days.

Weinstein Properties is hiring an EPA-certified Maintenance Technician for Kings Crossing in Richmond's Tuckahoe area. This is a full-time, Monday through Friday position (8am to 5pm) with rotating on-call coverage. Pay runs $21 to $23 per hour depending on experience, plus a $1,500 sign-on bonus, $150 per week in on-call pay regardless of call volume, and quarterly performance bonuses up to $980. That on-call structure matters: you get paid whether the phone rings or not.

What the Work Actually Covers

Day-to-day, you'll move between occupied unit repairs and vacant turns, keeping make-readies on schedule so units hit market-ready faster. HVAC troubleshooting and repair will be a consistent part of your week, along with electrical, plumbing, appliance work, and carpentry. You'll also contribute to the overall condition of the community, including grounds, amenities, and pool areas. The team shares the workload, but you'll need the independence to manage your own queue and prioritize without constant direction.

Weinstein owns and manages its properties directly, which means maintenance standards are consistent and decisions don't get filtered through layers of third-party management. When something needs to get done, the path to approval is short.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of apartment or residential maintenance experience
  • EPA certification, Type II or Universal
  • Hands-on HVAC troubleshooting and repair capability
  • Comfort with work order systems and basic computer tools (Outlook, mobile devices)
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and work indoors and outdoors year-round
  • Reliable transportation; ability to operate a golf cart on property
  • Background check required

Strong candidates at this level know the difference between a quick service call and a repair that needs a second look before it turns into a bigger capex issue. That kind of judgment, knowing when a fix is a fix and when something warrants escalation, is what separates a solid tech from a great one on a well-run property.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, PTO, paid holidays, a birthday day off, 401(k) with company match, an employee assistance program, a referral program, and a rent discount. For technicians who want a path forward, Weinstein notes that internal advancement is real and actively supported.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Copper Beech Statesboro serves the Georgia Southern University market, which means your leasing calendar runs on an academic rhythm. The biggest stretch of the year is Turn, when hundreds of residents cycle in and out within a compressed window and every task from touring to package retrieval to maintenance follow-up runs simultaneously. Outside of Turn, the role stays active: you'll lead property tours, field prospect inquiries, help execute resident engagement events, and keep the leasing office and common areas presentation-ready. You'll also support social media content and flag local marketing opportunities to the management team.

After-hours on-call rotation is part of the job. Lockouts happen, and you'll be expected to cover your share of them. That's a real commitment worth knowing upfront.

The title at Scion is Experience Team Member, which reflects what the company actually wants from this position: someone who treats every touchpoint, the first tour, a maintenance follow-up call, a package hand-off, as a customer service moment. Sales and hospitality are genuinely intertwined here.

What You Bring

  • Strong interpersonal skills and comfort communicating with a wide range of people, including prospective residents, current residents, and university-adjacent partners
  • Flexibility with a schedule that shifts across weekdays, weekends, holidays, and peak Turn periods
  • Self-discipline and reliability in a role that blends independent tasks with team coordination
  • Comfort with social media platforms used for resident communication and community promotion
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Context Worth Knowing

Student housing operates differently from conventional multifamily. Occupancy at properties like Copper Beech Statesboro is tied directly to enrollment cycles, so traffic patterns are predictable in one sense but extremely compressed in another. Strong ETMs learn to read objections early in the leasing season, communicate them clearly to the management team, and adjust their approach as availability tightens. That feedback loop between the leasing floor and management is something Scion builds into this role deliberately.

For someone early in a property management career, this position builds a foundation that transfers well. The combination of leasing, marketing, administration, and resident relations gives you exposure to most of the functions you'd need to move into an assistant manager or property manager role down the road, particularly within the student housing sector where operators like Scion, CA Student Living, and Greystar Student run at scale.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The assistant community manager role exists at the intersection of leasing, finance, and people operations. It's the position where someone transitions from executing tasks to understanding why those tasks matter to a property's overall performance. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, a Southeast-based multifamily company ranked among the top 50 largest in the country, this role sits at Reserve at Asheville, a community in the Asheville, NC market.

What This Role Actually Covers

The scope here is genuinely broad. On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, respond to leads, guide prospects through the application process, and manage renewals with accuracy and follow-through. Occupancy and resident retention are shared goals, and you'll contribute to both through consistent leasing performance and attentive resident relations. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which means translating on-site activity into content that reflects the community's character.

The financial side of this role carries real weight. You'll oversee rent collection, payment posting, and ledger reviews. Delinquency monitoring is a weekly responsibility, including follow-up calls and coordinating eviction procedures when necessary. You'll assist with financial reporting for the community manager and regional leadership, which means you need to understand what you're looking at, not just process data.

When the community manager is out, you step into that lead position. That's not ceremonial. It means maintaining team momentum, prioritizing daily operations, and handling resident concerns with the same professionalism and follow-through expected at the top of the org chart.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off per week to maintain a 40-hour schedule. Evening and weekend availability may be needed for resident events.

Skills Required vs. Skills Built

This role requires two years of property management experience, with six months in an assistant manager capacity preferred. You'll need a valid driver's license. A CALP credential is a plus but not a requirement. What you genuinely need coming in: comfort with financial reports, delinquency workflows, and the leasing cycle from lead to signed lease.

What the role builds is equally important. Candidates who move through this position well tend to develop sharper instincts around NOI awareness, because reviewing ledgers and tracking delinquency weekly trains you to connect daily decisions to financial outcomes. Conflict resolution skills deepen here too. Handling difficult resident situations regularly, at a level where you're sometimes acting as the most senior person on site, builds a confidence that transfers directly to community manager responsibilities.

Hawthorne offers a formal Career Path Program, and the progression from assistant community manager to community manager is a stated priority within their development structure. The commission and bonus structure (monthly leasing and renewal commissions plus quarterly performance bonuses, in addition to hourly pay) means your effort connects directly to your earnings. That structure also tells you something about what Hawthorne measures: occupancy, renewals, and financial accuracy are the metrics that matter most here.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of assistant manager experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP accreditation a plus

job.title: Market Property Manager I
job.description:
A resident calls Friday afternoon, frustrated about a rent charge they don't recognize. Your maintenance supervisor is waiting on your sign-off for a vendor contract. And your leasing team just flagged an application that needs a second look before the weekend. That's a fairly normal hour as a Property Manager at Stone Run East.

The Work Itself

John M. Corcoran and Company has been operating in New England since 1951, and Stone Run East in Weymouth is part of that portfolio. This is a full-cycle management role. You'll own rent collection and know when to escalate to corrective or legal action. You'll track the competitive market closely enough to bring real recommendations to the Senior Property Manager on rental rates, renewal rents, and marketing direction. Application approvals, annual property audits, internal and external reviews, and ongoing dialogue with ownership representatives on performance goals all fall within your scope.

You'll supervise a team that spans administrative, leasing, and maintenance functions. That means hiring, training, and holding people accountable in a way that keeps morale intact. You'll also monitor capital improvements and negotiate contracts, so comfort with budgets and vendor relationships matters as much as people skills here.

One practical note: the schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, with a 10am to 6pm shift on Wednesdays. If you've only worked a traditional Monday through Friday schedule, it's worth thinking through how that fits your life before applying.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least five years of property management experience, with demonstrated supervisory responsibility
  • Proficiency in affordable housing compliance, which is a real requirement here, not a nice-to-have
  • Working knowledge of Yardi and Microsoft Office
  • Comfort reading and managing to a budget, including capex tracking
  • A steady, strategic approach to both staff performance and property operations

The candidates who tend to stand out aren't just operationally solid. They read people well. Managing a mixed staff across leasing, admin, and maintenance means you're constantly adjusting your communication style, and the best property managers at this level know how to build loyalty without avoiding hard conversations.

JMC offers a pay range of $63,345 to $92,082, a $2,500 sign-on bonus, medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off and holidays, and a 401(k) with a company match. The company's long tenure in the region and its reputation for promoting from within make it a meaningful next step for someone who wants to grow in property management rather than just fill a seat.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Cottonwood Residential is filling an Assistant Property Manager position at Morgan Ridge Apartments in Winston-Salem. If you've spent time on the leasing floor or front desk and you're ready to take on more of the operational side, this is a natural next step.

The day-to-day here covers the full range of what an APM does at a conventional multifamily community. You're handling rent collection, managing delinquency, keeping resident files current, and processing the paperwork that comes with notices and formal correspondence. You'll coordinate with vendors and support leasing activity alongside the property manager. When the PM is out, you run the site. That's not a footnote; it's worth understanding upfront, because it means you need to be comfortable making judgment calls on your own.

Cottonwood has been an early adopter of self-guided tours, which reflects how they approach the leasing process generally. If you've only worked at communities where everything runs through a leasing agent, expect a slightly different rhythm here around prospect traffic and how tours convert.

Weekend availability is required. That's standard for this industry, but it bears saying plainly.

What Cottonwood is Looking For

  • Background in leasing, sales, or customer-facing service
  • Comfort with basic accounting concepts, especially around rent ledgers and delinquency tracking
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Entrata Core experience is a plus, not a requirement
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing law
  • Weekend availability

The compensation package includes a competitive base with quarterly bonuses, full medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage (available within the first month), a 401k with company match, HSA matching, three weeks of PTO in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays. That's a solid benefits structure for a site-level role.

APMs who do this job well tend to move into property manager roles within a couple of years. The skills that carry over are the ones that matter most at that level: delinquency management, vendor coordination, and the ability to hold a community together when the person above you is unavailable. If you treat this as a training ground and pay attention to the financials, the path forward is pretty clear.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor, 1-299 Units - Northglenn, CO
job.description:
Maintenance work in multifamily housing requires a particular combination of technical skill and people management that most trades jobs don't ask for. You're not just fixing things. You're running a team, tracking inventory, enforcing safety protocols, and keeping residents from losing patience. The Maintenance Supervisor role at Carrick Bend in Northglenn, CO asks for all of that at once, every day.

The Skills This Role Draws On

Hands-on technical competency is the baseline, but what separates a good Maintenance Supervisor from a great one is the coaching instinct. You're setting the standard for how your team works, how they prioritize their boards, how they handle a difficult resident interaction at 8am. That means your communication skills get used as much as your tools. Scheduling, quality checks, inventory control, and budget familiarity round out the day-to-day. If you've managed a shop before, you understand that an unorganized supply room and poor key security create downstream problems that show up at the worst possible times.

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties rather than operating under a fee management model. That distinction matters because decisions tend to move faster and the people in the field carry real accountability for outcomes. When the budget for a repair comes up in conversation, you're expected to have context on it.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Tour routes and models need to be inspection-ready. Make-readies need to stay on schedule. Work orders need to close. The property manager depends on you to uphold the physical and procedural standards of the community, which means you're a partner in operations, not just a responder to problems. You'll coach your team, set their daily schedules, monitor output, and step in when quality slips. You'll also field resident interactions directly, and some of those conversations require patience more than anything else.

The honest part: multifamily maintenance supervision isn't a 40-hours-and-done job in most weeks. Emergencies don't schedule themselves, and a community in the 1-299 unit range means your team is lean. You carry more of the weight when someone's out.

What Berkshire Brings to the Table

Berkshire Residential Investments positions itself as a people-first organization, and the benefits package reflects that claim to some degree. Three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and health insurance are included. For someone interested in growing within a nationally operating residential investment company, there's a structure here that supports that.

The minimum bar for this role: two or more years managing maintenance operations on a residential community, plus at least one year of direct team leadership. Comfort with technology and related software is expected.

  • 2+ years of residential maintenance experience in a community setting
  • 1+ year leading a maintenance team
  • Ability to manage schedules, inventory, and basic budget awareness
  • Comfortable with property management software and related tools
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

If you've been a lead tech looking to move into a supervisory seat, this role is a reasonable next step. Maintenance Supervisors who build strong operational track records in roles like this one tend to move toward Regional Maintenance Director positions or transition into facilities management at larger ownership groups.

job.title: Leasing Specialist - Full - Time
job.description:
Student housing leasing runs on a rhythm that's unlike conventional multifamily. Lease-ups concentrate into tight seasonal windows, traffic spikes sharply around university enrollment cycles, and prospects often have parents involved in the decision alongside the student. Redstone Residential manages more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, making it one of the largest third-party student housing operators in the country. This Leasing Specialist role in Provo sits at the front line of that operation.

What the Role Actually Involves

Day to day, you're the first point of contact for prospective residents and a consistent resource for current ones. That means fielding leasing inquiries, walking units, answering ledger questions, helping residents with rent payments, and supporting the Community and Leasing Managers in hitting weekly and monthly KPI goals. The work blends sales, customer service, and basic administrative follow-through in roughly equal measure. Entrata experience is a plus here since Redstone runs on property management software for lease tracking, communications, and reporting. You don't need to know it coming in, but you'll learn it quickly if you join.

The environment is described as entrepreneurial, which in practice means the team moves fast, shares ownership of outcomes, and doesn't wait to be told what needs doing. Staying calm when a frustrated resident has a billing dispute or when traffic peaks during a signing rush is a real skill this role tests regularly.

Skills Required and Skills Built

What you need to bring:

  • One to two years of customer service or sales experience in any setting
  • Clear, professional communication, both written and verbal
  • A warm, approachable manner that holds up under pressure
  • Basic computer proficiency for correspondence and data entry
  • High school diploma or equivalent

What you'll build here is equally worth naming. Leasing Specialists who pay attention to the full operation, not just their own traffic and tours, develop a working knowledge of how occupancy, delinquency, and concessions interact at the property level. That exposure is exactly what prepares someone to step into a Leasing Manager or Assistant Manager role. Redstone's scale across conventional and student housing also means internal mobility is realistic for people who perform well and want to grow.

One honest note: student housing leasing can involve long stretches of high volume followed by slower administrative periods. The ability to stay engaged and productive across both phases matters more than raw energy during peak season alone. Compensation starts at $16.00 per hour with performance bonuses available, and the benefits package includes health, vision, and dental coverage, PTO, paid holidays, 401k matching up to 6%, and parental leave, among others.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Affordable housing management runs on compliance. That's the honest starting point for this role. If your instincts run toward HUD regs, LIHTC reviews, and recertification timelines before you think about curb appeal and lease-up traffic, this position is built around your skillset. Fairstead is hiring a Community Manager at their Covington, Tennessee property, and the work here is compliance-heavy, operationally layered, and not for someone still learning the affordable side of the industry.

The Compliance and Occupancy Core

A significant portion of this role lives in the HUD 4350.3 Handbook. You'll own annual and interim recertification reviews, prep the site for REAC inspections and Management and Occupancy Reviews, and coordinate LIHTC reviews as they come up. When regulatory agencies need responses, you're drafting them in coordination with the compliance department. Tenants who fall out of compliance with lease or program requirements get intervention strategies, not just notices. EIV experience is expected here, and your COS or CPO certification should already be in hand.

TCS certification matters too if the property carries tax credit units, which in affordable housing at this scale, it likely does. Yardi and RealPage experience will serve you well from day one.

Operations, Delinquency, and the Day-to-Day

Beyond compliance, you're running the property. That means monitoring arrears, documenting lease violations, coordinating evictions, and pursuing delinquencies through legal channels when necessary. You'll track bad-debt write-offs, process applications, and collect rents. On the physical side, you supervise preventive and emergency maintenance, coordinate vendor bids and contractor quotes, and conduct unit inspections alongside bi-annual walk-throughs with the Building Superintendent. When construction or renovation work is happening on-site, you're the liaison keeping violations at bay and access coordinated.

Monthly financial meetings are part of the rhythm here. You'll review budgets, flag variances, and make sure the property's needs are documented and planned for, not reactive.

What Fairstead Brings to This Role

Fairstead operates a portfolio of over 30,000 units across 28 states as an integrated owner, developer, and manager. That matters for a site-level manager because the compliance department, construction team, and regional management aren't outsourced partners. They're internal. When you need to coordinate on a MOR or a renovation project, you're working across a unified platform rather than managing a chain of external contacts. The company also takes a tech-forward approach to affordable housing operations, so comfort with data systems and digital workflows fits the culture.

What separates strong candidates in this role from average ones is the ability to hold compliance precision and resident relations in the same hand without letting either slip. Affordable housing residents often have more at stake in their tenancy than market-rate residents do, and the regulatory environment doesn't offer much margin for error. Three or more years of team management experience, a working knowledge of HUD programs, and the certifications to back it up are the baseline. The rest is execution.

  • COS or CPO certification required
  • TCS certification for tax credit properties
  • EIV experience expected
  • Yardi and/or RealPage familiarity preferred
  • Minimum three years of management experience including direct team supervision
  • Affordable housing background required
  • Bachelor's degree preferred

job.title: Business Manager
job.description:
Property management companies that operate across residential, multifamily, and commercial assets need site-level leaders who can hold together leasing, collections, vendor coordination, and compliance without letting any one piece slip. The Business Manager role at Dream Live Prosper Communities sits at that intersection, working out of City Park in the Heights at 1640 East TC Jester Blvd in Houston.

What This Role Actually Covers

This is a full-cycle operations position. You'll support rent collection and delinquency follow-up, supervise leasing activity, execute lease signings and renewals, and maintain the lease and contract files that keep a property legally sound. You'll also coordinate vendors from bid procurement through invoice processing, conduct regular property inspections, and represent the organization at eviction hearings when the process gets to that point. The role requires close collaboration with project and construction teams as the company develops new residential, multifamily, and commercial assets, so you'll gain exposure to pre-leasing and lease-up work, not just stabilized operations.

The position carries a salary range of $45,000 to $55,000 annually and requires a flexible schedule that includes weekend availability.

What You'll Need and What You'll Build

The role requires at least three years of property management or real estate experience. Apartment management background is preferred, and familiarity with AppFolio, HUD programs, and insurance processes will strengthen your candidacy. Strong organizational skills and clear communication are baseline expectations, not things you'll develop on the job here.

Where this role builds skill is in the breadth of asset types you'll touch. Working across residential, multifamily, and commercial properties within a growing portfolio sharpens your ability to shift between operating contexts, a capability that translates directly to regional or portfolio-level roles later. Exposure to construction and development collaboration also gives you a foundation in understanding how properties are set up for success before stabilization, which most site-level managers never get.

  • 3+ years of property management or real estate experience required
  • Apartment management experience preferred
  • AppFolio experience preferred
  • HUD experience preferred
  • Insurance experience a plus
  • Strong organizational and communication skills

Candidates who separate themselves in this kind of role tend to be the ones who treat delinquency and lease compliance as proactive processes rather than reactive ones. If you're already tracking MTM exposure, following up on renewals before they lapse, and keeping vendor relationships organized before problems surface, you'll fit the pace here. Dream Live Prosper Communities is a subsidiary of DLP Capital, which has appeared on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies for 13 consecutive years, so the operational expectations reflect a company that runs at a deliberate tempo.

job.title: Administrative Assistant Apartment Community
job.description:
Property management offices run on paperwork, follow-through, and someone who keeps things from slipping. At a 151-unit community, that person is usually the administrative assistant. The Community Manager can't be in two places at once, and residents don't wait for convenient timing. This role exists to keep the office functional so the rest of the property can stay operational.

Blaisdell Apartments is a manufactured housing community in Minneapolis, managed by Investment Property Group, a firm that owns and operates 150 properties across 13 states. The pay range is $20 to $24 per hour, and the schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most days involve a mix of leasing support and office administration. You'll answer calls and emails from prospective residents, schedule tours, and walk people through the property. You'll process rental applications, chase down missing documents, and help prepare lease paperwork for move-ins. Resident correspondence, filing, data entry, and keeping records accurate and current are regular parts of the day.

You'll also support delinquency tracking and rent collection processes, which means you need to be comfortable having straightforward conversations with residents about their accounts. That's not the most comfortable part of the job, but it's real, and it matters. Community standards don't hold themselves up.

Proficiency in property management software is a genuine requirement here. IPG works with platforms like Yardi, Rent Cafe, Blue Moon, and Vendor Cafe. If you've used any of these before, say so clearly on your application.

Who Does Well in This Role

Strong candidates tend to come in already knowing how to manage competing priorities without needing constant direction. The Community Manager will set the tone, but they're not going to walk you through every task. You'll need to own the administrative side of the office.

  • Experience with leasing documentation, move-in paperwork, or residential records
  • Comfort handling resident complaints without escalating them unnecessarily
  • Familiarity with property management software (any of the platforms listed above)
  • Solid written communication, since a lot of resident correspondence goes out under the office's name
  • A valid driver's license

Manufactured housing communities have a specific resident demographic and culture. The best administrative staff adapt their communication style to fit the community rather than defaulting to one mode. If you've worked in affordable housing, senior housing, or any community with a strong resident culture, that experience translates well here.

This type of role often leads to assistant manager or leasing manager positions for people who develop their leasing and operations skills over time. IPG is a growing company with a national footprint, so internal movement is a real possibility for someone who performs well at the property level.

job.title: Maintenance Technician-Cortland Armour Yards
job.description:
It's 7:15 a.m. and there's already a work order flagged urgent: a resident's AC stopped cooling overnight, and Atlanta in July doesn't forgive slow response times. That's the rhythm of this role at Cortland Armour Yards.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Cortland is a vertically integrated operator with a sizable footprint, which means their maintenance teams carry real responsibility. At Armour Yards, you're handling the full range of building systems: electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliances, flooring, railings, and everything in between. You'll run work orders, support the preventative maintenance schedule, and keep an eye on building systems like automatic doors and surveillance equipment so small issues don't become capex problems. Inventory management matters here too. Running out of a common part mid-turn is the kind of thing that slows down a make-ready and nobody wants that conversation.

On-call rotation is part of the job. Emergencies don't schedule themselves, and Cortland expects you to respond when they happen. Resident interactions come with the territory, and handling them professionally is just as much a part of the job as the technical work itself.

What You Bring

  • EPA certification (Type I, II, or Universal) required before you start
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • One to three or more years in maintenance, facilities, or multifamily housing
  • Solid working knowledge of electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • Ability to prioritize a shifting work order queue without losing track of the details
  • Comfortable with ladders, tools, and working outdoors in Georgia heat
  • Willingness to participate in on-call rotation and respond to after-hours emergencies
  • Clear communication with both residents and teammates

What separates a strong candidate from an average one at a property like this: the ability to diagnose accurately on the first visit. Repeat trips on the same work order signal either a parts problem or a diagnostic problem, and Cortland tracks that. Technicians who close tickets cleanly and document recurring issues before they escalate tend to build credibility fast with site leadership.

Cortland operates as a recognized top-10 multifamily owner and operator nationally, with in-house design, construction, and management functions. For a maintenance technician, that structure can open doors. Techs who develop strong HVAC and electrical skills at a platform like this often move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles as the portfolio grows, and Cortland's growth trajectory has been consistent.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
Regional Manager roles at third-party management firms carry a different weight than in-house equivalents. You're accountable to ownership groups who expect NOI performance and accurate reporting, while simultaneously running the internal operations of a portfolio: hiring, coaching, compliance, leasing strategy, and capital planning. At Asset Living, one of the larger third-party operators in the country with an NMHC top 50 ranking, that dual accountability is the baseline expectation.

What This Role Covers

This is a full-portfolio oversight position based in San Diego. You'll carry responsibility across personnel management, financial performance, leasing strategy, and maintenance operations for a portfolio of multifamily communities. The financial side requires real fluency: developing annual operating budgets, writing monthly variance commentary on income and expense line items, monitoring vendor contracts and capex proposals, and keeping ownership reports accurate at closeout. NOI improvement isn't a background goal here. It's the primary metric, and you'll be expected to identify trends and adjust strategies proactively, not reactively.

On the personnel side, you'll screen, hire, train, and coach on-site staff, including Community Managers. That means handling performance documentation, working with HR on terminations when necessary, approving timesheets, and processing salary increase requests up the chain. The expectation is consistency: using company-standard techniques and benchmarks rather than improvising.

Leasing oversight includes building annual marketing plans, evaluating whether on-site teams are closing effectively, and developing resident retention programs. You'll also stay close to service request turnaround, property appearance, and emergency response protocols, all of which affect both resident satisfaction and liability exposure.

Skills Required vs. Skills Built

This role requires you to arrive with:

  • Experience managing on-site teams across multiple properties
  • Budget development and financial reporting skills, including variance analysis
  • Working knowledge of fair housing guidelines and compliance documentation
  • Comfort with vendor management, bidding processes, and capex oversight
  • Demonstrated ability to handle performance management and HR processes correctly

What the role builds is different. Managing a portfolio for a third-party firm sharpens your ability to communicate financial performance to external ownership groups, which is a distinct skill from internal reporting. You'll also develop deeper fluency in the kind of portfolio-level pattern recognition that separates strong regionals from average ones: spotting delinquency trends early, reading T-3 and T-12 data side by side, and knowing when a property's leasing issues are a training problem versus a pricing problem.

The San Diego Context

San Diego's multifamily market carries high baseline rents and consistently tight occupancy, but operating costs and regulatory complexity are also high. Strong regionals here learn to manage the gap between strong gross revenue and compressed NOI carefully. Vendor relationships matter more in competitive markets where contractor availability tightens during peak make-ready seasons. If you're already operating in this market, that familiarity translates directly into value on day one.

Asset Living's portfolio spans multifamily, single-family rentals, affordable housing, build-to-rent, and student housing, so there's real breadth to grow into as the company expands. For a Regional Manager who performs well, the natural trajectory runs toward Senior Regional, Vice President of Operations, or specialty division leadership within a growing third-party platform.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II
job.description:
The LOFTS at Seacrest Beach sits in one of the more demanding maintenance environments on the Gulf Coast. Rosemary Beach draws residents who expect things to work, and the coastal climate makes sure they're tested constantly. Salt air accelerates corrosion, pool chemistry shifts faster than it does inland, and HVAC systems earn their keep year-round. A Maintenance Technician II here needs to be technically solid and self-sufficient.

Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring for this role at the Seacrest Beach property, and the position carries real responsibility. You'll own your work order queue independently, completing repairs to Hawthorne's standards without needing close supervision. Make-ready work is a core part of the job. When a unit turns, you restore it to move-in condition on schedule. That means punch list execution, not just a walkthrough. Preventative maintenance follows company guidelines, and pool upkeep is part of your rotation. Grounds and common areas stay clean and presentable daily. The shop stays organized well enough that inventory can be assessed at a glance.

On-call rotation is real here. After-hours emergencies happen, and this role participates in that schedule. The Gulf Coast climate means HVAC calls don't slow down because it's inconvenient. If that kind of unpredictability bothers you, this probably isn't the right fit. If it doesn't, the compensation structure reflects the commitment: monthly renewal bonuses, quarterly performance bonuses, and resident satisfaction bonuses stack on top of hourly pay.

What Hawthorne Requires

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Two years of apartment maintenance experience (preferred)
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA/HVAC certification (required)
  • CPO certification (a plus given the pool component)

Hawthorne runs a structured career path program, and Maintenance Technician II is an explicit step on that ladder. The path to Technician III is defined, not vague. The company also offers education reimbursement for technical skill development, which matters if you want to expand into areas like plumbing or electrical without paying out of pocket. Benefits include free dental, medical and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid sick and vacation time (including your birthday), pet insurance, and paid parental leave options.

The technicians who perform best in coastal Class A communities like this one tend to combine strong HVAC and general repair skills with the kind of resident-facing communication that keeps satisfaction scores high. A work order closed fast is good. A resident who feels like they were treated well when it was closed is better. Both matter to how this property performs.

job.title: Limpiador de Plaza Exterior - Alexandria
job.description:
By 7:45 a.m., the sidewalks along the plaza need to be clear, dry, and presentable before the first wave of residents and visitors arrives. That standard doesn't set itself.

The Role

Comstock is hiring an Exterior Porter for its Alexandria, VA portfolio under the ParkX brand. This is a hands-on, boots-on-the-ground position responsible for keeping common areas, lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and public-facing spaces clean and guest-ready throughout every shift. You'll work from daily checklists assigned by the Senior Operations Manager and handle everything from pressure washing designated areas to window cleaning, trash collection, and routine upkeep. When events happen on-site, you support the setup and breakdown. When a cleanliness issue comes up between scheduled tasks, you respond to it directly.

This role requires showing up in the approved ParkX Porter uniform before your shift starts, maintaining your janitorial closet and supply storage in organized condition, and completing end-of-shift documentation so the next person picks up without gaps. You'll also track cleaning supply inventory, flag any safety hazards or maintenance concerns to management, and keep all equipment in working order through regular preventive care. Weekend availability and flexibility during high-traffic events are part of the job.

What Comstock Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Ability to work weekends and outside standard hours, particularly during events
  • Strong time management, communication, and problem-solving skills
  • High reliability and personal accountability
  • Comfortable working independently with minimal supervision
  • Positive, proactive attitude and a customer-focused mindset
  • Ability to lift, push, or pull up to 50 pounds; stand and move for extended periods; work in variable temperatures indoors and outdoors; and handle exposure to cleaning chemicals and environmental conditions

The strongest candidates in this role tend to be self-directed people who notice what needs to be done before anyone asks. Common area cleanliness is a direct input into resident satisfaction scores, and in a mixed-use or transit-oriented environment like Alexandria's Comstock portfolio, the volume of daily foot traffic means a small lapse in standards becomes visible fast. Reliability and attention to detail matter here as much as any technical skill.

Comstock offers medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) with employer match, life insurance, annual professional development funds, free parking with EV charging, and a parental leave program. Benefits may vary by position.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager - Navy Yard - $2,500 Sign-On Bonus
job.description:
Asset Preservation at a Bozzuto Community in Navy Yard

Bozzuto runs some of the more prominent Class A communities in the Mid-Atlantic, and their Navy Yard property sits in one of DC's most active residential corridors. An Assistant Maintenance Manager role here means you're not just fixing things. You're running a program: turns, preventative maintenance schedules, emergency response, and vendor oversight, all while keeping the building's systems and finishes at the standard a Bozzuto lease commands.

The $2,500 sign-on bonus reflects real competition for credentialed trades talent in this market. DC proper has a thin bench of candidates who can competently handle complex mechanical systems alongside the resident-facing side of the job. If you've got the certs and the supervisory experience, that's a combination worth paying for.

What the Role Actually Covers

Day to day, you're managing service ticket completion with the kind of follow-through residents notice, and the kind that protects renewal rates. Make-readies need to move on schedule so units can be leased without delay. Beyond turns, you're running the preventative maintenance program that keeps the building's systems from becoming expensive emergencies. Bozzuto places real emphasis on "preserve and protect," which in practice means you're thinking about asset value every time you walk the property.

On the technical side, the role requires hands-on proficiency across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair. Familiarity with more complex mechanical systems, central plant, boilers, chillers, split systems, is a meaningful differentiator for candidates. Basic carpentry, drywall, and paint round out the punch list work. You'll also manage grounds upkeep, snow removal, and general common area cleanliness, code and OSHA compliance, and you'll carry a rotation on the emergency on-call schedule.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • 5 or more years in trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification (required, not preferred)
  • Supervisory experience and the ability to hold a team accountable without micromanaging
  • Working knowledge of OSHA, MSDS, and risk management practices
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Physical capability to lift 25 to 50 pounds regularly and work in varying outdoor conditions

The candidates who thrive in this kind of role at a Bozzuto property tend to be the ones who take the building personally. They know every mechanical room, they track their PM schedule without being reminded, and they communicate with residents like adults. The supervisory piece matters too: you're a player-coach here, and the team will follow your lead on standards and professionalism.

Compensation runs $66,560 to $69,160 annually, plus bonus eligibility and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Olympus Las Colinas
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

At Olympus Las Colinas, the Assistant Manager sits at the intersection of resident experience and property financials. On any given day, that means posting rent, reconciling deposits before bank close, and reviewing move-out condition reports to get final account statements out accurately and on time. Delinquency doesn't wait, and neither does this role.

You'll keep resident files current, handle confidential records with care, and make sure every dollar collected hits the operations system correctly. When the Property Manager is out, you run the show. That includes fielding resident complaints, coordinating with the leasing team, walking make-ready units before move-in to catch punch list items, and keeping an eye on what's happening in the Las Colinas submarket: new lease-up activity nearby, competing concessions, hiring trends that drive renter demand in the area.

You'll also step into a leasing support role when traffic picks up. Showing units, supporting retention efforts, and participating in community events are part of the job, not exceptions to it. The role requires weekend availability on the first weekend of each month and some flexibility for after-hours resident events.

What You Bring

  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant
  • Hands-on familiarity with RealPage, Onesite, or Knock (strongly preferred)
  • Comfort handling collections, deposits, and financial recordkeeping with accuracy
  • Ability to assess move-out conditions and document apartment disposition properly
  • Strong attention to detail on both the people side and the numbers side of operations
  • Clear communication when escalating liability claims or legal matters to the Property Manager or Regional

The Role in Context

Irving's multifamily market is competitive, with significant Class A inventory in and around Las Colinas. An Assistant Manager who tracks local occupancy trends, watches competitive concessions, and understands what's being built nearby gives a property a real operational edge. Keeping delinquency low and renewals high directly protects NOI, and this role touches both levers daily.

For candidates thinking about career trajectory: strong Assistant Managers at portfolio companies like Olympus typically move into Property Manager or Business Manager roles as communities open or turnover creates opportunity. Olympus has noted active career pathing support as part of their structure, which matters if you're thinking beyond your next job title.

Compensation starts at $22 to $23 per hour, with monthly renewal bonuses and quarterly bonuses on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, an apartment rental allowance, tuition reimbursement, and a sabbatical program. Olympus has earned recognition as a top employer from the National Apartment Association three consecutive years running (2023, 2024, 2025).

job.title: Communications Associate
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Scion operates student housing communities across the country, and this role sits at the intersection of resident relations, reputation management, and cross-functional communication at the corporate level. As a Communications Associate based out of Scion's Chicago headquarters, you'll handle inbound contacts from residents and guarantors across phone, email, chat, and social channels. That includes everything from routine questions to sensitive, high-stakes complaints that require coordination with legal or operations leadership before you respond.

A significant portion of the work involves managing online review responses across multiple platforms, which means you're not just answering residents directly. You're shaping how Scion's communities appear publicly to prospective residents and their families. You'll also work alongside on-site teams to build their capacity in reputation management, review strategy, and proactive resident engagement, including tools like Review Harvest and Entrata. When incidents or operational disruptions hit a community, you'll help coordinate resident communications so that messaging stays consistent and on-brand under pressure.

Beyond individual interactions, you'll track feedback patterns, flag recurring themes, and contribute to the internal resources that keep communication consistent: templates, FAQs, and response guidelines. The documentation side of this role is real. You'll maintain records in a reputation tracker and help inform the broader strategy based on what you're hearing from residents day to day.

What You Bring

  • A bachelor's degree in Communications, Marketing, Hospitality, or a related field, or comparable professional experience
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write clearly under pressure and across different tones and audiences
  • Genuine comfort handling difficult conversations without becoming reactive or dismissive
  • Organizational discipline to manage multiple open cases, follow-up threads, and documentation tasks simultaneously
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; familiarity with ClickUp or Entrata is a plus
  • The ability to work independently and coordinate across teams without needing heavy oversight

Context Worth Knowing

Student housing operates on a cycle that's distinct from conventional multifamily. Guarantors (typically parents) are often as engaged as the residents themselves, and that dual audience shapes how communications need to be framed. Lease-up seasons, move-in windows, and academic calendars create predictable spikes in volume and urgency. Someone who can anticipate those pressure points and help communities prepare for them will add real value in this role beyond just answering tickets.

The $58,000 to $60,000 salary range reflects a corporate associate-level position with a clear path toward senior communications, reputation strategy, or operations support roles as Scion's portfolio continues to grow. Hours are primarily standard business hours, though some evening and weekend coverage is expected to meet resident needs. The role is fully in-office at Scion's Chicago headquarters.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
Curb appeal drives leasing traffic. Residents notice a well-kept community before they notice the unit finishes, the amenity package, or the rent. That's why the groundskeeper role carries more weight than its entry-level label suggests. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, this position in Jamestown, NC keeps the exterior of an apartment community looking like people actually care about it, because someone does.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your day happens outside, and that's by design. You'll move through the property consistently, picking up debris, clearing sidewalks and breezeways, keeping parking lots clean, and making sure pet stations and compactor areas don't become eyesores. Pool decks, courtyards, grilling stations, and outdoor seating areas all fall within your scope. Light landscaping tasks like raking, weeding, and trimming come up regularly, directed by the maintenance team.

You'll also handle smaller but visible details: replacing burned-out exterior bulbs, doing touch-up painting on curbs and signposts, and keeping the maintenance shop and storage areas organized. When a unit turns, you may assist with light cleaning or debris removal to help the team move through make-readies faster. During seasonal shifts, you'll support storm prep and cleanup. And from time to time, you'll distribute resident communications door to door, which puts you in direct contact with the people who live there.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM, with participation in an on-call rotation for after-hours needs.

Who Fits Well Here

A high school diploma or GED is required. A valid driver's license is required. Some background in yardwork or general facility upkeep is expected. Prior maintenance or repair experience is a plus, but Hawthorne has built a formal career path program specifically to develop people who don't yet have a full technical skill set.

What actually separates people who thrive in this role from those who don't isn't experience level. It's consistency. Showing up, completing the full walk of the property, not letting small things slide, and treating residents and coworkers with basic respect. A groundskeeper who does those things well tends to get noticed by maintenance leadership, and Hawthorne's internal career path formally supports movement from this role toward Maintenance Technician I and beyond.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • Some yardwork or facility maintenance experience expected
  • One year of maintenance or HVAC experience preferred, not required

Compensation includes an hourly rate plus a monthly renewal bonus program. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and 24/7 telehealth access.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Maintenance work at a residential community runs on a specific combination of hands-on trade knowledge and people skills. At Stonebriar of Frisco Apartments, a Cottonwood Residential community in Frisco, TX, you'll use both every day. The technical side covers plumbing repairs, electrical troubleshooting, general carpentry, and HVAC diagnostics. The human side means showing up to a resident's door, explaining what you're doing, and leaving the unit better than you found it. If you hold EPA Type II or Universal certification, or a CPO cert, those credentials give you a head start. HVAC troubleshooting experience is genuinely useful here, not just a checkbox.

This is an entry-level position, which means Cottonwood isn't expecting a seasoned maintenance supervisor. They're looking for someone who learns quickly, communicates clearly in English (written and verbal), and can handle the physical demands of the job: lifting up to 50 lbs., working on ladders and scaffolding, and spending most of the day on your feet. A valid driver's license is required.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical day moves between work orders and whatever comes up unexpectedly. You might start the morning running a make-ready punch list on a vacated unit, then shift to a plumbing call in the afternoon, then help with a grounds issue before the end of your shift. Evenings and weekends are part of the schedule, and on-call rotation means you'll occasionally respond to after-hours emergencies. You won't be handling those calls alone. The Service Manager provides backup and guidance, especially while you're still learning the property and the company's standards.

That on-call piece is worth being honest about. It's a real commitment, and it affects your schedule in ways that a standard 9-to-5 doesn't. For the right person, it's also where you build trust with residents fast. Showing up reliably during a leak or a lockout leaves a stronger impression than a dozen routine work orders.

What Makes Cottonwood a Particular Fit

Cottonwood Residential has positioned itself as a company that moves early on technology adoption. Their rollout of Self-Guided Tours is one example of how they approach the resident experience differently. For a maintenance tech, that context matters because it signals a company culture that values service delivery as a differentiator, not just a checkbox. Your work directly supports the experience residents have, from the condition of their units to how quickly problems get resolved.

The benefits package is worth noting for an entry-level role. Health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage becomes available within the first 30 days. The company also offers a 401(k) with a match, an HSA match, 120 hours of paid time off in year one, and 10.5 paid holidays. That's a meaningful package at this level of the career path.

For technicians looking at where this role leads: strong performers in entry-level maintenance positions typically move into lead tech or Service Manager roles as they build certifications and property-specific experience. EPA Universal and CPO certifications, in particular, open doors across the industry and increase your value on any property, regardless of where your career takes you.

job.title: Sales & Resident Experience Consultant - Georgetown, TX
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the front door of Villages of Georgetown, a Berkshire-owned and managed community in the Georgetown, TX market. You're the first real human interaction most prospects have with the property, and that matters. Your day moves between giving tours, following up on leads, closing leases, and making sure the office and model units are ready to show at a moment's notice. Berkshire expects a closing ratio of at least 20%, so you'll need to read prospects well, understand what they're looking for, and guide them toward a decision without being pushy about it.

Beyond leasing, you stay plugged into what's happening locally: which competitors are running concessions, where occupancy trends are heading, and what's driving traffic to the property. You bring those observations to your property manager and contribute ideas for improving marketing and resident satisfaction. Resident communication doesn't stop at the lease signing either. Strong written and verbal follow-through with current residents is part of keeping the community feeling well-run and cared for.

Tour routes and model units are your showcase. You're responsible for keeping them looking sharp, which means inspecting them regularly and flagging anything that's off. Small details add up when someone's deciding where to live.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience, leasing or otherwise
  • A genuine comfort with people: different personalities, different situations, different needs
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Solid administrative habits and attention to detail
  • Ability to pick up new technology without much friction
  • Energy that holds up across a full shift, not just the first hour

The Human Side of This Role

Georgetown has grown quickly over the last several years, and that growth brings a mix of prospective residents: retirees, remote workers relocating from larger metros, and families looking for space outside Austin. Knowing how to read different buyer personalities and adjust your approach is what separates a consultant who hits quota from one who builds genuine community trust. Residents who feel heard during the leasing process tend to renew. That connection starts with you.

Berkshire operates as both owner and manager, which means the decisions made at the property level actually matter to the investment side of the business. You're not working for a third-party operator trying to satisfy an outside client. That structure tends to give on-site teams a bit more autonomy and accountability at the same time. Benefits include three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, and personal development plans, among others.

job.title: Front Door Waste Technician-Cortland Sunbury Ridge
job.description:
Valet trash is one of those amenity services that residents notice immediately when it goes wrong and barely think about when it goes right. The Front Door Waste Technician at Cortland's Sunbury Ridge community in Columbus is the person who keeps it invisible in the best possible way: routes completed consistently, common areas clean, and residents who never have to wonder whether their bag got picked up.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Each shift, you'll walk the property collecting waste bags from resident doorsteps, transferring them into leak-proof carts and then into the designated vehicle for disposal at onsite compactors or containers. The route covers the full community, including stairwells, and you'll also clear trash from dog waste stations, pool areas, mail kiosks, parking lots, and other shared spaces. When there's a spill or debris near a compactor, you're the one who handles it before it becomes a bigger problem.

Prohibited or improperly disposed waste gets flagged and addressed according to company protocol, and you'll document your work through a mobile app, logging start and end times and capturing photos as needed. Cortland operates with clear productivity standards, so completing routes efficiently and on schedule matters.

You'll interact with residents, leasing staff, and management throughout your shifts. That contact is brief but meaningful. A friendly, professional presence on the property reinforces the resident experience that Cortland builds its reputation around.

What You Bring to the Role

  • At least one year of experience in waste services or a customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of EPA and OSHA regulations related to waste handling
  • Physical ability to climb stairs, walk extended distances, and lift up to 50 lbs
  • Comfort working outdoors in variable weather and tolerating strong odors
  • A valid Class E driver's license and ability to drive locally as needed
  • A personal smartphone (Android 2.2+ or iPhone iOS 4.3+) with an active data plan for app-based reporting
  • A high school diploma or equivalent is preferred
  • Bilingual ability is a plus

The Bigger Picture

Cortland is a vertically integrated owner and operator ranked among the top ten multifamily firms in the country. That structure means decisions about how a property looks and functions are made internally, and the people doing the daily work are genuinely part of how the company delivers on its resident-centric model. Sunbury Ridge is one community in a national portfolio, but how it's maintained day to day reflects directly on what Cortland promises residents.

Candidates who stand out in this kind of role tend to be self-directed on route and don't need supervision to stay on pace. They also understand that regular contact with residents, even quick exchanges at the door, is part of the job. The combination of physical reliability and consistent professionalism is what makes the difference between someone who fills the role and someone who owns it.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Lincoln Property Company runs a substantial commercial portfolio, and this Assistant Property Manager role sits at the intersection of tenant relations, financial reporting, and day-to-day operations. The skills that get used hardest here are financial literacy, lease administration, and vendor management. If you're comfortable reading a management agreement, understanding CAM reconciliation methodology, and tracking invoice approvals against authorization limits, this role will feel like natural territory.

The Financial and Lease Side

A meaningful portion of this role lives in the numbers. You'll support monthly reporting packages and budget deliverables, which means you need to understand what you're looking at: operating expenses, variance explanations, and the kind of basic financial analysis that turns raw data into a coherent picture for a client. CAM and OpEx reconciliations require close coordination with the accounting team, and the accuracy of that work has direct implications for tenant billing and client trust. Lease administration runs parallel to this: setup, amendments, move-in and move-out documentation, and keeping the applicable systems current. Commercial leases carry real financial weight, and keeping lease data clean is not a back-office afterthought.

Operations and Tenant Management

On the operational side, you'll coordinate tenant needs with building staff and vendors, making sure response times and outcomes stay within the bounds of policy and lease obligations. Vendor invoice review, procurement support, and participation in bidding processes round out the daily workload. You'll also participate in property inspections and walk-throughs alongside the Property Manager and tenant improvement teams, so comfort on a commercial property floor plate is part of the job. Emergency response planning and drill participation are also in scope.

This is an in-office, Dallas-based role with regular travel to assigned properties. Remote work isn't available.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • A bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of experience and coursework
  • One to two years of related experience, ideally in commercial office, retail, or industrial property
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills; familiarity with AP and CMMS platforms is a real advantage
  • Comfort with financial terms and intermediate calculations, including percentages and basic variance analysis
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to keep difficult conversations constructive
  • Organizational discipline to manage multiple deliverables across a property or small portfolio

The candidates who stand out in commercial APM roles typically know how to read a lease abstract and connect what it says to what gets billed. CAM rec season separates people who understand cost pools and gross-up provisions from those who are just entering data. Coming in with that baseline puts you ahead of the curve on Lincoln's reporting cycle.

Lincoln Property Company offers a benefits package covering medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and AD&D insurance, a 401(k) plan, flexible time off, paid sick leave, and company-paid holidays. Additional voluntary benefits may vary by location.

job.title: Business Manager, Property Operations
job.description:
The delinquency report lands in your inbox at 8 a.m., two properties are flagging collections issues, and a regional portfolio manager needs updated capex tracking before the afternoon call. That's a Tuesday.

Asset Living, one of the NMHC top 50 management firms and an IREM Accredited Management Organization, is hiring a Business Manager, Property Operations to support a regional portfolio out of Reno, Nevada. Founded in 1986, Asset Living operates across multifamily, affordable housing, build-to-rent, student housing, and single-family rental divisions. This is a third-party management environment, which means client expectations, jurisdictional compliance, and operational consistency across multiple sites are all live concerns every week.

What the Role Covers

Occupancy management is a core part of the work. You'll support retention strategies and renewal workflows, handle resident escalations, and oversee tenant-based voucher administration and its associated compliance requirements. On the maintenance side, you'll monitor service quality, track work order completion, and partner with site teams on preventive maintenance schedules to keep resident satisfaction from eroding.

The financial piece carries real weight here. You'll own delinquency oversight and rent recovery workflows, ensure move-out charges and timelines meet jurisdictional requirements, track capex against approved budgets, and manage the full invoice cycle from PO matching through vendor payment coordination with Accounts Payable. Compliance runs through every function: federal, state, and local regulations, internal Asset Living standards, lease enforcement, evictions, and coordination with outside counsel when disputes escalate.

You'll work closely with Regional Portfolio Managers, Community Managers, and leasing teams to drive KPIs across the assigned portfolio. That means pulling operational and financial data, identifying trends before they become problems, and keeping execution consistent across properties that may differ in asset class or regulatory environment.

What You Bring

  • Minimum three years of multifamily property management, operations, or asset management experience
  • Proficiency in Yardi, RealPage, MRI, or a comparable property management platform
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office and Google Workspace
  • Demonstrated understanding of leasing operations, financial controls, and regulatory compliance
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; bilingual Spanish/English preferred
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree in business, real estate, or a related field preferred
  • Must reside in Reno, Nevada; approximately 10% travel for property visits and internal meetings

The candidates who stand out in roles like this one tend to be operationally fluent across both the numbers and the compliance side. Knowing how to read a T-12 matters, but so does understanding what happens when a jurisdictional notice deadline gets missed. This role sits at that intersection, and comfort in both areas separates strong performers from candidates who lean only one direction.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Olympus at Memorial
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Assistant Manager at Olympus at Memorial sits at the intersection of financial accountability and daily operations. On any given morning, you're verifying that all rent receipts from the prior day cleared properly, reviewing delinquency to flag anything that needs a notice or a call, and cross-checking move-out account statements before they go out. Accuracy here matters. A misposted payment or a late deposit doesn't just create a bookkeeping headache. It affects the property's cash position and your T-12 picture.

Beyond the ledger, you're the operational backbone when the Property Manager is out. That means handling resident complaints before they escalate, inspecting make-ready units ahead of move-ins, and jumping into leasing traffic when the floor needs coverage. Olympus at Memorial expects you to know the submarket too. New construction in the Memorial corridor, hiring trends from nearby employers, concession activity at competing communities. That market awareness directly informs how you position the property on any given week.

Resident retention is part of the job description here, not an afterthought. You'll participate in community events and contribute to renewal efforts, which means the role touches occupancy and renewal rates in a real, measurable way. The base pay runs $22 to $23 per hour, with monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses layered on top.

What You Bring

  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant
  • Comfort with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite (strongly preferred)
  • Solid grasp of rent collection procedures, including daily deposit requirements
  • Ability to assess move-out conditions and produce accurate final account statements
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with flexibility for the first weekend of each month and occasional after-hours events
  • Detail orientation that holds up under volume, not just on quiet days

Where This Role Sits in the Bigger Picture

Assistant Manager is the standard proving ground for a Property Manager seat. Owners and regional managers watch how candidates handle delinquency management, whether they catch punch list issues before a resident moves in and discovers them, and how they perform when the manager is out. The candidates who move up fastest are the ones who treat the financial records with the same urgency they bring to resident relations. Both matter. Neither covers for weakness in the other.

Olympus Property has held a spot on the National Apartment Association's Top Employer list three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), and the company offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operated for over 70 years, managing more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. Their Bexley Summerhill community in Atlanta's Summerhill neighborhood is looking for a Leasing Consultant, and the way they've written this posting tells you something useful: they're not screening for a resume, they're screening for a person.

That's worth taking seriously. Weinstein trains from the ground up, and a meaningful number of their current leaders started exactly where this role begins. The company's hands-on ownership model means decisions happen closer to the property level than at most large institutional operators, and that tends to create more visible career paths for people who perform well on-site.

The role itself covers the full breadth of leasing work.
