You'll be the first contact for prospects, walking them through the community, handling follow-up, and working toward move-in goals that come with monthly bonuses on top of your base hourly rate and quarterly bonuses. But it doesn't stop at sales. You'll handle resident concerns, help maintain the property's appearance, and pitch in on administrative tasks. On a given day, you might greet a walk-in, respond to a maintenance-related complaint, prep a unit for a showing, and close out paperwork before end of shift. The role rewards people who can shift gears without losing momentum.

The schedule runs weekdays 9 to 6, with Saturdays 9 to 5 shared on a team rotation. Sundays are off. You should expect occasional evening or weekend commitments around resident events or weather-related needs. That's part of on-site life and worth knowing upfront.

What separates strong candidates here is less about prior leasing knowledge and more about how they handle the parts of the job that aren't glamorous. Anyone can be warm and engaging when a tour is going well. The people who advance are the ones who stay organized under interruption, follow through on small tasks without being reminded, and genuinely enjoy solving problems for residents who are frustrated. Summerhill is a growing neighborhood, which means traffic will likely include a mix of first-time renters and people relocating to Atlanta, so comfort with varied audiences matters.

What Weinstein is looking for

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • A customer-first approach, especially when situations are difficult
  • Comfort with a role that blends sales, service, and administrative work
  • Reliability and a collaborative attitude on a small on-site team
  • Goal orientation and the drive to meet leasing targets
  • Prior leasing experience is welcome but not required

Starting pay is $20 per hour, increasing with experience, plus the bonus structure noted above. Weinstein is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Santa Rosa
job.description:
A prospect walks in on a Saturday afternoon, having driven by the community twice before finally stopping. Within the first few minutes of that conversation, you'll qualify their interest, match them to an available floor plan, and start building the kind of trust that turns a tour into a signed lease. That's the core of this role.

What This Role Covers

MG Properties is hiring a Leasing Consultant for Santa Rosa Apartments in Wildomar, CA. With more than 30 years operating apartment communities across the Western U.S., MG Properties manages properties with a clear emphasis on resident experience and internal growth. This position sits at the front line of both.

Day to day, you'll greet and qualify prospective residents, guide them through tours, prepare leases, and oversee signings. You'll coordinate with the maintenance team to make sure new residents move in without friction, and you'll keep rental files accurate and current. When residents have questions, complaints, or maintenance concerns, you handle those interactions professionally and see them through to resolution. Monthly administrative tasks and data entry into the property management system are part of the rhythm as well.

Occupancy is the measurable outcome of this work. Every leasing interaction, follow-up call, and move-in coordination either supports or erodes it. You'll be expected to understand that connection and treat it as a professional standard, not just a company metric.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

This role requires strong sales instincts paired with genuine customer service ability. You need to be comfortable qualifying applicants thoroughly, managing paperwork accurately, and communicating clearly with both prospects and current residents. At least one year of property management experience is preferred, and professional etiquette is non-negotiable given the volume and variety of resident interactions.

What the role builds is equally worth noting. Leasing Consultants at companies that promote from within (MG Properties explicitly does) tend to move into Assistant Manager roles once they've demonstrated lease-up competency, administrative accuracy, and the ability to handle resident relations without escalation. The combination of sales performance data and file management discipline you develop here translates directly into the skills property management companies look for when hiring for their next tier.

  • Base pay: $22 to $23 per hour
  • Monthly and quarterly bonuses, plus company profit sharing
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 10 days PTO, 10 paid holidays, 2 personal days, and 40 hours paid sick time annually
  • Rental discounts, FSA, dependent care spending account, and employee assistance program

If you take the administrative side of leasing as seriously as the sales side, and you want to work somewhere that tracks that, this is a position worth pursuing.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Single-family rental management operates differently from traditional multifamily. There's no central leasing office, no on-site team to call, and properties are spread across neighborhoods rather than clustered in one building. That model works well for investors, but it puts real demand on the maintenance technicians who keep those homes in good shape. This role at Roofstock sits squarely in that world.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most days, you're moving between properties across the Tampa area, working from a company vehicle with a gas card. Your schedule is structured around service orders, make-readies, and property inspections rather than a fixed site. You'll handle HVAC, plumbing, and electrical repairs across the portfolio, and you'll also prepare vacant homes for incoming residents, which means completing turns efficiently and to a consistent standard.

Inspections are a regular part of the job too. Move-in and move-out walkthroughs, onboarding audits for newly acquired properties, and quality checks on work completed by outside vendors. That last piece matters more than it sounds. When a third-party contractor finishes a job, you're the one verifying it was done right before the company signs off. That requires both technical knowledge and the judgment to push back when something doesn't meet the mark.

Work orders come through a mobile app, and you'll use it throughout the day to log progress, communicate updates, and post legal notices as needed. If you're the type who prefers pen and paper and a single fixed location, this setup will feel uncomfortable. If you're organized, self-directed, and comfortable with digital tools, it fits naturally.

Who Tends to Succeed Here

The schedule is genuinely different from most maintenance roles: full-time hours, no on-call rotation, no weekends. That's a real quality-of-life difference, and it attracts technicians who've burned out on the traditional emergency-response model. What the role trades in return is independence. You're not working alongside a maintenance supervisor or a team. You're the one making judgment calls in the field.

  • HVAC Type II Certification is required; Universal Certification is preferred and worth having
  • Valid driver's license, since the vehicle and travel are central to the role
  • Comfort troubleshooting across trades, not just one specialty
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs, climb, bend, and work in both indoor and outdoor conditions
  • U.S. work authorization (no visa sponsorship available)

Pay runs $25 to $30 per hour depending on experience, licensure, and location. Strong candidates bring a track record across multiple trade types, not just HVAC, because a scattered residential portfolio generates a wide variety of repair needs on any given day. The technicians who thrive here are the ones who can close out five different work orders in five different neighborhoods and still do each one carefully.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Leasing isn't spread across twelve months of steady traffic. It compresses, it surges, and then Turn arrives and everything happens at once. The Experience Team Member role at Ion at the Ballpark exists because Scion understands that in student living, the leasing relationship doesn't end at the signed lease. It continues through move-in, through the academic year, and right up to renewal season.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-cycle customer-facing position, not a pure leasing role. You'll conduct community and amenity tours, field prospect and resident inquiries, and assist with social media and local marketing outreach. On the administrative side, expect package logging, office and amenity upkeep, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout coverage on rotation. The job description notes the responsibilities aren't exhaustive, which in student housing means you should assume the list will expand during peak periods.

Availability during summer and Turn is a real requirement here, not a formality. Turn at a student property is controlled chaos at best. If you haven't worked one before, it's worth knowing what you're signing up for: compressed timelines, high unit volume, and residents moving in and out on the same weekend.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • Genuine comfort working with a college-aged resident base and their parents
  • Strong communication skills across in-person, phone, and digital channels
  • Reliability and self-discipline, particularly for the on-call rotation
  • Flexibility in a leasing calendar that shifts with academic cycles
  • A customer-first instinct, not just a sales instinct

The candidates who do well in this kind of role tend to be organized enough to manage admin tasks without losing their energy on the floor. Student residents notice when the person giving them a tour is distracted or going through the motions. The ones who build real rapport, who actually know the neighborhood and can speak to the Birmingham market around the Ballpark District, tend to drive better close rates and better renewal conversations.

Scion offers health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid time off, paid parental and maternal leave, learning reimbursement, and a discretionary annual bonus. This is a non-exempt hourly position. Work authorization is required. Visa sponsorship is not available.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager of Permanent Supportive Housing (Immanuel Sobrato)
job.description:
Affordable housing management carries compliance weight that market-rate property work typically doesn't. At a property like Immanuel Sobrato, a permanent supportive housing community in San Jose, that means layering HUD, Tax Credit, and welfare exemption requirements on top of standard daily operations. MidPen Housing has been doing exactly this work since 1970, and this assistant-level role sits directly inside that operational reality.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The Assistant Community Manager here supports the full operating cycle of a permanent supportive housing property. On any given day, that means scheduling income verification appointments, processing lease agreements, managing the waitlist, and helping residents understand emergency preparedness procedures. Turnover work involves scheduling vacancies, preparing and monitoring turn forms, and coordinating with facilities staff to keep work orders moving. Rent collection, security deposit processing, petty cash logs, and bank deposit prep also fall within this role's scope.

Compliance is a meaningful part of the job. You'll assist with annual recertifications, welfare exemption documentation, and preparation for Management and Occupancy Reviews (MOR) and TCAC audits. File integrity matters here in a way that goes beyond the ordinary: resident files contain sensitive information, and maintaining confidentiality under audit conditions is a baseline expectation, not an occasional task.

The role also requires real relationship management. MidPen's property teams work closely with onsite Resident Services staff, local law enforcement, and community partners. At a permanent supportive housing property, those relationships carry more operational weight than at a standard affordable or market-rate community.

What MidPen Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED with at least one year of residential property management, customer service, or administrative experience (or an equivalent combination)
  • Proficiency in MS Office; RealPage experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with genuine attention to detail
  • Ability to work independently and stay organized across multiple compliance and operational tracks
  • Alignment with MidPen's mission around affordable housing and resident stability

Candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this have some prior exposure to income-restricted housing, even at the administrative level. Understanding the difference between a TCAC review and a standard lease audit, or knowing why recertification timelines matter, shortens the learning curve considerably. That said, MidPen explicitly considers equivalent experience, so strong administrative or customer service backgrounds from adjacent fields are worth presenting clearly.

The pay range is $23.27 to $26.18 per hour, based on experience. MidPen offers health, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement, FSA options, and an EAP program, among other benefits.

job.title: Groundskeeper (Lease Up)
job.description:
The morning starts before most residents have poured their first cup of coffee. You're doing a walkthrough of the grounds, checking that the property looks exactly the way it should when the first person steps outside. On a lease-up community, that standard matters even more: every prospective resident who tours the property is forming a first impression, and curb appeal either supports or undercuts everything the leasing team says.

The Work Itself

This is a Groundskeeper role supporting a lease-up community for Prometheus Real Estate Group in Los Altos, California. The core of the job is maintaining the physical condition and cleanliness of the property: common areas, exteriors, landscaping details, trash, and anything that affects how the community looks and feels to the people who live there and those considering it. You'll work with some independence, managing your own daily tasks without needing step-by-step supervision, while staying responsive to resident needs and the expectations of a team that takes curb appeal seriously.

Customer service is genuinely part of this job. Residents notice the person maintaining their community, and how you engage with them shapes how they feel about where they live. On a lease-up property, that sense of pride in the community is still being built, and everyone on the maintenance and grounds team contributes to it.

The physical demands are real. The role requires regular lifting (up to 50 lbs occasionally), extended time on your feet, climbing, and repetitive physical tasks. Prior custodial or apartment experience is helpful but not required to be considered.

Compensation and Benefits

The pay range for this position runs from $21.75 to $23.25 per hour, and Prometheus layers in additional earning opportunities including a discretionary semi-annual bonus, standby and on-call premium pay, a lease-up bonus, and referral and training bonuses where applicable. The benefits package is notably strong for a grounds-level role:

  • Medical, vision, and dental coverage at 100% company-paid (including eligible dependents), with buy-up options
  • Life insurance, AD&D, and long-term disability coverage
  • 24/7 behavioral health program access
  • Tax-free flexible spending accounts
  • 401(k) with employer matching
  • 10 days vacation to start, increasing with tenure, plus anniversary vacation at milestone years
  • 9 sick days annually, 12 paid holidays including your birthday
  • Paid volunteer time
  • Tenure-based housing discounts and educational assistance with tuition reimbursement

For someone entering property management, a role like this builds habits that carry forward throughout a maintenance career: attention to detail on make-readies, understanding how curb appeal connects to occupancy, and the discipline of maintaining standards on a schedule without being managed closely. Groundskeeping on a lease-up is a sharper environment than a stabilized property because the stakes of first impressions are higher and the expectations are set accordingly. That's a useful place to develop your eye for quality.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role splits its time across two pretty different kinds of work, and you need to be comfortable with both. On the leasing side, you're fielding leads, running tours, walking prospects through applications, and working to hit occupancy goals. You're also managing renewals and thinking about resident retention, because a lease that doesn't renew is a turn that costs money and time.

On the financial side, you're handling rent collection, payment posting, ledger reviews, and delinquency follow-up. That means weekly calls to residents behind on rent, coordinating with the Community Manager on eviction procedures when it gets to that point, and making sure account records are clean before they go up the chain. If you're not comfortable with that side of the work, this role will be harder than it looks.

You'll also step into the lead role when the Community Manager is out. That's not a ceremonial title. It means the team looks to you, residents escalate to you, and you're the one keeping operations on track until they're back.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with Saturdays from 10 to 4. One weekday off per week keeps it at 40 hours, but resident events and community needs can pull you in on evenings or weekends. That's the nature of on-site work.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of property management experience, with some time in an assistant manager role preferred
  • Comfort reading financial reports, catching billing errors, and making decisions with budget awareness
  • Leasing instincts: you know how to read a prospect, show a home, and close without being pushy
  • A valid driver's license
  • CALP accreditation is a plus, not a requirement
  • High school diploma or GED

Context Worth Knowing

Hawthorne Residential Partners manages communities across the Southeast and ranks among the top 50 largest multifamily operators in the country. The Oasis at Southpark sits in Lake Charles, Louisiana. This is a fee-managed portfolio where regional visibility matters, so your financial reporting and documentation need to be accurate and timely, not just close enough.

The career path here is real. Assistant Community Manager is a direct stepping stone to Community Manager, and Hawthorne has a formal development program to move people along that track. If you want that progression, the skill set you build here, reading a T-12, managing delinquency, running a team under pressure, carries directly into the next role.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k with match, paid time off including your birthday, pet insurance, and paid parental and adoption leave.

job.title: Concierge- Luxury Highrise (M-F 4pm-12am)
job.description:
This role runs on interpersonal skill and situational awareness. You're reading a lobby full of residents, guests, and prospects all at once, deciding who needs a warm greeting, who needs a quick answer, and who needs to be politely redirected. At a luxury high-rise in Reston, that judgment call happens dozens of times per shift.

What This Role Actually Requires

Customer service is the core skill here, but the specific application matters. Luxury residential concierge work sits somewhere between hospitality and security. You're coordinating amenity reservations, managing loading dock and elevator bookings, fielding calls, and keeping the front desk area clean and organized. You're also doing daily building walks to catch maintenance items before residents notice them. The shift runs 4pm to midnight, Monday through Friday, which means you're covering the high-traffic evening hours when residents come home, guests arrive, and deliveries need to be managed.

Strong problem-solving matters more than most postings let on. Evening shifts don't have a full management team behind you. When something comes up, you handle it or you escalate it correctly. Either way, the decision is yours in the moment.

Qualifications Worth Noting

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • At least one year of concierge or high-end customer service experience preferred
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office, especially Outlook, Word, and Excel
  • Ability to work holidays and pick up additional shifts when needed
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

Working at Comstock

Comstock manages a growing residential portfolio, which means there's real room to move into leasing or property management roles over time. Concierge positions at Class A properties are a common entry point for people who want to build a career in residential property management. You're learning how a luxury building operates from the front lines, which is useful context if you move toward leasing, assistant management, or community management later.

The benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, 401k match, life insurance, parental leave, commuter benefits, free parking with EV charging, and a housing discount. Comstock also provides annual professional development funds. Pay for this position ranges from $18 to $22 per hour, depending on experience.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Part-Time
job.description:
It's 7:45 a.m. and a new resident moves in at noon. The apartment needs a final walk, a light bulb swapped, and the grounds outside the building need a quick pass before the leasing team starts showing the property. That's where this role lives.

The Work

Redstone Residential manages more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, operating as one of the country's largest third-party student housing managers while also growing a conventional multifamily portfolio. This part-time Maintenance Technician position sits at their Orem, Utah property and pays $15.00 per hour.

Day-to-day, the role centers on two things: curb appeal and turns. You'll keep common areas, hallways, the clubhouse, and building exteriors clean and presentable. You'll manage apartment turnovers, making sure each unit is in move-in-ready condition before a new resident takes the keys. Basic repairs, grounds maintenance, landscaping, pool upkeep, and trash removal all fall within scope. When something exceeds your bandwidth, you flag it to the Maintenance Supervisor or Property Manager so nothing slips.

Emergency response is part of the job. Redstone has defined policies and procedures for after-hours situations, and you're expected to follow them. Customer service matters here too. Resident interactions happen constantly, and how you handle them affects satisfaction scores and retention.

What the Role Requires

  • At least one year of relevant experience; property management background is a plus
  • Working knowledge of pool service and maintenance
  • Strong attention to detail and solid basic maintenance skills
  • Ability to lift a minimum of 75 lbs. and work 8 to 10 hour shifts on your feet
  • Genuine customer service instincts

Redstone offers a 401(k) plan with up to 6% matching, which is a real benefit for a part-time hourly position.

One practical note for candidates: student housing properties run on tighter turn cycles than conventional multifamily. At a Redstone community, the make-ready window between a student lease-end and the next move-in can be compressed to days rather than weeks. If you've worked turns under that kind of time pressure before, that experience will translate directly here and set you apart from candidates who haven't.

job.title: Porter
job.description:
A resident flags a piece of litter near the building entrance at 8 a.m. By the time the morning is underway, the walkway is clear, the common areas are checked, and the property looks the way it should. That's the rhythm of this role.

What the Job Involves

Fairstead is an affordable housing owner and operator with a portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states. This Porter position is based at one of their Newark properties. The work is hands-on and exterior-focused: daily property walks, trash and debris removal, maintaining curb appeal, and keeping common areas clean and safe for residents.

You'll also assist with light maintenance and repairs to community features as needed. Resident interactions happen regularly, so basic customer service skills matter. The job requires weekend availability and on-call flexibility.

What You Bring

  • An interest in custodial or maintenance work, with some mechanical aptitude
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule, including weekends and occasional on-call shifts
  • Reliability and attention to detail on daily rounds

Pay runs $16 to $19 per hour depending on experience and location. Benefits include medical insurance through Meritain Health with a strong employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays.

One thing worth knowing: Porter roles at affordable housing properties tend to carry more resident-facing responsibility than similar positions at market-rate sites. Fairstead's residents rely on well-kept common spaces and responsive staff. Showing up consistently and communicating issues quickly carries real weight here.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Brockford Place
job.description:
Multifamily maintenance is where technical skill and resident experience intersect most directly. A leaking faucet at 11pm, a unit that needs to be rent-ready in three days, a pool that has to pass inspection by Friday: the maintenance technician is the person the whole operation depends on to keep those things from becoming bigger problems. Sunrise Management is hiring for that role at Brockford Place in Sacramento, and the position suits someone who takes real ownership of a property rather than just working through a ticket queue.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of the role covers the full range of hands-on maintenance: plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, painting, and pool upkeep. You'll keep common areas clean and presentable, manage curb appeal, and handle the make-ready process for vacant units with a target of three to five days from vacancy to rent-ready. Service requests need resolution within 24 hours, which means you'll need to prioritize quickly and communicate clearly when parts or scheduling push a timeline out.

Beyond reactive repairs, you'll work through monthly preventive maintenance checks covering lighting, fire safety, pool and spa systems, and life-safety hazards. You'll know where every shutoff lives on the property. You'll track tool and supply inventory, document vacant unit status, and assist with move-in and move-out inspections. On-call emergency coverage is part of the schedule, so flexibility on evenings and weekends is a real requirement, not a footnote.

What You Bring and Where This Can Lead

Sunrise is looking for one to two years of hands-on experience across the core trades, plus solid computer and mobile device skills since work orders and documentation run through software. Strong communication matters here: you're the face of the property for residents when something goes wrong, and how you handle a frustrated tenant during a repair visit shapes retention as much as the fix itself does.

  • 1 to 2 years of experience in plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, or painting
  • Comfortable using a mobile device for work order management
  • Able to work a flexible schedule including on-call emergency response
  • Familiarity with MSDS documentation and safety compliance practices
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision

Technicians who build depth across trades and develop strong documentation habits tend to move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles within two to three years. From there, the path to a regional maintenance director position or facilities management role opens up, especially at a company with a growing portfolio. The skills you compound here, specifically preventive maintenance planning, resident communication, and compliance documentation, are exactly what separates candidates for those senior roles. The pay range is $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience, with medical, dental, and vision coverage, FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Part-Time Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a sales job. The consultants who outperform their peers on traffic-to-lease ratios don't do it by accident. They qualify fast, follow up relentlessly, and close with urgency. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a part-time Leasing Consultant for their East Lansing community, and the skill set they're prioritizing is exactly what you'd expect from a company that tracks conversion metrics closely.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Multi-touch outreach is the engine here. Calls, emails, texts, timed right and personalized. A prospect who tours on Saturday and hears nothing by Monday morning is a lost lease. Strong candidates will have a documented history of follow-up discipline, not just a general sense that they're good with people. CRM fluency matters too. PeakMade works within platforms like Yardi, Entrata, or RealPage, and clean prospect data is how you track pipeline and identify where leads are stalling. If you've ever looked at your conversion funnel and asked why a stage is leaking, you'll fit the mindset here.

The tour itself is a sales conversation, not a walkthrough. Identifying what a prospect actually needs, creating urgency around availability, and handling objections before they harden into hesitation. These are teachable skills, but PeakMade wants at least one year of demonstrated leasing or sales experience before day one.

What You'll Own

  • Converting inbound and outbound leads across phone, digital, and in-person channels
  • Delivering tours that move prospects toward a decision
  • Maintaining current knowledge of pricing, unit availability, and competing properties
  • Accurate lease paperwork, deposit collection, and CRM data entry
  • Supporting move-in and move-out events and contributing to the annual turn process
  • Assisting with market surveys to keep competitive positioning sharp

This is a commission-eligible position, which means your earning potential tracks directly to your close rate. Occupancy targets are real, and the expectation is that you hit them and push past them.

The East Lansing Context

East Lansing is a student-housing market with a pronounced leasing cycle tied to Michigan State's academic calendar. Traffic spikes early, and the consultants who build their pipeline in the fall and winter are the ones celebrating strong occupancy numbers by spring. Understanding that seasonal urgency, and knowing how to communicate it honestly to prospects, is a real competitive edge in this market. Availability windows are tight, and hesitant prospects need accurate information quickly, not pressure tactics.

PeakMade pairs this role with housing discounts (which vary by community), a 401(k) match, and internal development opportunities for those who want to grow toward a full-time or senior leasing position. The part-time schedule includes weekends and peak leasing hours, which is standard in student housing and worth factoring into your decision. Availability during high-traffic periods is when this role has the most impact.

job.title: Floating Leasing Consultant
job.description:
It's 10 a.m. on a Saturday and you're pulling into a property you've only been to twice before. The model needs a quick check, there's a tour in 45 minutes, and the leasing office at your home site just texted asking for a renewal packet. That's a floating consultant's morning.

The Role

CommonPlace is hiring a Floating Leasing Consultant to cover multiple communities across Charlotte. This isn't a single-site position where you get comfortable with one floor plan and one comp set. You're moving between properties, stepping into different leasing offices, and expected to perform at the same level regardless of which site you're standing in. The pay runs $24 to $25 per hour plus commission, and benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short and long-term disability, and a 401k, along with paid vacation, sick time, and volunteer time.

The core of the job is traffic and conversion. You'll greet prospects, conduct tours, walk people through applications and screenings, collect deposits, execute lease agreements, and get residents to the move-in finish line with their files clean and their renter's insurance confirmed. Renewals are part of the job too: preparing documents, sitting down with residents, and keeping occupancy from bleeding out the back door.

Beyond the leasing cycle itself, you'll monitor curb appeal and make-ready readiness in coordination with maintenance, stay current on the local comp set, and keep digital lead sources active through social media, listing platforms, and property websites. Response time on leads matters here. Speed and follow-through are what separate a good leasing consultant from one who just shows units.

What CommonPlace Is Looking For

  • Prior leasing experience preferred; customer service or sales background considered
  • Comfortable with Microsoft Office; OneSite or AppFolio experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • Weekend availability is required
  • Valid driver's license, current insurance, and reliable transportation (you will be driving between sites regularly)
  • Ability to stand, walk, and move through properties for extended periods

The floating format is genuinely useful for consultants who want to build toward an assistant manager or property manager role. Exposure to multiple sites, multiple rent rolls, and different lease-up or stabilized scenarios gives you a broader read on operations than a single-site role typically allows. If you're early in your PM career and want to accelerate, this kind of multi-property visibility is hard to replicate otherwise.

Background check and E-Verify required. CommonPlace is an equal opportunity employer.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager - $3,500 Sign- On Bonus
job.description:
Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager for one of its residential communities in Cambridge, MA, and the role comes with a $3,500 sign-on bonus. The base salary is $70,000. Cambridge is a dense, high-demand submarket with a mix of older mechanicals and newer construction, so whoever takes this seat needs to be comfortable across a range of building systems, not just the basics.

The day-to-day is what you'd expect from a senior maintenance role at a well-run company: service ticket completion, turns, preventative maintenance, grounds upkeep, and keeping the building's mechanical systems running at peak. Where this role goes beyond wrench-turning is the supervisory component. You're expected to lead a team, set the tone for quality and professionalism, and own the make-ready process end to end. Sloppy turns cost the community days of vacancy and frustrated new move-ins. That's the kind of detail this role is accountable for.

On the technical side, Bozzuto wants someone who knows HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair at a working level, with certifications to back it up (EPA and HVAC certs are listed). Exposure to complex mechanical systems like chillers, boilers, and central plant equipment is a plus, which tells you something about the property. Basic carpentry, drywall, and paint round out the punch list skill set. If you've only ever worked in simpler garden-style product, this may be a stretch.

The on-call rotation is real. Weekend availability is required. That's not a small print item at a company like Bozzuto where resident experience expectations are high. The candidates who tend to thrive in these roles are the ones who treat emergency response as part of the job, not an imposition on it.

What You'll Need

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Supervisory or team lead experience preferred
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards and risk management practices
  • Comfort with property management technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office
  • Ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying weather conditions

Bozzuto offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of PTO plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. For someone with solid technical chops who's ready to step into a supervisory role at a company that takes building quality seriously, this is a reasonable place to do it.

job.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant, Bilingual
job.description:
Leasing at a large multifamily operator is a sales job with a hospitality wrapper. You're measured on conversion rates and occupancy, but you earn trust through the quality of every interaction along the way. Cortland, one of the ten largest multifamily owners and operators in the country, is hiring a bilingual leasing and sales consultant to fill that role at one of its communities.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your day centers on prospects: incoming leads, scheduled tours, follow-up calls, and CRM entries. You'll work a pipeline the way a sales role demands, tracking where each prospect stands and moving them toward a signed lease. Consultative selling matters here. That means listening for what someone actually needs before pitching an apartment, then connecting what the community offers to those specific priorities.

The bilingual requirement is a real part of the job. You'll serve residents and prospects who prefer to communicate in a language other than English, and your ability to do that fluently affects both conversion and resident experience.

Beyond the leasing side, you'll help maintain the community's social media presence, plan resident events, and handle the relationship-building that keeps renewals strong. Resident experience and occupancy are connected. Communities with engaged residents generate more referrals and fewer unexpected vacancies.

What Cortland Expects From You

  • At least six months of experience in a sales, customer-facing, or performance-driven role
  • Bilingual fluency (English plus one additional language)
  • Comfort being held to leasing goals, conversion targets, and KPIs
  • Organized follow-up habits and strong time management
  • Experience with or willingness to learn CRM platforms
  • A polished, professional presentation that fits a premium brand
  • Coachability. Cortland tracks performance closely, and feedback comes regularly.

One honest note: leasing roles at Class A operators carry real pressure. Traffic slows on weekends when you're still working, prospects ghost after tours, and monthly close-rate targets don't move. If you're wired for that kind of accountability, the environment suits you. If consistent goal-tracking feels like friction rather than motivation, this particular role probably won't.

For candidates who perform well, the leasing consultant path inside a vertically integrated company like Cortland has clear upward steps: assistant manager, then property manager, and from there into regional or corporate-facing roles. The internal structure is deep enough that lateral moves into training, marketing, or operations are also realistic over time.

job.title: General Manager
job.description:
Commercial property management at the General Manager level is fundamentally an ownership proxy role. The GM doesn't just run operations; they represent the client's interests across every decision that touches asset value, from lease administration and CAM reconciliations to capital planning and vendor procurement. Lincoln Property Company is hiring for that role in Clayton, MO, one of the St. Louis metro's most established commercial submarkets, anchored by Class A office and mixed-use assets that attract institutional ownership and demand institutional-grade management.

The Scope of the Role

This position carries full operational and financial accountability for a large or complex commercial asset, or a portfolio of assets, with property managers or senior property managers reporting directly to you. The day-to-day involves a wide range of concurrent responsibilities: tenant relationship management from initial onboarding through move-out, monthly financial reporting with variance analysis, annual operating and capital budget preparation, CAM and OpX recovery billing, and lease administration coordination with the accounting team. You'll approve vendor invoices within the management agreement's authorization limits, run competitive bid processes with written analysis and client recommendations, and maintain proactive AR collection with documented recommendations on delinquency.

Construction oversight is part of the job, whether that's tenant improvement coordination or capital projects. Emergency preparedness planning, monthly property inspections, and keeping vacant spaces tour-ready round out the operational side. On the financial side, you're expected to produce insightful reports, not just accurate ones. Clients at this level expect variance explanations tied to lease events, market conditions, or operational decisions, not just numbers on a page.

You'll also function as a people manager with real depth: recruiting, hiring, scheduling, cross-training, coaching, and delivering performance reviews for your team. Lincoln's structure involves collaboration across accounting, leasing, and construction support teams, and the GM is the one holding those threads together for the client.

What This Role Requires

  • 5 to 8 years of commercial property management experience, with office, retail, or industrial asset background required
  • Bachelor's degree preferred; a strong combination of education and hands-on experience is considered
  • Active real estate license where required by Missouri regulation; CPM or RPA designation (or active candidacy) preferred
  • Intermediate to advanced Excel proficiency; familiarity with MRI and Kardin is a plus
  • Working knowledge of leases, contracts, financial instruments, tax implications, and construction processes
  • Demonstrated ability to prepare budgets with long-term capital plans, forecast outcomes, and deliver ROI and cost/benefit analysis
  • Strong written communication skills, including business correspondence and procedure documentation
  • Availability for after-hours response, weekend coverage, and emergency situations as the role demands

What separates strong candidates from solid ones at this level is the ability to hold the financial narrative. GMs who can walk a client through a variance report, connect a CAM reconciliation discrepancy to a specific lease clause, and present a capital recommendation with a credible ROI case are the ones who build long-term client trust. Technical operations competence gets you in the room. Financial fluency and clear communication keep you there.

job.title: Groundskeeper - Apartment Community
job.description:
It's 8 a.m. on a Monday and the parking lot already has weekend debris scattered across it. You grab the blower and start from the far end, working your way toward the leasing office before residents head to their cars for work. That's often how the day begins at Bexley SoCo.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Weinstein Properties has owned and managed apartment communities for over 70 years, and they're still family-operated out of Richmond, Virginia. Their portfolio spans more than 60 communities across five states. This groundskeeper role sits at their Bexley SoCo property in South Austin, and the schedule is straightforward: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The day-to-day is honest, physical work. You'll pick up litter and pet waste daily, clean and restock pet waste stations, trash out vacant apartments as they turn, pressure wash, blow common areas, and do light planting and weeding. When the maintenance or leasing teams need an extra hand, you pitch in. Some days bring light painting or housekeeping-style tasks inside common spaces. The work is repetitive by nature, and that's worth knowing before you apply. If you need variety to stay engaged, this one might wear on you. If you're someone who takes genuine satisfaction in a clean, well-kept property, you'll find a rhythm here quickly.

You'll operate a backpack blower, power washer, and golf cart with trailer. The role requires lifting up to 50 pounds regularly, prolonged standing and walking, bending and stooping, and working outdoors year-round through Austin summers and the occasional cold snap. Heat in particular is real here. South Austin in July is not mild.

Who Fits This Role

  • Reliable and punctual. This is the single most important trait. The property doesn't look after itself while you figure out your morning.
  • Self-directed. A manager won't follow you around. You'll know your task list and you'll work through it.
  • Detail-oriented. Noticing a spill near the mailboxes or a broken bag dispenser before a resident complains is part of the job.
  • Physically capable of meeting all demands of the role, with or without accommodation.
  • Open to learning. Weinstein promotes from within, and groundskeeper is a legitimate starting point toward a maintenance tech role for the right person.

Pay starts at $18 per hour with quarterly bonuses, and there's currently a $1,000 stay-on bonus available after 90 days in good standing. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, a 401k, an Employee Assistance Program, and a rent discount. The recruiter can walk you through the stay-on bonus specifics.

Weinstein describes their approach as hands-on, and that extends to how they develop staff. If you show up, work hard, and keep a decent attitude, there's a real path here beyond the groundskeeper title.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Single-family rental at scale changes what a maintenance tech's day actually looks like. You're not the on-site guy at one apartment complex. You're the person keeping a distributed portfolio of homes running, which means your judgment matters more than it would in a traditional setting. No supervisor two doors down. No leasing office to loop in. You make the call, you document it, and you move on to the next address.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

Roofstock operates in the single-family rental space, and this Columbus-based role reflects that model directly. Your day is built around travel between properties: routine repairs, make-readies on vacant homes, move-in and move-out inspections, and onboarding audits when new properties come into the portfolio. HVAC, plumbing, and electrical work are all in scope. You'll also audit vendor work, which means you need a real eye for quality because if a contractor cut corners, you're the one who catches it before it becomes a bigger problem.

Work orders and communication run through mobile apps, so comfort with a smartphone isn't optional. A company vehicle and gas card are provided, which removes the wear-and-tear concern that comes with field-heavy roles.

The schedule is full-time with no on-call rotation and no weekend requirement. That's genuinely uncommon at this pay range in property maintenance, and it reflects a deliberate staffing model rather than an afterthought.

Who Fits This Role Well

The requirements here are straightforward:

  • HVAC Type II Certification (required); Universal Certification is preferred
  • Valid driver's license with a clean enough record to operate a company vehicle
  • Ability to work independently across multiple sites without daily supervision
  • Comfort using mobile tools for work orders, updates, and field communication
  • Physical capability for the role: lifting up to 50 lbs, bending, climbing, outdoor conditions
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Authorization to work in the U.S. (no visa sponsorship available)

Strong candidates tend to be people who can triage on the spot. In a scattered-site model, you'll sometimes arrive at a property and find something that wasn't on the work order. The technicians who do well here are the ones who troubleshoot accurately, document clearly, and don't need to be managed closely to stay productive. Self-direction isn't a soft skill in this context. It's the core of how the job functions.

Pay runs $25 to $30 per hour depending on experience, certifications, and location factors. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k, generous PTO plus 12 paid holidays, paid parental leave, volunteer time off, and monthly subsidies for wellness and home office or cell phone expenses.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Benton)
job.description:
Prometheus has been holding apartments in the Bay Area since 1965, which means they've seen more market cycles than most operators care to count. As the largest privately held apartment owner in the region, with a portfolio pushing 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle, they're not a startup figuring things out. The infrastructure is there. So is the expectation that you'll use it.

The Benton community in Santa Clara is looking for a Leasing Consultant, though Prometheus calls the role a Neighbor Ambassador internally. The title shift reflects something real about how they operate. This isn't a straight traffic-to-application conversion job. You're handling the full customer-facing experience: touring future residents, walking them through the leasing process, and staying involved after move-in to make sure people actually feel settled. On the admin side, you're preparing rental agreements, pulling market surveys, posting availability, and producing the kind of property-level reporting that keeps operations honest.

Weekend availability is required, full stop. The schedule runs with regular weekdays off, and Prometheus pays a weekend shift premium on top of the base hourly rate of $25.00 to $26.25. Add a $200 per-lease incentive, a discretionary semi-annual bonus, and additional bonuses tied to lease-up performance, referrals, and training coaching, and the compensation picture is more layered than most leasing roles at this level. Benefits include 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision for employees and eligible dependents, 401(k) with employer matching, and tenure-based housing discounts that become more meaningful the longer you stay.

On the candidate side, Prometheus is open about hiring across industries. Prior leasing experience isn't listed as a requirement. What they're actually screening for is harder to fake: comfort in a sales and service environment, genuine follow-through with people, and the kind of self-direction that doesn't need a manager standing nearby to stay productive.

One thing worth knowing about leasing roles at well-capitalized, vertically integrated owners like Prometheus: the exposure is broader than at a fee-management shop. Because acquisitions, development, value-add renovations, and operations all sit under one roof, leasing staff at the property level tend to see more of how the full business works. For someone early in a property management career, that context compounds quickly. Leasing consultants who absorb the operational side of the role, not just the customer-facing piece, tend to move into assistant manager and then manager positions faster than those who treat it as a pure sales job.

What You Bring

  • Experience in customer service, sales, or a client-facing environment (industry doesn't have to be property management)
  • Comfort managing competing tasks across leasing, admin, and resident communication
  • Availability on weekends as a standard part of your schedule
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • A track record of following through, not just initiating

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This position pulls on three skill sets simultaneously: leasing, financial administration, and people management. You're converting prospects into residents, tracking delinquency and posting payments, and stepping into the Community Manager's seat when they're out. All three happen in the same week, often the same day.

Strong candidates already know how to read a ledger, handle a collections call without escalating tension, and close a tour. The financial side here is real work: ledger audits, payment posting, delinquency follow-up, and supporting reporting for regional leadership. If numbers aren't your thing, this role will feel harder than it should.

What You'll Be Doing at Hawthorne at Stillwater

Day to day, you're supporting leasing activity at this garden-style community in Sneads Ferry. That means responding to leads, conducting tours, processing applications, and keeping renewals moving on schedule. Occupancy is a shared goal, and your leasing activity directly affects it.

On the financial side, you'll oversee rent collection, post payments, scan checks, and run weekly delinquency follow-ups. You'll also conduct regular ledger reviews to catch billing errors and verify account accuracy before they become bigger problems.

You'll manage the community's social media presence, keep common areas and the leasing office presentable, and handle resident concerns with composure. When the Community Manager is unavailable, you run point.

  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of prior assistant community manager experience preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a plus
  • Availability for some Saturdays (10 AM to 4 PM) and occasional evenings for resident events

What's Distinctive Here

Hawthorne ranks among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally, with deep roots in the Southeast. For this role specifically, they offer a structured career path program with real intent behind it: Assistant Community Manager to Community Manager is a stated trajectory, backed by a Learning and Development team. That's worth noting if upward mobility matters to you.

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, and paid parental leave options.

The Sneads Ferry market sits near Camp Lejeune, which creates a steady, military-affiliated renter base. That population tends toward shorter lease terms and higher turnover, so MTM management and renewal retention skills get real exercise here.

job.title: Market Maintenance Technician (Part-Time)20 hours per
job.description:
This part-time role at Dexter Street Commons in Pawtucket covers the full range of day-to-day physical plant work that keeps a residential property running and looking well-maintained. At 20 hours per week, the schedule is flexible, but the work itself is varied and hands-on.

What You'll Actually Do

Most of your time goes toward completing maintenance requests as they come in: repairing doors, locks, tiles, and handrails, swapping out light fixtures, installing smoke detectors, and handling appliance repairs. Cosmetic work is a real part of this position too. Painting units, replacing window screens, and similar make-ready tasks are regular responsibilities, not occasional add-ons. You'll also need to stay sharp on documentation, keeping paperwork and invoices organized for the work you complete.

The role requires availability for emergency situations, including flood response and back-to-back move-ins. Even at part-time hours, those moments call for someone who stays composed and moves quickly. You'll coordinate with outside contractors and vendors, which means you need to know enough about the trades to hold a productive conversation with specialists and verify that work meets the property's standards.

What You Bring

  • At least six months of hands-on trade or building maintenance experience
  • Working familiarity with electrical and mechanical systems at a repair level
  • Comfort identifying safety concerns and acting on them without waiting to be told
  • Specialized trade background in plumbing, electrical, HVAC, or roofing is a meaningful advantage
  • Reliability and the ability to manage your own work order flow with minimal supervision

Context Worth Knowing

John M. Corcoran and Company has operated in New England since 1951, and the culture reflects that longevity: long tenure on staff, institutional knowledge that gets passed down, and a genuine emphasis on quality over speed. That context matters for a maintenance role because it shapes expectations. Properties managed by firms with that kind of history tend to hold high standards for presentation and resident experience, which means cosmetic attention and follow-through on punch list items carry real weight, not just the mechanical repairs.

For someone building a maintenance career, part-time work at a well-run property is genuinely useful experience. The breadth of work here, from appliance repairs to contractor coordination to emergency response, covers skills that transfer directly to a full-time maintenance technician or lead tech role. If you're looking to develop a well-rounded maintenance background while working a flexible schedule, this position builds exactly the kind of varied, documented experience that makes future employers pay attention.

Compensation runs between $26.75 and $32.00 per hour, and the position includes a $1,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off, and a 401(k) with company match.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work at a residential apartment community covers a wide range of trades, and the technician who thrives here is someone who can shift from a plumbing call in the morning to an electrical issue in the afternoon without losing focus. Cottonwood Residential is adding a Maintenance Technician at Stratford at Hillcrest Apartments in Winston-Salem, and this is a role that draws on what you already know while steadily expanding what you can do.

On the technical side, you'll handle repairs across plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry, both inside units and across the property grounds. The role operates within standard community hours, and it includes on-call responsibility for after-hours emergencies. That after-hours piece is worth being clear-eyed about: it's part of the job, and it's where your ability to diagnose and resolve problems under pressure gets sharpened most. You won't be doing it alone. The Service Manager provides support, and you'll work within established company standards on every call.

Physically, the role demands real stamina. You'll be on your feet most of the day, climbing stairs and ladders, working in tight spaces, and lifting up to 50 pounds regularly. A valid driver's license is required. EPA Type II or Universal certification, HVAC troubleshooting experience, and CPO certification each strengthen your candidacy, though they aren't listed as hard requirements.

What the role requires vs. what it builds

Coming in, you need working knowledge of residential repairs across at least a couple of trades, solid physical capability, and the communication skills to work through work orders and interact with residents clearly. What the role builds is something different: diagnostic instincts. Apartment maintenance is repetitive enough that patterns emerge quickly. Over time, you develop a mental model of how systems fail in a garden-style residential setting, which makes you faster and more accurate on every turn and make-ready you touch.

Technicians who grow fastest in roles like this are the ones who treat the on-call rotation as a learning accelerator rather than just an obligation. Emergency calls, by definition, involve conditions you haven't seen before, and the problem-solving you do at 10 PM on a Saturday builds judgment that routine daytime work can't replicate.

  • Valid driver's license (required)
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work on your feet for extended periods
  • Availability for on-call after-hours emergency coverage
  • Ability to work evenings and weekends as part of standard scheduling
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (a plus)
  • HVAC troubleshooting experience (a plus)
  • CPO certification (a plus)

Cottonwood Residential offers health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage with a quick eligibility window, a 401k with company match, HSA matching, three weeks of paid time off in the first year, and over ten paid holidays annually.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
This role covers five apartment communities across two Pittsburgh-area submarkets: four properties totaling 198 units in Greensburg and one 97-unit community in New Kensington. Multi-site portfolios at this scale demand someone who can move fluidly between hands-on skilled trades work and the logistical side of managing people, vendors, and budgets. Birgo is looking for a maintenance supervisor who does both well.

The day-to-day splits roughly into two modes. Some of it is field work: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, drywall, turns, punch lists, and groundskeeping across properties that aren't all in the same zip code. The rest is coordination: leading a two-person tech team, sourcing and managing contractors when the scope exceeds what the crew can handle, tracking expenditures against budget, and serving as the operational link between maintenance and property management. AppFolio handles work orders in a paperless workflow, so comfort with mobile tools matters here.

The Greensburg and New Kensington markets sit in the older housing stock belt east and northeast of Pittsburgh. Properties in these corridors tend to be garden-style or low-rise buildings with aging mechanical systems, which means HVAC and plumbing calls come with some frequency. A supervisor who can personally handle high-skill repairs keeps vendor costs down and reduces unit downtime on turns. That's a real budget lever at this portfolio size.

Birgo emphasizes servant leadership internally, and that framing is worth taking seriously in the context of this role. Managing two techs means coaching and developing them, not just directing work. Strong candidates will have experience building a team's technical capability over time, not just assigning jobs and checking completions. Emotional intelligence in conflict resolution, which comes up in any maintenance team eventually, matters as much as trade credentials here.

What Birgo is Looking For

  • 5 or more years of multifamily maintenance experience
  • 3 or more years in a supervisory capacity
  • Hands-on expertise across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and drywall
  • Experience managing a multi-site portfolio
  • Comfort with mobile work order platforms (AppFolio experience is a plus)
  • Budget awareness and cost control discipline
  • Active driver's license, reliable insured vehicle, and ability to lift 50 pounds unassisted

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, with participation in an on-call rotation. Compensation is $31 per hour. Birgo offers medical, dental, vision, life, and short-term disability insurance with a company contribution, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, paid holidays, sick time, mileage and boot reimbursements, uniforms, a professional development reimbursement program, profit-sharing, and a discount at Birgo properties.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (The Reserve)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Maintenance technicians at The Reserve handle the full range of day-to-day upkeep: HVAC service and repairs, plumbing, electrical work, and structural fixes across the property's interior and exterior. You're also responsible for preventative maintenance, which means staying ahead of issues before they turn into emergency calls. Speaking of which, after-hours emergencies are part of this role. When a resident loses heat in January or has a water leak at midnight, someone has to respond. That's you sometimes.

On a typical day, you'll work through a queue of resident service requests, document what you find, complete the work, and move on to the next one. Keeping accurate records matters here, both for accountability and for spotting recurring problems on the property. The job keeps you moving physically, so expect time on your feet, climbing, bending, and lifting throughout your shift.

What You Bring

  • 2 to 3 years of maintenance experience in a residential or comparable setting
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal certification (preferred but not required)
  • Ability to communicate clearly with residents and teammates, even when the situation is frustrating

The EPA certification is worth mentioning separately. If you have it, you're more useful on HVAC work from day one. If you don't, it's a credential worth pursuing early and one that adds real value to your skill set across any property you work on in the future.

The Role in Context

BAM Companies has been operating since 2010 and manages properties across multiple markets. The Reserve in Evansville is part of that portfolio. Pay for this position ranges from $17 to $19 per hour depending on experience and qualifications. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage with BAM covering a significant share of the cost, paid life insurance, rent discounts at BAM properties, and a PTO structure that gives you 88 hours after 90 days and 120 hours after your first year, plus 14.5 paid holidays.

One honest note for anyone weighing this against other maintenance roles: the difference between a solid technician and an exceptional one at a property like this usually comes down to how they handle resident interactions, not just the technical work. You can fix a unit perfectly, but if you leave a resident feeling dismissed or uninformed, the job isn't really done. The technical skills get you hired. The communication habits are what build a reputation on site.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Richardson, TX
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. and you're already walking the grounds at The Pradera in Richardson, TX, punch list in hand, checking curb appeal before residents head to work. By 9 a.m., you're knee-deep in a plumbing call. That's a typical Tuesday.

What the Role Actually Covers

Berkshire Residential Investments owns and manages its own portfolio, which means decisions move faster and accountability runs deeper than at a typical third-party shop. As a Maintenance Technician at The Pradera, you're a core part of keeping the physical asset performing. That means more than just closing work orders. You'll help preserve the property's condition over time, support management in holding community standards, and keep safety protocols consistently enforced.

Day to day, you're working across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems. You'll help manage the shop, track inventory, and maintain key security. Curb appeal is taken seriously here. A well-kept exterior drives traffic, supports occupancy, and reflects directly on resident retention. You'll be expected to treat that as your responsibility, not just a manager's concern.

Customer service is part of the job description for real, not as an afterthought. Residents notice whether maintenance staff are approachable and communicative. How you carry yourself during a service call affects renewal decisions more than most people realize.

What Berkshire Is Looking For

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across the core trades: appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and building maintenance
  • Comfort with basic computer use and related applications for work order management
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
  • A self-directed approach to quality and follow-through on punch list items

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and solid insurance coverage. The company emphasizes internal growth, which means a technician who performs consistently has a real path toward a lead or service manager role over time.

One thing worth knowing: Richardson sits in a dense DFW submarket with a lot of multifamily competition. Properties that stay tight on make-ready times and curb appeal hold occupancy better than those that don't. A technician who owns their work order queue and keeps turns moving on schedule contributes directly to that NOI story, even if the numbers don't show up on your daily to-do list.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Leasing skills sit at the center of this role, and they show up in concrete, measurable ways. At Redstone Residential's Rexburg community, a Leasing Manager's effectiveness gets measured in occupancy trends, renewal rates, and the quality of every prospect interaction from the first phone call to the signed lease. This is a hands-on leasing position with real operational responsibility layered in.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Sales and customer service aren't background skills here. They drive the core function of the job. You'll conduct prospect tours, manage phone and email pipelines, and run renewal campaigns designed to hold occupancy. Redstone uses Entrata as its leasing platform, so comfort with structured software workflows matters. You'll also work within their online and social marketing systems, which means basic SEO awareness and digital communication skills translate directly into leasing performance.

On the administrative side, you'll maintain resident ledgers and keep balances accurate. That requires attention to detail and a working comfort with cloud-based tools like Google Drive and Dropbox. Mistakes in ledger management create downstream problems for collections and delinquency tracking, so accuracy carries real weight.

The Operational Layer

Beyond leasing, this role supports the Community Manager across broader operations. That includes budget performance awareness, rent collections, and some staff administration. You're not just filling units. You're helping keep the property running day to day, which gives you visibility into how leasing activity connects to NOI and overall community health.

Rexburg is a student-market town built largely around BYU-Idaho's enrollment calendar. That means leasing cycles here follow a rhythm that differs from conventional multifamily. Traffic peaks and lease-up pressure align with academic timelines, and renewal campaigns need to account for the transient nature of a student population. Experience in or awareness of student housing dynamics is a genuine advantage in this market.

What Separates Strong Candidates

  • Demonstrated ability to hit leasing goals without waiting to be directed, especially during peak traffic periods
  • Comfort using Entrata or a comparable leasing CRM, not just basic office software
  • A communication style that works equally well with prospects, current residents, and teammates
  • Enough composure to handle a high-volume leasing season without letting service quality slip

Redstone operates at scale, managing over 38,000 beds across 20 states as a third-party manager. That structure means their systems, reporting standards, and leasing processes are well-developed. For someone early in a property management career, working inside that kind of operational framework builds transferable skills quickly. The Leasing Manager role is a natural stepping stone toward a Community Manager position, particularly for candidates who develop both the leasing and administrative sides of the job.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the center of daily operations at a Fairstead affordable housing property in Dallas. You'll work alongside the Property Manager to keep the property compliant, occupied, and financially sound. A good portion of your time goes toward HUD compliance: executing the 4350.3 Handbook requirements, coordinating annual and interim recertification reviews, and helping prepare the property for REAC inspections, Management and Occupancy Reviews, LIHTC reviews, and investor site visits. When EHS violations surface, you help get them cleared.

On the financial side, you'll track arrears daily, ensure rents are collected, posted, and deposited, and create purchase orders in Yardi. You'll work with the in-house legal team to monitor rent payment status and coordinate evictions when lease violations escalate past intervention. On the resident-facing side, you're responding to calls, emails, and complaints within a few hours, alerting staff to move-ins and move-outs, and making sure the maintenance team closes out service requests. You also manage the lease renewal program to protect retention.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of experience in affordable housing leasing or property management (required)
  • Working knowledge of EIV, Yardi, and RealPage
  • Familiarity with HUD 4350.3 compliance requirements and LIHTC recertification processes
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, specifically for resident relations and documentation
  • Knowledge of the Dallas residential market

What This Role Builds

Affordable housing compliance is a distinct discipline within property management, and this position develops real depth in it. Candidates who come from conventional multifamily often underestimate how different the regulatory cadence is. You'll sharpen your ability to read and apply HUD guidance, manage recertification timelines, and prepare a property for formal review cycles. Those skills transfer directly into Community Manager roles at affordable properties, compliance specialist positions, or regional roles within affordable housing portfolios. Fairstead operates across 28 states with more than 30,000 units, so internal advancement for people who prove themselves operationally is a realistic path.

The candidates who thrive here combine genuine attention to detail on the compliance and financial side with the interpersonal steadiness that resident-facing work requires. Affordable housing residents often face real housing instability, so the ability to handle difficult conversations with patience and professionalism matters as much as knowing your way around Yardi. If you've worked affordable housing and already understand the distinction between market-rate delinquency follow-up and the specific protocols required under HUD guidelines, you'll hit the ground running.

job.title: Community Manager - Multi site - The Hixon and Terava Apartments
job.description:
You're wrapping up a site visit at The Hixon, then driving across Bend to check in with the team at Terava before the afternoon leasing rush. That's the rhythm of this role: two communities, one manager, constant context-switching.

The Role

CloudTen Residential is hiring a Multi-Site Community Manager to oversee day-to-day operations at two Bend, Oregon apartment communities: The Hixon and Terava. You'll report to a Regional Manager and carry full operational accountability across both sites. That means staffing, leasing, financials, maintenance oversight, compliance, and resident relations. A valid driver's license is required.

On the financial side, you'll manage rent collection, work delinquent accounts within Oregon landlord-tenant law, handle daily deposits, monitor expenses, and contribute to budget preparation. You're expected to flag inefficiencies and recommend cost-effective improvements, not just report numbers up the chain.

Leasing and marketing are part of the job too. You'll oversee unit advertising, conduct showings, keep lease records clean, and analyze local market data to guide pricing decisions. Renewal outreach and retention efforts fall under your scope as well.

People management is a core part of this position. You'll hire, train, and evaluate on-site staff across both properties. That includes building a team culture that reflects CloudTen's standards and giving people what they need to do their jobs well.

What You Need

  • At least two years of property management experience; multi-site experience is a plus
  • Solid working knowledge of Oregon landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing regulations
  • Comfort with property management software and Microsoft Office (Word and Excel in particular)
  • Strong organizational skills, since you'll be managing schedules, records, and priorities across two locations simultaneously
  • High school diploma required; college coursework or a degree in a related field is preferred
  • Valid driver's license

Compensation is set at $85,000 annually. CloudTen offers medical, dental, and vision insurance, company-paid life insurance, FSA options, paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.

One thing worth knowing about this specific setup: managing two separate communities means your authority is real, but your time is divided. Strong candidates for multi-site roles tend to be people who build systems rather than rely on memory. If you've managed a single property well by staying on top of every detail personally, that approach gets harder to sustain when you're splitting time between two sites. Managers who document processes, delegate effectively, and trust their on-site teams tend to do better in this structure than those who prefer to control everything directly.

job.title: Service Manager
job.description:
What This Role Covers

Multifamily maintenance operations run on the Service Manager. Leasing fills units; the Service Manager keeps residents in them. At Huntington at Stonefield, a Dream Live Prosper Communities property in Houston, this position owns the full maintenance function: work order turnaround, make-ready scheduling, preventative maintenance, vendor oversight, and budget control through AppFolio.

The property requires lease-up experience. That's a specific ask. During a lease-up, vacant units hit the schedule in waves, turn timelines compress, and the make-ready process has to run without much margin for error.
