The financial side of this job is real and daily. You'll oversee rent collection, manage delinquency under California landlord-tenant law, handle bank deposits, and work within a budget you help shape. If you've ever had to defend a line item to a regional manager or flag an expense trend before it became a problem, that's the muscle this role uses. Proficiency in property management software and Excel isn't optional here; it's how the work gets done accurately.

On the people side, you'll hire, train, and evaluate on-site staff. That means setting expectations clearly, addressing performance issues without letting them fester, and building a team that can handle the day-to-day without constant hand-holding. Resident relations run through you as well. Service requests, lease renewals, community concerns, Fair Housing compliance: all of it lands at your desk.

Leasing and marketing round out the picture. You'll track market conditions, adjust pricing as needed, and make sure the property's advertising and showing activity stays consistent. Occupancy and traffic don't manage themselves, and at a property like this, you're the one accountable for both.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

A typical week moves between inspections of common areas and units, reviewing delinquency reports, following up on open maintenance tickets, and meeting with prospective residents. You'll handle payroll submissions, coordinate with your regional manager, and field whatever comes in from residents. The 24 to 48 hour service request standard is a real commitment, and keeping that up requires a team that's organized and a manager who stays on top of the punch list.

Encinitas is a competitive rental submarket with educated, discerning renters. Residents here notice when something's off and they'll tell you. Retention matters, and the way you run renewals and community engagement will show up in your occupancy numbers over time.

What Sunrise Is Looking For

Two years of property management experience is the floor. California landlord-tenant law knowledge is expected, not something you'll pick up on the job. A background that includes both leasing and financial oversight will carry more weight than depth in just one area.

  • Minimum two years of property management experience
  • Working knowledge of California Fair Housing, ADA, and landlord-tenant law
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and property management software
  • Experience managing on-site staff
  • Basic accounting knowledge: budgets, delinquency, deposit procedures
  • College degree or related coursework preferred

Sunrise describes its culture around resident hospitality and a positive living experience. For the Community Manager, that translates to tone-setting. How your team treats residents reflects how you've built and led that team. Pay ranges from $24.00 to $29.00 per hour depending on experience, with medical, dental, and vision coverage, FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
It's 7:45 a.m. and a resident just flagged a leak under their kitchen sink before heading to class. You're already on your way, work order in hand, because your morning started with a walk of the grounds and a quick scan of overnight requests. That rhythm, showing up consistently and handling what comes, is the core of this job.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

PeakMade Real Estate manages off-campus student housing and multi-family communities, and this Maintenance Technician role is based at their Westfield, Indiana property. The day-to-day covers the full range: service requests, preventative maintenance, turns, pool upkeep, and exterior curb appeal. You'll work alongside a Maintenance Supervisor rather than running solo, which means there's structure and collaboration built into how the team operates.

Turns are a real part of this role. When residents move in and out, you're part of the process that gets units ready. That means punch list work, unit inspections, and coordinating with the broader team to hit deadlines. You'll also participate in an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies, so reliable transportation and flexibility with your schedule aren't optional.

Pool maintenance and chemical logging are part of the scope. So is monitoring supply and tool inventory, keeping common areas clean, and helping the team maintain accurate records. You'll communicate regularly with residents, vendors, and your supervisor, and how you handle a frustrated resident in the middle of a repair matters just as much as the repair itself.

What PeakMade Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year of maintenance experience, apartment industry preferred
  • EPA 608 Type I and II certification preferred
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and appliances
  • Comfortable using hand tools, ladders, refrigerant recovery units, and landscaping equipment safely
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property and have reliable transportation
  • Able to lift up to 50 pounds, work outdoors in variable temperatures, and handle physical demands including frequent bending and ladder use
  • Technicians are expected to bring their own hand tools

One thing worth knowing about student housing specifically: the resident population turns over on a compressed cycle tied to academic calendars. That creates predictable pressure points around move-in and move-out seasons. Technicians who stay organized, communicate well under volume, and take the make-ready process seriously tend to stand out here. If you've worked lease-up or high-turnover communities before, that experience translates directly.

PeakMade offers technical training, HVAC and CPO certification opportunities, a wellness program, paid parental leave, 401(k) matching, 17 total days off including wellbeing days, monthly renewal bonuses, and a facilities leadership program for those who want to grow into supervisory or management roles over time.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a full-time, on-site maintenance role at a 202-unit apartment community in Pilsen. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 7:30am to 3:30pm, with rotating on-call coverage for after-hours emergencies. Most of your day involves working through assigned work orders, keeping common areas clean and functional, and turning vacant units so they're ready for incoming residents.

Unit turns are a consistent part of the workload. That means punch list repairs, paint touch-ups, drywall patching, and general make-ready tasks that get a unit back to rentable condition. Beyond turns, you'll handle routine preventive maintenance on building systems, resolve minor plumbing and electrical issues, and do light carpentry and appliance repairs as needed.

Exterior upkeep is part of the job too. Trash pickup, snow removal, and seasonal amenity maintenance (including pool cleaning and basic equipment checks) all fall under this role. You'll work closely with the property manager to stay on top of priorities and make sure residents get responsive, courteous service when you're in their home.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on apartment or building maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of electrical, plumbing, HVAC, carpentry, and appliance repair
  • Comfortable with hand and power tools
  • Physically able to lift up to 50 lbs, climb ladders, kneel, and bend as needed
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Self-directed and reliable. You don't need someone checking in on every task
  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Pilsen is a dense, active Chicago neighborhood. A 202-unit building in that area sees real daily wear, so the work order volume is steady. Technicians who do well in roles like this tend to be fast at diagnosing problems accurately on the first visit rather than returning multiple times. Residents notice the difference, and so does your manager.

The on-call rotation is real. If after-hours emergency response doesn't fit your life right now, that's worth weighing before you apply. For candidates who are fine with it, the Monday-through-Friday daytime schedule is otherwise predictable, which is a genuine advantage over some maintenance roles that run irregular hours throughout the week.

Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k), paid time off, and a referral program.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Ridgeview
job.description:
A resident puts in a request at 7 a.m.: the kitchen faucet has been dripping all weekend. By the time you've pulled the work order on your phone, grabbed the right parts from a stocked shop, and knocked on the door, it's 9:15 and the resident is already calling the office to say thank you. That rhythm, quick diagnosis, clean repair, satisfied resident, is what this role is built around.

The Work at Ridgeview

AIR Communities is hiring a Maintenance Technician at Ridgeview, a 320-unit luxury apartment community in Moreno Valley, CA. The compensation range runs $24.00 to $26.00 per hour based on your skills and experience, and technicians who consistently earn strong resident satisfaction scores can pick up an additional $250 per month through AIR's customer service bonus program.

Day-to-day responsibilities cover the full range of residential maintenance. You'll complete apartment turns as residents move out and new ones prepare to move in, working through make-ready punch lists to get units rent-ready. You'll handle resident service requests across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and carpentry, with the expectation that you bring proficiency in at least two of those trades. Depending on your experience level, you may also help coordinate vendor work, conduct move-in and move-out inspections, and provide informal technical guidance to newer team members. Workload and specific duties shift with the season and the community's needs, so flexibility is part of the job.

AIR uses technology to route and prioritize work orders, which keeps the day organized and reduces time spent chasing down what needs attention next. The shops are stocked and maintained so you're not hunting for parts mid-job. On-call rotation is part of the schedule, at least one week per month, and you'll need reliable transportation to respond to after-hours emergencies.

What This Role Requires

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities, building, or residential setting
  • Demonstrated skill in two or more trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, or carpentry
  • Ability to work flexible hours including evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts
  • Physical capability to move heavy equipment and machinery as needed
  • Reliable transportation for after-hours emergency response

AIR offers a 50% rent discount at any of its communities, which is a real financial advantage if you want to live onsite at Ridgeview or at a nearby AIR property. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance; HSA and FSA options; short and long-term disability paid by the company; a 401(k) with employer contribution; up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave; and tuition assistance plus full reimbursement for job-related certifications and licenses.

One thing worth noting for technicians thinking about career trajectory: AIR has a maintenance development program called Ascend that's designed around your individual path, not a generic checklist. For a technician who already has solid trade skills and wants a clear route toward a lead or service manager role, that kind of structured investment tends to matter more than it sounds on paper.

Moreno Valley's residential growth over the past several years has added significant multifamily inventory to the Inland Empire, and luxury communities in the area compete hard on resident experience. A technician who treats service quality as a point of professional pride, not just a task to close, will find that reputation travels quickly within a community like Ridgeview.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the operational center of commercial property management for Lincoln Property Company in Rock Hill, SC. You'll work alongside the Property Manager to keep a commercial portfolio running cleanly across office, retail, or industrial assets. That means tenant communication, vendor invoice review, lease administration, and monthly financial reporting all fall within your daily scope.

On the financial side, you'll help prepare monthly reports and budget packages to client specifications, and you'll take the lead on collecting data and drafting CAM and operating expense reconciliations in coordination with the accounting team. Getting those OpEx recs right matters: errors surface during audits and erode tenant trust fast. You'll also review vendor invoices for accuracy and compliance with the management agreement before they move toward payment.

Lease administration is a consistent part of the workload. You'll handle lease setup, track changes, and coordinate tenant move-ins and move-outs, including walk-throughs with the Property Manager and tenant improvement teams. When a tenant space turns, you'll be part of documenting the condition and making sure nothing falls through the cracks between the outgoing tenant and any TI work ahead.

Beyond the desk work, expect regular property inspections and travel to assigned sites. Emergency response planning and participation in drills are also part of the job. This is a fully in-office position with no remote option.

What You Bring

  • A bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and hands-on experience; 1 to 2 years in commercial property management or a related field
  • Comfort with financial concepts: percentages, reconciliations, basic variance analysis
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills; familiarity with AP platforms and a CMMS is a plus
  • Experience with commercial asset types (office, retail, industrial) gives you a real head start here
  • Clear written and verbal communication, especially when coordinating between tenants, vendors, and internal teams
  • Strong organizational habits and the ability to deliver on deadlines without constant follow-up
  • Current authorization to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

Context Worth Knowing

Rock Hill sits just south of Charlotte and has seen steady commercial development pressure as businesses look for more affordable footholds in the greater Charlotte metro. That growth means active lease activity and tenant expectations that mirror larger markets, which makes experience with lease administration and OpEx reconciliation especially relevant here.

Lincoln Property Company manages over 680 million square feet of commercial space nationally, which means the systems, reporting standards, and client expectations you'll work within are institutional-grade. For someone early in their commercial PM career, that exposure is genuinely useful. Assistant Property Managers at firms like Lincoln who build strong financial and lease admin skills often move into full Property Manager roles overseeing their own portfolios within a few years. The breadth of asset types Lincoln handles also means lateral moves into different property sectors are realistic as you grow.

job.title: Business Manager - Olympus at Memorial
job.description:
Running a multifamily asset well takes more than keeping occupancy up. It takes someone who can read a budget, lead a team, build resident trust, and still show up to a community event on a Friday evening without losing steam. That's the job Olympus Property is hiring for at Olympus at Memorial in Houston.

What the Role Actually Covers

As Business Manager, you're the operator of record for this community. The financial side is real and regular: you'll own budget forecasts, monitor NOI, track delinquency, review monthly performance against projections, and sit down with your Regional Manager and Regional VP to talk strategy when the numbers need attention. You'll also bid and negotiate vendor contracts, inspect units and common areas for market-ready condition, and keep the property performing at a Class A standard.

The people side carries just as much weight. You'll directly oversee both the office team and the maintenance crew, which means hiring, training, counseling, and motivating people who often have very different day-to-day realities. Leasing, renewals, resident retention programs, marketing execution, and vendor relationships all run through you. This is a coordinating role as much as it's a managing one.

Schedule is Monday through Friday with hours that shift between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. depending on what the day needs. After-hours resident events and the occasional emergency come with the territory.

Who Fits Here

  • At least two years of experience as a property manager in multifamily, with Class A luxury experience strongly preferred
  • Comfort with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite platforms
  • Demonstrated ability to build and manage to a budget, not just report against one
  • A track record of developing people, not just directing them

What separates strong candidates at this level isn't just experience with the tools or the paperwork. It's the ability to hold the team together when occupancy dips, a vendor disappoints, or a resident complaint escalates. The managers who thrive in roles like this tend to be steady communicators who don't lose their composure when multiple things need attention at once.

The Olympus Piece

Olympus Property has earned a spot on the National Apartment Association's Top Employer list three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), which reflects something real about how the company treats the people doing the work. The culture language in their materials is consistent with what they actually offer: leadership conferences, sabbatical eligibility, a career pathing program, and genuine investment in internal growth. Compensation for this role starts between $70,000 and $80,000 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly bonuses on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and an apartment rental allowance.

If you want a role where the relationships you build with your team and your residents actually matter to the company above you, this one's worth a close look.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Artesia Apartments
job.description:
Maintenance Supervisor roles at mid-size apartment operators tend to be hands-on from day one. You're not just managing a clipboard. You're the person who sets the pace for how quickly turns get done, how residents feel about the community, and whether the property manager can trust that work orders are actually closed out.

What the Work Looks Like at Artesia

MG Properties has been acquiring and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, and Artesia Apartments in Everett is part of that portfolio. As Maintenance Supervisor, you'll oversee all maintenance and repair activity at the property. That means diagnosing issues yourself when needed, delegating routine work to your team, and inspecting completed work to make sure it holds up. You'll manage the service request system, coordinate scheduling with your team, and work alongside the property manager to keep staffing organized.

Beyond reactive work orders, you'll run regular safety meetings, track preventive maintenance, and maintain accurate records on expenditures and completed work. Equipment upkeep is part of the scope too. MG Properties expects experience across trades, so this isn't a role where you hand off electrical to someone else and call it done.

What You'll Need Coming In

  • At least 2 years of experience in a Maintenance Supervisor capacity
  • Prior experience at a property of 150 units or more
  • Hands-on competency across multiple trades
  • A valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Comfort leading a team without micromanaging every task

Customer service matters here. Residents notice how your team communicates as much as how fast the work gets done. If you're the type who gets defensive when a resident follows up on an open ticket, this role will wear on you. If you take it as useful information, you'll fit in fine.

Compensation and Honest Context

The pay range is $36 to $39 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, paid holidays, personal days, sick time, and rental discounts. It's a solid package for a working supervisor role.

One honest note about this kind of position: after-hours calls happen. A pipe doesn't care that it's Sunday. How often and how the on-call structure is set up is worth asking about in your interview, but go in knowing that's part of the job at most communities this size. The upside is that supervisors who handle the unpredictable parts well tend to build strong credibility with both residents and ownership, which creates real room to grow into regional or facilities management roles over time.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the center of Roofstock's single-family rental platform, which means your portfolio won't look like a traditional apartment community. You'll manage a geographically dispersed collection of SFR properties across state lines, working virtually with investors who have varying goals, risk tolerances, and expectations. On any given day, you might be tracking a delinquency situation in one market, coordinating a make-ready in another, reviewing R&M costs against an investor's NOI targets, and following up with internal teams on a task that's been sitting too long. You'll use Roofstock's proprietary technology alongside standard property management platforms to keep everything moving.

You'll serve as the primary liaison between investors and the rest of the Roofstock organization, which means you're not just fielding calls. You're synthesizing information from leasing, maintenance, accounting, and resident services into a clear picture that investors can act on. When complex problems surface (and they will), you're expected to resolve the immediate issue and identify the root cause so it doesn't repeat. You'll also need to be comfortable representing the company at eviction-related court proceedings when required, including contested hearings or appeals.

What You Bring

  • An active real estate license (required before starting)
  • At least two years of residential or commercial property management or real estate operations experience
  • Comfort working across multiple property management software platforms
  • A track record of managing cost and revenue, with some exposure to owner reporting preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, specifically in a virtual, high-volume environment
  • A valid driver's license and the ability to travel within your assigned area roughly 10% of the time
  • A bachelor's degree in business or a related field, or equivalent professional experience

Context Worth Knowing

Managing SFR portfolios at scale is a different discipline than managing a garden-style or mid-rise community. There's no leasing office, no on-site team you can walk down the hall to find, and no single rent roll that neatly captures your whole portfolio in one view. The skills this role builds, specifically remote portfolio oversight, cross-functional coordination in a tech-driven environment, and investor-level communication, transfer directly to institutional SFR operations, asset management, and fee management roles. Companies running large SFR portfolios at scale increasingly need people who've learned to manage complexity without physical presence, and this role develops exactly that capability.

The base salary for this position is $60,000 annually. Roofstock notes that total compensation extends beyond base pay and includes benefits such as health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k program, generous PTO, parental leave, and wellness and home office subsidies.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Student Housing Operations at Scale

Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Annual turn isn't a seasonal inconvenience; it's the operational event of the year. Leasing velocity, gain to lease, and concessions all get stress-tested against a move-in deadline that doesn't move. The General Manager at Redpoint Wilmington owns all of it, from the T-12 budget to the punch list on the last unit before move-in day.

Scion operates student communities nationally, and this role sits at the center of a purpose-built operational structure. You're not managing up to a regional director for every decision. You're running the property as a business, with partner departments in Legal, Facilities and Capital, Talent Acquisition, and Finance supporting your execution rather than directing it.

What the Role Actually Covers

Financial performance is the backbone. That means preparing annual and capital budgets, managing variance reporting, hitting revenue targets, and actively identifying ways to improve NOI through expense control and incremental revenue. You'll work inside platforms like Vena for budgeting and Entrata for day-to-day property management. If you've lived in Entrata before, you'll feel at home. If you haven't, expect a learning curve on Scion's full tech stack, which also includes ClickUp, Qualtrics, Turnable, and Lattice.

The annual turn process deserves its own mention. Student housing turns are high-volume, time-compressed, and physically demanding. This role requires hands-on involvement: move-out inspections, vendor walks, furniture moves, punch list completion, and coordinating staffing to hit hard move-in deadlines. You'll manage the financial performance of the turn as well, keeping controllable expenses within budget while the clock runs.

On the people side, you'll lead hiring through Greenhouse, manage scheduling including after-hours on-call coverage, and develop your team with an eye toward their next step at Scion. Staff morale and retention matter here because turnover during peak periods has direct operational consequences.

  • 3 or more years managing residential communities with a team of 3 or more direct reports
  • Proficiency in a property management system (Entrata strongly preferred)
  • Strong financial acumen: budget preparation, variance analysis, expense management
  • Conflict resolution and resident de-escalation experience
  • Vendor management and contract administration familiarity
  • Ability to work non-traditional hours during peak leasing, turn, and emergency situations

Where Strong Candidates Separate Themselves

Wilmington is home to UNC Wilmington, and the student housing market there reflects a mix of purpose-built communities competing on amenities, location, and resident experience scores. Operators who understand how reputation management and Qualtrics survey data translate into leasing velocity have a real edge. A score uptick on resident satisfaction often shows up in renewal rates and referral traffic before it shows up in occupancy numbers. GMs who track that connection and act on it outperform those who treat surveys as a reporting requirement.

The benefits package includes health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with matching, paid parental and maternal leave, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. The role is exempt and based on-site at Redpoint Wilmington. Scion does not offer visa sponsorship.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager (Colibri Commons)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Colibri Commons sits in East Palo Alto, one of the Bay Area's most historically underserved communities, and this role puts you at the center of keeping an affordable housing community running day to day. You'll report to the Community Manager and carry real operational weight across several functions that most ACM roles cover: rent collection, security deposit processing, petty cash reconciliation, and bank deposit prep. Compliance work here means supporting MOR reviews and TCAC recertifications, so familiarity with affordable housing regulatory frameworks matters. If you've touched Tax Credit properties before, that background translates directly.

On the leasing side, you'll manage the waitlist, schedule income verification appointments, process lease agreements, and coordinate vacancy turns. That means issuing notices, tracking turnover forms, and working with facilities staff to move work orders through the system at a pace that keeps units available. Property inspections are part of the rhythm, not a quarterly event. You'll also handle resident communications around emergency preparedness and help coordinate resident meetings, which in an affordable community often means working with people navigating real instability in their lives.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of residential property management, customer service, or administrative experience. A combination of education and relevant experience is considered.
  • Working knowledge of MS Office; RealPage experience is a plus in this environment
  • Comfort with affordable housing compliance processes, or a genuine willingness to learn them quickly
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, and the judgment to handle confidential resident files with care
  • The ability to work independently without someone checking in on you constantly
  • Alignment with affordable housing as a mission, not just a job category

A Word on the Role

Affordable housing management carries compliance obligations that market-rate properties don't. TCAC and MOR reviews require precision and documentation habits that take time to build. If you're coming from a conventional portfolio, expect a learning curve on the regulatory side. That said, the skills you build here transfer well: detailed file management, resident relations in high-need environments, and compliance fluency are all things that open doors in affordable housing, nonprofit housing, and even public agency roles over time.

MidPen has been in this work since 1970 and manages over 130 properties across Northern California. That scale means internal mobility exists for people who perform well and want to grow. The pay range for this position is $21.15 to $23.80 per hour, depending on experience, with a benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, retirement, and paid parental leave among other offerings.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The assistant community manager role exists at a specific intersection in multifamily operations: close enough to daily leasing activity to drive occupancy, and deep enough in the financials to understand what occupancy actually means for a property's health. At Hawthorne at Southside, a garden-style community in Asheville, NC, this position carries real operational weight across both of those dimensions.

What This Role Requires You to Bring

Hawthorne is looking for someone with at least two years of property management experience, and prior time in an assistant manager seat is a genuine advantage here. The financial side of this role demands more than familiarity with software. You'll own delinquency follow-up, post and reconcile payments, conduct ledger reviews, and coordinate eviction procedures when necessary. That's not administrative support work. That's hands-on accountability for the financial integrity of the property.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, respond to leads, process applications and renewals, and contribute directly to occupancy goals. Resident retention is part of the job too, which means handling conflict resolution with consistency and staying engaged with residents beyond the lease signing. Social media content management for the community is part of the scope as well, so comfort with resident-facing communication in that format matters.

When the Community Manager is out, you run the operation. That expectation is built into the role, not a rare occurrence.

What This Role Will Build

Candidates who grow fastest in assistant manager roles are those who treat the financial reporting exposure as a real education. Reading a T-12, understanding NOI, tracking delinquency trends, and connecting those numbers to leasing decisions are skills that separate community managers who can execute from those who can also think strategically about a property's performance. Hawthorne's Career Path Program formalizes that trajectory, with a stated path from assistant manager to community manager.

A CALP credential is a plus here. If you don't have one yet, this role gives you the operational foundation that makes that coursework click rather than feel abstract.

Schedule runs Monday through Friday with Saturday hours (10 AM to 4 PM), one weekday off per week to maintain a 40-hour schedule, and occasional evening availability for resident events. Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses.

  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of prior assistant manager experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP accreditation is a plus
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent required

Hawthorne is a Southeast-rooted company that ranks among the 50 largest multifamily management firms nationally. For someone who wants a defined path toward community manager and is ready to develop the financial fluency that role demands, this is a position worth taking seriously.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Workforce housing communities run on maintenance. Residents in market-rate, attainable product don't have concierge services or on-site amenities teams to absorb the gaps. When something breaks, the maintenance technician is the direct line between a livable home and a frustrated resident. Hillpointe, one of the Sun Belt's most active workforce housing developers, is hiring a Maintenance Technician for their Jacksonville portfolio to handle exactly that responsibility.

What This Role Actually Demands

The core of the job is mechanical diagnosis and repair across buildings, common areas, and grounds. You'll work through resident-submitted work orders, conduct inspections, and keep a punch list mentality on vacant units moving through the make-ready process. Preparing turns for incoming residents means working efficiently without cutting corners on quality, since a poorly prepped unit generates callbacks that eat into everyone's time.

Beyond reactive work, the role carries a preventive maintenance load. That means scheduled inspections, documentation, and inventory management so the property doesn't run short on parts when something urgent comes up. You'll also coordinate with vendors and contractors, which requires clear communication and enough technical knowledge to verify that outside work meets the property's standards.

  • Diagnose and repair mechanical issues in units, buildings, and common areas
  • Complete resident work orders and participate in a rotating on-call schedule (evenings, weekends, mornings)
  • Prepare vacant apartments through the make-ready process
  • Conduct pre-move-out inspections and maintain accurate documentation
  • Manage parts inventory and coordinate with vendors
  • Follow OSHA safety protocols and participate in safety meetings
  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification required (or willingness to obtain)
  • Valid driver's license required; physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly and work at heights

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Hillpointe builds and operates its own communities with in-house construction and asset management, which means maintenance staff work inside a more integrated ownership structure than you'd find at a typical third-party managed property. That's worth understanding. The standards are set by people who built the product, so attention to how things were constructed, and why certain systems work the way they do, genuinely matters.

The technicians who perform best in workforce housing maintenance are the ones who troubleshoot before they replace. Diagnostic thinking, the ability to read a situation and work through it systematically, is the skill that builds your value over time. The role also builds real competency in preventive maintenance planning, vendor coordination, and documentation habits that transfer directly if you move toward a Lead Technician or Maintenance Supervisor position down the road. The on-call rotation is an honest part of the job and requires someone who can respond effectively outside of standard hours without it affecting the quality of their daytime work.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (Broadlands Apartments)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a hands-on maintenance role at Broadlands Apartments, a Van Metre community in Ashburn, VA. You'll report to both the Property Manager and Service Manager, handling the day-to-day upkeep that keeps the property running and residents satisfied.

Most of your time breaks down into three areas: responding to resident service requests, performing unit turns on vacants, and keeping up with preventative maintenance and curb appeal. You'll walk the property daily, catch issues before they become problems, and flag safety or liability concerns to your supervisors. You'll also manage inventory in the maintenance storage areas and keep accurate records of completed work.

After-hours emergency coverage is part of the job. The property operates 24/7 and you'll rotate into that on-call schedule.

What You Bring

  • 1 to 2 years of maintenance experience, or equivalent hands-on training
  • Working knowledge of appliance repair, electrical, and plumbing
  • Basic HVAC knowledge; EPA certification preferred
  • Familiarity with OSHA and current building safety standards
  • Your own basic tools and the ability to use them safely
  • Valid driver's license
  • Availability on weekends

Compensation and Context

Pay runs $23 to $24 per hour depending on experience. Van Metre also offers up to $5,000 in annual bonus paid out quarterly, plus renewal commissions. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a company-matched 401(k), tuition reimbursement, company-paid certifications, and an annual wellness reimbursement up to $900. PTO includes 11 holidays, 10 vacation days, 10 sick days, and a handful of additional personal days including your birthday and an annual physical day.

One thing worth noting for candidates new to residential property maintenance: strong techs in this type of role often move into Service Manager positions within a few years, particularly at companies like Van Metre that promote from within and invest in certifications. If you're aiming to grow into a supervisory maintenance track, this kind of structured environment with clear performance evaluations gives you a real path to get there.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Community managers at stabilized multifamily properties spend a lot of time protecting what's already working. Occupancy is up, the team is in place, and the instinct is to maintain. Waypoint Management Services is looking for someone who treats that stability as a floor, not a ceiling, and keeps pushing NOI, retention, and team performance in the right direction.

This role is based in Jeffersonville, IN, directly across the Ohio River from Louisville. That market context matters: Southern Indiana has seen steady multifamily demand tied to Louisville's growth, and competitive awareness between submarkets is real. A manager here needs to watch what's happening on both sides of the bridge.

What the Role Actually Demands

You're running the full operation. That means owning the P&L, keeping delinquency tight, managing capex projects alongside day-to-day maintenance, and keeping your leasing team converting traffic at a rate that sustains occupancy. Waypoint expects Class A-level service delivery, which means resident experience isn't a soft metric here. It shows up in renewals, referrals, and eventually in the T-12 when you're defending your numbers. You'll prepare and manage the budget, report on financial performance, and bring solutions when variances appear. Collections, expense control, and rent growth strategies are all yours to drive.

On the team side, you're recruiting, coaching, and holding people accountable. Leasing consultants, maintenance techs, service staff. Building a culture where the team performs consistently, not just when you're watching, is a core part of this job. Waypoint also wants managers who think ahead on talent, keeping a pipeline so you're not scrambling when someone leaves.

Marketing and leasing aren't handed off to a centralized team. You're expected to develop and execute outreach strategy, run market surveys, and stay current on what competing communities are doing with concessions, pricing, and amenities.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least 3 years as a property manager and 5 or more years in multifamily overall, with Class A experience specifically
  • Demonstrated financial acumen: budgeting, AR/AP, capital project oversight, and reporting
  • Proficiency in Yardi and a CRM platform
  • Solid grounding in Fair Housing compliance and maintenance operations
  • A track record of developing leasing and service teams, not just managing them

The managers who stand out in roles like this are the ones who can read a variance report and immediately connect it to something happening on the ground, whether that's a spike in MTM residents, a delinquency trend, or a make-ready backlog that's slowing lease-ups. Financial fluency and operational instinct working together is the differentiator.

Waypoint offers a quarterly manager bonus, monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, an employee housing discount, medical, dental, and vision coverage starting day one, 401k with company match, 120 hours of PTO in year one with progressive increases, and two floating days annually.

job.title: Limpiador Residencial (Lunes a Viernes 7am-3pm y Domingo 7am-12pm)
job.description:
Residential properties run on first impressions. Lobbies, hallways, restrooms, and exterior walkways set the tone for how residents and visitors experience a community every single day. This porter role at Comstock's Reston, VA location keeps those spaces clean, safe, and presentable across a consistent weekday and Sunday schedule.

What the Work Looks Like

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 7am to 3pm, plus Sunday mornings from 7am to noon. You'll cover common areas throughout the property: lobbies, sidewalks, public restrooms, and shared spaces. Daily tasks include routine cleaning, pressure washing assigned areas, trash collection, and window cleaning. You'll follow checklists provided by the Senior Operations Manager and complete shift-end documentation before handing off to the next team member.

Beyond the daily routine, you'll support event setup and breakdown when the property hosts resident or public gatherings. If a cleaning concern comes up mid-shift, you address it. You'll also monitor supply inventory, flag equipment issues, and report any safety hazards or maintenance problems to management. Covering for teammates during absences is part of the job.

You'll wear the approved ParkX Porter uniform and arrive on site before your shift starts. Residents and guests will interact with you throughout the day, so professionalism and a friendly presence matter here as much as the physical work.

What You'll Need

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Ability to lift, push, or pull up to 50 pounds and stay on your feet for extended periods
  • Comfort working in variable temperatures, outdoors and indoors, with exposure to cleaning chemicals and biological hazards
  • Flexibility for weekend work and occasional off-schedule shifts during events or high-activity periods
  • Strong reliability and time management. Showing up on time and following through on assigned tasks is non-negotiable here
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision while staying accountable to team standards
  • Clear communication skills and a professional, approachable manner with residents and staff

Comstock offers medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) matching, life insurance, parental leave, free parking, and EV charging. The company also provides annual professional development funding, and there are advancement opportunities within their growing portfolio.

One thing worth knowing: porter roles at well-managed residential properties often serve as a reliable entry point into broader facilities or maintenance operations. Candidates who pay close attention to detail, communicate problems clearly, and build trust with the management team frequently move into lead or supervisory positions over time.

job.title: Administrative Assistant
job.description:
Property Management Associates has been running residential and commercial portfolios across greater Los Angeles County for over 30 years. This administrative role sits at the center of that operation, supporting both the residential department and the company's COO directly. That dual support structure means the work is genuinely varied, and the pace reflects it.

Day to day, you'll keep training schedules organized across the residential division, maintain spreadsheets that feed into reporting, and manage online advertising content for the portfolio. You'll also handle utility account setup and conduct utility audits, which requires attention to billing detail and a comfort with numbers even if you're not in an accounting role. The position puts you in contact with a wide range of people: site staff, corporate team members, vendors, residents, and property owners. That's a lot of different communication styles and expectations to manage in a single workday.

Honestly, the job has real administrative weight to it. Deadlines are firm, the COO's needs don't always align with a predictable schedule, and keeping spreadsheets accurate across a large residential portfolio is the kind of work that punishes distraction. If you're someone who finds that kind of precision satisfying rather than draining, this role is probably a good fit. If you prefer loosely structured days, it's probably not.

One thing worth knowing: administrative roles at full-service property management companies with portfolios this size tend to build transferable skills quickly. You get exposure to operations, owner communication, leasing systems, and financial tracking at a scale that smaller shops can't offer. People who start here often move into coordinator or property manager roles within a few years, especially at a company that says directly it invests in staff growth.

What You Bring

  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office and Outlook skills (this is a real requirement, not a formality)
  • Strong written and verbal communication, you'll be writing and speaking to everyone from maintenance staff to property owners
  • Genuine organizational discipline and the ability to meet firm deadlines without being managed toward them
  • Comfort navigating online platforms and managing digital content
  • Bilingual Spanish is a plus given the LA market

Compensation runs $25 to $28 per hour. Full-time employees receive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with an employer contribution, a 401(k) with company match, short and long-term disability coverage, and a solid PTO package that includes vacation, sick time, personal days, holidays, and parental leave. Fridays end an hour early, which is a small but genuine quality-of-life detail. The Culver City location keeps you close to the westside without the Santa Monica price tag.

job.title: Cleaner - Full-Time-Temporary
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. in Pullman and move-in weekend is two days out. The hallways need a pass, the parking garage has tracked-in mud from last night's rain, and a resident cleaning check is already on the schedule before noon. That's the rhythm of this role.

Redstone Residential operates one of the largest third-party student housing portfolios in the country, with more than 38,000 beds across 20 states. This position supports one of their Pullman communities, which means working within a student housing environment where turnover is seasonal, occupancy expectations are high, and curb appeal directly affects leasing traffic. The role is full-time and temporary, paying $18.00 per hour, with a 401(k) plan that includes up to 6% matching.

What the Work Looks Like

This is a hands-on, on-your-feet position. Most of the shift involves keeping common areas clean and presentable: hallways, the clubhouse, the leasing office, model units, and outdoor grounds. You'll conduct scheduled cleaning checks inside resident apartments to confirm units meet the property's cleanliness standards, a task that requires both consistency and a professional manner with residents. Snow and ice clearing, trash and debris removal, landscaping upkeep, and basic maintenance assists round out the day-to-day. You'll be expected to manage your task list with minimal supervision.

Pullman's student population means this property likely sees concentrated turnover periods around the academic calendar. Keeping common areas sharp during peak traffic times matters more here than it would at a conventional mid-rise with staggered lease expirations. A strong cleaner in this context understands that the condition of a hallway or entrance is often the first impression a prospective resident gets on a tour.

What Redstone Is Looking For

  • Prior janitorial or cleaning experience in a residential, commercial, or institutional setting
  • Ability to complete daily tasks independently and stay on schedule without close direction
  • Physical capability to lift 50 or more pounds and remain on your feet for four to six hours at a stretch
  • A genuinely friendly, professional manner when interacting with residents and team members
  • Willingness to participate in Redstone's required training program

Candidates who do well in roles like this tend to take visible pride in the finished product, not just the completion of a checklist. In student housing specifically, the ability to stay consistent during busy periods (move-in, move-out, inspection weeks) without cutting corners is what separates reliable team members from ones who don't last through the season.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Roving -Terava, The Hixon and Lakeside Place
job.description:
Roving maintenance roles exist because no single property can always justify a full bench of technicians, but every property still needs consistent, skilled coverage. CloudTen Residential has structured this position to float across three Bend, Oregon communities: Lakeside Place, Terava, and The Hixon. If you know Bend's rental market, you know it's grown fast over the past decade, and the properties that hold occupancy are the ones that keep units tight and curb appeal sharp. This role sits at the center of that.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day shifts between sites depending on where the need is greatest. One morning you might be knocking out a punch list of service requests at one property; by afternoon you're helping another team get a unit rent-ready before a new lease starts. The 3-to-5-day turn window is the standard here, so you'll move through make-readies with purpose: appliance repair, basic electrical, plumbing, painting, and anything else a unit needs to get back on the market clean and safe.

Beyond turns, you're handling day-to-day service requests with a 24-hour resolution target, supporting pool and spa upkeep, keeping common areas presentable, and running monthly preventive maintenance rounds that cover life safety systems, lighting, fire safety checks, and pool equipment. You'll need to know where shutoffs live at each site and be comfortable communicating delays to both residents and site managers when parts or scheduling push timelines out.

On-call emergency response is part of the job. After-hours calls come with the territory in any maintenance role, and this one is no exception. The flexibility to respond on evenings and weekends is a real requirement, not a footnote.

What CloudTen Is Looking For

  • One to two years of hands-on maintenance experience across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and painting
  • A valid driver's license (required, since you're moving between properties)
  • Comfort working independently and managing your own schedule across multiple sites
  • Basic computer and mobile device skills for work order systems and documentation
  • Strong communication habits, both with residents and with site management teams you're supporting
  • Availability for weekends, evenings, and holiday coverage

Pay runs $25.00 to $27.00 per hour depending on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, company-paid life insurance, an FSA option, and paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.

One thing that separates strong candidates in a roving role: the ability to walk into a property you don't manage daily and still get things done efficiently. You won't always have the home-field advantage of knowing where every tool is stored or which residents tend to submit repeat requests. Adaptability and organization matter here more than they do in a single-site position, and technicians who build that skill set often move into lead or supervisor roles as a natural next step.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A prospect walks in off the street after seeing the listing online. They have questions, a budget, and maybe a move-in date three weeks out. Your job starts the moment they walk through the door.

Griffis Residential is hiring a Leasing Consultant for their Seattle community. This is a front-line sales and service role. You'll handle inbound traffic from prospects, conduct apartment tours, qualify applicants, and carry deals from first contact through signed lease. You'll also support renewals, move-in and move-out procedures, and coordinate with the maintenance team when resident concerns need follow-up.

What the Work Looks Like

Day to day, you're fielding calls and emails, scheduling tours, and walking prospects through available units. You match what you know about the apartment to what the prospect actually needs. You prep leases, track applications, and make sure nothing falls through the cracks between inquiry and move-in. On the marketing side, you support efforts to keep the community visible and the pipeline moving. Weekend availability is required; some evenings come with the territory.

Griffis operates luxury apartment communities, so the expectation is polished, professional communication across every channel. Residents and prospects notice when that standard slips.

What Griffis Is Looking For

  • High school diploma required; a bachelor's degree or NALP certification is preferred
  • At least one year of onsite leasing experience, or a background in hospitality, sales, or a similar customer-facing field
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort multitasking across phone, email, and in-person interactions simultaneously
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing regulations (a plus, but not a hard requirement)
  • Availability to work weekends and occasional evenings

The pay range is $23 to $25 per hour. Benefits include a 50% rental discount, a quarterly bonus program (up to $2,000 annually), per-lease occupancy bonuses starting at $175, medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with up to 4% company match, a minimum of three weeks PTO accruing from day one, 11 paid holidays, tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 per year, and paid parental leave.

One thing worth knowing: leasing consultant experience translates directly into assistant manager and property manager roles. Companies like Griffis promote from within, and time spent in leasing builds the resident relations, sales, and administrative skills that those next-level roles require. If you're treating this as a stepping stone into property management, this is a reasonable place to build that foundation.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Student housing operates on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Lease-up happens in the fall for the following academic year, the turn is compressed into a few brutal weeks in August, and your residents' parents are often just as involved as the residents themselves. The Assistant Community Manager role at The Domain at Waco exists inside that specific rhythm, and the person who thrives here understands that the financial office and the leasing floor aren't separate jobs , they're the same job.

The financial responsibilities here are real and central. You own the delinquency process from first notice through payment plan negotiations to guarantor outreach to coordinating with legal on evictions when it comes to that. You're posting payments, reconciling ledgers, preparing weekly and monthly reporting on occupancy and variance, handling security deposit dispositions, and coding invoices against budget. Clean books aren't a bonus , they're the baseline expectation. If spreadsheets make you anxious, this isn't the right fit.

At the same time, you carry an individual leasing and renewal goal during pre-lease season. By-the-bed leasing has its own mechanics: roommate matching, unit assignments, guarantor verification, and the particular patience required when you're explaining a joint-and-several lease structure to a parent in Houston who's never rented an apartment. You'll work the full pipeline from lead to signed lease, support renewal campaigns, and participate in on-campus outreach. Baylor's student population is the market , knowing that calendar matters.

When the Community Manager is off-site, you run the property. That means you need to already understand how the pieces connect: what a delinquency spike does to NOI, why curb appeal on move-in day matters to retention, how a botched punch list during turn creates maintenance headaches for twelve months. You'll also help hire and train leasing staff and Community Assistants, participate in the on-call rotation, and assist with annual turn inspections, punch walks, and move-in readiness.

What separates strong candidates in this role isn't leasing charisma. It's follow-through. Student housing offices get loud in August and quiet in October, and the people who struggle are usually the ones who can close a lease but let the ledger slide, or who handle the front desk well but disappear when a parent calls upset about a damage charge. The job rewards people who close every loop, document every outcome, and treat the delinquency number as their own.

What Karya is looking for

  • At least one year in property management, leasing, hospitality, or a comparable customer-facing role
  • Comfort with ledgers, reconciliation, and spreadsheet-level math
  • Ability to work weekends and extended hours during pre-lease season, turn, and move-in
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Prior student housing or by-the-bed leasing experience is preferred, as is familiarity with Entrata or RealPage
  • Bilingual English/Spanish is a plus

Compensation includes an hourly rate, leasing commissions, renewal bonuses, and quarterly or annual performance bonuses tied to occupancy and delinquency targets. Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, and paid time off are included. A housing discount or on-site apartment may be available depending on circumstances.

job.title: Leasing Agent
job.description:
Urban lease-up shops live and die by first impressions, and at FLATS, the leasing agent is that impression. This Chicago-based lifestyle brand operates with a design-forward identity and a tech-integrated approach to apartment living, which means the leasing role here carries more brand weight than a typical Class B shop where you're just filling units.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

You'll own the full leasing cycle: fielding inquiries, conducting tailored tours, following up on leads through calls, texts, and email, and closing leases while hitting monthly targets. The follow-up cadence is where most leasing agents either earn their keep or fall behind. Traffic without conversion is just noise. Beyond closing, you'll handle applications, prepare lease documents, and keep records clean and compliant, which matters in Illinois where leasing activity is regulated and your license status is a real requirement. Either an Illinois Leasing Agent or Broker's License, or the ability to get a 120-day Student Permit before your start date, is non-negotiable here.

Move-in coordination is part of the role too. You'll make sure units are market-ready and that the move-in experience matches the brand promise. Resident concerns that surface early in a tenancy often land on the leasing agent's desk before anyone else's. How you handle those moments affects retention as much as it affects your own reputation on the team.

Weekend and evening availability is part of the job. That's true at most lease-up focused properties, and FLATS is direct about it.

What FLATS Is Looking For

  • Illinois Leasing Agent or Broker's License, or eligibility for a 120-day Student Permit
  • Prior leasing or sales experience, with a track record of closing
  • Strong written and verbal communication, the kind that works across email threads, phone calls, and face-to-face tours
  • Organized enough to manage multiple leads, applications, and move-in timelines simultaneously
  • Flexible schedule that covers evenings and weekends when prospect traffic peaks

Where This Role Can Take You

Leasing agents who develop genuine sales instincts and operational fluency tend to move into assistant manager or property manager roles within a few years. At a company like FLATS that runs multiple urban properties, internal mobility is realistic for people who demonstrate both closing ability and the kind of ownership mentality the company explicitly values. The skills that transfer are real ones: lead management, lease compliance, market comp knowledge, and resident relations. Those carry weight at virtually any multifamily operator.

What separates strong candidates here from average ones is the ability to sell the lifestyle authentically without it feeling like a script. FLATS leans hard into brand identity. Prospects who tour these properties are often choosing between a FLATS unit and several other well-appointed options in the same neighborhood. The agent who can articulate what makes the community distinct, and back it up with genuine product knowledge and a polished follow-up process, is the one who closes.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Supervisor - Venue at Lakewood
job.description:
Maintenance supervisors at AIR Communities carry two distinct skill sets at once: hands-on technical competence and people management. This role at Venue at Lakewood in Bradenton demands both, every day. If you're stronger in one area than the other, this probably isn't the right fit.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

The technical side covers what you'd expect from a full-service apartment maintenance operation: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and general building systems. You'll oversee preventative maintenance schedules, manage apartment turns to get units ready for move-in, and field resident service requests alongside your team. AIR uses modern maintenance technology to track and prioritize work orders, so comfort with digital tools matters here.

The management side is just as active. You'll lead at least one direct report, coordinate vendor relationships, and communicate capital and maintenance needs up to property management. Budget oversight is part of the job. You're expected to track spend, flag issues early, and keep quality high without letting costs drift.

Environmental health and safety compliance is a real part of this role. AIR has operating procedures and regulatory requirements that the maintenance team is responsible for following. You'll need to know those standards and make sure your team does too.

What the Role Requires

  • At least 3 years of technical maintenance and facilities experience in residential property management
  • 1 to 3 years of supervisory or team lead experience in a maintenance or customer service setting
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule including evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts (at minimum one week per month)
  • Physical ability to move heavy equipment and machinery
  • Reliable personal transportation
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and genuine attention to detail
  • English fluency (read, write, speak)

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The supervisors who do well in roles like this are the ones who troubleshoot fast and communicate clearly. Bradenton's climate means HVAC demand stays high through much of the year. Candidates who know refrigerant systems well and can diagnose problems without waiting on a vendor call will have a real advantage. On the management side, the difference usually comes down to how well someone can develop a team member who's still learning. That's a different skill than doing the repair yourself, and AIR puts weight on it.

AIR offers an on-site apartment benefit, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, paid parental leave, tuition assistance, and full reimbursement for job-related certifications and licenses. That last point is worth noting for anyone looking to add credentials like EPA 608 or CAMT to their resume while working.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Bozzuto operates some of the most well-regarded residential communities on the East Coast, and their maintenance teams carry a real operational weight. The Assistant Maintenance Manager role at their Alexandria property sits at the intersection of hands-on trade work and team leadership. You're not just fixing things. You're running a program.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day is built around two priorities: keeping current residents comfortable and getting vacant units back online fast. That means staying sharp on service ticket volume, making sure HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance calls get closed out properly, and following up with residents so nothing slips. On the make-ready side, you're managing the turn process from punch list to move-in ready, which directly affects how quickly new leases can start. A slow turn is a real NOI drag, and you'll feel that pressure in a community like this one.

Beyond the reactive work, you're also executing preventative maintenance programs that protect the asset long-term. That includes mechanical systems like boilers, chillers, and central plant components, not just unit-level repairs. Snow removal and grounds upkeep fall in your scope too, and so does maintaining the safety and code compliance standards that keep the property operating without incident.

Weekend availability and participation in the emergency on-call rotation are part of this role. That's standard at this level in multifamily, but worth knowing going in.

What Bozzuto Expects You to Bring

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities maintenance, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems including split systems, boilers, and chillers
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Understanding of OSHA, MSDS, and risk management practices
  • Supervisory experience or a demonstrated ability to lead a small team
  • Comfort with technology platforms, work order systems, and Microsoft Office basics
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb ladders, and work in varying weather

Where This Role Can Take You

Strong Assistant Maintenance Managers at companies like Bozzuto typically move into Maintenance Manager roles within a few years, taking full ownership of a community's physical plant and maintenance budget. The skills you build here, specifically preventative maintenance discipline, turn efficiency, and team supervision, translate directly to portfolio-level facilities roles as well. The salary range for this position runs from $68,000 to $70,000, with bonus eligibility, plus a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off, 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

If you think in terms of asset preservation and take personal ownership of the physical product your residents experience every day, this is a role worth a serious look.

job.title: Affordable Housing Compliance Specialist
job.description:
A file lands in the queue at 8 a.m. By 8 a.m. the next day, it needs a compliance decision. That 24-hour review window is the operational heartbeat of this role.

The Work

Asset Living, one of the NMHC top 50 third-party management firms, is hiring an Affordable Housing Compliance Specialist for a position based in Staten Island, NY. This role sits inside Asset Living's affordable housing division and focuses on keeping resident files audit-ready and fully aligned with LIHTC regulatory requirements.

Day to day, you'll review incoming applicant files for eligibility and compliance, working against that 24-hour turnaround standard. You'll track regulatory changes in the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program and translate those changes into updated internal processes. When outside entities conduct tax credit reviews, you're in the room. When TDHCA schedules its annual training, you're on the calendar. This position also carries a significant travel component: roughly 50% of your time annually, covering property visits, conferences, and training sessions.

The HCCP designation is a clear milestone in this role. If you don't already hold it, you'll be expected to complete the Housing Credit Certified Professional training and pass the exam within your first two years. That credential signals genuine fluency in tax credit compliance, and Asset Living is investing in getting you there.

What You Bring

  • Detail orientation that holds up under volume. Compliance errors in affordable housing files can trigger findings during audits, so accuracy isn't negotiable.
  • Working knowledge of LIHTC eligibility rules and regulatory frameworks. HUD program familiarity is a plus.
  • Hands-on experience with RealPage Onesite Tax Credit software, or the computer literacy to get there quickly.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills. You'll document findings clearly and interact with property staff, applicants, and external reviewers.
  • HCCP designation, or the willingness to pursue it on the timeline described above.

The salary for this role in New York is set at $60,000.

One thing worth understanding about affordable housing compliance as a career path: specialists who build deep LIHTC and HUD audit experience tend to move into regional compliance manager roles or portfolio-level compliance director positions. The combination of file-level technical skill and regulatory monitoring you'll develop here translates directly into higher-level oversight work as Asset Living's affordable housing portfolio grows.

job.title: Business Manager - The Overlook at Quarry Hill
job.description:
Austin's Class A multifamily market keeps pushing rents and expectations upward, which means the Business Manager role at a luxury community carries real weight. You're running the full asset: financial performance, team development, resident experience, and physical condition of the property. That's not a coordinator title with a manager label slapped on it.

The Overlook at Quarry Hill is an Olympus Property community, and Olympus has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer recognition three consecutive years. The Business Manager here reports to Regional Leadership and owns the daily operation from every angle, including budgeting, vendor contracts, leasing programs, and maintenance oversight.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On the financial side, you're building and managing annual business plans, reviewing T-12 performance, tracking NOI, and having real conversations with your Regional Manager and Regional VP about where the asset is and where it's headed. You're not just reporting numbers; you're expected to have a point of view on them. Monthly budget projections, occupancy strategy, and capex decisions all run through you.

On the people side, you're leading an onsite team of both office and maintenance staff. That means hiring, training, counseling, and motivating people who handle everything from make-readies and punch lists to lease renewals and traffic conversion. Keeping a luxury Class A community in market-ready condition requires a maintenance team that's on its game and a leasing team that knows how to close.

Vendor relationships matter here too. You'll bid, negotiate, and manage service contracts and one-time projects, which requires some comfort with the numbers behind those decisions, not just the relationship side.

RealPage, Knock, and OneSite experience is strongly preferred. If you've been running reports and managing delinquency out of OneSite for a few years, that's a real advantage.

Who Fits This Role

  • Minimum two years of experience as a property manager in multifamily, with luxury or Class A background preferred
  • Comfort reading and presenting financial reports to regional leadership
  • Experience managing both leasing and maintenance staff at the same time
  • RealPage/OneSite/Knock platform familiarity
  • Availability Monday through Friday with flexibility for after-hours resident events and emergencies

The base salary range is $65,000 to $68,000, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program, among others.

One thing worth noting for candidates coming from smaller operators: Olympus runs a structured career pathing program and sends managers to Budget Camp and Leadership Conferences. If you've been running a community without much institutional support, this environment offers more infrastructure than you might be used to, and that's either appealing or an adjustment depending on your style.

job.title: Field Support Supervisor - Multifamily Regional Maintenance
job.description:
Regional maintenance roles at multifamily companies tend to fall into two buckets: the ones that are mostly administrative oversight, and the ones that actually put you on the ground with tools, blueprints, and conversations that matter. This one is clearly the second kind. Weinstein Properties, a family-owned operator with more than 70 years in the business, is adding a Field Support Supervisor to cover several of their Dallas-Fort Worth communities.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll move between properties regularly, so a desk isn't your home base. On any given week, you might be reviewing a contractor's proposal for exterior repairs at one community, walking a punch list on a project transitioning from the construction team at another, and helping a site maintenance supervisor think through a water intrusion problem at a third. The role touches capital projects, vendor management, and day-to-day operational support in equal measure.

Weinstein self-manages their portfolio, which means the Asset Management and Support team you'd join works closely with the people actually running the properties. You're not a third-party consultant parachuting in. You're a resource that property teams can rely on, which means your relationships with maintenance supervisors and community managers matter as much as your technical knowledge.

  • Frequent property visits to assess needs and provide hands-on technical guidance
  • Managing projects from scoping through completion, including vendor selection and proposal review
  • Supporting the handoff of construction projects to property teams, including documentation and knowledge transfer
  • Evaluating products, equipment, and contractors, and encouraging qualified vendors to bid competitively
  • Identifying capital needs, erosion issues, water intrusion, and exterior building concerns, then writing clear work requirements to address them

Who Fits This Role Well

The minimum bar here is real: EPA certification (Type I and II or Universal), at least five years in multifamily maintenance, and three or more years in a regional support capacity. The ability to read blueprints and a valid driver's license are both required, not optional. If you've spent time on capex projects and know how to evaluate a contractor's scope before signing off on it, that experience will be put to use immediately.

What separates stronger candidates from technically qualified ones in this kind of role is usually communication. You're working across property managers, maintenance supervisors, vendors, and a construction group. The ability to give clear guidance without being dismissive of what site teams are already dealing with makes a significant difference in whether people actually call you for help or try to work around you.

A Note on the Company

Weinstein Properties has operated for over 70 years as a family-owned company with communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That longevity in a competitive industry reflects something real about how they operate. The company's stated focus on customer experience isn't just marketing language here. It shows up in how they think about property operations, which means the support function you'd be filling is tied directly to resident outcomes, not just asset performance numbers.

Compensation is competitive, and the company offers benefits and a 401k. If you're based in or near DFW and want a regional role with genuine variety and direct impact on how properties run day to day, this is worth a serious look.

job.title: Dual-Site Leasing & Marketing Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

Student housing leasing moves fast and follows a rhythm most conventional multifamily managers never experience. Annual turnover isn't a figure on a T-12; it's a full operational event where hundreds of residents move out and a new cohort moves in within a compressed window. The Leasing and Marketing Manager role at Scion's Ion Austin and Lark Austin communities requires someone who can hold a sales conversation in the morning, pull traffic and conversion KPIs in the afternoon, and still coach a team member through a difficult prospect interaction before the day ends. Interpersonal skill, data literacy, and genuine comfort with a six-day workweek during peak periods all matter here.

This is a dual-site position, so the ability to context-switch between two communities without losing track of either property's occupancy goals, concession budgets, or resident feedback loops is a real daily demand.
