That last piece matters more than most postings let on. A rocky move-in can undo a great sales experience, so your relationship with the maintenance team isn't just collegial, it's functional. Residents remember how their first day went.

Beyond traffic and tours, you'll handle the administrative side of leasing: keeping rental files current, entering data accurately, and making sure the paperwork behind each new resident is organized and complete. Monthly admin tasks come with the territory too. It's detail work that doesn't always get glamorized in job descriptions, but it's what keeps occupancy numbers reliable and delinquency low.

The multi-site nature of this position means you'll build familiarity with more than one community. That exposure accelerates learning. You start to see how different properties operate, what drives traffic at each location, and how occupancy challenges vary by asset. For someone with ambitions beyond a single-site leasing role, that context is genuinely useful early in a career.

What separates strong candidates in a role like this is usually the balance between sales instincts and follow-through. Plenty of people can give a great tour. Fewer stay sharp on the file management, the lease prep details, and the resident communication after move-in. MG Properties is looking for someone who handles both ends of that spectrum consistently.

What you'll bring

  • At least one year of property management experience (preferred)
  • Solid sales and customer service skills, with professional communication habits
  • Comfort working in a team environment across multiple properties
  • Attention to detail in data entry and file organization
  • Ability to interact with residents calmly and professionally when handling complaints or maintenance concerns

Compensation includes monthly and quarterly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401k with employer match, and a full benefits package covering medical, dental, and vision. Employees also receive rental discounts, paid holidays, personal days, and paid sick time. MG Properties participates in E-Verify, maintains a drug-free workplace, and requires a background check and drug screen prior to hire.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Student housing operates on a calendar that doesn't care about yours. Lease-up timelines are locked to academic years, turn happens in a matter of weeks rather than months, and the resident base turns over almost entirely in a single summer. If you've managed conventional multifamily, you understand occupancy and NOI. Student housing adds a layer of intensity that sharpens every one of those skills faster.

The Scion Group is filling a Community Manager position at University House Midtown in Atlanta, a market with deep student housing demand anchored by Georgia Tech and Georgia State. This role carries the full weight of general management: budget ownership, team leadership, leasing performance, facilities oversight, and the annual turn process that defines whether the asset starts the academic year in strong shape or scrambling to catch up.

Day-to-day, the job moves between financial and operational work. You're reviewing variance reports and managing month-end processes one hour, then walking units with a vendor on a punch list the next. During turn, the role gets genuinely physical. Scion is direct about this: moving furniture, clearing resident trash, and helping the facilities team hit deadlines are part of the job. That's not a footnote. It's how you build credibility with your team and keep the timeline intact when volume spikes.

The financial scope here is real. You'll prepare annual and capital budgets, manage NOI targets, track concessions and leasing velocity, and work through month-end close with partner departments. Scion uses Vena for budgeting and Entrata as the property management system, so comfort with purpose-built PM platforms matters. The role also carries revenue responsibility beyond base rents, including gain-to-lease performance and market rate achievement.

From a career development standpoint, this role builds something specific. General managers who succeed in student housing tend to develop unusually strong turn execution skills, high-volume leasing instincts, and team management experience under real deadline pressure. Those skills translate directly into regional manager roles, director-level operations positions, or asset management functions. Scion's internal structure includes a learning reimbursement program, which signals that upward movement is supported rather than assumed.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • At least three years managing a residential community with a team of three or more direct reports
  • Demonstrated experience with financial reporting, budgeting, and expense management
  • Proficiency with property management software, with Entrata experience preferred
  • Strong conflict resolution and vendor management skills
  • Availability for after-hours on-call response and non-traditional hours during peak periods
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

The candidate who stands out in this kind of role combines financial discipline with genuine presence on the property. Reviewing numbers in isolation isn't enough. Scion's scorecard model and monthly property walks mean the GM is expected to see problems before they appear in the data, not after. If you've managed through a full academic-year cycle and understand how turn performance connects to NOI, you'll find the scope here both familiar and worth growing into.

job.title: Community Manager (Mission Gateway)
job.description:
A resident stops you in the courtyard to ask about her recertification paperwork, a maintenance request from the night before is still sitting open, and your leasing coordinator needs a quick answer before the office fills up with foot traffic. That's the rhythm of this role at Mission Gateway in Union City.

The Work Itself

MidPen Housing has been developing and managing affordable communities across Northern California since 1970, and this Community Manager position sits at the center of daily operations at Mission Gateway. You'll report to the Property Manager and lead a small on-site team through the full range of property operations: rent collection, delinquency management, unit turns, and lease-ups for available units, alongside the compliance work that affordable housing demands. That means accurate income certifications, recertifications, and documentation that satisfies HUD, TCAC, and Fair Housing requirements. The regulatory piece is real and ongoing, not occasional.

Facilities are part of the picture too. You'll set preventative maintenance schedules, walk the property daily, coordinate repairs, and keep curb appeal where it needs to be. You'll also build relationships outside the property itself, connecting with local community organizations, city contacts, and safety partners to support the broader health of the community. MidPen's Resident Services team works alongside Property Management, so you'll have colleagues focused on resident stability, and you'll need to collaborate with them regularly.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least three years of multi-family residential management experience, with a minimum of two years specifically in affordable housing
  • At least one year of supervisory experience, with a real track record of coaching and developing staff
  • Tax Credit Specialist or Certified Occupancy Specialist certification, or the commitment to earn one within six months (MidPen covers the cost)
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing law and the ability to pass the FHA test within your first 60 days
  • Comfort with RealPage and the Microsoft Office Suite
  • An Associate degree or equivalent combination of education and experience

What separates strong candidates here is comfort holding two things at once: the compliance and fiscal discipline that affordable housing requires, and genuine care for the people living in the community. Managers who treat recertifications as purely administrative tend to struggle in this environment. The residents at Mission Gateway are working families, seniors, and people with special needs. They notice when you're present, and they notice when you're not.

The pay range for this role is $28.46 to $32.02 per hour, based on experience. MidPen offers health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, FSA options, an employee education reimbursement program, and an EAP, among other benefits. MidPen was certified as a Great Place to Work in 2025, which reflects something real about the culture, though any honest observer would tell you that affordable housing management is demanding work. The mission is genuine. So is the workload.

job.title: Property Manager (Hadley)
job.description:
Mountain View sits inside one of the most closely regulated rental markets in California, where local rent ordinances, just-cause eviction rules, and tenant protection laws create real operational complexity. The Neighborhood Director role at Prometheus Real Estate Group exists precisely because managing a property here demands more than occupancy tracking. It requires someone who can hold financial, operational, and cultural accountability simultaneously.

What This Role Actually Demands

Prometheus uses the title "Neighborhood Director" rather than Property Manager, and the distinction reflects a genuine difference in scope. You'll own the financial performance of your community, reading variance reports, managing to an operating budget, and making judgment calls on everything from capital project recommendations to day-to-day expense control. You'll need fluency with market dynamics and local rental ordinances, because in a jurisdiction like Mountain View, compliance isn't background knowledge. It's a daily operational reality.

On the customer side, you're the final escalation point. When a resident brings a complex housing law question or a service complaint that's gone unresolved, it lands with you. The role also keeps you close to the leasing floor when traffic picks up. Touring prospects and answering phones aren't beneath this position. They're part of how you stay connected to your team and your community's performance.

Leadership here is direct and hands-on. You'll work alongside your Neighborhood Service Manager to make sure your maintenance and leasing teams have what they need to do their jobs well. Coaching your team and tracking their development is part of your scorecard, not an afterthought.

What You'll Bring vs. What You'll Build

The role requires at least two years in a leasing position, along with demonstrated strength in customer service, sales, and marketing. A bachelor's degree is preferred, though a high school diploma or GED meets the minimum. You should arrive with a clear understanding of how a residential community runs financially and operationally.

What the role builds is harder to list but worth naming. Managing a community in a high-scrutiny California market sharpens your regulatory literacy faster than most roles will. Owning both the people side and the financial side at the same time develops the kind of judgment that carries into regional management. Directors who perform well here often move into oversight of multiple communities or into operations leadership.

Candidates who stand out tend to combine financial discipline with genuine relationship skills. The ones who struggle usually excel at one and underinvest in the other. In a market where residents know their rights and expect accountability, the interpersonal dimension of this role carries real weight.

Compensation ranges from $109,720 to $119,600 annually, with a discretionary semi-annual bonus plan and additional incentive opportunities tied to referrals, training, renovation, lease-up performance, and leasing contests. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage for eligible employees and dependents, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, tenure-based housing discounts, and paid volunteer time.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Hawthorne Residential Partners runs a tight, Southeast-rooted portfolio and consistently ranks among the 50 largest multifamily operators in the country. The District at Phenix City, located on College Drive, is one of those communities where the assistant manager role carries real operational weight. This position covers the full range of day-to-day responsibilities: leasing, rent collection, delinquency follow-up, ledger reviews, and stepping in for the Community Manager when needed.

The financial side of this role is more demanding than many ACM positions at comparable properties. You'll post payments, monitor delinquencies with weekly follow-up calls, coordinate eviction procedures when necessary, and conduct ledger audits to catch billing errors before they become disputes. That kind of financial discipline, applied consistently, is what keeps NOI stable and reporting clean for regional leadership.

On the leasing side, you'll handle tours, respond to leads, process applications and renewals, and manage the community's social media presence to support traffic and retention. Occupancy goals are real targets here, not suggestions. The office runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays from 10 to 4, with one weekday off to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Some evenings and weekends come up for resident events.

Phenix City sits directly across the Chattahoochee from Columbus, Georgia, and draws a notable share of its renter base from Fort Moore (formerly Fort Benning). That military-adjacent demand creates a steady flow of relocating residents on tight timelines, which means your leasing process needs to be efficient and your paperwork needs to be accurate. PCS-driven turnover also puts a premium on strong retention efforts with the residents who do stay longer term.

What Hawthorne is looking for

  • High school diploma or GED; two years of property management experience preferred
  • At least six months in an assistant community manager role is a plus
  • Comfort reading financial reports and making decisions within budget constraints
  • Proven ability to de-escalate resident conflicts calmly and follow through on resolution
  • Valid driver's license; CALP certification is a bonus but not required

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Hawthorne also runs a formal Career Path Program, so ACMs who perform well have a defined route toward a Community Manager role. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, and paid parental and adoption leave.

Strong candidates for this role tend to be people who already understand that leasing and financial administration aren't separate jobs. They feed each other. High occupancy without clean ledgers creates problems. Clean ledgers without consistent leasing create different ones. The ACMs who advance at companies like Hawthorne are the ones who treat both sides of the role with equal seriousness from day one.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance technicians are the operational backbone of any apartment community. Leasing fills units; maintenance keeps residents in them. When service requests pile up and turns take too long, occupancy numbers follow. Paragon Properties understands this, which is why the Maintenance Service Technician role at Knottingham Apartments in Clinton Township carries real weight and real compensation to match.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a full-cycle maintenance position at a residential apartment community. Day to day, you'll work through service requests across plumbing, electrical, appliances, HVAC, and pool or spa equipment. When a unit turns, you're handling the make-ready: drywall patching, painting, rough carpentry, and whatever punch list items stand between a vacant unit and a new resident moving in. You're also responsible for curb appeal and the physical integrity of the property, which means flagging potential liabilities and recommending improvements before small issues compound into capital expenses. After-hours on-call rotation is part of the job, including weekends and holidays, and Paragon pays a bonus for that availability.

Pay runs up to $26 per hour depending on experience and certifications, and the schedule is guaranteed full-time at 40 hours per week. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision with a short enrollment wait, 401(k) with employer contribution, paid time off, nine company holidays, a rent discount, company-paid life and disability insurance, and a tool kit issued after your first 30 days. Paragon also runs a formal training and certification program with advancement built into the structure.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience, whether technical, vocational, or on the job
  • HVAC Type II or Universal certification strongly preferred; heating and cooling repair and replacement is a core part of this work
  • Solid grasp of safety procedures and the judgment to apply them in the field
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • High school diploma required; trade school or college-level coursework preferred
  • Ability to work outdoors across all seasons
  • Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and physical are required

The candidates who thrive here tend to have breadth, not just depth. A technician who can handle an HVAC diagnostic in the morning, close out a plumbing ticket at midday, and prep a unit for move-in by afternoon moves turns faster and builds trust with residents in a way that specialist-only technicians can't. That versatility is what separates a strong candidate from an average one in this kind of role.

From a career standpoint, a position like this builds the foundation for lead technician and maintenance supervisor roles. Technicians who add HVAC Universal certification, develop vendor relationships, and take ownership of preventive maintenance schedules tend to move into those supervisory tracks within a few years. Paragon's stated commitment to training and advancement makes that trajectory more accessible than it is at companies where technicians are left to develop on their own.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor, 300-500 Units - Houston, TX
job.description:
Maintenance Supervisors at Berkshire Residential carry real operational weight. You're not just fixing things , you're running a service team, keeping the physical asset in shape, and making sure residents actually feel that effort. At Tinsley on the Park, a 300 to 500 unit community in Houston, that means managing both the day-to-day work order flow and the longer view on property condition.

What the Job Covers

You'll lead the service team directly: scheduling work, monitoring output, coaching staff, and setting the standard for quality on every turn and make-ready. The property manager leans on you to uphold physical standards across the community, so communication between maintenance and the office side needs to be tight. You'll also own the shop itself , equipment, supplies, inventory, and key security fall under your watch.

  • Lead and mentor the maintenance team; model the performance standards you expect
  • Schedule daily and ongoing service activities, balancing urgency with quality
  • Tour routes and models regularly to keep them show-ready
  • Enforce safety protocols across all maintenance operations
  • Stay familiar with the property budget and flag long-range capital needs
  • Deliver consistent, professional service to residents and prospective residents

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which matters here. You're not working for a third-party operator whose priorities shift with every ownership change. The decisions made on-site have a direct line to the investment. That tends to create a more stable environment for maintenance leadership.

What They're Looking For

At minimum: two years of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community, plus at least one year leading a team. You should be comfortable with property management technology and able to communicate clearly in writing and in person. Beyond the checklist, the candidates who thrive in this kind of role are the ones who treat the service team as something worth developing, not just deploying. Coaching matters here as much as wrenches.

A Note on the Role's Scope

Houston's apartment market runs hot, and Class A and B communities in the area face real pressure to hold occupancy through service reputation. A well-run maintenance operation reduces delinquency friction, cuts unit downtime on turns, and keeps renewal rates from slipping. Supervisors who understand that connection between physical operations and financial performance tend to move into regional or portfolio-level roles faster than those who stay heads-down on work orders alone.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and competitive benefits. If you have the experience and want a role where your work has visible impact on both the team and the asset, this one is worth a close look.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Redstone Residential runs more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, making it one of the larger third-party student housing operators in the country. This Community Manager role sits at their Logan, Utah property. It's the top site-level position, which means full ownership: financials, leasing, staff, and resident experience all land on your desk.

Day-to-day, you're tracking KPIs, managing the property to an approved operating budget, and keeping delinquency in check. You'll drive occupancy through leasing and renewal strategies, coordinate marketing, and submit weekly and monthly performance reports to the regional team. When a construction or capital project comes up, you're managing that too. The role requires someone who can shift between P&L review in the morning and a resident issue in the afternoon without losing momentum.

Student housing runs on an annual lease cycle tied to the academic calendar, which creates predictable high-pressure windows around lease-up season. Strong candidates know how to build renewal momentum early rather than scrambling in the spring. If you've managed a property through a full lease-up cycle and come out with occupancy intact, that experience matters here more than almost anything else on your resume.

Redstone uses Entrata, so familiarity helps, though they'll train the right person. Comfort with Google Workspace and Microsoft Office is expected.

What they're looking for

  • At least 3 years in student housing or multifamily property management
  • At least 2 years in a property manager role with direct budget and P&L responsibility
  • Experience working with clients or ownership groups directly
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage several projects at once under pressure
  • A track record of leading and developing on-site teams

This is a part-time, hourly position at $22.00 per hour with the opportunity to earn performance bonuses. It reports to a Regional Manager.

Logan is a college town anchored by Utah State University, so the resident base here is almost entirely student-oriented. Understanding that population, how they communicate, what they expect, and how to retain them through summer months, is a real skill. Managers who've worked in similar university markets tend to ramp up faster in roles like this one.

job.title: Service Manager
job.description:
A Service Manager role lives or dies on technical range. HVAC certification is the baseline here, but the day-to-day at Dream Marine Creek pulls across plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, pool maintenance, painting, and grounds. If your skill set runs deep in one trade and thin everywhere else, this will be a grind. If you're genuinely multi-skilled, it plays to your strengths.

What This Role Actually Demands

You're running the service department at a Fort Worth community, which means owning work order flow, turn scheduling, vendor relationships, and the OpEx maintenance budget simultaneously. The 5-day turn target is the metric that tends to separate organized service managers from overwhelmed ones. Vacant apartments need to move through make-ready on a defined punch list, and your team's scheduling discipline drives whether that happens.

Day-to-day responsibilities include:

  • Assigning and tracking service requests with a 24-hour turnaround standard
  • Managing on-call rotation and your team's daily focus
  • Overseeing vendor relationships and supply inventory without over-ordering
  • Processing purchases through AppFolio and keeping spending aligned with budget
  • Handling security deposit dispositions for vacant units
  • Keeping grounds and common areas in order and addressing hazards proactively
  • Leading from the front, including doing technician and groundskeeper work when needed

HVAC certification is required, and you'll need a valid driver's license, a clean driving record, a reliable personal vehicle for daily assignments and on-call rotation, and your own basic tools. Physical demands are real: lifting 50-plus pounds and stairs, daily.

The Leadership Layer

This is a supervisory role, not just a senior technician position. You'll coach and mentor the maintenance team, manage schedules, and set the tone for how service gets done at the property. Budget fluency matters. Cost-saving initiative isn't a nice-to-have here; it's part of the job description. Candidates who've only ever been handed a work order queue and told to clear it will find the management side of this role a bigger adjustment than they expect.

Strong candidates tend to be people who already think in systems. They track turn timelines without being asked, notice when inventory is creeping up before it becomes a budget problem, and can coach a junior tech through a repair rather than just handling it themselves.

The Property and the Company

Dream Marine Creek is located at 5222 Shadydell Dr in Fort Worth, a garden-style community in a market that continues to see meaningful multifamily activity. Dream Live Prosper Communities operates as part of DLP Capital, which has been on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies for thirteen consecutive years. The company focuses on attainable housing, which shapes the culture and the priorities at the property level.

Benefits include PTO, health, dental, vision, and life insurance, plus a 401(k). Schedule flexibility is expected, including weekends. That's standard for this role in any organization.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II (Sherman Central)
job.description:
A resident submits a work order at 8 a.m.: no hot water. By 9, you've diagnosed a failing heating element, sourced the part, and closed the ticket before lunch. That's the rhythm at Sherman Central, a 475-unit, 11-building community in Denver's Capitol Hill corridor where the maintenance queue moves fast and the work is genuinely varied.

What the Role Covers

RedPeak is a Denver-focused owner-operator with 24 years in this specific market, and Sherman Central sits at the heart of their portfolio. As a Maintenance Technician II, you'll carry real diagnostic responsibility across electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliance repair, drywall, and painting. This isn't a role where you shadow someone else's punch list. You're the one diagnosing problems, executing repairs, and coordinating outside contractors when the scope calls for it.

Day-to-day, you'll work through service requests in Yardi, assist the Service Supervisor with scheduling and vendor oversight, and complete routine inspections of common areas and vacant units. On-call rotation is part of the deal, so emergency response comes with the territory. You'll also handle property security systems, including cameras, access controls, and lock changes, and keep detailed maintenance records that support the broader operations of the community.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., with on-call coverage as needed. Pay ranges from $23 to $25 per hour, with monthly maintenance bonus potential on top of base.

What RedPeak Is Looking For

  • 1 to 2 years of hands-on multifamily maintenance, construction, or equivalent trade experience
  • Intermediate working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems
  • Comfort with Yardi or similar work order platforms for ticket management and inventory tracking
  • HVAC/EPA, CPO, electrical, or plumbing certifications are preferred; RedPeak covers EPA and CPO certification costs for the right candidate
  • Reliable transportation and a valid driver's license
  • Strong communication habits, both with residents and with the maintenance team

The candidates who do well here tend to be self-directed on high-volume days. When a property spans 11 buildings and 475 units, work orders stack up quickly, and the technicians who thrive are the ones who triage efficiently, communicate proactively with residents during delays, and close tickets with durable fixes rather than temporary patches. Repeat work orders on the same unit are a signal worth watching in this environment.

Benefits include full medical, dental, and vision coverage, employer-paid short-term disability, a 401(k) with immediate vesting and company match, 16 PTO days, 13 paid holidays, a 30 percent rent discount, student debt repayment assistance, and health club reimbursement up to $75 monthly.

job.title: Part-Time Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a sales job. That's worth saying plainly, because some people come into this role expecting mostly hospitality work and discover quickly that conversion is the scoreboard. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a part-time Leasing Consultant at their Allendale, Michigan community, and they want someone who already understands the difference between a good tour and a closed lease.

Allendale is home to Grand Valley State University, which means this is almost certainly a student housing community. That context matters. Student housing leasing runs on a compressed timeline. The bulk of your lease-up happens in a defined window, traffic spikes hard, and prospects are often comparing you against three other communities they toured the same afternoon. Speed of follow-up and the quality of your first impression carry more weight here than in conventional multifamily. If you've worked student housing before, you know the urgency. If you haven't, expect to learn it fast.

Day to day, you're converting leads that come in through phone, email, and walk-in traffic. You'll run tours, follow up across multiple touchpoints (calls, texts, emails), and handle the paperwork side when a prospect is ready to sign. That includes accurate lease documentation, deposit collection, and keeping prospect data current in the CRM. During turn season, you'll support the move-out and move-in process. It's not glamorous work, but it's real volume and it teaches you how a property actually operates.

The commission structure gives you a direct line between your effort and your paycheck. That's either motivating or it isn't. PeakMade is also upfront that this role comes with weekend availability requirements and peak-hour coverage. Student housing traffic doesn't follow a Monday-through-Friday schedule.

What They're Looking For

  • At least one year of sales or leasing experience with measurable conversion results
  • Comfort working in a CRM (Yardi, Entrata, RealPage, or comparable)
  • A documented follow-up habit, multi-touch outreach across calls, emails, and texts
  • Availability on weekends and during high-traffic leasing periods
  • Enough product knowledge discipline to stay current on pricing, availability, and the competitive set

Strong candidates tend to be self-managing. In a part-time role, you don't have someone watching every lead in your pipeline. The people who succeed here are the ones who treat every prospect with the same follow-up energy whether the leasing office is busy or slow. That consistency is what separates decent conversion rates from strong ones.

Beyond commission, the role includes housing discounts (which vary by community), a 401(k) match, wellness programs, and access to PeakMade's internal development track. For someone early in a property management career, part-time leasing at a student housing property is a legitimate on-ramp. The skills you build here, closing under pressure, CRM discipline, handling high-volume traffic periods, carry directly into full-time leasing roles and eventually into Assistant Manager and Property Manager positions.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager Manufactured Housing Community
job.description:
Big Valley Woods sits in Boring, Oregon, but the role itself has a fair amount of range to it. Investment Property Group operates 150 properties across 13 states, spanning multifamily, manufactured housing, and RV communities, and this Assistant Community Manager position puts you at a 229-home community that also includes 68 RV spots and a handful of tiny homes. That mix of asset types under one roof is genuinely uncommon, and it builds a breadth of operational exposure that a conventional apartment job rarely offers.

The day-to-day here splits roughly between sales and operations. On the sales side, you'll be promoting and closing on available homes, conducting tours, hosting open houses, and staying current on what the local market is doing. On the operations side, you're supporting rent collection, working delinquency procedures, coordinating maintenance and vendor activity, handling resident concerns, and keeping the administrative documentation clean. The Community Manager sets direction; you're the person making sure things actually move.

IPG is looking for someone with at least a year of hands-on experience at a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100 or more homes. Familiarity with property management software matters here, specifically platforms like Manage America, Rent Café, or similar tools. Beyond the technical baseline, the qualities that tend to separate strong candidates from average ones in this kind of role are sales follow-through and conflict resolution composure. You'll meet prospective buyers who need a nudge and residents who have a grievance, sometimes on the same afternoon. Staying steady and professional across both is a real skill.

What the role typically requires

  • 1+ years of experience at a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100+ units
  • Demonstrated ability to manage delinquency and support rent collection processes
  • Sales and marketing skills with the ability to close on available homes
  • Strong written and verbal communication across residents, vendors, and local agencies
  • Proficiency in property management software (Manage America, Blue Moon, Rent Café, or comparable platforms)
  • Valid driver's license
  • Availability for occasional after-hours marketing events, with flexible weekday hours to keep the schedule at 40 hours

From a career trajectory standpoint, this role builds exactly the mixed-portfolio fluency that positions you well for a Community Manager role, either within IPG's growing footprint or elsewhere in the manufactured housing sector. MHC management is a specialized corner of the industry, and operators who understand both the home-sales component and the land-lease operational side are genuinely in demand. The exposure to RV and tiny home product types adds another layer that's increasingly relevant as alternative housing formats attract more institutional attention.

The position pays $26 to $30 per hour depending on qualifications and experience, runs Monday through Friday, and comes with a full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, a 401k with company match, and four weeks of accrued PTO. Benefits begin on the first of the month after 30 days of employment.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician - Preston Reserve
job.description:
Preston Reserve is an AIR Communities property in Cary, NC, and they're adding a Maintenance Technician to the onsite team. The rate lands between $20.00 and $23.78 per hour depending on what you bring, and there's a quarterly customer service bonus program that can add up to $1,500 per quarter for techs who consistently deliver for residents. That's real money, and it's tied to something measurable.

What You'll Actually Do

The work splits fairly predictably between turns and service requests, with the ratio shifting by season. Make-readies require following a defined process to get units presentable for move-in. Service requests cover the usual range: plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliances, general repairs. AIR uses tech-driven work order management, which keeps task prioritization organized and cuts down on the time you'd otherwise spend figuring out what to tackle next. More experienced techs may also mentor newer team members and assist with vendor oversight or move-in/move-out inspections. Scope adjusts based on your skill level and what the community needs.

On-call is part of the deal. At least one week per month, you need reliable transportation and the ability to respond to after-hours emergencies. That's standard in this industry, but worth stating plainly.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment
  • Proficiency in at least two trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, or similar
  • Flexibility for evenings, weekends, and rotating on-call coverage
  • Physical capability to handle and move heavy equipment
  • Detail orientation and a habit of fixing things correctly the first time

Context Worth Knowing

AIR runs a maintenance development program called Ascend, which is built around individual career paths rather than a generic training track. For techs who want to move toward a lead or service manager role, that kind of structured development is worth factoring in. AIR's stated preference is to promote from within, and in our industry, that's genuinely how career progression works at the better operators. A tech who builds HVAC certification on top of solid plumbing and electrical skills is well-positioned for a lead role within a few years, especially at a portfolio company with multiple communities in a market.

The 50% rent discount at any AIR community is one of the stronger resident benefit packages in the sector. Living onsite eliminates commute and puts you close for on-call response. Whether that appeals depends on the person, but it's a tangible financial offset worth calculating against the hourly rate.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, company-paid short and long-term disability, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, 16 weeks paid parental leave, tuition assistance, and full reimbursement for job-related certifications and licenses. That last one matters if you're working toward an HVAC certification or an EPA 608.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Lease Up
job.description:
Lease-up is one of the highest-pressure phases in multifamily. A new community needs to hit occupancy targets fast, often while the building is still finishing punch list work and residents are moving into units that haven't fully settled. The traffic is real, the competition is paying concessions, and every tour counts. Bozzuto is hiring a Leasing Consultant in Atlanta to carry that responsibility at a community in the 30309 corridor.

What the Role Actually Involves

Your core metric is conversion. Traffic coming through the door or filling out online forms needs to turn into signed leases, and that starts before anyone sets foot on property. You'll work every lead in the pipeline, following up with prospects and giving them enough context about the community and the neighborhood to keep momentum alive between first contact and tour. Atlanta's Midtown market is competitive, so knowing how to frame value against comparable product matters.

Tours are where the role gets personal. Bozzuto expects these to be tailored, not scripted. A prospect looking for proximity to MARTA has different priorities than someone relocating from out of state who wants walkability and green space. Reading that quickly and adjusting your pitch is what separates consultants who hit their lease-up targets from those who post a lot of traffic with thin close rates.

Social media is part of the job description, not an afterthought. You'll generate content on platforms like Instagram and Facebook to build awareness during the lease-up phase, when brand recognition for a new community is essentially zero.

The schedule runs three weekends per month, with two weekdays off. That's standard for leasing roles and reflects when most prospects are actually out shopping.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with social media content creation, specifically Instagram and Facebook
  • Sales instincts and a professional presentation
  • Proficiency with software and property management apps
  • A real estate license, or the ability to obtain one within 90 days of hire where required

The base salary is $48,000, with bonus opportunities on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

Where This Role Can Lead

Lease-up experience is genuinely valuable on a multifamily resume. Consultants who can prove they drove a new community from 0% to stabilized occupancy have demonstrated something that steady-state leasing roles don't require. That track record opens doors to Assistant Manager positions and, for those who develop their financial fluency alongside their sales skills, to Property Manager roles where you're accountable for NOI, delinquency, and the full operating picture. Starting in lease-up compresses the learning curve significantly.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Cortland Ten Mile
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role covers the full range of day-to-day maintenance at Cortland Ten Mile, a multifamily community in Meridian. Work orders come in steady: electrical issues, plumbing repairs, HVAC troubleshooting, appliance fixes, flooring, railings, and general building systems. You diagnose what's wrong, fix it correctly, and document it. That last part matters more than people expect. Recurring issues that don't get reported stay recurring issues.

Preventative maintenance is part of the job too, not an afterthought. You'll schedule and perform PM work on HVAC units and building equipment, which keeps downtime low and extends the life of assets the property depends on. You'll also keep an eye on building and security systems, flagging anything that needs attention before it becomes a liability. Hazards like broken lighting, damaged gates, or open holes get corrected fast.

On-call rotation is real. You'll respond to after-hours emergencies when it's your turn, and some of those calls will come at inconvenient times. That's part of the job at any well-run multifamily community, and Cortland structures their teams to share that load, but it's worth knowing upfront.

What You Bring

  • EPA certification (Type I, II, or Universal) required before starting
  • 1 to 3 or more years in maintenance, facilities, or multifamily housing
  • Solid hands-on skills across electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • Ability to manage multiple open work orders and prioritize without losing track of details
  • Comfort working outdoors in Idaho's weather range, climbing ladders, and lifting as needed
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Willingness to participate in on-call schedules and respond when emergencies come up

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Cortland is a large, vertically integrated owner-operator with in-house design, construction, and operations. For a maintenance technician, that structure means you're working within a company that takes asset preservation seriously at the ownership level, not just the management level. There's generally more consistency in how properties are maintained and resourced compared to smaller fee-management operations.

Strong candidates in this type of role tend to be self-directed once they learn a property. You're not going to have someone looking over your shoulder on every work order. The technicians who do well here know how to prioritize their own queue, communicate clearly when something's outside their scope, and treat resident interactions as part of the job rather than an interruption to it. Meridian is a growing market, and a well-maintained community with low delinquency and high occupancy starts with the people keeping the building functional.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Cadia Crossing
job.description:
The morning starts with a stack of rent receipts to reconcile before the bank deadline, a maintenance call forwarded from a resident who moved out last week, and a leasing consultant flagging a prospective renter waiting in the lobby. That's a normal Tuesday at Cadia Crossing, and it's exactly the kind of morning this role is built for.

What This Role Actually Covers

As Assistant Manager at this Olympus Property community in Gilbert, AZ, you'll sit at the intersection of operations, finance, and resident relations. You'll keep financial records accurate, ensure all rent collected hits the bank before close each day, and manage move-out account statements with the kind of precision that protects the property from disputes down the line. Delinquency monitoring and rental collections fall in your lane, and you'll need to be comfortable working through those conversations with residents directly.

On the leasing side, you'll step in to show apartments when volume demands it and inspect make-ready units before move-in to make sure they meet standard. Resident retention, community events, and day-to-day service issues are also part of the job. When the Property Manager is out, you step into that seat and keep operations moving without a gap.

Staying current on the submarket matters here too. Gilbert is a growing East Valley market with active new construction, which means knowing what competitors are offering and how nearby retail and hiring trends affect traffic and occupancy is part of how you add value beyond the office.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant
  • Familiarity with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite (strongly preferred)
  • Comfort handling financial records, deposits, and collections with accuracy and discretion
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with flexibility for resident events and the first weekend of each month
  • A systematic approach to detail without losing sight of the resident experience

Pay runs $22.00 to $24.00 per hour depending on experience, with monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses on top of base. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Olympus has earned recognition as a top employer from the National Apartment Association three consecutive years running.

From a career standpoint, the Assistant Manager role is one of the most instructive positions in residential property management. You're building fluency in collections, financial reporting, leasing, and team coordination simultaneously. That combination is exactly what prepares someone to move into a Property Manager role. Candidates who treat this position as a training ground for full-site ownership tend to advance quickly, and Olympus has a stated commitment to internal career pathing.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Skye Apartments
job.description:
MG Properties has been acquiring, rehabbing, and operating apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. That track record matters when you're evaluating who you work for. Skye Apartments in Vista, CA is their current opening for a Maintenance Supervisor, and it's a real hands-on role at a community of meaningful scale.

Vista sits in North San Diego County, a market with strong rental demand and a resident base that tends to expect a well-maintained product. At the community level, that means your punch list discipline, preventive maintenance tracking, and turn quality are visible in the NOI. A sloppy make-ready process or deferred work orders show up fast in renewal rates and delinquency conversations. The Maintenance Supervisor here carries real operational weight.

Day to day, you'll diagnose maintenance issues, perform work yourself where it makes sense, and delegate to your team where it doesn't. You'll manage the service request workflow, coordinate scheduling with the property manager, run safety meetings, and keep records on preventive maintenance and expenditures. Multi-trade competency is expected. This is a working supervisor position, not a desk job with occasional walkthroughs.

What separates strong candidates in this role from adequate ones usually comes down to two things: systems discipline and crew accountability. Anyone can fix an HVAC unit or a leaking supply line. The supervisors who actually move the needle are the ones who keep the PM schedule current without being reminded, close work orders with documentation that holds up to an audit, and manage techs in a way that raises the whole team's output rather than just covering for gaps.

Minimum qualifications include:
  • At least 2 years of experience in a Maintenance Supervisor capacity
  • Prior experience at a property of 150 units or more
  • Working knowledge across all major trades
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Strong customer service orientation and comfort working as part of a team

Compensation lands at $35 to $36 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of that. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, paid holidays, paid sick time, and rental discounts. It's a complete package by industry standards.

MG Properties participates in E-Verify, operates drug-free, and conducts background checks and drug screens prior to hire. Employment also includes acknowledgment that audio recordings may occur during work duties.

job.title: Director of Resident Well-Being
job.description:
Student housing sits at an unusual intersection: it's a real estate operation, but the residents are 18-to-22-year-olds living away from home for the first time, often under academic and social pressure that property management teams aren't trained to handle. Scion built a national portfolio of off-campus student communities, and this role exists because the gap between "property concern" and "mental health concern" is narrower than most operators acknowledge. The Director of Resident Well-Being is the person who closes that gap at scale.

What This Role Actually Does

This is a strategy and infrastructure role, not a clinical one. The posting is explicit about that boundary, and it matters. You won't be counseling residents, diagnosing anything, or stepping in as a crisis responder. What you will do is build the systems, training, and partnerships that make sure a General Manager at a Scion property in any market knows what to do at 11pm when a resident's roommate calls the front desk worried. That's the real deliverable: confident, protocol-equipped teams who can recognize a concern, document it correctly, and connect a resident to the right resource without overstepping.

The external partnership work is substantial. You'll maintain relationships with university counseling centers, Dean of Students offices, Behavioral Intervention Teams, campus police, disability services, and community crisis-response agencies. Each university market has its own referral pathways and escalation contacts, and keeping those maps current and usable for field teams is ongoing work. On the internal side, you'll partner with Learning and Development to build role-specific training for GMs, regional leaders, and security personnel, and you'll sit alongside Legal, Risk Management, Operations, and HR when a significant incident requires coordinated response.

The resident-facing programming side covers a real range: transition to college, belonging, academic pressure, financial wellbeing, roommate conflict, substance misuse awareness, and crisis-resource literacy. You'll also develop peer-connection strategies, including resident ambassador and wellness champion programs, with careful attention to keeping peer leaders in a connection role rather than a counseling one.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least 10 years of progressive leadership in student affairs, student success, wellness administration, public health, higher education, or behavioral health administration
  • A bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline (psychology, higher education administration, social work, public health, organizational development); an advanced degree is preferred
  • Demonstrated experience building enterprise-wide programs and training frameworks, not just individual initiatives
  • Real familiarity with college-age populations, student development theory, FERPA and privacy considerations, and the professional boundaries around non-clinical wellness roles
  • Background in student housing, residential life, or counseling-services administration is a meaningful advantage
  • Licensed clinical credentials aren't required and won't substitute for the leadership and program-building experience this role demands

The candidates who will stand out aren't necessarily the ones with the most clinical depth. They're the ones who've built programs that actually got adopted at scale, who know how to train non-clinical staff to respond appropriately without overreaching, and who've managed the politics of university partnerships where Scion is a private operator sitting adjacent to a campus bureaucracy. That relationship management skill is harder to teach than wellness content knowledge.

This role is based in Chicago and covers Scion's national portfolio. The work will involve real-time guidance during incidents, which means occasional after-hours coordination when something significant happens at a property. That's worth knowing going in.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II
job.description:
HVAC certification gets you in the door. What keeps a technician valuable at this level is the full package: a working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, and the judgment to sequence a make-ready efficiently when three units are turning at the same time. That's the skillset this role draws on daily.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Hawthorne at the Station is a garden-style community in Wilmington, NC, and this Maintenance Technician II position covers the range you'd expect: completing service requests independently, contributing to preventative maintenance schedules, and getting vacant units to make-ready status on time. Pool maintenance and common area upkeep are part of the rotation too, not afterthoughts. You'll also carry a share of the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That's standard in this industry, and worth knowing going in.

Day-to-day, you're moving between work orders, coordinating with the rest of the maintenance team, and keeping the shop organized well enough that supply inventory is readable at a glance. The residents notice the work when it's done poorly. They rarely notice when it's done well. That's just the job.

Qualifications Worth Having

  • Two years of apartment maintenance experience (preferred, not negotiable in practice)
  • EPA/HVAC certification (required)
  • Valid driver's license
  • CPO certification (a genuine plus at a property with a pool)
  • High school diploma or GED

The technicians who move up quickly in this type of role are the ones who can diagnose before they repair. Anyone can swap a part. Fewer people can walk into a unit, ask the right questions, and identify root cause before ordering anything. That diagnostic habit is what separates a solid tech from a great one.

At Hawthorne Specifically

Hawthorne Residential Partners operates with a defined career path structure, and the Technician II classification sits in the middle of it intentionally. The Learning and Development program is built to move people toward Technician III, and they back that with education reimbursement for maintenance-related coursework. The bonus structure here is more layered than most: monthly renewal bonuses, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses on top of hourly pay. The benefits package includes free dental, medical and vision options, 401k match, and paid parental leave.

Wilmington's rental market has stayed active, and properties along the Station corridor have seen steady occupancy. Hawthorne's portfolio leans into community culture, so resident satisfaction scores carry real weight internally. If you're the kind of technician who fixes the problem and treats the resident like an adult in the process, that combination gets noticed here.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Maintenance leadership at an affordable housing company carries a different weight than at a typical market-rate property. The residents depend on the physical environment in ways that go beyond preference. When something breaks, it matters. That's the context for this Service Manager role with Fairstead in Jonesboro, Georgia.

What This Role Actually Involves

Fairstead operates an integrated platform that brings development, construction, and property management together under one roof. With more than 30,000 units across 28 states, they run at real scale, and they expect their site-level maintenance leadership to match that. As Service Manager, you'll oversee the day-to-day repair and maintenance of buildings on your property, supervise other maintenance team members, and take point on special projects as they arise. Keeping mechanical systems and electrical equipment running, managing inspections, and holding the property to Fairstead's cleanliness and safety standards are core to the position.

This role isn't purely hands-off supervision. You'll work independently on routine tasks and step in on more complex projects with support when needed. Overtime comes with the territory during emergencies or larger initiatives, and that's worth knowing upfront. The ability to implement and improve procedures matters here, not just follow them.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least three years of property maintenance experience, with genuine depth in at least one skilled trade
  • Solid working knowledge of building systems, mechanical trades, and the tools and terminology that go with them
  • Strong safety awareness and the habit of leading others toward it, not just practicing it yourself
  • Organizational skills that hold up when multiple tasks and people need direction at the same time
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office Suite; experience with Yardi or RealPage is a plus

The strongest candidates tend to be people who've already supervised others in a maintenance context and understand that leading a team means setting the standard, not just assigning tasks. If you've worked in affordable housing before, you'll likely appreciate how that experience shapes the way you approach resident interactions and communicate urgency up the chain.

The Broader Picture

Fairstead describes itself as tech-forward and data-driven for an affordable housing operator, which means you'll likely encounter software tools and digital workflows more than you might at a smaller management company. That's worth factoring in if you're used to a more paper-based environment. It also creates a clearer path for maintenance leaders who want to grow: operators like Fairstead tend to promote from within when regional or facilities-level roles open up, and a Service Manager who's demonstrated operational discipline and team development is well-positioned for that next step.

The benefits package includes medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match, 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays, among other perks.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Property management at the community level is where all the disciplines converge: leasing, financials, maintenance coordination, staff development, and resident relations all land on one desk. CommonPlace is hiring a Property Manager for their Raleigh-area community, and this role carries the full weight of that responsibility. You're running the site, leading the team, and owning the resident experience from first tour through renewal.

What This Role Covers

Day-to-day, you're overseeing leasing activity and guiding prospective residents through the full cycle: tours, applications, screenings, deposits, lease execution, and move-in. You're also managing the financial side, building and tracking budgets, monitoring variances, handling accounts payable and receivable, and completing month-end and year-end reporting. That financial fluency matters here. CommonPlace expects accurate, timely reporting, not just operational instincts.

On the maintenance side, you'll conduct regular property inspections and coordinate with your team to keep units move-in-ready and common areas clean and safe. Retention programs, resident concerns, vendor relationships, and marketing campaigns all fall within your scope as well. You're also the hiring manager, trainer, scheduler, and performance evaluator for your on-site staff, which means your leadership style directly shapes how the team operates.

  • 3 to 5 years of property management experience in a leadership capacity
  • Fair Housing knowledge with certification required
  • Demonstrated experience managing budgets and producing financial reports
  • Strong communication and conflict resolution skills across residents, staff, and vendors
  • OneSite and AppFolio experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license and current auto insurance
  • On-site presence five days per week

Where This Role Builds Skills

The craft of property management compounds in a full-cycle role like this one. You already need to arrive with budget fluency, leasing fundamentals, and the confidence to lead a team through conflict and change. What you'll develop further is the judgment that comes from owning outcomes completely. When occupancy dips, you're diagnosing the cause and adjusting marketing strategy. When delinquency creeps up, you're making the call on how to address it. When a make-ready falls behind, you're working the punch list alongside your maintenance team. That kind of decision-making, practiced consistently, is what prepares a property manager to step into a regional or multi-site role.

CommonPlace grounds its work in a community-first philosophy, which shows up in how they expect their managers to handle resident relationships: with professionalism, approachability, and genuine follow-through. The company offers a base salary of $65,000 with performance-based incentives, along with medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability coverage, 401k, and paid vacation, sick, and volunteer time.

job.title: Regional Property Manager - West Coast Portfolio (San Diego Preferred)
job.description:
It's 7:45 a.m. and you're already pulling last month's T-12 across three states, flagging a delinquency spike at one community in Las Vegas while mentally scheduling a site visit to check on punch list progress at a new Southern California lease-up. That's the rhythm of this role.

The Portfolio and What It Demands

Flats LLC operates multifamily communities across California, Nevada, and Washington, with ground-up developments currently underway in Southern California. The Regional Property Manager owns the operational and financial performance of this multi-market portfolio, reporting into executive leadership while managing a layer of on-site Property Managers who need both direction and room to grow.

Budget ownership is real here. You'll build and manage annual operating budgets, run monthly financial analysis, and develop action plans when NOI trends the wrong direction. Owner reporting, quarterly business reviews, and capex recommendations all fall to you. When a new community opens, you're supporting the lease-up strategy and tracking the transition from delivery to stabilization. When a stabilized asset softens, you're diagnosing the traffic-to-lease conversion, reviewing concessions strategy, and working with marketing on a recovery plan.

Day-to-day operations span rent collections, delinquency management, vendor performance, preventative maintenance coordination, and compliance across Fair Housing, ADA, OSHA, and state and local regulations in multiple jurisdictions. California, Nevada, and Washington each carry their own regulatory environment, so experience across more than one of these markets is a genuine asset.

Travel is built into the structure of this role. Expect monthly portfolio visits, frequent day trips between San Diego, Las Vegas, and Portland, and quarterly leadership meetings in Chicago. The company covers travel expenses and provides a company card. A San Diego base is strongly preferred given where the portfolio growth is concentrated.

What Flats Is Looking For

  • Active California Real Estate License (required)
  • At least 3 to 5 years of multifamily experience, including regional or multi-site oversight
  • Demonstrated track record managing budgets, driving NOI, and reporting to ownership groups or investors
  • Experience supporting lease-up of new developments, not just stabilized assets
  • Comfort leading geographically dispersed teams with varying levels of experience
  • Strong communication skills with ownership groups, including presenting financial performance with confidence

The candidates who tend to stand out for roles like this are the ones who've already managed through a lease-up and know what it costs operationally to ramp a new community while keeping stabilized assets at target occupancy. Flats is actively expanding its Southern California footprint, which means this Regional Manager will carry both a stabilized portfolio and a pipeline of new deliveries simultaneously. Candidates with experience on that dual track will hit the ground faster than those whose background is purely in steady-state portfolio management.

This is a hybrid position with a preference for candidates already located in or willing to relocate to the San Diego area.

job.title: Leasing Consultant at Vintage Raleigh West Apartments
job.description:
Leasing roles exist on a spectrum. At some companies, the leasing consultant is a form-processor who hands off to management at every turn. At others, the consultant owns the full prospect relationship and has real authority to solve problems on the spot. Bluecore Residential sits firmly in the second camp, and that shapes what this role at Vintage Raleigh West actually looks and feels like day to day.

The Role at Vintage Raleigh West

Bluecore manages over 10,000 units with roughly $2 billion in assets under management, and they've built their operating model around decentralized decision-making. That means you're not waiting on regional approval to handle a prospect's concern or adjust how a unit is shown. You're expected to think like an owner of your asset, not a gatekeeper for someone else's process.

The core of the job is conversion: turning traffic into leases and leases into renewals. That starts each morning with a walk of the show path, checking that curb appeal, show units, and amenities are ready before the first prospect arrives. From there, the day runs on lead management through the CRM (Yardi preferred), with a hard standard of responding to all inquiries within 30 minutes. Tours, closing, asking for the deposit, following up, and staying current on what competitors are offering are all daily responsibilities, not occasional ones.

Resident retention carries equal weight here. Bluecore expects their leasing consultants to maintain one-on-one touchpoints with current residents and participate in monthly resident events. Occupancy doesn't hold without renewal activity, and this role treats both sides of that equation seriously.

Marketing is part of the job too. Posting ads, verifying website accuracy daily, and managing the property's social media presence across platforms are ongoing tasks, not things that get delegated upward.

What Bluecore Is Looking For

  • Prior leasing or residential sales experience (preferred, not required)
  • Customer service background with a track record of following through
  • Comfort with technology and CRM tools; Yardi experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Reliable transportation for on-site and off-site duties
  • A competitive, organized work style with tolerance for direct feedback and internal debate

Bluecore offers performance bonuses tied to leasing, renewals, and CNOI results, plus certification reimbursement for CAM, CPO, EPA, and other approved credentials. The benefits package includes medical (PPO and HDHP options), dental, vision, FSA/HSA with employer match, a 401(k) with 25% company match up to 6%, PTO starting at hire, and a 25% housing discount on any Bluecore unit.

One thing worth noting for candidates considering this role: the Raleigh market has remained highly competitive through recent years, with significant new Class A supply coming online in the west corridor. That means your comp knowledge and speed-to-follow-up aren't soft skills here. They're the difference between a lease and a lost prospect. Consultants who track concessions trends and understand how their property positions against nearby competition will have a real edge in this market.

This role commonly serves as a foundation for advancement into assistant manager or property manager positions, particularly at operators like Bluecore who promote based on performance metrics and cultural fit. If you have leasing instincts and want room to grow without layers of bureaucracy slowing you down, this is a realistic path to do that.

job.title: Resident Support Lead
job.description:
AIR Communities sits among the largest multifamily owners in the country, and this role sits at the center of one of the most operationally sensitive parts of any portfolio: renewals. The Resident Support Lead position is centralized, meaning you're not walking a property every day. You're working across AIR's portfolio, owning a renewal book, handling escalations from onsite teams, and keeping the notice-to-vacate process clean and compliant.

That sounds straightforward until you're managing a resident who's upset about a renewal offer, a system discrepancy in Entrata that's held up documentation, and a coaching conversation with a teammate, all on the same afternoon. This role demands steady judgment more than speed. You'll field calls and emails from residents at difficult moments in their tenancy, process lease documentation accurately under volume, and serve as the person onsite teams call when something falls outside their lane.

Renter's insurance compliance is a real piece of this job, not an afterthought. You'll track it, enforce it, and follow up when residents fall out of compliance. NTV processing requires the same discipline: entries need to be accurate and timely, because errors downstream affect move-out scheduling, unit turns, and occupancy reporting. Data integrity isn't abstract here. It shows up in audits and corrections that you'll own directly.

The lead title carries real weight. You'll support training and coaching within the team, help distribute workload, and assist leadership on reporting and special projects. You're not a supervisor, but you're the person the team leans on when the work gets complicated.

What a strong candidate looks like

Candidates who do well in centralized renewal roles have usually spent time onsite long enough to understand what a busy leasing office actually feels like, but they've also developed the discipline to manage a portfolio from a desk without the physical cues a property provides. Entrata proficiency matters here. AIR lists it as preferred, not optional in practice. If you've generated renewals, managed NTV workflows, and corrected resident account issues inside a property management system, you're starting from the right place. If you've also helped train or guide teammates through process questions, that's the combination this role is built around.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; at least 3 years of relevant property management experience
  • Hands-on experience with lease renewals, resident retention, and notice-to-vacate processes
  • Proficiency with Entrata or a comparable property management system
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills across multiple channels
  • Ability to manage a personal workload while supporting broader team operations
  • Comfort interpreting and applying policy in situations that require independent judgment

Pay runs $31 to $34 per hour, with a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, paid parental leave, tuition assistance, and a 25% rent discount at any AIR community. The application deadline is July 24, 2026, though AIR will continue reviewing on a rolling basis after that date.

job.title: Full and Part time Leasing Agent Boone North Carolina Rivers Edge
job.description:
Student housing leasing runs on a tighter calendar than most property types. At a university market like Boone, the pre-lease window for the following academic year opens in the fall and closes fast. Hitting occupancy before competitors do matters. River's Edge, serving the Appalachian State University community, has two open positions on its leasing team: one full-time and one part-time.

What the Full-Time Role Actually Involves

At $16 to $19 per hour plus leasing commissions and renewal bonuses, the full-time position is a 40-hour-per-week role that reports to the Property Manager or Leasing Manager. The core of the job is converting traffic into signed leases. That means touring prospective residents and their parents, fielding inquiries across every channel (phone, text, email, walk-ins), processing applications and lease documents, and following up on leads consistently enough to move conversion numbers week over week.

Beyond the leasing funnel, you'll support renewal campaigns, assist with campus marketing and housing fairs, help plan resident events, and keep model units and common areas tour-ready. During turn season in July and August, the role shifts toward supporting move-in and move-out operations. Accurate data entry in platforms like Entrata or RealPage is part of the daily rhythm. Saturdays are part of the schedule, with extended hours during peak leasing season (September through March).

The full-time role includes health, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off and holidays, a 401(k) with company match, a housing discount where applicable, and a clear advancement path toward Assistant Manager or Property Manager.

What the Part-Time Role Looks Like

The part-time position runs 15 to 25 hours per week at $15 to $17 per hour, plus per-lease commissions on every signed lease you generate. Karya builds schedules around class commitments, which makes this a genuine option for current App State students. Responsibilities overlap with the full-time role on the leasing and tour side, with additional front-desk and administrative support. At least one weekend shift per week is required.

Campus involvement actually carries weight here. Someone already embedded in student organizations or Greek life comes with a referral network that converts. Social media or content creation skills are a plus for campus marketing support.

What Separates Strong Candidates

Student housing leasing has a specific dynamic: you're often selling to a parent writing the check while simultaneously convincing the student it's the right fit. The ability to read that room, address guarantor concerns about lease terms and liability, and still make the tour feel welcoming to the prospective resident separates average leasing consultants from strong ones. Prior experience in leasing, sales, hospitality, or retail helps. Familiarity with the Boone market or App State's housing cycles is a genuine advantage. Bilingual English/Spanish candidates are encouraged to apply.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required for both roles
  • Reliable weekend and occasional evening availability
  • Physical ability to walk the property and climb stairs during tours
  • Basic computer proficiency; experience with property management software preferred
  • Valid driver's license preferred for the full-time role

Both roles offer paid training. For the right candidate, the part-time position can evolve into a full-time opportunity after graduation, and the full-time role carries a direct path toward management. In student housing, leasing consultants who learn to read traffic patterns, track lead-to-lease conversion, and support a disciplined renewal campaign tend to move up quickly.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Wye Junction
job.description:
Wye Junction is a Bozzuto-managed community in Durham, NC, and this Maintenance Technician role sits at the center of daily property operations. Technicians at this level handle the full range of residential maintenance work, from routine service tickets to after-hours emergencies, and the position rewards people who bring real trade instincts and a genuine interest in developing them further.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On any given day, you might close out three service tickets before noon, covering a tripped breaker, a running toilet, and an HVAC filter swap, then spend the afternoon pushing a vacant unit through turn-over repairs so it's ready for move-in on schedule. Grounds upkeep, snow removal, and general building cleanliness are part of the rotation too. You'll work weekends and evenings on a rotating basis, and you'll carry on-call responsibility for after-hours emergencies. That's a real part of this job, and it's worth knowing upfront.

The core technical areas are HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance repair. Bozzuto is looking for beginner to intermediate proficiency across those systems, meaning you don't need to be a master in every discipline, but you need enough foundational knowledge to diagnose and resolve common issues independently. Make-ready work, specifically preparing vacant apartments for new residents, will be a consistent part of your workload.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

Coming in, you'll need:

  • Hands-on experience in building maintenance or a trades education
  • Beginner to intermediate proficiency in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
